Amygdalodon.etymology: From Greek 'amygdale' meaning 'almond' and 'odon' meaning 'tooth', meaning 'almond tooth', referring to the almond-shaped teeth.
Amygdalodon.description: Amygdalodon is an extinct genus of basal sauropod from the Early Jurassic of Argentina. The type species is Amygdalodon patagonicus. Fossils of Amygdalodon have been found in the Toarcian-aged Cerro Carnerero Formation (about 180-172 million years ago). Very little is known about it, but it is one of the few Jurassic dinosaurs from South America found thus far.

species.name: Amygdalodon patagonicus
species.etymology: Named for Patagonia, the region of Argentina where the fossils were discovered in the Cerro Carnerero Formation.

Anabisetia.etymology: Named for the late Ana Maria Biset, an influential archaeologist from Neuquén Province, Argentina, where the remains were found.
Anabisetia.description: Anabisetia is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of Patagonia, South America. It was a small bipedal herbivore, around 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) long.

species.name: Anabisetia saldiviai
species.etymology: Named for Roberto Saldivia Blanco, a local farmer who discovered the fossils in 1985 and brought them to the attention of science in 1993.

references.authors: Coria, Rodolfo A.; Calvo, Jorge O.
references.title: A new iguanodontian ornithopod from Neuquen Basin, Patagonia, Argentina

Analong.etymology: Named for the village of A'na in Yunnan, China, where the fossils were discovered.
Analong.description: Analong is an extinct genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod from the Chuanjie Formation in Yunnan, China. The type and only species is Analong chuanjieensis.

species.name: Analong chuanjieensis
species.etymology: Named for the town of Chuanjie in Lufeng County, Yunnan, China, where the fossils were unearthed.

Anasazisaurus.etymology: Named for the Anasazi (Ancestral Pueblo Native Americans) of the American Southwest, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'Anasazi lizard'.
Anasazisaurus.description: Anasazisaurus is a genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid ("duckbill") ornithopod dinosaur that lived about 74 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous Period. It was found in the Farmington Member of the Kirtland Formation, in the San Juan Basin of New Mexico, United States. Only a partial skull has been found to date. It was first described as a specimen of Kritosaurus by Jack Horner, and has been intertwined with Kritosaurus since its description. It is known for its short nasal crest, which stuck out above and between its eyes for a short distance.

species.name: Anasazisaurus horneri
species.etymology: Named for Jack Horner, the influential paleontologist who first described the skull in 1992.

references.journal: New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science Bulletin

Anchiceratops.etymology: From Greek 'anchi' meaning 'near' or 'close to' and 'keratops' meaning 'horned face', indicating its close relationship to Triceratops.
Anchiceratops.description: Anchiceratops is an extinct genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur that lived approximately 73 to 68 million years ago during the latter part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now Alberta, Canada.

species.name: Anchiceratops ornatus
species.etymology: Named for the ornate margin of the skull frill, which is edged by large, coarse triangular projections.

location.locality: 12 miles north of Morrin (70 ft level)

Anchiornis.etymology: From Greek 'anchi' meaning 'near' and 'ornis' meaning 'bird', meaning 'near bird', reflecting its close morphological similarity to modern birds.
Anchiornis.description: Anchiornis is a genus of small, four-winged paravian dinosaurs, with only one known species, the type species Anchiornis huxleyi, named for its similarity to modern birds. Anchiornis fossils have been found only in the Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China, in rocks dated to the Late Jurassic, about 160 million years ago. It is known from hundreds of specimens, and given the exquisite preservation of some of these fossils, it became the first Mesozoic dinosaur species for which almost the entire life appearance could be determined, and an important source of information on the early evolution of birds.

synonyms.name: Aurornis
synonyms.reason: Possible junior subjective synonym of Anchiornis; identification is tentative. Per Olshevsky's Dinosaur Genera List.

species.name: Anchiornis huxleyi
species.etymology: Named for Thomas Henry Huxley, an early proponent of biological evolution and one of the first to propose a close evolutionary relationship between birds and dinosaurs.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.title: A new feathered maniraptoran dinosaur fossil that fills a morphological gap in avian origin

Anchisaurus.etymology: From Greek 'anchi' meaning 'near' or 'close to' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', referring to its placement near the base of the sauropodomorph family tree.
Anchisaurus.description: Anchisaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur. It lived during the Early Jurassic Period, and its fossils have been found in the red sandstone of the Upper Portland Formation, Northeastern United States, which was deposited from the Hettangian age into the Sinemurian age, between about 200 and 192 million years ago. Until recently it was classed as a member of Prosauropoda. The genus name Anchisaurus comes from the Greek αγχι (agkhi) anchi-; "near, close" + Greek σαυρος (sauros); "lizard". Anchisaurus was coined as a replacement name for "Amphisaurus", which was itself a replacement name for Hitchcock's "Megadactylus", both of which had already been used for other animals.

synonyms.name: Amphisaurus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Amphisaurus (Reptilia).

synonyms.name: Megadactylus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Megadactylus (Coleoptera).

species.name: Anchisaurus polyzelus
species.etymology: Means 'much sought for' in Greek, referring to the fact that the ichnologist Edward Hitchcock had for many years vainly sought to discover the identity of the track-maker.

holotype.institution: Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History

synonyms.name: Yaleosaurus
synonyms.reason: Originally described as Y. colurus (later Anchisaurus colurus); now considered referable to Anchisaurus polyzelus, with apparent differences attributed to misinterpretation and growth stage.

synonyms.name: Ammosaurus
synonyms.reason: Originally described as A. major and later treated as Anchisaurus major; ultimately recognized as referable to An. polyzelus, with supposed differences attributed to growth and misinterpretation.

Andesaurus.etymology: Named for the Andes mountain range, near where the fossils were found in South America, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'Andes lizard'.
Andesaurus.description: Andesaurus is a genus of basal titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which existed during the middle of the Cretaceous Period in South America. Like most sauropods, it would have had a small head on the end of a long neck and an equally long tail.

species.name: Andesaurus delgadoi
species.etymology: Named for Alejandro Delgado, the person who found the fossils of Andesaurus.

Angolatitan.etymology: Named after Angola where the fossils were found, combined with Latin/Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'; meaning 'Angolan giant'
Angolatitan.description: Angolatitan is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous. It is also the first non-avian dinosaur discovered in Angola. The genus contains a single species, Angolatitan adamastor, known from a partial right forelimb. Angolatitan was a relict form of its time; it was a Late Cretaceous basal titanosauriform, when more derived titanosaurs were far more common.

species.name: Angolatitan adamastor
species.etymology: Derived from Adamastor, a mythological sea monster that represented the dangers Portuguese sailors faced in the southern Atlantic, a reference to Angola's history as a Portuguese colony until 1975.

Angulomastacator.etymology: From Latin 'angulus' meaning 'bend' or 'angle' and 'masticator' meaning 'chewer'; meaning 'bend chewer', referring to the bent shape of the jaw and the Big Bend area of Texas
Angulomastacator.description: Angulomastacator is a genus of duck-billed dinosaur from the Campanian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Aguja Formation of Big Bend National Park, Texas.

Anhuilong.etymology: Named after Anhui province in China combined with Chinese 'long' meaning 'dragon'; meaning 'Anhui dragon'
Anhuilong.description: Anhuilong is a genus of mamenchisaurid dinosaur known from the Hongqin Formation of Anhui province, China. The genus contains a single species, Anhuilong diboensis.

species.name: Anhuilong diboensis
species.etymology: Named for the locality where the holotype is reposited.

references.title: The second mamenchisaurid dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of Eastern China

Aniksosaurus.etymology: From Modern Greek 'anoixi' meaning 'spring' (the season) and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'spring lizard', referring to the onset of spring in the Southern Hemisphere when the fossil was found
Aniksosaurus.description: Aniksosaurus is a genus of avetheropod dinosaur from what is now Chubut Province, Argentina. It lived during the Cenomanian to Turonian of the Cretaceous period, between 96-91 million years ago. The type species, Aniksosaurus darwini, was formally described from the Bajo Barreal Formation of the Golfo San Jorge Basin by Rubén Dario Martínez and Fernando Emilio Novas in 2006; the name was first coined in 1995 and reported in the literature in 1997. The specific epithet honors Charles Darwin who visited Patagonia in 1832/1833 during the Voyage of the Beagle.

Animantarx.etymology: From Latin 'animatus' meaning 'living' or 'animated' and 'arx' meaning 'fortress' or 'citadel', meaning 'living citadel', referring to its heavily armored body.
Animantarx.description: Animantarx is a genus of nodosaurid ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Early and Late Cretaceous of western North America. Like other nodosaurs, it would have been a slow-moving quadrupedal herbivore covered in heavy armor scutes, but without a tail club. The skull measures approximately 25 cm (10 inches) in length, suggesting the animal as a whole was no more than 3 meters (10 feet) long.

Ankylosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'ankylos' meaning 'fused', 'bent', or 'crooked' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'fused lizard' or 'bent lizard'
Ankylosaurus.description: A genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of western North America. Ankylosaurus was the largest known ankylosaurid, covered in massive bony armor plates (osteoderms) and possessing a large club at the end of its tail. It was among the last non-avian dinosaurs, living alongside Tyrannosaurus and Triceratops.

Anodontosaurus.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'an' meaning 'without', 'odon' meaning 'tooth', and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'toothless lizard', inspired by compression damage to the specimen that removed the teeth and misled the describer into assuming large trituration plates had replaced the normal dentition.
Anodontosaurus.description: Anodontosaurus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaurs within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae. It is known from the entire span of the Late Cretaceous Horseshoe Canyon Formation (mid Late Campanian to "middle" Maastrichtian stage, about 72.8-67 Ma ago) of southern Alberta, Canada, and is also known from the Dinosaur Park Formation (75.6 Ma ago). It contains two species, A. lambei and A. inceptus.

Anomalipes.etymology: From Latin 'anomalus' meaning 'peculiar' or 'abnormal' and 'pes' meaning 'foot'; meaning 'unusual foot', referring to the unusual shape of its foot
Anomalipes.description: Anomalipes is an extinct genus of caenagnathid oviraptorosaurian dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian age) Wangshi Group of China. The genus contains a single species, Anomalipes zhaoi, known from a partial hindlimb.

Anoplosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'anoplos' meaning 'unarmed' or 'unarmored' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'unarmed lizard'
Anoplosaurus.description: Anoplosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian age) Cambridge Greensand of Cambridgeshire, England. It has in the past been classified with either the armored dinosaurs or the ornithopods, but current thought has been in agreement with the "armored dinosaur" interpretation, placing it in the Ankylosauria.

Anserimimus.etymology: From Latin 'anser' meaning 'goose' and Greek 'mimos' meaning 'mimic', meaning 'goose mimic'.
Anserimimus.description: Anserimimus is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaur, from the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now Mongolia. It was a lanky, fast-running animal, possibly an omnivore. From what fossils are known, it probably closely resembled other ornithomimids, except for its more powerful forelimbs.

species.name: Anserimimus planinychus
species.etymology: From Latin planus, meaning 'flat', and the Ancient Greek onyx, meaning 'claw', in reference to the peculiarly flattened claws that characterize the genus.

Antarctopelta.etymology: From 'Antarctica' and Greek 'pelta' meaning 'shield', meaning 'Antarctic shield', reflecting its discovery in Antarctica.
Antarctopelta.description: Antarctopelta is a genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur, a group of large, quadrupedal herbivores, that lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period on what is now James Ross Island, Antarctica. Antarctopelta is the only known ankylosaur from Antarctica and a member of Parankylosauria. The only described specimen was found in 1986, the first dinosaur to be found on the continent, by Argentine geologists Eduardo Olivero and Robert Scasso. The fossils were later described in 2006 by paleontologists Leonardo Salgado and Zulma Gasparini, who named the type species A. oliveroi after Olivero.

Antarctosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'antarktikos' meaning 'southern' (opposite of the north/arctic) and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'southern lizard'
Antarctosaurus.description: Antarctosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now South America. The type species, Antarctosaurus wichmannianus, and a second species, Antarctosaurus giganteus, were described by prolific German paleontologist Friedrich von Huene in 1929. Three additional species of Antarctosaurus have been named since then but later studies have considered them dubious or unlikely to pertain to the genus.

Anteavis.etymology: From Latin 'ante' meaning 'before' and 'avis' meaning 'bird', meaning 'before birds', reflecting its position as an early theropod predating modern birds.
Anteavis.description: Anteavis is an extinct genus of early theropod dinosaurs known from the Late Triassic (Carnian age) Ischigualasto Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Anteavis crurilongus, known from a partial skeleton and skull.

Antetonitrus.etymology: From Latin 'ante' meaning 'before' and 'tonitrus' meaning 'thunder', meaning 'before thunder', referring to its existence before Brontosaurus (the 'thunder lizard').
Antetonitrus.description: Antetonitrus is a genus of sauropodiform dinosaur found in the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation of South Africa. The only species is Antetonitrus ingenipes. Sometimes considered a basal sauropod, it is crucial for the understanding of the origin and early evolution of this group. It was a quadrupedal herbivore, like its later relatives, but shows primitive adaptations to use the forelimbs for grasping, instead of purely for weight support.

species.name: Antetonitrus ingenipes
species.etymology: From Latin ingens, meaning 'massive', and pes, meaning 'foot', because it shows the beginning of the development of feet designed solely to support weight.

holotype.institution: Evolutionary Studies Institute, University of the Witwatersrand

Anzu.etymology: Named for Anzu, a feathered demon from Mesopotamian (Sumerian and Akkadian) mythology.
Anzu.description: Anzu is a genus of caenagnathid dinosaur from North Dakota, South Dakota, and Montana that lived during the Late Cretaceous (upper Maastrichtian stage, 67.2-66.0 Ma) in what is now the Hell Creek Formation. The type species, Anzu wyliei, is known from numerous skeletons that preserve cranial and postcranial elements.

species.name: Anzu wyliei
species.etymology: Named for Wylie J. Tuttle, the grandson of one of the museum's donors, Lee B. Foster.

Aoniraptor.etymology: From Tehuelche 'aoni' meaning 'south' and Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief', meaning 'southern thief'.
Aoniraptor.description: Aoniraptor is an extinct genus of megaraptoran theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Aoniraptor libertatem, known from a partial skeleton.

species.name: Aoniraptor libertatem
species.etymology: From Latin word for freedom, as the specimen was discovered in the bicentennial year of Argentina's independence from Spain in 1810.

Aorun.etymology: From Mandarin Chinese, a shortened masculine name of Ao Run, the Chinese mythical deity and Dragon King of the West Sea in the epic Journey to the West. The species name honors Professor Zhao Xijin.
Aorun.description: Aorun (敖闰 pinyin Áo rùn) is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur first discovered in 2006, with its scientific description published in 2013. It is generally considered one of the oldest known coelurosaurian dinosaurs and is estimated to have lived ~161.6 million years ago during the Late Jurassic Period, though some researchers consider it to be a carnosaurian instead.

Apatoraptor.etymology: From Greek 'apate' meaning 'deception' and Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief'; meaning 'deceptive thief'
Apatoraptor.description: Apatoraptor is a genus of caenagnathid dinosaur which contains a single species, A. pennatus. The only known specimen was discovered in the Campanian-aged Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta.

species.name: Apatoraptor pennatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'pennatus' meaning 'feathered', referring to the discovery of quill knobs on the ulna showing the animal had wings.

Apatosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'apate' meaning 'deception' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'deceptive lizard'
Apatosaurus.description: Apatosaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic period. Othniel Charles Marsh described and named the first-known species, Apatosaurus ajax, in 1877, and a second species, Apatosaurus louisae, was discovered and named by William H. Holland in 1916. Apatosaurus lived about 152 to 151 million years ago (mya), during the late Kimmeridgian to early Tithonian age, and are now known from fossils in the Morrison Formation of modern-day Colorado, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Wyoming, and Utah in the United States. Apatosaurus had an average length of 21–23 m (69–75 ft), and an average mass of 16.4–22.4 t (16.1–22.0 long tons; 18.1–24.7 short tons). A few specimens indicate a maximum length of 11–30% greater than average and a mass of approximately 33 t (32 long tons; 36 short tons).

species.name: Apatosaurus louisae
species.etymology: Named for Louise Carnegie, wife of industrialist Andrew Carnegie, who funded field research to find complete dinosaur skeletons in the American West.

Appalachiosaurus.etymology: Named for the Appalachian region of eastern North America where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'Appalachian lizard'.
Appalachiosaurus.description: Appalachiosaurus is a genus of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of what is now eastern North America. It was a basal member of the clade Eutyrannosauria, meaning it was rather close in relation to the true tyrannosaurids such as Tyrannosaurus. Like most theropods, it was a bipedal predator. Only a juvenile skeleton has been found, representing an animal approximately 6.5 metres (21 ft) long and weighing 623 kilograms (1,373 lb), which indicates an adult would have been significantly larger.

species.name: Appalachiosaurus montgomeriensis
species.etymology: Named for Montgomery County, Alabama, where the holotype was discovered.

references.authors: Carr, Thomas D.; Williamson, Thomas E.; Schwimmer, David R.
references.title: A new genus and species of tyrannosauroid from the Late Cretaceous (Middle Campanian) Demopolis Formation of Alabama

Aquilarhinus.etymology: From Latin 'aquila' meaning 'eagle' and Greek 'rhinos' meaning 'snout' or 'nose'; meaning 'eagle snout', after the unusual beak morphology
Aquilarhinus.description: Aquilarhinus is a genus of hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur from the Aguja Formation from Texas in the United States. The type and only species is Aquilarhinus palimentus. Due to its unusual dentary, it has been inferred to have had shovel-like beak morphology, different from the beaks of other hadrosaurs. It was originally classified as a Kritosaurus sp. before being reclassified as a new genus in 2019.

species.name: Aquilarhinus palimentus
species.etymology: From Latin, combining pala, meaning 'shovel', and mentus, meaning 'chin', referring to the shape of the predentary and its resemblance to a spade or shovel.

Aquilops.etymology: From Latin 'aquila' meaning 'eagle' and Greek 'ops' meaning 'face', meaning 'eagle face', referring to its eagle-like hooked beak.
Aquilops.description: Aquilops is an early herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur dating from the Early Cretaceous of North America, approximately 109 million to 104 million years ago. The type species is A. americanus.

species.name: Aquilops americanus
species.etymology: Named for the fact that the species represents the first unequivocal very basal neoceratopsian found in America.

references.title: A Ceratopsian Dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of Western North America, and the Biogeography of Neoceratopsia

Arackar.etymology: From Kunza (the language of the Atacameno people of Chile) 'arackar' meaning 'skeleton'
Arackar.description: Arackar is an extinct genus of lithostrotian sauropod, possibly part of the Saltasauridae, discovered in the Hornitos Formation of Atacama Province, Chile. The genus contains a single species, Arackar licanantay, described by Rubilar-Rogers et al. in 2021.

synonyms.reason: Nomen nudum; never officially described, treated as junior synonym of Arackar (named 2001, two years prior).

species.name: Arackar licanantay
species.etymology: From the Kunza language, the full binomial Arackar licanantay translating to 'bones of the Atacamans', referring to the Atacameno people indigenous to the region of discovery in Chile.

Aragosaurus.etymology: Named after the Aragon region of Spain where fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Aragon lizard'
Aragosaurus.description: Aragosaurus was a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of Galve, province of Teruel, in the autonomous territory of Aragón, Spain. It was deposited in the Villar del Arzobispo Formation.

species.name: Aragosaurus ischiaticus
species.etymology: From 'ischium', referring to the ischial bones that are part of the known fossil material from this dinosaur.

references.title: Dinosaurios del Cretácico inferior de Galve (Teruel, España) [Dinosaurs from the Lower Cretaceous of Galve (Teruel, Spain)]

Aralosaurus.etymology: Named after the Aral Sea (near where the fossils were found northeast of it) combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Aral Sea lizard'
Aralosaurus.description: Aralosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Kazakhstan. It is known only by a posterior half of a skull (devoid of its mandible) and some post-cranial bones found in the Bostobe Formation in rocks dated from the Upper Santonian - lower Campanian boundary, at about 83.6 Ma (millions of years ago). Only one species is known, Aralosaurus tuberiferus, described by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky in 1968. The genus name means "Aral Sea lizard", because it was found to the northeast of the Aral Sea. The specific epithet tuberiferus means "bearing a tuber" because the posterior part of the nasal bone rises sharply in front of the orbits like an outgrowth.

species.name: Aralosaurus tuberiferus
species.etymology: Means 'bearing a tuber', referring to the posterior part of the nasal bone, which rises sharply in front of the orbits like an outgrowth.

Aratasaurus.etymology: From Tupi 'ara' meaning 'born' and 'atá' meaning 'fire', combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The full name is intended to mean 'the dinosaur born from the National Museum fire', honoring the fire-devastated National Museum of Brazil.
Aratasaurus.description: Aratasaurus is an extinct genus of basal coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian) Romualdo Formation of Brazil. The genus contains a single species, A. museunacionali, known from a partial right leg. Aratasaurus represents the only tetrapod fossil known from the lower levels of the Romualdo Formation.

Archaeoceratops.etymology: From Greek 'archaios' meaning 'ancient', 'keras' meaning 'horn', and 'ops' meaning 'face', translating to 'ancient horned face'.
Archaeoceratops.description: Archaeoceratops, meaning "ancient horned face", is a genus of basal neoceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage) of north central China. It appears to have been bipedal and quite small, reaching 0.9 m (3.0 ft) in length and 10 kg (22 lb) in body mass. It had a comparatively large head but no horns, possessing only a small bony frill projecting from the back of its head.

Archaeocursor.etymology: From Greek 'archaios' meaning 'ancient' or 'old' and Latin 'cursor' meaning 'runner'; meaning 'old runner'
Archaeocursor.description: Archaeocursor is an extinct genus of basal ornithischian dinosaurs from the Early Jurassic Ziliujing Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, A. asiaticus, known from a single femur. Archaeocursor represents the oldest and most basal ornithischian described from Asia.

Archaeodontosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'archaios' meaning 'ancient', 'odous' (genitive 'odontos') meaning 'tooth', and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'ancient-toothed lizard'
Archaeodontosaurus.description: Archaeodontosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic. Its fossils were found in the Isalo III Formation of Madagascar. The type species, Archaeodontosaurus descouensi, was described in September 2005. The specific name honours the collector, Didier Descouens. It is a probable sauropod, with prosauropod-like teeth. It may be a basal member of Gravisauria.

Archaeopteryx.etymology: From Greek 'archaios' meaning 'ancient' and 'pteryx' meaning 'feather' or 'wing', meaning 'ancient wing'.
Archaeopteryx.description: Archaeopteryx , sometimes referred to by its German name, "Urvogel " (lit. 'Primeval Bird') is a genus of bird-like dinosaurs. The genus name derives from the Ancient Greek ἀρχαῖος (archaîos), meaning 'ancient', and πτέρυξ (ptérux), meaning 'feather, wing'. Between the late 19th century and the early 21st century, Archaeopteryx was generally accepted by palaeontologists and popular reference books as the oldest known bird (member of the group Avialae). Older potential avialans have since been identified, including Anchiornis, Xiaotingia, Aurornis, and Baminornis.

Archaeornithomimus.description: Archaeornithomimus is a genus of ornithomimosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period (around 96 million years ago) in the Iren Dabasu Formation of Inner Mongolia, China.

Arcovenator.description: Arcovenator is an extinct genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs hailing from the Late Cretaceous of France and possibly Spain. The type and only described species is Arcovenator escotae. Its name derives from the river Arc flowing near the site of its first discovery.

Arcusaurus.etymology: From Latin 'arcus' meaning 'rainbow', a reference to South Africa being known as the Rainbow Nation, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Arcusaurus.description: Arcusaurus is an extinct genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic (Pliensbachian stage) of South Africa. Arcusaurus was first named by Adam Yates, Matthew Bonnan and Johann Neveling in 2011 and the type species is Arcusaurus pereirabdalorum. The generic name is derived from Latin arcus, "rainbow", a reference to the Rainbow Nation. The specific epithet honours Lucille Pereira and Fernando Abdala who discovered the fossils.

Ardetosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'ardērē' meaning 'to burn' and Ancient Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', referring to the holotype specimen's burn damage from the 2003 Dinosaurier Freilichtmuseum fire.
Ardetosaurus.description: Ardetosaurus is an extinct genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Morrison Formation of northern Wyoming, United States. The genus contains a single species, Ardetosaurus viator. It was first described in 2024 on the basis of a partial articulated skeleton, including vertebrae from the neck, back, and tail, hip bones, and part of the left hindlimb. The genus is a member of the Diplodocinae, a subfamily of large long-necked dinosaurs with whiplike tails. Ardetosaurus represents one of many distinct sauropod taxa that coexisted in this formation.

Arenysaurus.etymology: Named for Arén, the town in the Pyrenees of Spain near where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Arenysaurus.description: Arenysaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (66 million years ago), being one of the last non-avian dinosaurs and it went extinct during the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event. It is known from a partial skull and skeleton found in the late Maastrichtian-age Tremp Formation of the Pyrenees Mountains in Spain. The type species is A. ardevoli, described in 2009 by Pereda-Suberbiola et al., a group of researchers from Spain. The genus name refers to Arén, where it was found, and the specific epithet honours geologist Lluís Ardèvol. Arenysaurus was a lambeosaurine, a member of the hadrosaurid subfamily with hollow and decorative cranial crests. It is one of the most complete and best dated ever found in the Late Cretaceous period.

Argentinosaurus.etymology: From Argentina (the country where fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'lizard from Argentina'.
Argentinosaurus.description: Argentinosaurus is a genus of giant sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina. Although it is only known from fragmentary remains, Argentinosaurus is one of the largest known land animals of all time, perhaps the largest, measuring 30–35 m (98–115 ft) long and weighing 65–80 t (72–88 short tons). It was a member of Titanosauria, the dominant group of sauropods during the Cretaceous.

Argyrosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'argyros' meaning 'silver' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'silver lizard', named for Argentina (from Latin 'argentum', silver).
Argyrosaurus.description: Argyrosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived about 70 million years ago, during the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now Argentina.

Aristosuchus.description: Aristosuchus is a genus of small coelurosaurian dinosaur that lived in the Early Cretaceous period (Barremian stage, sometime between 130 and 123 million years ago) of what is now England, UK. Arkansaurus.etymology: From Arkansas (the U.S. state where fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Arkansas lizard'.
Arkansaurus.description: Arkansaurus is an extinct genus of ornithomimosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived during the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous in what is now North America. The type and only species is Arkansaurus fridayi.

references.authors: Hunt, Rebecca K.; Quinn, James H.
references.title: A new ornithomimosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Trinity Group of Arkansas

Arrhinoceratops.etymology: From Ancient Greek a-/alpha privative (ἀ-) meaning 'no/without' + rhis (ῥίς) meaning 'nose' + keras (κέρας) meaning 'horn' + ops (ὤψ) meaning 'face'; overall meaning 'no nose-horn face'.
Arrhinoceratops.description: Arrhinoceratops is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur. The name was coined as its original describer concluded it was special because the nose-horn was not a separate bone, however further analysis revealed this was based on a misunderstanding. It lived during the latest Campanian/earliest Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, predating its famous relative Triceratops by a few million years, although it was contemporary with Anchiceratops. Its remains have been found in Canada.

species.name: Arrhinoceratops brachyops
species.etymology: Means 'short-faced', derived from the Greek brachys, meaning 'short'.

location.locality: Neill's Ranch, Red Deer River (125 ft level)

references.authors: Parks, W. A.
references.title: Arrhinoceratops brachyops, a new genus and species of Ceratopsia from the Edmonton Formation of Alberta
references.journal: University of Toronto Studies, Geology Series

Arrudatitan.etymology: Named after Arruda (a person's name honoured in the genus), combined with Greek Titan meaning 'giant'; overall meaning 'Arruda's giant'.
Arrudatitan.description: Arrudatitan is an extinct genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian-Maastrichtian)-aged Adamantina Formation of Brazil. The type species, A. maximus, was named and described in 2011 as a species of Aeolosaurus, but was separated into its own genus in 2021. It was relatively gracile for a titanosaur.

species.name: Arrudatitan maximus
species.etymology: From Latin 'maximus' meaning 'greatest' or 'largest', in reference to the large size of the taxon; originally published as 'Aeolosaurus maximus' before the genus was renamed Arrudatitan to honour the late Professor Antonio Celso de Arruda Campos, one of the original describers.

references.authors: Silva Junior, Julian C. G.; Martinelli, Agustín G.; Iori, Fabiano V.; Marinho, Thiago S.; Hechenleitner, E. Martín; Langer, Max C.
references.title: Reassessment of Aeolosaurus maximus, a titanosaur dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Southeastern Brazil

Asfaltovenator.etymology: From the Cañadón Asfalto Formation (the fossil formation where remains were found, named for asphalt deposits) + Latin venator meaning 'hunter'; overall meaning 'Cañadón Asfalto Formation hunter'.
Asfaltovenator.description: Asfaltovenator is a genus of possibly allosauroid dinosaur from the Early to Middle Jurassic Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina. The type and only species is Asfaltovenator vialidadi.

species.name: Asfaltovenator vialidadi
species.etymology: Named for the Dirección Nacional de Vialidad (Argentina's national road authority), which assisted the Museo Paleontológico 'Egidio Feruglio' in recovering the fossil.

references.authors: Rauhut, Oliver W. M.; Pol, Diego
references.title: Probable basal allosauroid from the early Middle Jurassic Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Argentina highlights phylogenetic uncertainty in tetanuran theropod dinosaurs
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Asiaceratops.etymology: From Asia (the continent where the genus was found) + Greek keras (κέρας) meaning 'horn' + ops (ὤψ) meaning 'face'; overall meaning 'Asian horned face'.
Asiaceratops.description: Asiaceratops is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur. It lived during the Early-Late Cretaceous. The type species, A. salsopaludalis is known from Uzbekistan, while A. sulcidens is known from China and Mongolia.

species.name: Asiaceratops salsopaludalis
species.etymology: From Latin 'salsopaludalis' meaning 'of the salt marsh', referring to the environment of the Khodzhakul Formation in Uzbekistan where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Chernyshev Central Museum of Geological Exploration

references.authors: Nessov, L. A.; Kaznyshkina, L. F.; G. O. Cherepanov
references.title: [Mesozoic ceratopsian dinosaurs and crocodiles of central Asia]
references.journal: In Bogdanova and Khozatskii (eds.), Theoretical and Applied Aspects of Modern Palaeontology

Asiatyrannus.etymology: From Asia (the continent where fossils were found) + Greek tyrannos (τύραννος) meaning 'tyrant'; overall meaning 'Asian tyrant'.
Asiatyrannus.description: Asiatyrannus is an extinct genus of tyrannosaurine theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, A. xui, known from a single specimen consisting of a skull and partial postcranial skeleton. Asiatyrannus is notable for its deep-snouted skull and small body size, in contrast to the gracile snout and larger size of the contemporary Qianzhousaurus. It represents the southernmost record of an Asian tyrannosaurid.

species.name: Asiatyrannus xui
species.etymology: Named for prominent dinosaur researcher Xu Xing and his contributions to paleontological research in China.

holotype.material: Articulated skull and disarticulated postcranial elements including caudal vertebrae and leg bones

references.authors: Zheng, Wenjie; Jin, Xingsheng; Xie, Junfang; Du, Tianming
references.title: The first deep-snouted tyrannosaur from Upper Cretaceous Ganzhou City of southeastern China
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Astigmasaura.etymology: From compound Latin 'astigma' meaning 'without signs' and Ancient Greek 'saura' (feminine of sauros) meaning 'lizard'; references the type locality El Orejano, whose name refers to unmarked animals.
Astigmasaura.description: Astigmasaura is an extinct genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Astigmasaura genuflexa, known from an incomplete articulated skeleton.

species.name: Astigmasaura genuflexa
species.etymology: From Medieval Latin, combining 'genu', meaning 'knee', and 'flecto', meaning 'to flex', translating roughly as 'kneeling', in reference to the discovery of the holotype with both hindlimbs angled backward.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino Urquiza, Rincón de los Sauces

references.authors: Bellardini, Flavio; Filippi, Leonardo S.; Carballido, José L.; Garrido, Alberto C.; Baiano, Mattia A.
references.title: Side by side with titans: A new rebbachisaurid dinosaur from the Huincul Formation (upper Cenomanian) of Patagonia, Argentina

Astrodon.etymology: From Greek 'astron' meaning 'star' and 'odon' meaning 'tooth', referring to the star-like cross-sectional pattern seen in its tooth enamel.
Astrodon.description: Astrodon is a genus of large herbivorous sauropod dinosaur, measuring 20 m (66 ft) in length, 9 m (30 ft) in height and 20 metric tons (22 short tons) in body mass. It lived in what is now the eastern United States during the Early Cretaceous period, and fossils have been found in the Arundel Formation, which has been dated through palynomorphs to the Albian about 112 to 110 million years ago.

synonyms.name: Astrodontaurus
synonyms.reason: Original genus name proposed by Johnston, who shortened it to Astrodon for the published 1859 description.

synonyms.name: Astrodonius
synonyms.reason: Material is indistinguishable from Astrodon and is treated as a junior synonym.

species.name: Astrodon johnstoni
species.etymology: Named for Christopher Johnston, the dentist and professor at Baltimore Dental College who first studied and named the genus in 1859.

holotype.institution: Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History

references.authors: Johnston, C.
references.title: Note upon odontology
references.journal: The American Journal of Dental Science, new series
references.notes: Genus authority: Johnston named Astrodon (genus) here based on tooth morphology but did not designate a species. The type species A. johnstoni was named separately by Leidy 1865.

references.authors: Leidy, J.
references.title: Cretaceous reptiles of the United States

Astrophocaudia.etymology: From Greek 'a-' meaning 'not', 'stropho-' meaning 'twisting', and 'caud-' meaning 'tail', giving 'non-twisting tail' in reference to the closely-connected hyposphene-hypantrum articulation of the caudal vertebrae; alternatively readable as 'star tail' (Greek 'astron' + 'caud'), also honouring Astrodon.
Astrophocaudia.description: Astrophocaudia is an extinct genus of somphospondylan sauropod known from the later part of the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) of Texas, United States. Its remains were discovered in the Paluxy Formation. The type species is A. slaughteri, described in 2012.

species.name: Astrophocaudia slaughteri
species.etymology: Named for Robert Slaughter, the paleontologist who originally discovered and excavated the fossil remains in Texas in the 1960s.

holotype.institution: Schuler Museum of Paleontology, Southern Methodist University
holotype.material: Single tooth (SMU 203/73655) and partial postcranial skeleton (SMU 61732) together comprising the holotype

references.authors: D’Emic, Michael D.
references.title: Revision of the sauropod dinosaurs of the Lower Cretaceous Trinity Group, southern USA, with the description of a new genus

Asylosaurus.etymology: From Ancient Greek asylos (ἄσυλος) meaning 'unharmed, inviolable, having right of asylum' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'unharmed lizard', referring to the specimens surviving World War II bombardment unlike the Thecodontosaurus holotype.
Asylosaurus.description: Asylosaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic Avon Fissure Fill of England. It is based on partial remains, discovered in the autumn of 1834, described in 1836 by Henry Riley and Samuel Stutchbury as pertaining to Thecodontosaurus, that Othniel Charles Marsh brought to Yale University between 1888 and 1890. These remains thus escaped destruction by a bombardment in 1940 during World War II, unlike the original holotype of Thecodontosaurus. Asylosaurus was described in 2007 by Peter Galton. The type species is A. yalensis, referring to Yale. The bones originally came from a Rhaetian-age cave fill at Durdham Down, Clifton, Bristol.

species.name: Asylosaurus yalensis
species.etymology: Named for Yale University, where the bones were brought by Othniel Charles Marsh between 1888 and 1890 and where they were preserved.

holotype.institution: Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History

references.authors: Galton, P. M.
references.title: Notes on the remains of archosaurian reptiles, mostly basal sauropodomorph dinosaurs, from the 1834 fissure fill (Rhaetian, Upper Triassic) at Clifton in Bristol, southwest England

Atacamatitan.etymology: Named for the Atacama Desert of Chile where it was found, combined with 'titan' meaning 'giant', meaning 'Atacama Desert titan'.
Atacamatitan.description: Atacamatitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Tolar Formation of Chile.

species.name: Atacamatitan chilensis
species.etymology: Named for Chile, the country where the holotype was discovered.

references.authors: Kellner, Alexander W.A.; Rubilar-Rogers, David; Vargas, Alexander; Suárez, Mario
references.title: A new titanosaur sauropod from the Atacama Desert, Chile
references.journal: Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências

Athenar.etymology: Named for Cleveland metal artist Athenar, whose music was described as 'the soundtrack to the majority of the work done on this specimen'. The species name honors David Berman, who carried out foundational modern work on diplodocoid skulls.
Athenar.description: Athenar is an extinct genus of dicraeosaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of Utah, United States. The genus contains a single species, Athenar bermani, which was described by John Whitlock and colleagues in 2025 based on the holotype specimen CM 26552: a braincase and skull roof previously ascribed to the genus Diplodocus. The specimen was found in rocks belonging to the Morrison Formation at the Carnegie Quarry at Dinosaur National Monument.

species.name: Athenar bermani
species.etymology: Named for David Berman, who together with John McIntosh carried out much of the foundational modern work on diplodocoid skulls at the Carnegie Museum of Natural History and was responsible for the initial description of the holotype specimen.

holotype.material: Braincase and partial skull roof (frontal, parietal, partial postorbital, squamosal fragments)

references.authors: Whitlock, John A.; Garderes, Juan Pablo; Gallina, Pablo; Lamanna, Matthew C.
references.title: Athenar bermani, a new species of dicraeosaurid sauropod from Dinosaur National Monument, Utah, U.S.A.

Atlasaurus.etymology: Named for the Atlas Mountains of North Africa, where its fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Atlasaurus.description: Atlasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaurs from Middle Jurassic (Bathonian to Callovian stages) beds in North Africa.

species.name: Atlasaurus imelakei
species.etymology: From Arabic 'imelakei' meaning 'giant', reflecting the large size of the animal.

holotype.institution: Ministère de l'Énergie et des Mines

references.authors: Monbaron, Michel; Russell, Dale A.; Taquet, Philippe
references.title: Atlasaurus imelakei n.g., n.sp., a brachiosaurid-like sauropod from the Middle Jurassic of Morocco alen
references.journal: Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences - Series IIA - Earth and Planetary Science

Atlascopcosaurus.etymology: Named for Atlas Copco, the company whose equipment sponsored the Dinosaur Cove excavation in Australia, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Atlascopcosaurus.description: Atlascopcosaurus is a genus of herbivorous basal iguanodont dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Eumeralla Formation of Australia.

species.name: Atlascopcosaurus loadsi
species.etymology: Named for William Loads, the state manager for Atlas Copco at the time of the excavations, who assisted during the dig that discovered the dinosaur.

references.authors: Rich, T. H.; Vickers-Rich, P.
references.title: Polar dinosaurs and biotas of the Early Cretaceous of southeastern Australia

Atrociraptor.etymology: From Latin 'atrox' meaning 'savage' or 'cruel' and 'raptor' meaning 'robber' or 'thief', meaning 'savage robber'.
Atrociraptor.description: Atrociraptor is a genus of dromaeosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Alberta, Canada. The first specimen, a partial skull, was discovered in 1995 by the fossil collector Wayne Marshall in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, about 5 km (3 mi) from the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology where it was brought for preparation. In 2004, the specimen became the holotype of the new genus and species Atrociraptor marshalli; the generic name is Latin for "savage robber", and the specific name refers to Marshall. The holotype consists of the premaxillae (frontmost bones of the upper jaw), a maxilla (main bone of the upper jaw), the dentaries (tooth-bearing bones of the lower jaw), associated teeth, and other skull fragments. Isolated teeth from the same formation have since been assigned to Atrociraptor.

species.name: Atrociraptor marshalli
species.etymology: Named for Wayne Marshall, the fossil collector who discovered the holotype specimen in 1995 in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta.

location.locality: 5 km west of Royal Tyrrell Museum

references.authors: Currie, P. J.; Varricchio, D. J.
references.title: A new dromaeosaurid from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation (Upper Cretaceous) of Alberta, Canada
references.journal: Feathered Dragons. Indiana University Press, Bloomington

Atsinganosaurus.etymology: From the Greek word 'τσιγγάνος' or 'αθίγγανος' meaning 'gypsy', referring to the possible migration from east to west of the species, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name honors its discovery locality Velaux-La Bastide Neuve.
Atsinganosaurus.description: Atsinganosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which existed in what is now France during the Late Cretaceous. Well-preserved remains (and the only known) of Atsinganosaurus were collected from the Grès à Reptiles Formation of the Aix-en-Provence Basin. The type and only species is A. velauciensis.

species.name: Atsinganosaurus velauciensis
species.etymology: Named for the discovery site at Velaux-La Bastide Neuve in southern France.

references.authors: Garcia, Géraldine; Amico, Sauveur; Fournier, Francois; Thouand, Eudes; Valentin, Xavier
references.title: A new Titanosaur genus (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the Late Cretaceous of southern France and its paleobiogeographic implications
references.journal: Bulletin de la Société Géologique de France

Aucasaurus.etymology: Named after Auca Mahuevo, the fossil site in Argentina where it was found; 'saur' from Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Auca Mahuevo lizard'.
Aucasaurus.description: Aucasaurus is a genus of medium-sized abelisaurid theropod dinosaur from Argentina that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Santonian to Campanian stage) of the Anacleto Formation. It was smaller than the related Carnotaurus, although more derived in some ways, such as its extremely reduced arms and almost total lack of fingers.

species.name: Aucasaurus garridoi
species.etymology: Named in homage to Alberto Garrido, who discovered the holotype.

references.authors: Coria, Rodolfo A.; Chiappe, Luis M.; Dingus, Lowell
references.title: A new close relative ofCarnotaurus sastreiBonaparte 1985 (Theropoda: Abelisauridae) from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia

Augustynolophus.etymology: Named after the Augustyn family (donors to the Los Angeles County Museum) combined with Greek lophos meaning 'crest', a reference to its relative Saurolophus.
Augustynolophus.description: Augustynolophus is an extinct genus of herbivorous saurolophine hadrosaur dinosaur which was discovered in the Moreno Formation in California, dating to the late Maastrichtian age, making it one of the last non-avian dinosaurs known from the fossil record before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.

species.name: Augustynolophus morrisi
species.etymology: Named for palaeontologist William Morris.

holotype.institution: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County

references.authors: PRIETO-MÁRQUEZ, ALBERT; WAGNER, JONATHAN R.; BELL, PHIL R.; CHIAPPE, LUIS M.
references.title: The late-surviving ‘duck-billed’ dinosaur Augustynolophus from the upper Maastrichtian of western North America and crest evolution in Saurolophini

Auroraceratops.etymology: From Latin aurora meaning 'dawn' and Greek keras/ceratops meaning 'horned face'. Full meaning: 'dawn horned face', referring to its status as an early ceratopsian and also honouring Dawn Dodson.
Auroraceratops.description: Auroraceratops, meaning "dawn horned face", is a genus of bipedal basal neoceratopsian dinosaur, from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian age) of north central China. The etymology of the generic name refers to its status as an early ceratopsian and also to Dawn Dodson, wife of Peter Dodson, one of the palaeontologists who described it.

species.name: Auroraceratops rugosus
species.etymology: Named for the rugose, or rough, texturing of the skull and jaws of the holotype specimen.

holotype.institution: Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences-Institute of Geology

references.authors: You, H.; Li, D.; Q. Ji, M. C. Lamanna, P. Dodson
references.title: On a new genus of basal neoceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Gansu Province, China

Australodocus.etymology: From Latin australis meaning 'southern' + Greek dokos (δοκός) meaning 'beam'; overall meaning 'southern beam', referring to its discovery in southern Tanzania.
Australodocus.description: Australodocus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic period, around 150 million years ago, in what is now Lindi Region, Tanzania. Though initially considered a diplodocid, recent analyses suggest it may instead be a titanosauriform.

species.name: Australodocus bohetii
species.etymology: Named for Boheti bin Amrani, a native crew supervisor and chief preparator who was an important contributor to the German expeditions that first excavated the Tanzanian fossil sites.

references.authors: REMES, KRISTIAN
references.title: A SECOND GONDWANAN DIPLODOCID DINOSAUR FROM THE UPPER JURASSIC TENDAGURU BEDS OF TANZANIA, EAST AFRICA

Australotitan.etymology: From Latin 'australis' meaning 'southern' and Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant', referring to the large size of this dinosaur from southern Australia.
Australotitan.description: Australotitan is an extinct genus of possibly titanosaurian somphospondylan dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation (Cenomanian–Turonian) of southern-central Queensland, Australia. The genus contains a single species, A. cooperensis, known from multiple partial skeletons. The genus Australotitan may be synonymous with Diamantinasaurus, a contemporary relative.

species.name: Australotitan cooperensis
species.etymology: Named for the Cooper Creek system near the initial location of the holotype, and the nickname 'Cooper' given to the holotype when it was discovered.

references.authors: Hocknull, Scott A.; Wilkinson, Melville; Lawrence, Rochelle A.; Konstantinov, Vladislav; Mackenzie, Stuart; Mackenzie, Robyn
references.title: A new giant sauropod, Australotitan cooperensis gen. et sp. nov., from the mid-Cretaceous of Australia

Australovenator.etymology: From Latin australis meaning 'southern' + Latin venator meaning 'hunter'; overall meaning 'southern hunter', referring to its discovery in Australia.
Australovenator.description: Australovenator is a genus of megaraptoran theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation (Cenomanian, 95 million years ago) of Australia. Some specimens from the Albian-aged Eumeralla Formation and the Wonthaggi Formation may belong to Australovenator. It is known from partial cranial and postcranial remains, which were described in 2009 by Scott Hocknull and colleagues, although additional descriptions and analyses continue to be published. It is the most complete predatory dinosaur discovered in Australia. It has been suggested that Australovenator is a sister taxon to Fukuiraptor, although some phylogenetic analyses find it to be a more derived member of the Megaraptora, possibly being part of the main Megaraptoridae family itself.

species.name: Australovenator wintonensis
species.etymology: Named for nearby Winton, the town in Queensland, Australia, near where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Australian Age of Dinosaurs Fossil Museum of Natural History

references.authors: Hocknull, Scott A.; White, Matt A.; Tischler, Travis R.; Cook, Alex G.; Calleja, Naomi D.; Sloan, Trish; Elliott, David A.
references.title: New Mid-Cretaceous (Latest Albian) Dinosaurs from Winton, Queensland, Australia

Austrocheirus.etymology: From Latin austro- meaning 'southern' + Greek cheir (χείρ) meaning 'hand'; overall meaning 'southern hand', referring to its discovery in southern Argentina and the partial hand fossils known.
Austrocheirus.description: Austrocheirus is an extinct genus of theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period. It was named and described by Martin Ezcurra, Federico Agnolin and Fernando Novas in 2010. It contains the type species Austrocheirus isasii. The generic name means "southern hand". The specific epithet honours discoverer and preparator Marcelo Pablo Isasi.

species.name: Austrocheirus isasii
species.etymology: Named for Marcelo Pablo Isasi, the discoverer and preparator of the fossil remains.

references.authors: EZCURRA, MARTÍN D.; AGNOLIN, FEDERICO L.; NOVAS, FERNANDO E.
references.title: An abelisauroid dinosaur with a non-atrophied manus from the Late Cretaceous Pari Aike Formation of southern Patagonia

Austroposeidon.etymology: From Latin austro- meaning 'southern' + Poseidon (Ποσειδῶν), the Greek god of the sea, used here as a reference to enormous size (as in Sauroposeidon); overall meaning 'Southern Poseidon'.
Austroposeidon.description: Austroposeidon is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Presidente Prudente Formation of Brazil. It contains one species, Austroposeidon magnificus (meaning "Magnificent Southern Poseidon").

species.name: Austroposeidon magnificus
species.etymology: From Latin 'magnificus' meaning 'great, elevated, noble', referring to the large size of the specimen.

location.locality: Raposo Tavares road, close to the Assis Chateaubriand Road

holotype.institution: Collection of the Earth Science Museum of the National Department of Mineral Production

references.authors: Bandeira, Kamila L. N.; Medeiros Simbras, Felipe; Batista Machado, Elaine; de Almeida Campos, Diogenes; Oliveira, Gustavo R.; Kellner, Alexander W. A.
references.title: A New Giant Titanosauria (Dinosauria: Sauropoda) from the Late Cretaceous Bauru Group, Brazil

Austroraptor.etymology: From Latin auster meaning 'south' and Latin raptor meaning 'thief/plunderer'. Full meaning: 'southern thief/plunderer', referring to its South American (southern) origin.
Austroraptor.description: Austroraptor is a genus of unenlagiine theropod dinosaur that lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.

species.name: Austroraptor cabazai
species.etymology: Named for Héctor 'Tito' Cabaza, who founded the Museo Municipal de Lamarque in Argentina where the specimen was partially studied.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales ‘Bernardino Rivadavia’

references.authors: Novas, Fernando E; Pol, Diego; Canale, Juan I; Porfiri, Juan D; Calvo, Jorge O
references.title: A bizarre Cretaceous theropod dinosaur from Patagonia and the evolution of Gondwanan dromaeosaurids
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

Austrosaurus.etymology: From Latin auster meaning 'south' and Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'southern lizard', referring to its Australian origin.
Austrosaurus.description: Austrosaurus was an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Allaru Formation, dated to the early Cretaceous (112-100 million years ago), of Central-Western Queensland in Australia. Several specimens are known.

species.name: Austrosaurus mckillopi
species.etymology: Named for H. Mackillop, the station manager of Clutha Station who was alerted to the fossil discovery and helped bring it to scientific attention.

references.authors: Longman, H. A.
references.title: A new dinosaur from the Queensland Cretaceous

Avaceratops.etymology: Named after Ava Cole, wife of fossil hunter Eddie Cole who discovered the specimen, combined with Greek 'ceratops' meaning 'horned face'. The species name honors the Lammers family, owners of the Careless Creek Ranch where the fossil was found.
Avaceratops.description: Avaceratops is a genus of small herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaurs which lived during the late Campanian in what are now the Northwest United States. Most fossils come from the Judith River Formation.

species.name: Avaceratops lammersi
species.etymology: Named for the Lammers family, owners of the Careless Creek Ranch in Montana where the first remains were discovered.

references.authors: Dodson, P.
references.title: Avaceratops lammersi: a new ceratopsid from the Judith River Formation of Montana
references.journal: Proceedings of the Academy of Natural Sciences of Philadelphia

Avimimus.etymology: From Latin avis meaning 'bird' + Latin mimus meaning 'mimic'; overall meaning 'bird mimic', named for its bird-like characteristics.
Avimimus.description: Avimimus is a genus of oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaur, named for its bird-like characteristics, that lived in the late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia, during the Maastrichtian.

species.name: Avimimus portentosus
species.etymology: From Latin 'portentosus' meaning 'monstrous' or 'extraordinary', referring to the unusual bird-like characteristics of the animal.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Kurzanov, S. M.
references.title: O neobuchnykh teropodakh iz verkhnego mela MNR [An unusual theropod from the Upper Cretaceous of Mongolia]
references.journal: Fossil Reptiles of Mongolia. Sovmestnaya Sovetsko-Mongol'skaya Paleontologicheskaya Ekspeditsiya, Trudy [The Joint Soviet-Mongolian Paleontological Expedition, Transactions]

Baalsaurus.etymology: Named after the Baal fossil site in Argentina (itself named after the ancient Phoenician god Baal) combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Baal lizard'.
Baalsaurus.description: Baalsaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina. The type and only known species is B. mansillai, with the specific name honoring the discoverer Juan Eduardo Mansilla, a museum technician at the Geology and Paleontology Museum of the National University of Comahue.

species.name: Baalsaurus mansillai
species.etymology: Named for Juan Eduardo Mansilla, a museum technician at the Geology and Paleontology Museum of the National University of Comahue who discovered the holotype.

Bactrosaurus.etymology: From Greek baktron (βάκτρον) meaning 'club' or 'walking stick' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'club lizard'.
Bactrosaurus.description: Bactrosaurus is a genus of herbivorous hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, from about 96 to 85 million years ago. The position Bactrosaurus occupies in the Cretaceous makes it one of the earliest known hadrosauroids, and although it is not known from a full skeleton, Bactrosaurus is one of the best known of these early hadrosauroids, making its discovery a significant finding.

Bagaceratops.etymology: From Mongolian baga meaning 'small' + Greek keras (κέρας) meaning 'horn' + ops (ὤψ) meaning 'face'; overall meaning 'small-horned face'.
Bagaceratops.description: Bagaceratops is a genus of small protoceratopsid dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, around 72 to 71 million years ago. Bagaceratops remains have been reported from the Barun Goyot Formation and Bayan Mandahu Formation. One specimen may argue the possible presence of Bagaceratops in the Djadochta Formation.

Bagualia.etymology: From Spanish baguala meaning 'wild horse', referencing Bagual Canyon in Chubut, Argentina, where the fossils were discovered.
Bagualia.description: Bagualia is an extinct genus of eusauropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic (middle Toarcian) Cañadón Asfalto Formation in what is now the Chubut Province of Argentina. The type species, B. alba, was formally described in 2020. Bagualia represents the oldest known definitive eusauropod, and due to the completeness of its material, it represents one of the most important taxa for understanding the early evolution of the group.

Bagualosaurus.etymology: From 'bagual', a term in the dialect of Rio Grande do Sul (Brazil) meaning 'strongly built fellow', referring to the strong hindlimbs of the animal, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name refers to the provenance from the town of Agudo.
Bagualosaurus.description: Bagualosaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Candelária Sequence (Uppermost Santa Maria Formation) of Brazil, dating to around 230 million years ago, in the Carnian of the Late Triassic. It includes one species, Bagualosaurus agudoensis.

Bahariasaurus.etymology: From Bahariya (the Bahariya Oasis and Formation in Egypt, where the fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Bahariya lizard'.
Bahariasaurus.description: Bahariasaurus is an enigmatic genus of large theropod dinosaur. The genus contains a single species, Bahariasaurus ingens, which was found in North African rock layers dating to the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous. The only fossils confidently assigned to Bahariasaurus were found in the Bahariya Formation of the Bahariya Oasis in Egypt by Ernst Stromer. This material was destroyed during a World War II bombing raid, with the same raid also destroying the holotypes of Spinosaurus, Aegyptosaurus, and other animals found in the Bahariya Formation.

Baiyinosaurus.etymology: From Baiyin (the city of Baiyin in Gansu Province, China, near where the fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Baiyin reptile'.
Baiyinosaurus.description: Baiyinosaurus is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaurs from the Middle Jurassic Wangjiashan Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, B. baojiensis, known from a partial skeleton including cranial bones. The skeletal anatomy of Baiyinosaurus demonstrates transitional features between basal thyreophorans and stegosaurs. While many stegosaurs are known from China, Baiyinosaurus is the only one currently named from Gansu Province.

Bajadasaurus.etymology: Named after La Bajada, the locality in Patagonia, Argentina where it was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Bajada lizard'.
Bajadasaurus.description: Bajadasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous epoch (late Berriasian to Valanginian stages, between 145 and 132.9 million years ago) of northern Patagonia, Argentina. It was first described in 2019 based on a single specimen found in 2010 that includes a largely complete skull and parts of the neck. The only species is Bajadasaurus pronuspinax. The genus is classified as a member of the Dicraeosauridae, a group of relatively small and short-necked sauropods.

Balaur.etymology: From Romanian balaur ('dragon' of Romanian folklore)
Balaur.description: Balaur is a genus of paravian theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of what is now Romania. It contains a single species, Balaur bondoc, known from two partial skeletons. Its short, stocky build and double sickle claws on each foot are interpreted as an example of island syndrome on the Late Cretaceous Hațeg Island archipelago.

Bambiraptor.etymology: Named after the Disney movie character Bambi (itself from Italian bambino meaning 'child') combined with Latin raptor meaning 'thief'. Full meaning: 'Bambi thief', referring to its small size.
Bambiraptor.description: Bambiraptor is a genus of bird-like dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (about 72 million years ago) of Montana. It was described by scientists at the University of Kansas, Yale University, and the University of New Orleans. The holotype fossil is less than 1 m (3.3 ft) long, although this specimen appears to be a juvenile, and it is possible that Bambiraptor is a juvenile Saurornitholestes. It is even suspected that the type specimen is a chimera, based on the fact that "there are elements of three different similarly sized lower legs included in the holotype." Because of its small size, it was named Bambiraptor feinbergi, after the popular Disney movie character (the name literally translates to "Bambi thief") and the surname of the wealthy family who bought and lent the specimen to the new Graves Museum of Natural History in Florida.

species.name: Bambiraptor feinbergi

Banji.etymology: From Chinese '斑嵴' (bān jǐ) meaning 'striped crest', referring to the prominent crest on its skull; the full species name Banji long means 'striped crest dragon' in Chinese.
Banji.description: Banji is an extinct genus of oviraptorid dinosaur that lived approximately 66 million years ago during the later part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now China. It was a small, lightly built, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore, that was an estimated 65 cm (2.1 ft) long, as a juvenile.

Bannykus.description: Bannykus is an extinct genus of alvarezsauroid from the Early Cretaceous Bayin-Gobi Formation of Inner Mongolia, China. It includes one species, Bannykus wulatensis.

Baotianmansaurus.etymology: Named for the Baotianman National Nature Reserve in Henan Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Baotianmansaurus.description: Baotianmansaurus is an extinct genus of somphospondylian sauropod. Its fossils were discovered in the Late Cretaceous Gaogou Formation of Henan Province, China. The type and only species is B. henanensis — named after the province in which it was found.

Barapasaurus.etymology: From 'bara' meaning 'big' and 'pa' meaning 'leg' in several Indian languages including Bengali, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'big-legged lizard', referring to a femur measuring over 1.7 m. The species name honors Bengali poet Rabindranath Tagore.
Barapasaurus.description: Barapasaurus is a genus of basal sauropod dinosaur from Jurassic rocks of India. The only species is B. tagorei. Barapasaurus comes from the lower part of the Kota Formation, which is of Early to Middle Jurassic in age. It is therefore one of the earliest known sauropods. Barapasaurus is known from approximately 300 bones from at least six individuals, so that the skeleton is almost completely known except for the anterior cervical vertebrae and the skull. This makes Barapasaurus one of the most completely known sauropods from the Early Jurassic.

Barilium.description: Barilium is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur which was first described as a species of Iguanodon (I. dawsoni) by Richard Lydekker in 1888, the specific epithet honouring the discoverer Charles Dawson, who collected the holotype during the 1880s.

Barosaurus.etymology: From Greek barys (βαρυς) meaning 'heavy' and Greek sauros (σαυρος) meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'heavy lizard'.
Barosaurus.description: Barosaurus is an extinct genus of giant, long-tailed, long-necked, plant-eating sauropod dinosaur closely related to the more familiar Diplodocus. Definitive remains have been found in the Morrison Formation from the Upper Jurassic Period of South Dakota, Utah and Montana, with other possible remains also found in Colorado, eastern Wyoming and Oklahoma. The generic name, Barosaurus, comes from the Greek words barys (βαρυς) meaning "heavy" and sauros (σαυρος) meaning "lizard", and thus meaning "heavy lizard".

Barrosasaurus.etymology: Named for the Sierra Barrosa in Neuquén Province, Argentina, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name honors Argentine paleontologist Rodolfo Casamiquela.
Barrosasaurus.description: Barrosasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur, first described by paleontologists Leonardo Salgado and Rodolfo Coria in 2009. The fossils, consisting of three fossil dorsal (back) vertebrae, are well-preserved but incomplete. They were discovered in the Anacleto Formation of the Neuquén province of western Argentina. The type species is Barrosasaurus casamiquelai. The genus name is named after the Sierra Barrosa in Neuquén. The specific epithet honours the Argentinian paleontologist Rodolfo Magín Casamiquela. It has been estimated to be 18 meters (60 ft) in length and 13.5 tonnes (14.9 short tons) in weight.

Barsboldia.etymology: Named after Rinchen Barsbold, a well-known Mongolian paleontologist, with the Latin suffix -ia; overall meaning 'of Barsbold'.
Barsboldia.description: Barsboldia is a genus of large hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Maastrichtian Nemegt Formation of Ömnogöv, Mongolia. It is known from a partial vertebral column, partial pelvis, and some ribs.

Baryonyx.etymology: From Greek 'barys' meaning 'heavy' and 'onyx' meaning 'claw', referring to the large, heavy thumb claw that is characteristic of this dinosaur.
Baryonyx.description: Baryonyx is a genus of theropod dinosaur which lived in the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous period, about 130–125 million years ago. The first skeleton was discovered in 1983 in the Smokejack Clay Pit, of Surrey, England, in sediments of the Weald Clay Formation, and became the holotype specimen of Baryonyx walkeri, named by palaeontologists Alan J. Charig and Angela C. Milner in 1986. The genus name Baryonyx comes from Ancient Greek βαρύς (barús), meaning "heavy" or "strong", and ὄνυξ (ónux), meaning "claw", alluding to the animal's very large claw on the first finger; the specific name, walkeri, refers to its discoverer, amateur fossil collector William J. Walker. The holotype specimen is one of the most complete theropod skeletons from the UK (and remains the most complete spinosaurid), and its discovery attracted media attention. Specimens later discovered in other parts of the United Kingdom and Iberia have also been assigned to the genus, though many have since been moved to new genera.

Bashanosaurus.description: Bashanosaurus is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian age) Shaximiao Formation of Yunyang County, China. The genus contains a single species, Bashanosaurus primitivus, known from incomplete skeletons belonging to three individuals. It is one of the basalmost stegosaurs, as well as one of the oldest known stegosaurs, along with Adratiklit, Isaberrysaura, and Thyreosaurus.

Batyrosaurus.description: Batyrosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous basal hadrosauroid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Bostobe Formation (Santonian to Campanian stage) of central Kazakhstan. Baurutitan.description: Baurutitan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Brazil. The type species, Baurutitan britoi, was described in 2005 by Kellner and colleagues, although the fossil remains had already been discovered in 1957. Baurutitan is classified as a lithostrotian titanosaur, and is distinguished from related genera based on its distinctive caudal vertebrae. This South American dinosaur was found in the Serra da Galga Formation near Uberaba, in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais.

Bayannurosaurus.etymology: Named for the Bayin-Gobi (Bayannur) region of China where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Bayannurosaurus.description: Bayannurosaurus is a non-hadrosauriform ankylopollexian ornithopod described in 2018 by Xu Xing. It lived during the early Aptian period, being found in the Bayin-Gobi Formation of China. The genus includes the type species Bayannurosaurus perfectus. A phylogenetic analysis of Bayannurosaurus indicates that it is more derived than Hypselospinus, yet less derived than Ouranosaurus and just outside of the Hadrosauriformes. It was a large iguanodontian, measuring up to 9 metres (30 ft) in total body length. The genus name Bayannurosaurus comes from Bayannur, the area where it was found, while the species name perfectus comes from the "perfect" preservation of the holotype specimen (IMMNH PV00001).

Beibeilong.description: Beibeilong is a genus of large caenagnathid dinosaurs that lived in China during the Late Cretaceous epoch, about 96 million to 88 million years ago. The genus contains a single species, Beibeilong sinensis. The species was named and described in 2017 through analysis of an embryonic skeleton (nicknamed Baby Louie) and partial nest with large eggs that were discovered in the Gaogou Formation of China (Henan Province) between 1992 and 1993.

species.etymology: Named for its country of discovery, China, derived from the prefix Sino meaning 'Chinese'.

Beipiaognathus.etymology: Named after Beipiao, a city in Liaoning Province, China, combined with Greek gnathos meaning 'jaw'. Full meaning: 'Beipiao jaw'.
Beipiaognathus.description: Beipiaognathus is a dubious genus of coelurosaurian theropod from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China. The type species is Beipiaognathus jii and it was named and described by Hu et al. in 2016.

species.name: Beipiaognathus jii
species.etymology: Named in honor of Prof. Ji Qiang for his contributions to the study of compsognathids.

Beipiaosaurus.etymology: Named for Beipiao City in Liaoning Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Beipiaosaurus.description: Beipiaosaurus is a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous in the Yixian Formation. The first remains were found in 1996 and formally described in 1999. Before the discovery of Yutyrannus, Beipiaosaurus were among the heaviest dinosaurs known from direct evidence to be feathered. Beipiaosaurus is known from three reported specimens. Numerous impressions of feather structures were preserved that allowed researchers to determine the feathering color which turned out to be brownish.

species.name: Beipiaosaurus inexpectus
species.etymology: From Latin 'inexpectus' meaning 'unexpected', referring to the surprising features found in this animal.

references.title: A therizinosauroid dinosaur with integumentary structures from China

Beishanlong.etymology: From Chinese Bei Shan meaning 'North Mountains' combined with Chinese long (龙) meaning 'dragon'. Full meaning: 'North Mountains dragon'.
Beishanlong.description: Beishanlong is a genus of giant ornithomimosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China. It is the second-largest ornithomimosaur discovered, only surpassed by the related Deinocheirus.

species.name: Beishanlong grandis
species.etymology: From Latin 'grandis' meaning 'large', in reference to the body size of this giant ornithomimosaur.

holotype.institution: The Fossil Research and Development Center of the Third Geology and Mineral Resources Exploration Academy of Gansu Provincial Bureau of Geo-exploration and Mineral Development

Bellusaurus.etymology: From Vulgar Latin bellus meaning 'beautiful' + Ancient Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'beautiful lizard'.
Bellusaurus.description: Bellusaurus was a sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) known from juvenile specimens that would have measured about 4.8 metres (16 ft) long. Its fossils were found in Shishugou Formation rocks in the northeastern Junggar Basin in China.

species.name: Bellusaurus sui
species.etymology: Named for Senior Preparator Youling Sui, a notable restorer of dinosaur remains for whom Bellusaurus was the last restoration undertaken.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

Berberosaurus.etymology: From Berber (referring to the Berber people of Morocco, near where the fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Berber lizard'.
Berberosaurus.description: Berberosaurus is a genus of neotheropod dinosaur, possibly a ceratosaur, from the Toarcian-age (Lower Jurassic) "Toundoute Continental Series" (Azilal Formation) found in the Central High Atlas of Toundoute, Ouarzazate, Morocco. The type species of the genus Berberosaurus is B. liassicus, in reference to the Lias epoch. Berberosaurus might be the oldest known ceratosaur, and is based on partial postcranial remains. This genus represents the oldest formally identified theropod from the North of Africa, as well one of the few from the region in the Early Jurassic.

species.name: Berberosaurus liassicus
species.etymology: Named for the Lias epoch, the geological period from which the fossil was recovered.

holotype.material: Partial skeleton cataloged as MHNM-Pt9, Pt16, Pt19, Pt20, Pt21, Pt22, and Pt23
