Berthasaura.etymology: Named after Bertha Lutz, a prominent Brazilian scientist and feminist, combined with Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Bertha's lizard'.
Berthasaura.description: Berthasaura is an extinct genus of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous Goio-Erê Formation of Paraná, Brazil. The genus contains a single species, Berthasaura leopoldinae, known from a nearly complete skeleton.

species.name: Berthasaura leopoldinae
species.etymology: Named for Maria Leopoldina, the first Empress of Brazil, with the naming timed near the bicentennial of Brazil's independence in 2022.

Betasuchus.etymology: From Greek 'beta' (the second letter) and 'suchos' meaning 'crocodile'; von Huene coined the name when renaming 'Megalosaurus bredai' in 1932, giving 'B crocodile'.
Betasuchus.description: Betasuchus is a genus of probable abelisaurid theropod dinosaur which lived during the Late Cretaceous Period. Betasuchus is, besides Orthomerus and birds such as Enantiornithines, the only dinosaur genus named from remains found in the Netherlands and the only non-avian theropod found in the Maastrichtian Beds.

species.name: Betasuchus bredai
species.etymology: Named for the late Dutch biologist and geologist Jacob Gijsbertus Samuël van Breda, a director of the Teylers Museum who collected the fossil sometime between 1820 and 1860.

Bicentenaria.etymology: From Latin bicentenaria meaning 'two hundred year anniversary', named after the 200th anniversary of the 1810 May Revolution in Argentina.
Bicentenaria.description: Bicentenaria is an extinct genus of carnivorous coelurosaurian theropods which lived during the early Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) Candeleros Formation of Argentina. It contains the type species, B. argentina.

species.name: Bicentenaria argentina
species.etymology: Named for Argentina, the country where the fossils were discovered.

Bissektipelta.etymology: From Bissekty (the Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan, where the fossils were found) + Greek pelte (πέλτη) meaning 'shield'; overall meaning 'Bissekty shield'.
Bissektipelta.description: Bissektipelta is a genus of ankylosaurine thyreophoran dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan. Bissektipelta is a monospecific genus, containing only the type species B. archibaldi.

species.name: Bissektipelta archibaldi
species.etymology: Named for James David Archibald, who led the URBAC (Uzbekistan, Russia, Britain, America, and Canada) project that performed the excavation of the holotype.

Bistahieversor.etymology: From Bistahi (the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness area in New Mexico, where fossils were found; from Navajo bistahi meaning 'among the adobe formations') + Latin eversor meaning 'destroyer'; overall meaning 'Bistahi destroyer'.
Bistahieversor.description: Bistahieversor, also known as the "Bisti Beast", is a genus of basal eutyrannosaurian theropod dinosaur. The genus contains only a single known species, B. sealeyi, described in 2010, from the Late Cretaceous of New Mexico. The holotype and a juvenile were found in the Hunter Wash Member of the Kirtland Formation, while other specimens came from the underlying Fossil Forest member of the Fruitland Formation. This dates Bistahieversor approximately 75.5 to 74.5 million years ago during the Campanian age, found in sediments spanning a million years.

species.name: Bistahieversor sealeyi
species.etymology: Named for Paul Sealey, Research Associate at the New Mexico Museum of Natural History, in recognition of his discovery of the holotype specimen.

holotype.institution: New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science

references.authors: Carr, Thomas D.; Williamson, Thomas E.

Bisticeratops.etymology: From Bisti (the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness area in New Mexico, where fossils were found; from Navajo bistahi meaning 'among the adobe formations') + Greek keras (κέρας) meaning 'horn' + ops (ὤψ) meaning 'face'; overall meaning 'Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness horned face'.
Bisticeratops.description: Bisticeratops is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian from outcrops of the Campanian age Kirtland Formation found in the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness in northwestern New Mexico, United States. The type and only species is B. froeseorum, known from a nearly complete skull.

species.name: Bisticeratops froeseorum
species.etymology: Named for Edgar Froese, founder of the band Tangerine Dream, and his son Jerome, former member of Tangerine Dream and founder of the band Loom, whose music inspired the describers.

holotype.institution: New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science

references.authors: Dalman, S. G.; Jasinski, S. E.; S. G. Lucas
references.title: A new chasmosaurine ceratopsid from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) Farmington Member of the Kirtland Formation, New Mexico
references.journal: New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science Bulletin

Blasisaurus.etymology: Named after the Blasi 1 fossil site in Spain where the specimen was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Blasi lizard'.
Blasisaurus.description: Blasisaurus is a genus of lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous. It is known from a partial skull and skeleton found in late Maastrichtian-age rocks of Spain. The type species is Blasisaurus canudoi, described in 2010 by Penélope Cruzado-Caballero, Xabier Pereda-Suberbiola and José Ignacio Ruiz-Omeñaca, a group of researchers from Spain.

species.name: Blasisaurus canudoi
species.etymology: Named for paleontologist José Ignacio Canudo.

Blikanasaurus.etymology: Named for the Blikana locality in South Africa where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'lizard from Blikana'.
Blikanasaurus.description: Blikanasaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the late Triassic of South Africa. The generic name Blikanasaurus is derived from Greek, meaning "lizard from Blikana". The species name cromptoni is taken from the surname of A.W. "Fuzz" Crompton, an American paleontologist who led numerous field expeditions in Elliot Formation outcrop localities in South Africa. Blikanasaurus is only known from partial hindlimb bones that were recovered from the lower Elliot Formation (LEF) in the Eastern Cape.

species.name: Blikanasaurus cromptoni
species.etymology: Taken from the surname of A.W. 'Fuzz' Crompton, an American paleontologist who led numerous field expeditions in Elliot Formation outcrop localities in South Africa.

Bolong.etymology: From the names of the brothers Bo Hai-chen and Bo Xue (who helped uncover the specimen) + Mandarin lóng (龍) meaning 'dragon'; overall meaning 'Bo's dragon'.
Bolong.description: Bolong is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of western Liaoning Province, China. It lived about 125 million years ago in the earliest Aptian.

species.name: Bolong yixianensis
species.etymology: Named for the Yixian Formation where the holotype was found.

references.authors: Wu, W.-h.; Godefroit, P.; D.-y. Hu
references.title: [Bolong yixianensis gen. et sp. nov.: a new iguanodontoid dinosaur from the Yixian Formation of western Liaoning, China]

Bonapartenykus.etymology: Named after José F. Bonaparte, the prominent Argentine paleontologist, combined with Greek onyx/onykhos (ὄνυξ/ὄνυχος) meaning 'claw'; overall meaning 'José F. Bonaparte's claw'.
Bonapartenykus.description: Bonapartenykus is an extinct genus of alvarezsauroid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian–Maastrichtian) of what is now the Allen Formation of the Río Negro Province, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Bonapartenykus ultimus, known from a partially articulated, incomplete skeleton that was found in close association to two incomplete eggs and several clusters of eggshells belonging to the oogenus Arriagadoolithus. Bonapartenykus was named in 2012. It has an estimated length of 2.5–3.3 m (8.2–10.8 ft) and weight of 43–72 kg (95–159 lb), making it the largest member of the clade Alvarezsauroidea. Additional skeletons referrable to this genus have subsequently been described.

species.name: Bonapartenykus ultimus
species.etymology: From Latin word meaning 'latest', as it is one of the geologically youngest alvarezsaurids from South America.

Bonapartesaurus.etymology: Named after José Bonaparte, the prominent Argentine paleontologist, combined with Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Bonaparte's lizard'.
Bonapartesaurus.description: Bonapartesaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur belonging to Hadrosauridae, which lived in the area of modern Argentina during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.

species.name: Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis
species.etymology: Named for Río Negro province of Argentina, where the holotype specimen was excavated.

references.authors: Cruzado-Caballero, Penélope; Powell, Jaime
references.title: Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis, a new hadrosaurine dinosaur from South America: implications for phylogenetic and biogeographic relations with North America

Bonatitan.etymology: Named in honor of Argentine paleontologist José Bonaparte, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'. The species name honors Osvaldo Reig.
Bonatitan.description: Bonatitan is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Allen Formation of Argentina. It was named in 2004.

species.name: Bonatitan reigi
species.etymology: Named for the Argentine paleontologist Osvaldo Reig.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales ‘Bernardino Rivadavia’

Bonitasaura.etymology: Named after the La Bonita fossil quarry in Argentina where remains were found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'La Bonita lizard'.
Bonitasaura.description: Bonitasaura is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur hailing from uppermost layers of the Late Cretaceous (Santonian) Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Neuquén Group of the eastern Neuquén Basin, located in Río Negro Province, Northwestern Patagonia, Argentina. The remains, consisting of a partial sub-adult skeleton jumbled in a small area of fluvial sandstone, including a lower jaw with teeth, a partial vertebrae series, and limb bones, were described by Sebastian Apesteguía in 2004.

species.name: Bonitasaura salgadoi
species.etymology: Named in homage to Leonardo Salgado, a renowned Argentine paleontologist.

references.authors: Apesteguía, S.
references.title: Bonitasaura salgadoi gen. et sp. nov.: a beaked sauropod from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia

Borealopelta.etymology: From Greek boreas meaning 'northern/north wind' and Greek pelta meaning 'shield'. Full meaning: 'northern shield', referring to its armored body and Canadian (northern) origin.
Borealopelta.description: Borealopelta is an extinct genus of herbivorous nodosaurid ankylosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of what is today Alberta, Canada. It contains a single species, B. markmitchelli, named in 2017 by Caleb Brown and colleagues from a well-preserved specimen known as the Suncor nodosaur. Discovered at an oil sands mine north of Fort McMurray, Alberta, the specimen is remarkable for being among the best-preserved dinosaur fossils of its size ever found. It preserved not only the armor (osteoderms) in their life positions, but also remains of their keratin sheaths, overlying skin, and stomach contents from the animal's last meal. Melanosomes were also found that indicate the animal had a reddish pinkish skin tone.

species.name: Borealopelta markmitchelli
species.etymology: Named for technician Mark Mitchell, who spent six years preparing the holotype fossil for study at the Royal Tyrrell Museum.

Borealosaurus.etymology: From Greek Boreas meaning 'north wind' and Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'northern lizard', referring to its northern China origin.
Borealosaurus.description: Borealosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of northern China. The type species is Borealosaurus wimani, which was named in 2004.

species.name: Borealosaurus wimani
species.etymology: Named for Swedish paleontologist Carl Wiman, who named the first Chinese dinosaur.

Boreonykus.etymology: From Greek 'boreos' meaning 'northern' and 'nykus' or 'onyx' meaning 'claw', referring to its discovery in northern Canada.
Boreonykus.description: Boreonykus is an extinct genus of dromaeosaurid dinosaur, that lived during the Late Cretaceous in the area of present Canada.

Borogovia.etymology: Named after the 'borogoves', the fantasy creatures in Lewis Carroll's poem 'Jabberwocky' from 'Through the Looking-Glass'.
Borogovia.description: Borogovia is a troodontid theropod dinosaur genus which lived during the Late Cretaceous Period, in what is now Mongolia. It contains one species, Borogovia gracilicrus.

species.name: Borogovia gracilicrus
species.etymology: From Latin, combining 'gracilis' meaning 'lightly built' and 'crus' meaning 'shin', in reference to the elegant build of the lower leg.

Brachiosaurus.etymology: From Greek brachion (βραχίων) meaning 'arm' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'arm lizard', referring to its proportionately long forelimbs.
Brachiosaurus.description: A genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of North America. Brachiosaurus is unusual among sauropods for its proportionally long forelimbs, giving it a giraffe-like posture with the body sloping upward toward the head. It was one of the tallest and largest dinosaurs known from relatively complete remains.

features: Long forelimbs giving a distinctive upward-sloping body profile
Tall, arched nasal crest on the skull
Extremely long neck held at a steep angle

Elongate metacarpals
Arched nasal bones forming a crest above the skull

Brachyceratops.etymology: From Greek brachys (βραχύς) meaning 'short', Greek keras (κέρας) meaning 'horn', and Greek ops (ὤψ) meaning 'face'. Full meaning: 'short horned face'.
Brachyceratops.description: Brachyceratops is a dubious genus of ceratopsian dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of Montana, United States. Brachyceratops has historically been known from juvenile remains, with one specimen having since been re-classified as Rubeosaurus ovatus.

Brachylophosaurus.etymology: From Greek brachys meaning 'short', Greek lophos meaning 'crest', and Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'short-crested lizard', referring to its reduced flat crest.
Brachylophosaurus.description: Brachylophosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of western North America. It was first named in 1953 by Charles Mortram Sternberg for a skull and skeleton he discovered in 1936 in the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada, for which he named the new taxon Brachylophosaurus canadensis. While this single specimen was the only known material of Brachylophosaurus for a long time, extensive discoveries in the Judith River Formation of Montana, USA have uncovered not only additional skulls and skeletons with extensive impressions of skin, but also a bonebed of 800 specimens. The earliest of these discoveries in Montana was named Brachylophosaurus goodwini by John R. Horner, but it is now believed that there was only a single species of Brachylophosaurus, with B. goodwini as either a junior synonym of B. canadensis or an indeterminate member of Brachylophosaurini.

species.name: Brachylophosaurus canadensis
species.etymology: Named for Canada, where the holotype specimen was discovered in the Oldman Formation of Alberta.

Brachytrachelopan.etymology: From Greek 'brachys' meaning 'short', 'trachelos' meaning 'neck', and 'pan' referencing the god Pan, a homage to the short-necked sauropod and the pastoral deity.
Brachytrachelopan.description: Brachytrachelopan is a genus of short-necked sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian to Tithonian) of Argentina. The holotype and only known specimen (Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio MPEF-PV 1716) was collected from an erosional exposure of fluvial sandstone within the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation on a hill approximately 25 kilometres (16 mi) north-northeast of Cerro Cóndor, Chubut Province, in west-central Argentina, South America. Though very incomplete, the skeletal elements recovered were found in articulation and include eight cervical, twelve dorsal, and three sacral vertebrae, as well as proximal portions of the posterior cervical ribs and all the dorsal ribs, the distal end of the left femur, the proximal end of the left tibia, and the right ilium. Much of the specimen was probably lost to erosion many years before its discovery. The type species is Brachytrachelopan mesai. The specific name honours Daniel Mesa, a local shepherd who discovered the specimen while searching for lost sheep. The genus name translates as "short-necked Pan", Pan being the god of the shepherds.

species.name: Brachytrachelopan mesai
species.etymology: Named for Daniel Mesa, a local shepherd who discovered the specimen while searching for lost sheep.

Bradycneme.etymology: From Ancient Greek bradys (βραδύς) meaning 'slow, ponderous' + kneme (κνήμη) meaning 'leg'; overall meaning 'ponderous leg', referring to the robust leg bone on which the genus is based.
Bradycneme.description: Bradycneme is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous-aged (Maastrichtian) Sânpetru Formation of the Hațeg Basin, Transylvania, Romania. The type species is Bradycneme draculae, known only from a partial right lower leg (specimen BMNH A1588), which its original describers believed it came from a giant owl.

Brontomerus.etymology: From Greek bronte meaning 'thunder' and Greek meros meaning 'thigh'. Full meaning: 'thunder thigh', referring to its enormously muscled thighs.
Brontomerus.description: Brontomerus is a genus of camarasauromorph sauropod which lived during the early Cretaceous (Aptian or Albian age, approximately 110 million years ago). It was named in 2011 and the type species is Brontomerus mcintoshi. It is probably a fairly basal camarasauromorph, though the taxon is difficult to resolve due to incompleteness of the material. It is most remarkable for its unusual hipbones, which would have supported the largest thigh muscles, proportionally, of any known sauropod. The specific name is in honor of physicist and North American sauropod expert John Stanton McIntosh.

Brontosaurus.etymology: From Greek bronte (βροντή) meaning 'thunder' and Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'thunder lizard'.
Brontosaurus.description: Brontosaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day United States during the Late Jurassic period. It was described by American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879, the type species being dubbed B. excelsus, based on a partial skeleton lacking a skull found in Como Bluff, Wyoming. In subsequent years, two more species of Brontosaurus were named: B. parvus in 1902 and B. yahnahpin in 1994. Brontosaurus lived about 156 to 146 million years ago (mya) during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian ages in the Morrison Formation of what is now Utah and Wyoming. For decades, the animal was thought to have been a taxonomic synonym of its close relative Apatosaurus, but a 2015 study by Emmanuel Tschopp and colleagues found it to be distinct. It has seen widespread representation in popular culture, being the archetypal "long-necked" dinosaur in general media.

Bruhathkayosaurus.etymology: From Sanskrit bruhath (बृहत्) meaning 'huge, great' + kaya (काय) meaning 'body' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'huge-bodied lizard'.
Bruhathkayosaurus.description: Bruhathkayosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur found in the Kallamedu Formation of India. The fragmentary remains were originally described as a theropod, but it was later determined to be a titanosaur sauropod. Length estimates by researchers exceed those of the titanosaur Argentinosaurus, as longer than 35 metres (115 ft) and weighing over 80 tonnes. A 2023 estimate placed Bruhathkayosaurus as potentially weighing 110–170 tonnes (110–170 long tons; 120–190 short tons), with paleontologist Michael Benton, estimating a length of 45 metres (148 ft). If the upper estimates of the 2023 records are accurate, Bruhathkayosaurus may have rivaled the blue whale as one of the largest animals to ever exist. However, all of the estimates are based on the dimensions of the fossils described in 1987, but these fossils have since disintegrated and no longer exist, making it impossible to affirm these estimates.

Calamosaurus.etymology: From Greek kalamos (κάλαμος) meaning 'reed' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'reed lizard', likely referring to the slender, hollow vertebrae.
Calamosaurus.description: Calamosaurus is a genus of small theropod dinosaur, from the Early Cretaceous of the Isle of Wight, England. It is based on two cervical vertebrae (NHMUK PV R 901), collected by Reverend William Fox. These fossils come from sedimentary rocks of the Wessex Formation and are Barremian in age. The type species of Calamosaurus, named Calamospondylus foxi by Richard Lydekker, was named in honour of Fox. Calamospondylus, however, was a preoccupied name, forcing Lydekker to change the genus name to Calamosaurus. This has subsequently led to immense confusion, with some authors believing the two genera to be synonymous. The systematic position of Calamosaurus within theropods has been controversial, and placements within Compsognathidae and Ornithomimosauria have been suggested. More recently, researchers have suggested affinities with the Tyrannosauroidea and Alvarezsauroidea.

Camarasaurus.etymology: From Greek kamara (καμάρα) meaning 'vaulted chamber' or 'anything with an arched cover' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'chambered lizard', referring to the hollow pleurocoels in its cervical vertebrae.
Camarasaurus.description: Camarasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic in what is now the United States. Its fossils are primarily known from the Morrison Formation dating to the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian ages of the Jurassic, between 155 and 145 million years ago (mya). It was named by Edward Drinker Cope in 1877; it definitively contains three species, C. supremus, the type species, C. grandis, and C. lentus, while some researchers consider C. lewisi to be in its own genus, Cathetosaurus. The generic name means "chambered lizard", referring to the hollow chambers, known as pleurocoels, in its cervical vertebrae (Greek καμαρα [kamara] meaning 'vaulted chamber', or anything with an arched cover, and σαυρος [sauros] meaning 'lizard'). Hundreds of specimens have been excavated to date, including some nearly complete skeletons. It is among the best understood dinosaurs, with detailed studies of its anatomy, paleobiology, paleoecology, and more.

Described in 2014, it was originally identified as a ceratosaurian theropod, but later studies suggested affinities to the Spinosauridae. Camarillasaurus is one of several spinosaurid taxa known from the Iberian peninsula, the others being Iberospinus, Protathlitis, Baryonyx, Riojavenatrix, and Vallibonavenatrix.

Camelotia.etymology: Named after Camelot, the legendary castle and court of King Arthur, referring to the discovery location in southwest England (near the supposed location of Camelot); overall meaning 'from Camelot'.

It is best known from a partial postcranial skeleton found in the Westbury Formation and named by Peter M. Galton in 1985. Subsequent work has generally placed Camelotia as a relatively derived sauropodomorph close to the origin of Sauropoda, although its exact position among early non-sauropod sauropodomorphs remains debated. It is sometimes placed in Melanorosauridae as a close relative of Melanorosaurus. With a body length and mass estimated at 8–10 metres (26–33 ft) and 3.8 tonnes (8,400 lb), respectively, it is one of the largest sauropodomorphs known from the Triassic.

Camptosaurus.etymology: From Greek kamptos (καμπτος) meaning 'bent/flexible' and Greek sauros (σαυρος) meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'flexible lizard'.
Camptosaurus.description: Camptosaurus is an extinct genus of plant-eating, beaked ornithischian dinosaurs of the Late Jurassic period of western North America and possibly also Europe. The name means 'flexible lizard' (Greek καμπτος (kamptos) meaning 'bent' and σαυρος (sauros) meaning 'lizard').

synonyms.name: Camptonotus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Camptonotus (Orthoptera).

synonyms.name: Symphyrophus
synonyms.reason: Material is now generally considered indistinguishable from Camptosaurus.

synonyms.name: Brachyrophus
synonyms.reason: Material is now widely recognized as indistinguishable from Camptosaurus.

synonyms.name: Uteodon
synonyms.reason: Possible junior subjective synonym of Camptosaurus; identification is tentative. Per Olshevsky's Dinosaur Genera List.

species.name: Camptosaurus dispar
species.etymology: From Latin 'dispar' meaning 'unlike' or 'unequal'; the reason for the choice is unclear.

holotype.institution: Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History

Campylodoniscus.etymology: Diminutive form of Campylodon; from Greek kampylos (καμπυλος) meaning 'bent/curved' and Greek odon (ὀδών) meaning 'tooth'. Full meaning: 'little bent tooth'.
Campylodoniscus.description: Campylodoniscus is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now Argentina.

synonyms.name: Campylodon
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Campylodon (Pisces).

species.etymology: Named for Florentino Ameghino, the renowned Argentine naturalist and palaeontologist.

Canardia.etymology: From French 'canard' meaning 'duck', referring to the duck-billed (hadrosaur) nature of this dinosaur found in France.
Canardia.description: Canardia is an extinct genus of lambeosaurine dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Marnes d'Auzas Formation (late Maastrichtian stage) of Haute-Garonne department, in Occitanie region, southwestern France. The type species Canardia garonnensis was first described and named by Albert Prieto-Márquez, Fabio M. Dalla Vecchia, Rodrigo Gaete and Àngel Galobart in 2013. It is only known from juvenile specimens.

species.name: Canardia garonnensis
species.etymology: Named for the Haute-Garonne department of southwestern France, where the holotype was discovered.

Carcharodontosaurus.etymology: From Greek Carcharodon (the great white shark genus, itself from Greek karcharos meaning 'jagged/sharp' and odous meaning 'tooth') and Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'shark-toothed lizard'.
Carcharodontosaurus.description: Carcharodontosaurus is a genus of large theropod dinosaur that lived in Northwest Africa from about 100 to 94 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage of the Cretaceous. The taxon was first described in 1925 by French paleontologists Charles Depéret and Justin Savornin as Megalosaurus saharicus, based on two fossil teeth discovered in Algeria, which are now lost. A partial skeleton was discovered in Egypt as early as 1914 by crews of German paleontologist Ernst Stromer, although he did not report the find until 1931. Based on this specimen, together with the teeth previously described by Depéret and Savornin, Stromer established the genus Carcharodontosaurus and its type species (species a genus in named for) C. saharicus. Although the Egyptian skeleton was destroyed during World War II, it was subsequently redescribed as the holotype (name-bearing) specimen of a distinct carcharodontosaurid genus, Tameryraptor. In 1995, a large incomplete skull attributed to C. saharicus was discovered in the Kem Kem Beds of Morocco, which was officially proposed as the neotype (replacement holotype) in 2007. In the same year, fossils unearthed from the Farak Formation of Niger were described and named as another species, C. iguidensis, though this taxon might belong to a different genus.

species.name: Carcharodontosaurus saharicus
species.etymology: Means 'of the Sahara', referring to the Sahara Desert region of North Africa where the type specimen was found.

holotype.institution: Service Géologique du Maroc, Ministére de l’Energie et des Mines
holotype.material: Partial skull; proposed as neotype by Brusatte and Sereno (2007) but formal ICZN ruling is pending

Cariocecus.etymology: Named for Cariocecus (also spelled Cariociecus), the Iberian god of war who became syncretised with Mars and Ares.
Cariocecus.description: Cariocecus bocagei is an extinct species of hadrosauroid ornithopod dinosaurs known from the Early Cretaceous of what is now Portugal. C. bocagei is the only species in the genus Cariocecus. It is known from a partial skull that was discovered in 2016 and subsequently given a scientific name and description in 2025. This specimen represents the first iguanodontian skull to be found in the country.

species.name: Cariocecus bocagei
species.etymology: Named in honor of the Portuguese naturalist Jose Vicente Barbosa du Bocage, in recognition of his academic work and impact.

references.authors: Bertozzo, F.; Camilo, B.; R. Araújo, F. Manucci, J. C. Kullberg, D. G. Cerio, V. F. d. Carvalho, P. Marrecas, S. D. Figueiredo, P. Godefroit

Carnotaurus.etymology: From Latin caro/carnis meaning 'flesh/meat' and Latin taurus meaning 'bull'. Full meaning: 'meat-eating bull' or 'flesh bull', referring to its bull-like horns and carnivorous diet.
Carnotaurus.description: Carnotaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous period, between 69 and 66 million years ago. The only species is Carnotaurus sastrei. Known from a single well-preserved skeleton, it is one of the best-understood theropods from the Southern Hemisphere. The skeleton, found in 1984, was uncovered in the Chubut Province of Argentina from rocks of the La Colonia Formation. Carnotaurus is a derived member of the Abelisauridae, a group of large theropods that occupied the large predatorial niche in the southern landmasses of Gondwana during the late Cretaceous. Within the Abelisauridae, the genus is often considered a member of the Brachyrostra, a clade of short-snouted forms restricted to South America.

species.name: Carnotaurus sastrei
species.etymology: Named for Angel Sastre, the owner of the ranch where the only known skeleton was found.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales ‘Bernardino Rivadavia’

Caseosaurus.etymology: Named after Ermine Cowles Case, the scientist who discovered it, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Case's lizard'.
Caseosaurus.description: Caseosaurus is a genus of saurischian dinosaur that lived approximately 221.5 to 212 million years ago during the latter part of the Triassic Period in what is now Texas, North America. It was a small, lightly-built, bipedal, ground-dwelling carnivore, and could grow up to 2 m (6.6 ft) long.

species.name: Caseosaurus crosbyensis
species.etymology: A Latinized rendering of Crosby County in Texas, the site of the holotype's discovery.

Cathartesaura.etymology: From Cathartes (the New World vulture genus) + Greek saura ('lizard', feminine). The name also alludes to the turkey vulture Cathartes aura, whose Spanish name 'buitre' named the 'La Buitrera' locality where the fossils were found.
Cathartesaura.description: Cathartesaura is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur from Late Cretaceous strata of the Huincul Formation, at the "La Buitrera" locality, in the Neuquén Basin of Río Negro Province, Argentina. The fossil remains, described by Gallina and Apesteguía in 2005, consist of a partial skeleton including vertebrae and limb bones. These were found at the base of the formation, which dates back to the Cenomanian and Turonian epochs, in mudstone and sandstone levels.

species.name: Cathartesaura anaerobica
species.etymology: Named for the Argentinian adhesive company Anaeróbicos, which provided field and laboratory support during the extraction and preparation of the fossils.

Caudipteryx.etymology: From Latin cauda ('tail') + Greek pteryx ('feather' or 'wing'), meaning 'tail feather'.
Caudipteryx.description: Caudipteryx is a genus of small oviraptorosaurian dinosaurs that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous, around 124.6 million years ago. They were feathered and extremely bird-like in their overall appearance, to the point that some paleontologists suggested it was a bird. Two species have been described: C. zoui (the type species), in 1998, and C. dongi, in 2000. Caudipteryx had a stout trunk, long legs, and was probably a swift runner. Its discovery has led to many intensive studies and debate over the relationship between birds and dinosaurs.

species.name: Caudipteryx zoui
species.etymology: Named for Zou Jiahua for his prominent support to the scientific community as the vice premier of China.

Cedarosaurus.etymology: From Cedar (referring to the Cedar Mountain Formation where it was discovered) + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Cedar lizard'.
Cedarosaurus.description: Cedarosaurus is a genus of nasal-crested macronarian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Period (Valanginian). The fossils were discovered in 1996 in eastern Utah within the rocks of the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation. It was officially named and described by Tidwell, Carpenter and Brooks in 1999. It shows similarities to the brachiosaurid Eucamerotus from the Wessex Formation of southern England, as well as to Brachiosaurus from the Morrison Formation.

species.name: Cedarosaurus weiskopfae
species.etymology: Named for the late Carol Weiskopf, in recognition of her hard work in the field and laboratory.

Cedarpelta.etymology: Named for the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'pelta' meaning 'shield', referring to its ankylosaurid armor.
Cedarpelta.description: Cedarpelta is an extinct genus of basal ankylosaurid dinosaur from Utah that lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation. The type and only species, Cedarpelta bilbeyhallorum, is known from multiple specimens including partial skulls and postcranial material. It was named in 2001 by Kenneth Carpenter, James Kirkland, Don Burge, and John Bird. Cedarpelta has an estimated length of 7 metres (23 feet) and weight of 5 tonnes (11,023 lbs). The skull of Cedarpelta lacks extensive cranial ornamentation and is one of the only known ankylosaurs with individual skull bones that are not completely fused together.

species.name: Cedarpelta bilbeyhallorum
species.etymology: Named for Sue Ann Bilbey and Evan Hall, who discovered the remains of Cedarpelta.

holotype.institution: College of Eastern Utah Prehistoric Museum

Cedrorestes.etymology: From Latin 'cedrus' meaning 'cedar' and Greek 'oros' meaning 'mountain' (after the Cedar Mountain Formation where the fossil was found), with Greek suffix '-etes' meaning 'dweller'.
Cedrorestes.description: Cedrorestes is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Utah. It is based on an incomplete skeleton which was found in the Valanginian-age Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.

species.name: Cedrorestes crichtoni
species.etymology: Named for Michael Crichton, author of Jurassic Park and The Lost World.

holotype.institution: Denver Museum of Nature and Science

Centrosaurus.etymology: From Greek kentron (κέντρον) meaning 'point' and Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'pointed lizard', referring to the small hornlets along the margin of its frill.
Centrosaurus.description: Centrosaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from the Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous of Canada. Its remains have been found in the Dinosaur Park Formation, dating from 76.5 to 75.5 million years ago. The type and only species seen as valid today is Centrosaurus apertus.

synonyms.name: Eucentrosaurus
synonyms.reason: Proposed as a replacement name when Centrosaurus was thought to be preoccupied by the stegosaur Kentrosaurus; the perceived conflict was later determined to be invalid.

species.name: Centrosaurus apertus
species.etymology: From Latin 'apertio' meaning 'an opening' or 'aperture', referring to the two large, open fenestrae in the frill that distinguish it from other ceratopsians.

Cerasinops.etymology: From Greek kerasos meaning 'cherry' and Greek ops meaning 'face'. Full meaning: 'cherry face', likely referring to the shape or color of its facial features.
Cerasinops.description: Cerasinops was a small ceratopsian dinosaur. It lived during the Campanian of the late Cretaceous Period. Its fossils have been found in Two Medicine Formation, in Montana. The type species of the genus Cerasinops is C. hodgskissi.

species.name: Cerasinops hodgskissi
species.etymology: Named for Wilson Hodgskiss, who owned the land where the holotype specimen was found.

Ceratonykus.etymology: From Greek keras/keratos ('horn') + onyx/nykos ('claw'), meaning 'horned claw'.
Ceratonykus.description: Ceratonykus is a monospecific genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur from Mongolia that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) in what is now the Barun Goyot Formation. The type and only species, Ceratonykus oculatus, is known from a fragmentary skeleton, including an incomplete skull, of an adult individual. It was named and described in 2009 by Vladimir Alifanov and Rinchen Barsbold. Its describers questioned the traditional placement of alvarezsaurs in Theropoda, instead suggesting they were ornithischians, but this has not been accepted since. Ceratonykus has an estimated length of 75 centimetres (2.46 feet) and weight of 760 grams (1.68 pounds). It has been considered as a possible junior synonym of Parvicursor.

species.name: Ceratonykus oculatus
species.etymology: From Latin word meaning 'sharp-sighted' or 'big-eyed', in reference to the large orbits of the skull.

Ceratosuchops.etymology: From Greek keras/keratos ('horn') + Latin suchus ('crocodile', from Greek) + ops ('face'), meaning 'horned crocodile face', in reference to the bony boss on the postorbital bone.
Ceratosuchops.description: Ceratosuchops is a genus of spinosaurid from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Wessex Formation of Britain. The type species is C. inferodios, known from skull fragments (a snout tip and a partial braincase) recovered between 2013–2017 from Chilton Chine on the Isle of Wight, and housed at the Dinosaur Isle Museum in Sandown. It was named in 2021 by a team consisting of Chris Tijani Barker, Darren Naish, David W. E. Hone, and colleagues, alongside Riparovenator milnerae.

species.name: Ceratosuchops inferodios
species.etymology: From Latin, combining 'infernus' ('hell' or 'underworld') and Greek 'erodios' ('heron'), referencing the research team's inference that its ecology resembled that of modern herons, earning it the nickname 'hell heron'.

holotype.institution: Isle of Wight County Museum Service at Dinosaur Isle

Cetiosauriscus.etymology: From Greek 'ketos' meaning 'sea monster' or 'whale', 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', and '-iskos' meaning 'resembling', meaning 'resembling Cetiosaurus' (the whale lizard).
Cetiosauriscus.description: Cetiosauriscus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived between 166 and 164 million years ago during the Callovian (Middle Jurassic Period) in what is now England. A herbivore, Cetiosauriscus had – by sauropod standards – a moderately long tail, and longer forelimbs, making them as long as its hindlimbs. It has been estimated as about 15 m (49 ft) long and between 4 and 10 t (3.9 and 9.8 long tons; 4.4 and 11.0 short tons) in weight.

species.name: Cetiosauriscus stewarti
species.etymology: Named for Sir Ronald Stewart, the chairman of the London Brick Company that owned the clay pit where the fossils were found.

Cetiosaurus.etymology: From Greek keteios/ketos ('sea monster', later 'whale') + sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'whale lizard'. Named by Richard Owen who initially believed it was a large marine creature.
Cetiosaurus.description: Cetiosaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Period, living about 171 to 165 million years ago during the Bajocian and Bathonian ages in what is now Britain and probably France.

synonyms.name: Cardiodon
synonyms.reason: Possible junior subjective synonym of Cetiosaurus; identification is tentative. Per Olshevsky's Dinosaur Genera List.

species.name: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis

Chadititan.etymology: From Spanish chadi ('salt' or referring to the salt flats of the Salitral Moreno region) + Greek Titan (a giant from mythology), meaning 'titan of the salt'.
Chadititan.description: Chadititan is an extinct genus of titanosaurian dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Anacleto Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, C. calvoi, known from several fragmentary skeletons. Chadititan is characterized by its small size compared to related taxa and its particularly gracile limbs.

species.etymology: Named for Argentine paleontologist Jorge O. Calvo, who coined the taxonomic group Rinconsauria, to which this taxon belongs.

Chakisaurus.etymology: From Mapudungun chaki ('elder guanaco') + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'elder guanaco lizard'.
Chakisaurus.description: Chakisaurus is an extinct genus of elasmarian ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, C. nekul, known from multiple partial skeletons belonging to individuals of different ages. Chakisaurus represents the first ornithischian species to be named from the Huincul Formation.

species.name: Chakisaurus nekul
species.etymology: From Mapudungun 'nekul' meaning 'swift', in reference to the cursorial habits inferred for this ornithopod.

Changchunsaurus.etymology: Named after Changchun, the city near where it was discovered in Jilin Province, China, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Changchun lizard'.
Changchunsaurus.description: Changchunsaurus is an extinct genus of small herbivorous neornithischian dinosaur from Early or Late Cretaceous deposits of Gongzhuling, Jilin, China. It is the first named dinosaur genus from that region.

species.name: Changchunsaurus parvus
species.etymology: From Latin 'parvus' meaning 'petite' or 'small', named for the small size of the animal.

Changmiania.etymology: From Chinese changmian (长眠, 'eternal sleep'), referring to the life-like buried positions of the specimens, which suggest they were buried alive while sleeping.
Changmiania.description: Changmiania is a genus of basal ornithopod dinosaur that lived in what is now China during the Early Cretaceous. It contains a single species, Changmiania liaoningensis.

species.name: Changmiania liaoningensis
species.etymology: Named for the provenance of the fossils from Liaoning Province, China.

Changyuraptor.etymology: From Chinese 'chang' meaning 'long', 'yu' meaning 'feather', and Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief' or 'seizer', referring to its long feathers.
Changyuraptor.description: Changyuraptor is a genus of "four-winged", predatory dinosaurs. It is known from a single fossil specimen representing the species Changyuraptor yangi, which was discovered from Early Cretaceous (125 million year old) deposits in Liaoning Province, China. C. yangi belongs to the group of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaurs called the Microraptoria.

species.name: Changyuraptor yangi
species.etymology: Named for researcher Professor Yang Yandong.

Chaoyangsaurus.etymology: Named after Chaoyang, the region in Liaoning Province, China where fossils were found, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Chaoyang lizard'.
Chaoyangsaurus.description: Chaoyangsaurus is a genus of marginocephalian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (about between 150.8 and 145.5 million years ago) of China. Chaoyangsaurus belonged to the Ceratopsia (Greek for "horned faces"). Chaoyangsaurus, like all ceratopsians, was primarily a herbivore.

species.name: Chaoyangsaurus youngi
species.etymology: Named for the Chinese paleontologist Yang Zhongjian (known as 'C. C. Young'), regarded as the founder of Chinese vertebrate paleontology.

Charonosaurus.etymology: Named after Charon, the ferryman of the dead in Greek mythology who ferried souls across the river (the Amur River, near where the fossils were found, divides China and Russia), combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Charon's lizard'.
Charonosaurus.description: Charonosaurus is a genus of lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur similar to Parasaurolophus that lived in the latest Cretaceous Yuliangze Formation of China. Its fossils were described by Godefroit, Zan, and Jin in 2000, on the south bank of the Amur River, dividing China from Russia. It is monotypic, consisting of the species, C. jiayinensis.

species.name: Charonosaurus jiayinensis
species.etymology: Named for the type locality of Jiayin, in Heilongjiang Province, China, where the fossils were discovered.

Chasmosaurus.etymology: From Greek chasma meaning 'opening/hollow/gulf' and Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'opening lizard', referring to the large fenestrae (openings) in its frill.
Chasmosaurus.description: Chasmosaurus is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period in North America. Its given name means 'opening lizard', referring to the large openings (fenestrae) in its frill (Greek chasma, meaning 'opening', 'hollow', or 'gulf'; and sauros, meaning 'lizard'). With a length of 4.3–4.8 metres (14.1–15.7 ft) and a weight of 1.5–2 tonnes (1.7–2.2 short tons)—or anywhere from 2,200 to nearly 5,000 lbs—Chasmosaurus was of a slightly smaller to "average" size, especially when compared to larger ceratopsids (such as Triceratops, which were about the size of an African bush elephant).

synonyms.name: Mojoceratops
synonyms.reason: Initially synonymized with Chasmosaurus based on overlapping diagnostic features; recent fieldwork in Dinosaur Provincial Park suggests Mojoceratops may yet prove to be a valid genus.

synonyms.name: Eoceratops
synonyms.reason: Originally described as Monoclonius canadensis and later re-erected as Eoceratops; the material is now treated as morphological variation within Chasmosaurus.

species.name: Chasmosaurus belli
species.etymology: Named for collector Walter Bell, from whose discovery area the holotype parietal bone was recovered.

synonyms.name: Protorosaurus belli
synonyms.reason: Originally described as Protorosaurus belli; the genus name was preoccupied, and the species was reassigned to Chasmosaurus.

references.title: On Gryposaurus notabilis, a new genus and species of trachodont dinosaur from the Belly River Formation of Alberta, with a description of the skull of Chasmosaurus belli

Chebsaurus.etymology: From colloquial Arabic 'cheb' (شاب) meaning 'young man', referring to the juvenile nature of the fossils found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Chebsaurus.description: Chebsaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur, specifically a eusauropod. It lived in present-day Algeria, in the Callovian aged Aïssa Formation. The type species, C. algeriensis, was named in 2005 by Mahammed et al. and is the most complete Algerian sauropod known. It was around 8 to 9 metres (26 to 30 ft) long.

species.name: Chebsaurus algeriensis
species.etymology: Named for Algeria, the country where the fossils were discovered.

Chenanisaurus.etymology: Named after Sidi Chennane, the locality in Morocco (Khouribga phosphate mines) where the fossil was found, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Sidi Chennane lizard'.
Chenanisaurus.description: Chenanisaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Morocco. The genus belongs to the family Abelisauridae. It is known from a partial dentary (lower jawbone) and several teeth that were found in the phosphate mines of Khouribga, in rocks of the Maastrichtian-aged Ouled Abdoun Basin. Chenanisaurus was described in 2017 by British paleontologist Nicholas Longrich and colleagues. The genus contains a single species, Chenanisaurus barbaricus.

species.name: Chenanisaurus barbaricus
species.etymology: From Greek word 'barbaros' meaning 'barbaric' and also refers to Barbary, as in the Barbary Coast of Morocco and northwest Africa, where the fossils were found.

Chialingosaurus.etymology: Named after the Chialing River (now Jialing River) in Sichuan Province, China, where fossils were discovered, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Chialing lizard'.
Chialingosaurus.description: Chialingosaurus is a genus of herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur similar to Kentrosaurus from the Upper Shaximiao Formation, Late Jurassic beds in Sichuan Province in China. Its age makes it one of the oldest species of stegosaurs, living about 160 million years ago. Since it was an herbivore, scientists think that Chialingosaurus probably ate ferns and cycads, which were plentiful during the period when Chialingosaurus was alive.

species.name: Chialingosaurus kuani
species.etymology: Named for geologist Kuan Yaowu (also spelled Guan Yao-Wu), who collected the fossils in 1957 while surveying the Chialing River.

Chilantaisaurus.etymology: Named after Jilantai (also romanized as Chilantai) Salt Lake in Inner Mongolia, China, where the fossils were found, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Jilantai Salt Lake lizard'.
Chilantaisaurus.description: Chilantaisaurus is an extinct genus of large theropod dinosaur that lived in present-day China during the Late Cretaceous period. It was described by Chinese paleontologist Hu Show-Yung in 1964. The genus contains a single valid species, C. tashuikouensis, though several other species have been assigned to the genus. C. tashuikouensis is known from a single, incomplete postcranial skeleton, the holotype specimen. This specimen was found by a joint Sino-Soviet expedition to Inner Mongolia in rock layers coming from the Ulansuhai Formation. This indicates these fossils date to the Santonian or Campanian stages of the Cretaceous period, around 85.7 to 72.2 million years ago. However, the age of the Ulansuhai Formation is debated.

species.etymology: Named for the Tashuikou site in Inner Mongolia, China, where the holotype fossils were discovered.

Chilesaurus.etymology: Named after Chile, the country in South America where it was discovered, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Chile lizard'.
Chilesaurus.description: Chilesaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous dinosaur. While its exact classification is uncertain, many researchers believe it is a theropod, with a minority of academics suggesting that it may be an ornithischian. The type and only known species so far is Chilesaurus diegosuarezi. Chilesaurus lived between 148-147 million years ago (Mya) in the Late Jurassic period of Chile. Showing a combination of traits from theropods, ornithischians, and sauropodomorphs, this genus has far-reaching implications for the evolution of dinosaurs, such as whether the traditional saurischian-ornithischian split is superior or inferior to the proposed group Ornithoscelida. This however, has been contested by several other authors, who believe that the weight of evidence supports its membership within Theropoda, and possibly as a member of Tetanurae.

species.etymology: Named for Diego Suárez, the seven-year-old who first discovered the fossils in the Aysén Region of Chile in 2004.

Chindesaurus.etymology: Named for the Chinde Point area of Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Chindesaurus.description: Chindesaurus is an extinct genus of basal saurischian dinosaur from the Late Triassic (213-210 million years ago) of the southwestern United States. It is known from a single species, C. bryansmalli, based on a partial skeleton recovered from Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona. The original specimen was nicknamed "Gertie", and generated much publicity for the park upon its discovery in 1984 and airlift out of the park in 1985. Other fragmentary referred specimens have been found in Late Triassic sediments throughout Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas, but these may not belong to the genus. Chindesaurus was a bipedal carnivore, approximately as large as a wolf.

Chingkankousaurus.etymology: Named after Ch'ing-kang-kou (Wade-Giles romanization; pinyin: Jin-gang-kou, meaning 'diamond port', Chinese: 金刚口), the village in Shandong Province, China where it was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Chingkangkou lizard'.
Chingkankousaurus.description: Chingkankousaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur containing the single species Chingkankousaurus fragilis. C. fragilis is known only from a single fossilized bone fragment (specimen number IVPP V836) from the late Cretaceous Period Wangshi Series of Shandong province in eastern China.

Chinshakiangosaurus.etymology: Named after the Chinshakiang (now Jinsha River) in China, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Chinshakiang lizard'.
Chinshakiangosaurus.description: Chinshakiangosaurus is a genus of basal sauropod dinosaur. The only species, Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis, is known from a fragmentary skeleton found in Early Jurassic rocks in China. It is one of the few basal sauropods with preserved skull bones and therefore important for the understanding of the early evolution of this group, and also shows that early sauropods may have possessed fleshy cheeks.

species.etymology: Named for the village of Zhonghe (Chungho in older romanization) near the discovery site in Yunnan Province, China.

Chirostenotes.etymology: From Greek cheir meaning 'hand' and Greek stenos meaning 'narrow'. Full meaning: 'narrow-handed', referring to the narrow, slender hands of the fossil.
Chirostenotes.description: Chirostenotes is a genus of oviraptorosaurian dinosaur from the late Cretaceous (about 76.5–75 million years ago) of Alberta, Canada. The type species is Chirostenotes pergracilis.

Choconsaurus.etymology: Named after Villa El Chocón, the locality in Neuquén Province, Argentina where the holotype was found, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'El Chocón lizard'.
Choconsaurus.description: Choconsaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur belonging to the group Titanosauriformes, which lived in the area of present-day Argentina at the end of the Cretaceous.

species.name: Choconsaurus baileywillisi
species.etymology: Named for American geologist Bailey Willis, who traced the stratigraphy of the Neuquén region of Argentina between 1910 and 1914.

Chondrosteosaurus.etymology: From Greek chondros ('cartilage') + osteon ('bone') + sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'cartilage and bone lizard', referring to the mix of cartilaginous and bony structures in its vertebrae.
Chondrosteosaurus.description: Chondrosteosaurus is a dubious genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation of England. Two species have been named: C. gigas and C. magnus, both of which are now considered invalid.

species.name: Chondrosteosaurus gigas
species.etymology: From Latin 'gigas' meaning 'giant', referring to the large size of the sauropod vertebrae on which the species was based.

Choyrodon.etymology: Named for the city of Choyr in Mongolia, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'odon' meaning 'tooth'.
Choyrodon.description: Choyrodon is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian) Khuren Dukh Formation of Mongolia. The type and only species is Choyrodon barsboldi. The generic name is derived from the city of Choyr, and -odon, from Latin for tooth; the specific name barsboldi honours paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold. The material consists of a holotype partial skull and cervical ribs, with two other partial skulls both with associated postcranial material. It was found to be the sister taxon of Eolambia.

Chromogisaurus.etymology: From Greek chroma meaning 'colour' and Greek ge meaning 'earth', combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'coloured earth lizard', a reference to the Valle Pintado ('Painted Valley') where it was found.
Chromogisaurus.description: Chromogisaurus is an extinct genus of saturnaliid sauropodomorph which existed in Argentina during the Late Triassic (Carnian) period. It is from the Cancha de Bochas, Valle Pintado member of the Ischigualasto Formation. It was a small, bipedal herbivore, about 2 metres (6 ft 7 in) in length.

Chuandongocoelurus.description: Chuandongocoelurus is a genus of carnivorous tetanuran theropod dinosaur from the Jurassic of China.

Chuanjiesaurus.etymology: Named for the village of Chuanjie in Yunnan Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Chuanjiesaurus.description: Chuanjiesaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaurs from the middle Jurassic Period. They lived in what is now China. The type species, Chuanjiesaurus anaensis, was first described by Fang, Pang, Lü, Zhang, Pan, Wang, Li and Cheng in 2000. Fossils of the species were found in the village of Chuanjie, Lufeng County, Yunnan Province, (in Chuanjie Formation deposits) and are named after the location where the fossils were discovered. Holtz gave a length of 25 meters (82 ft).

Chuanqilong.etymology: From Chinese chuanqi (传奇, 'legendary') + long (龙, 'dragon'), meaning 'legendary dragon'.
Chuanqilong.description: Chuanqilong is a monospecific genus of basal ankylosaurid dinosaur from the Liaoning Province, China that lived during the Early Cretaceous (late Barremian to Aptian stage, 122.0 to 118.9 Ma) in what is now the Jiufotang Formation. The type and only species, Chuanqilong chaoyangensis, is known from a nearly complete skeleton with a skull of a juvenile individual. It was described in 2014 by Fenglu Han, Wenjie Zheng, Dongyu Hu, Xing Xu, and Paul M. Barrett. Chuanqilong shows many similarities with Liaoningosaurus and may represent a later ontogenetic stage of the taxon.

species.etymology: Named for the broader geographical area of Chaoyang in Liaoning Province, China, which encompasses the type locality.

Chubutisaurus.etymology: Named after Chubut Province in Patagonia, Argentina, where the fossils were discovered, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Chubut lizard'.
Chubutisaurus.description: Chubutisaurus is a genus of somphospondylan sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian) Cerro Barcino Formation of Argentina. The type species, Chubutisaurus insignis, was described by del Corro in 1975. Chubutisaurus had a more robust radius than Venenosaurus. In 2010 Gregory S. Paul gave a length of 18 metres (59 ft) and a weight of 12 tonnes (13 short tons). Thomas Holtz estimated its length at 23 metres (75 ft) in 2012.

Chucarosaurus.etymology: From Mapudungun or Quechua chucaro ('indomitable' or 'wild, untamed') + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'indomitable reptile'.
Chucarosaurus.description: Chucarosaurus is an extinct genus of titanosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (middle Cenomanian–lower Turonian) Huincul Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, C. diripienda, known from various limb and pelvic bones.

Chungkingosaurus.etymology: Named after Chongqing (formerly romanized as Chungking), the city in Sichuan Province, China where fossils were found, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Chongqing lizard'.
Chungkingosaurus.description: Chungkingosaurus is a genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Upper Shaximiao Formation in what is now China. The type species is Chungkingosaurus jiangbeiensis.

Cienciargentina.etymology: From Spanish 'ciencia' meaning 'science' and 'Argentina', combining a tribute to Argentine science with the country of discovery.
Cienciargentina.description: Cienciargentina is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian–Turonian) Huincul Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Cienciargentina sanchezi, known from three partial skeletons of different sizes. Cienciargentina is the fourth definitive rebbachisaurid to be named from the Huincul Formation.

Cionodon.etymology: From Greek kion meaning 'column/pillar' and Greek odon meaning 'tooth'. Full meaning: 'column tooth', referring to the pillar-like shape of its teeth.
Cionodon.description: Cionodon is a dubious genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous. The type species, C. arctatus, was found in the Denver Formation of Lodge Pole Creek, Colorado and was formally described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1874 based on the holotype AMNH 3951, collected in 1873. It is a nomen dubium because it is based on very fragmentary remains. Two other species have since been described: Cionodon kysylkumensis (Riabinin, 1931), based on the holotype CCMGE 1/3760 (a set of vertebrae) from Uzbekistan, and Cionodon stenopsis (Cope, 1875), discovered in rocks from the Judith River Formation of Alberta, Canada in 1874. Although both are probably hadrosaurs, they are known only from fragmentary remains and Cionodon kysylkumensis has since been reclassified as Bactrosaurus kysylkumensis.

species.etymology: From Latin 'arctatus' meaning 'compressed', likely referring to the compressed form of the teeth.

Citipati.etymology: From Sanskrit/Tibetan Buddhist mythology, citipati refers to the 'lords of the cemetery' or 'funeral pyre lords', two monks who became the guardians of the dead. The name alludes to individuals found atop nests, interpreted as brooding over eggs.
Citipati.description: Citipati is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period, about 75 million to 71 million years ago. It is mainly known from the Ukhaa Tolgod locality at the Djadochta Formation, where the first remains were collected during the 1990s. The genus and type species Citipati osmolskae were named and described in 2001. A second species from the adjacent Zamyn Khondt locality may also exist. Citipati is one of the best-known oviraptorids thanks to a number of well-preserved specimens, including individuals found in brooding positions atop nests of eggs, though most of them were initially referred to the related Oviraptor. These nesting specimens have helped to solidify the link between non-avian dinosaurs and birds.

Citipes.etymology: From Latin 'citus' meaning 'swift' or 'fleet' and 'pes' meaning 'foot', translating to 'fleet-footed'.
Citipes.description: Citipes is an extinct genus of caenagnathid theropod from the Late Cretaceous Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada. The genus contains only one species, the type species, C. elegans. The generic name of Citipes is Latin for "fleet-footed", and the specific epithet "elegans" is Latin for "elegant". The type specimen of Citipes has a convoluted taxonomic history, and has been previously assigned to the genera Ornithomimus, Macrophalangia, Elmisaurus, Chirostenotes, and Leptorhynchos before being given its own genus in 2020.

Claosaurus.etymology: From Greek klao (κλάω) meaning 'broken' and Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'broken lizard', referring to the unusual position of the fossils when discovered.
Claosaurus.description: Claosaurus is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period (Santonian-Campanian) of what is now North America. The type and only known valid species is Claosaurus agilis. Traditionally classified as an early member of the family Hadrosauridae, a 2008 analysis found Claosaurus to be outside of the clade containing Hadrosaurus and other hadrosaurids, making it the closest non-hadrosaurid relative of true hadrosaurids within the clade Hadrosauromorpha.

Coahuilaceratops.etymology: Named after Coahuila, the state in northern Mexico where the fossils were found, + Greek ceratops ('horned face'), meaning 'horned face from Coahuila'.
Coahuilaceratops.description: Coahuilaceratops is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur that lived during the early Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous epoch, about 71.5 to 70.5 million years ago in what is now northern Mexico. It contains a single species, Coahuilaceratops magnacuerna.

species.name: Coahuilaceratops magnacuerna
species.etymology: Named for the large size of the animal's horns, combining the Latin 'magna' meaning 'great' and the Spanish 'cuerna' meaning 'horn'.

holotype.institution: Colección Paleontológica de Coahuila, Museo del Desierto (MUDE)

Coahuilasaurus.etymology: Named after Coahuila, the state in Mexico where the fossils were found, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Coahuila lizard'.
Coahuilasaurus.description: Coahuilasaurus is an extinct genus of kritosaurin ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Cerro del Pueblo Formation of Coahuila, Mexico. The genus contains a single species, C. lipani, known from the associated tips of the upper and lower jaw and other fragmentary skull bones. It is a large kritosaurin with an estimated body length of 8–9 metres (26–30 ft) and body mass of over 4 metric tons (4.4 short tons).

species.name: Coahuilasaurus lipani
species.etymology: Named for the Lépai-Ndé or Lipani, a tribe of Apache Native Americans known from the area of Coahuila, Mexico, where the fossils were found.

holotype.institution: Instituto de Geología, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México
holotype.material: Partial skull (tips of upper and lower jaw and other fragmentary skull bones)

references.title: Coahuilasaurus lipani, a New Kritosaurin Hadrosaurid from the Upper Campanian Cerro Del Pueblo Formation, Northern Mexico

Colepiocephale.etymology: From Greek kolepion ('knuckle') + kephale ('head'), meaning 'knucklehead', referring to the distinctive domed skull.
Colepiocephale.description: Colepiocephale is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from Late Cretaceous (middle Campanian stage) deposits of Alberta, Canada. It was collected from the Foremost Formation. The type species, C. lambei, was originally described by Sternberg in 1945 as Stegoceras lambei, and later renamed by Sullivan in 2003. C. lambei is a domed pachycephalosaur characterized principally by the lack of a lateral and posteriosquamosal shelf, a steeply down-turned parietal, and the presence of two incipient nodes tucked under the posterior margin of the parietosquamosal border.

species.name: Colepiocephale lambei
species.etymology: Named for the deceased Canadian palaeontologist Lawrence M. Lambe.

references.authors: Sullivan, Robert M.
references.title: Revision of the dinosaur Stegoceras Lambe (Ornithischia, Pachycephalosauridae)

Coloradisaurus.etymology: Named after the Los Colorados Formation in La Rioja Province, Argentina, where fossils were found, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Los Colorados lizard'.
Coloradisaurus.description: Coloradisaurus is a genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur. It lived during the Late Triassic period (Norian stage) in what is now La Rioja Province, Argentina. It is known from two specimens collected from the Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin.

synonyms.name: Coloradia
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Coloradia (Lepidoptera).

species.name: Coloradisaurus brevis
species.etymology: From Latin 'brevis' meaning 'short', likely assigned by José F. Bonaparte to describe the relatively short skull compared to other dinosaurs from the same locality.

holotype.institution: Colección de Paleontologia de Vertebrados de la Fundación Instituto Miguel Lillo

Comahuesaurus.etymology: Named after the Comahue region of Patagonia, Argentina, where the fossils were found, + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Comahue lizard'.
Comahuesaurus.description: Comahuesaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur of the family Rebbachisauridae. It was found in the Lohan Cura Formation in Argentina, and lived during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian). The type species is C. windhauseni, named for Anselmo Windhausen, who contributed significantly to the geological study of Patagonia.

species.name: Comahuesaurus windhauseni
species.etymology: Named for Anselmo Windhausen, who contributed significantly to the geological study of Patagonia.

location.locality: Cerro Aguade del León, La Picaza

holotype.institution: Museo Provincial de Ciencias Naturales "Dr, Prof. Juan A. Olsacher"

Compsognathus.etymology: From Greek kompsos (κομψός) meaning 'elegant/refined/dainty' and Greek gnathos (γνάθος) meaning 'jaw'. Full meaning: 'elegant jaw' or 'dainty jaw'.
Compsognathus.description: Compsognathus is a genus of small, bipedal, carnivorous theropod dinosaur. Members of its single species Compsognathus longipes could grow to around the size of a chicken. They lived about 150 million years ago, during the Tithonian age of the late Jurassic period, in what is now Europe. Paleontologists have found two well-preserved fossils, one in Germany in the 1850s and the second in France more than a century later. Today, C. longipes is the only recognized species, although the French specimen was once thought to belong to a separate species named C. corallestris.

species.name: Compsognathus longipes
species.etymology: From Latin 'longipes' meaning 'long-footed', referring to the long legs of this small theropod.

holotype.institution: Bayerische Staatssammlung für Paläontologie und Geologie

references.authors: Wagner, J. A.
references.title: Neue Beiträge zur Kenntniss der urweltlichen Fauna des lithographischen Schiefers [New contributions to the knowledge of the ancient fauna of the lithographic slates]

Compsosuchus.etymology: From Greek kompsos ('elegant', 'refined') + Latin suchus ('crocodile', from Greek soukhos), meaning 'elegant crocodile'.
Compsosuchus.description: Compsosuchus is a dubious genus of abelisauroid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Lameta Formation of India.

species.name: Compsosuchus solus
species.etymology: From Latin 'solus' meaning 'alone' or 'sole'; the reason for the choice is unclear, though it may refer to the fact that the genus is based on a single specimen.

references.authors: Huene, F. v.; Matley, C. A.

Comptonatus.etymology: From Compton (the village near the Isle of Wight discovery site) + Latin tonatus ('thundered'), meaning 'the Compton thunderer'.
Comptonatus.description: Comptonatus is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the early Cretaceous period. Its remains are known from the Wessex Formation in England. The type and only species is C. chasei.

species.name: Comptonatus chasei
species.etymology: Named for the late Nick Chase, who discovered the holotype specimen and won the Palaeontological Association's Mary Anning Award in 2018.

holotype.institution: Isle of Wight County Museum Service at Dinosaur Isle

references.authors: Lockwood, Jeremy A. F.; Martill, David M.; Maidment, Susannah C. R.
references.title: Comptonatus chasei, a new iguanodontian dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, southern England

Concavenator.etymology: From Latin Conca, an old name for Cuenca (the Spanish city near the discovery site), + Latin venator ('hunter'), meaning 'Cuenca hunter'.
Concavenator.description: Concavenator is a genus of carcharodontosaurian dinosaur that lived in Spain during the Early Cretaceous epoch, about 125 million years ago. The genus contains a single species, Concavenator corcovatus, named and described in 2010 from a nearly complete skeleton collected from the Las Hoyas fossil site of the La Huérguina Formation.

species.name: Concavenator corcovatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'corcovatus' meaning 'hump-backed', referring to the hump-like structure formed by the elongated dorsal vertebrae.

holotype.institution: Museo de las Ciencias de Castilla-La Mancha

references.title: A bizarre, humped Carcharodontosauria (Theropoda) from the Lower Cretaceous of Spain

Conchoraptor.etymology: From Greek konche ('conch shell') + Latin raptor ('plunderer' or 'thief'), meaning 'conch plunderer', suggesting the animal may have fed on mollusks.
Conchoraptor.description: Conchoraptor is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous epoch, about 70 million years ago. It is known from the Barun Goyot and possibly the Nemegt formation of Mongolia.

species.name: Conchoraptor gracilis
species.etymology: From Latin 'gracilis' meaning 'gracile' or 'slender', referring to the slender build of the animal.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.title: Avialan status for Oviraptorosauria

Condorraptor.etymology: From Cerro Condor (a nearby village in Argentina) + Latin raptor, 'robber/thief'; means 'robber from Cerro Condor'
Condorraptor.description: Condorraptor is an extinct genus of megalosauroid theropod dinosaur. Its genus name means 'robber from Cerro Condor', referencing a nearby village, while its species name, currumili, is named after Hipolito Currumil, the landowner and discoverer of the locality. It was among the earliest large South American theropods, having been found in Lower Jurassic strata of the Cañadón Asfalto Formation in the Cañadón Asfalto Basin of Argentina. The type species, described in 2005, is Condorraptor currumili. It is based on a tibia, with an associated partial skeleton that may belong to the same individual. Initially described as a basal tetanuran, Benson (2010) found it to be a piatnitzkysaurid megalosauroid and the sister taxon of Piatnitzkysaurus, a finding supported by later studies.

species.name: Condorraptor currumili
species.etymology: Named for Hipolito Currumil, the landowner who discovered the fossil locality in the Cañadón Asfalto Basin of Argentina.

references.authors: RAUHUT, OLIVER W. M.
references.title: Osteology and relationships of a new theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of Patagonia

Convolosaurus.etymology: From Latin convolo ('to flock together') + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'flocking lizard', in reference to the concentration of juvenile fossils found together at the discovery site.
Convolosaurus.description: Convolosaurus is a genus of basal ornithopod dinosaur from the Twin Mountains Formation from Proctor Lake in Comanche County, Texas. The type and only species is Convolosaurus marri.

species.name: Convolosaurus marri
species.etymology: Named for Dr. Ray H. Marr, who propagated the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology at Southern Methodist University.

location.locality: North Quarry/Camp Quarry, Proctor Lake Dinosaur Locality

holotype.institution: Schuler Museum of Paleontology, Southern Methodist University

references.title: A new basal ornithopod (Dinosauria: Ornithischia) from the Early Cretaceous of Texas

Coronosaurus.etymology: From Latin corona, 'crown', + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'crowned lizard', referring to the crown-like horn arrangement on its frill
Coronosaurus.description: Coronosaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaurs which lived in the Late Cretaceous, in the middle Campanian stage. Its remains, two bone beds, were discovered by Phillip J. Currie in the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada, and its type and only species, Coronosaurus brinkmani, was first described in 2005, as a new species within the genus Centrosaurus. Later studies questioned the presence of a direct relationship, and in 2012 it was named as a separate genus. Coronosaurus means "crowned lizard", coming from "corona", Latin for crown, and "sauros", Greek for lizard; this name refers to the unique, crown-like shape of the horns on the top of its frill.

species.name: Coronosaurus brinkmani
species.etymology: Named for Donald Brinkman, in recognition of his research into the palaeoecology of Late Cretaceous environments of Alberta.

references.authors: Ryan, Michael J.; Evans, David C.; Shepherd, Kieran M.
references.title: A new ceratopsid from the Foremost Formation (middle Campanian) of Alberta

Corythoraptor.etymology: From Greek korythos, 'helmet', + Latin raptor, 'thief'; means 'helmeted thief', referring to its tall cassowary-like head crest
Corythoraptor.description: Corythoraptor is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur from the late Maastrichtian Nanxiong Formation of South China. It contains one species, C. jacobsi, known from a single well-preserved skeleton, and named after paleontologist Louis L. Jacobs. It bears a tall crest similar to that of the modern cassowary, and possibly had a similar functionality of display and resonance to detect lower-frequency sounds.

species.name: Corythoraptor jacobsi
species.etymology: Named for American vertebrate paleontologist Louis L. Jacobs, who mentored three of the describing authors during their doctoral studies at Southern Methodist University.

references.authors: Lü, Junchang; Li, Guoqing; Kundrát, Martin; Lee, Yuong-Nam; Sun, Zhenyuan; Kobayashi, Yoshitsugu; Shen, Caizhi; Teng, Fangfang; Liu, Hanfeng

Corythosaurus.etymology: From Greek korys (κόρυς), 'helmet', + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'helmeted lizard', referring to its helmet-like head crest
Corythosaurus.description: Corythosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid "duck-billed" dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period, about 77–75.7 million years ago, in what is now western North America. Its name is derived from the Greek word κόρυς, meaning "helmet", named and described in 1914 by Barnum Brown. Corythosaurus is now thought to be a lambeosaurine, thus related to Lambeosaurus, Nipponosaurus, Velafrons, Hypacrosaurus, and Olorotitan. Corythosaurus has an estimated length of 7.7–9 metres (25–30 ft) and has a skull, including the crest, that is 70.8 centimetres (27.9 in; 2.32 ft) tall.

species.name: Corythosaurus casuarius
species.etymology: Named for the cassowary (Casuarius), a modern bird with a similarly prominent skull crest.

Craterosaurus.etymology: From Greek krater, 'bowl' or 'mixing vessel', + Greek sauros, 'lizard/reptile'; means 'bowl reptile' or 'krater reptile'
Craterosaurus.description: Craterosaurus is a dubious genus of stegosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous (possibly Aptian stage) of the Woburn Sands Formation of England. Estimated to measure around 4 m (13 ft) in length and weighing approximately 560 kg (1,230 lb), Craterosaurus may actually be a junior synonym of Regnosaurus, but only one fossil, a partial vertebra, was recovered.

species.name: Craterosaurus pottonensis
species.etymology: Named for Potton, the locality in Bedfordshire, England, near which the fossil was discovered.
