Eocursor.etymology: From Greek eos (dawn) + Latin cursor (runner): 'dawn runner', indicating it is one of the earliest known ornithischians.
Eocursor.description: Eocursor is genus of basal ornithischian dinosaur that lived in what is now South Africa during the Early Jurassic. Remains of this animal have been found in the Upper Elliot Formation and it is among the most completely known early ornithischians, shedding new light on the origin of the group.

species.name: Eocursor parvus
species.etymology: From Latin 'parvus' meaning 'little', referring to the small size of this early ornithischian.

references.authors: Butler, Richard J; Smith, Roger M.H; Norman, David B
references.title: A primitive ornithischian dinosaur from the Late Triassic of South Africa, and the early evolution and diversification of Ornithischia
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

Eodromaeus.etymology: From Greek eos (dawn) + dromeus (runner): 'dawn runner', reflecting its status as one of the earliest known theropods.
Eodromaeus.description: Eodromaeus is an extinct genus of probable basal theropod dinosaurs from the Late Triassic of Argentina. Like many other of the earliest-known dinosaurs, it hails from the Carnian-age (~230 Ma) Ischigualasto Formation, within the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin of northwestern Argentina. Upon its discovery, it was argued to be one of the oldest true theropods, supplanting its contemporary Eoraptor, which was reinterpreted as a basal sauropodomorph.

species.name: Eodromaeus murphi
species.etymology: Named for Jim Murphy, an Earthwatch volunteer who helped discover the first fossils near the Ischigualasto Formation of Argentina.

holotype.institution: División de Paleontología de Vertebrados del Museo de Ciencias Naturales y Universidad Nacional de San Juan

references.authors: Martinez, Ricardo N.; Sereno, Paul C.; Alcober, Oscar A.; Colombi, Carina E.; Renne, Paul R.; Montañez, Isabel P.; Currie, Brian S.
references.title: A Basal Dinosaur from the Dawn of the Dinosaur Era in Southwestern Pangaea
references.publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

Eolambia.etymology: From Greek eos (dawn) + Lambeosaurinae: 'dawn lambeosaurine', indicating it is an early relative of lambeosaurine hadrosaurs.
Eolambia.description: Eolambia is a genus of herbivorous hadrosauroid dinosaur from the early Late Cretaceous of the United States. It contains a single species, E. caroljonesa, named by paleontologist James Kirkland in 1998. The type specimen of Eolambia was discovered by Carole and Ramal Jones in 1993; the species name honors Carole. Since then, hundreds of bones have been discovered from both adults and juveniles, representing nearly every element of the skeleton. All of the specimens have thus far been found in Emery County, Utah, in a layer of rock known as the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.

synonyms.name: Eohadrosaurus
synonyms.reason: Informal name ('Eohadrosaurus caroljonesi') used by Kirkland before the 1998 paper; replaced by the formal name Eolambia.

species.name: Eolambia caroljonesa
species.etymology: Named for Carole Jones, who together with her husband Ramal discovered the type specimen in 1993.

holotype.institution: College of Eastern Utah Prehistoric Museum

references.authors: Kirkland, J. I.
references.title: A new hadrosaurid from the upper Cedar Mountain Formation (Albian-Cenomanian: Cretaceous) of eastern Utah - the oldest known hadrosaurid (lambeosaurine?)
references.journal: Lower and Middle Cretaceous Terrestrial Ecosystems, S. G. Lucas, J. I. Kirkland & J. W. Estep (eds.). New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science Bulletin

Eomamenchisaurus.etymology: From Greek eos (dawn) + Mamenchisaurus (the related sauropod genus): 'dawn Mamenchisaurus', reflecting its status as an early mamenchisaurid.
Eomamenchisaurus.description: Eomamenchisaurus is a genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Zhanghe Formation of Yuanmou, Yunnan, China. The type species is E. yuanmouensis, described by Lü Junchang and colleagues in 2008.

species.name: Eomamenchisaurus yuanmouensis
species.etymology: Named for Yuanmou County in Yunnan, China, where the holotype was discovered.

references.authors: Lü, J.; Li, T.; S. Zhong, Q. Ji, S. Li
references.title: A new mamenchisaurid dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of Yuanmou, Yunnan Province, China

Eoneophron.etymology: From Greek eos, 'dawn/early', + Neophron (genus of Egyptian vulture); means 'dawn Neophron', drawing a comparison to the vulture genus and emphasizing its early appearance
Eoneophron.description: Eoneophron is an extinct genus of caenagnathid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Hell Creek Formation of South Dakota, US. The genus contains a single species, E. infernalis, known from a partial hindlimb.

species.name: Eoneophron infernalis
species.etymology: From Latin 'infernalis' meaning 'of hell', referencing the Hell Creek Formation in which the fossil material was discovered.

holotype.material: Partial right hindlimb: femur, tibia with fused astragalocalcaneum, metatarsals III and IV

references.authors: Atkins-Weltman, Kyle L.; Simon, D. Jade; Woodward, Holly N.; Funston, Gregory F.; Snively, Eric
references.title: A new oviraptorosaur (Dinosauria: Theropoda) from the end-Maastrichtian Hell Creek Formation of North America

Eoraptor.etymology: From Greek eos, 'dawn', + Latin raptor, 'seizer/thief'; means 'dawn thief' or 'dawn plunderer', reflecting its status as one of the earliest known dinosaurs
Eoraptor.description: Eoraptor is a genus of small, lightly built, basal sauropodomorph dinosaur. One of the earliest-known dinosaurs and one of the earliest sauropodomorphs, it lived approximately 231 to 228 million years ago, during the Late Triassic in Western Gondwana, in the region that is now northwestern Argentina. The type and only species, Eoraptor lunensis, was first described in 1993, and is known from an almost complete and well-preserved skeleton and several fragmentary ones. Eoraptor had multiple tooth shapes, which suggests that it was omnivorous.

species.name: Eoraptor lunensis
species.etymology: From Latin 'luna' meaning 'moon' with the suffix '-ensis' meaning 'from', a reference to the Valle de la Luna ('Valley of the Moon') in Argentina where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: División de Paleontología de Vertebrados del Museo de Ciencias Naturales y Universidad Nacional de San Juan

references.authors: Sereno, Paul C.; Forster, Catherine A.; Rogers, Raymond R.; Monetta, Alfredo M.
references.title: Primitive dinosaur skeleton from Argentina and the early evolution of Dinosauria
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Eosinopteryx.etymology: From Greek eos, 'dawn/daybreak', + Latin Sinae, 'Chinese', + Greek pteryx, 'feather' or 'wing'; means 'dawn Chinese feather', referring to its early age and feathered Chinese specimen
Eosinopteryx.description: Eosinopteryx is an extinct genus of theropod dinosaurs known to the Late Jurassic epoch of China. It contains a single species, Eosinopteryx brevipenna. Some researchers consider it a junior synonym of Anchiornis.

species.name: Eosinopteryx brevipenna
species.etymology: From Latin 'brevis' meaning 'short' and 'penna' meaning 'feather', referring to the reduced plumage preserved in the type specimen.

holotype.material: Nearly complete articulated skeleton

references.authors: Godefroit, Pascal; Demuynck, Helena; Dyke, Gareth; Hu, Dongyu; Escuillié, François; Claeys, Philippe
references.title: Reduced plumage and flight ability of a new Jurassic paravian theropod from China
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Eotrachodon.etymology: From Greek eos (dawn) + Trachodon (an early hadrosaurid genus): 'dawn Trachodon', indicating it is a primitive relative of hadrosaurids.
Eotrachodon.description: Eotrachodon is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous of eastern North America. The holotype was found in the Mooreville Chalk Formation (Upper Santonian) of Alabama in 2007 and includes a well-preserved skull and partial skeleton, making it a rare find among dinosaurs of Appalachia.

species.name: Eotrachodon orientalis
species.etymology: From Latin 'orientalis' meaning 'of the east', referring to its discovery in eastern North America.

references.authors: Prieto-Marquez, Albert; Erickson, Gregory M.; Ebersole, Jun A.
references.title: A primitive hadrosaurid from southeastern North America and the origin and early evolution of ‘duck-billed’ dinosaurs

Eotriceratops.etymology: From Greek eos (dawn) + treis (three) + keras (horn) + ops (face): 'dawn three-horned face', marking it as an early relative of Triceratops.
Eotriceratops.description: Eotriceratops is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaurs which lived in the area of North America during the late Cretaceous period. The only named species is Eotriceratops xerinsularis.

species.name: Eotriceratops xerinsularis
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'xeros' meaning 'dry' and Latin 'insula' meaning 'island', a reference to the Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park in Alberta, Canada, where the holotype was found.

location.locality: Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincal Park

references.authors: Wu, Xiao-chun; Brinkman, Donald B; Eberth, David A; Braman, Dennis R
references.title: A new ceratopsid dinosaur (Ornithischia) from the uppermost Horseshoe Canyon Formation (upper Maastrichtian), Alberta, Canada

Eotyrannus.etymology: From Greek eos (dawn) + tyrannos (tyrant): 'dawn tyrant', indicating it is an early member of the tyrannosaur lineage.
Eotyrannus.description: Eotyrannus is a genus of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur hailing from the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation beds, included in Wealden Group, located in the southwest coast of the Isle of Wight, United Kingdom. The remains (MIWG1997.550), consisting of assorted skull, axial skeleton and appendicular skeleton elements, from a juvenile or subadult, found in a plant debris clay bed, were described by Stephen Hutt and colleagues in early 2001. The etymology of the generic name refers to the animal's classification as an early tyrannosaur or "tyrant lizard", while the specific name honors the discoverer of the fossil.

synonyms.name: Lengosaurus
synonyms.reason: Informal name used for material now considered referable to Eotyrannus.

synonyms.name: Kittysaurus
synonyms.reason: Informal name used for material now considered referable to Eotyrannus.

synonyms.name: Gavinosaurus
synonyms.reason: Informal name used for material now considered referable to Eotyrannus.

synonyms.name: Fusinasus
synonyms.reason: Informal name used for material now considered referable to Eotyrannus.

species.name: Eotyrannus lengi
species.etymology: Named for Gavin Leng, the local collector who discovered the fossil on the Isle of Wight and revealed its location to researchers.

location.locality: 100 m east of Grange Chine (bed L11)

references.authors: Hutt, Stephen; Naish, Darren; Martill, David M.; Barker, Michael J.; Newbery, Penny
references.title: A preliminary account of a new tyrannosauroid theropod from the Wessex Formation (Early Cretaceous) of southern England

Eousdryosaurus.etymology: From Greek eous (eastern) + Dryosaurus (the related genus): 'eastern Dryosaurus', referring to its geographic origin in Portugal relative to other dryosaurid relatives.
Eousdryosaurus.description: Eousdryosaurus is a genus of basal iguanodontian dinosaur known from a partial skeleton discovered in Upper Jurassic rocks in western Portugal. The type, and only species, is Eousdryosaurus nanohallucis, named and described in 2014.

species.name: Eousdryosaurus nanohallucis
species.etymology: From Greek 'nanos' meaning 'small' and Latin 'hallux' meaning 'big toe', referring to the unusually small first digit of the foot.

references.authors: Escaso, Fernando; Ortega, Francisco; Dantas, Pedro; Malafaia, Elisabete; Silva, Bruno; Gasulla, José M.; Mocho, Pedro; Narváez, Iván; Sanz, JosÉ L.
references.title: A new dryosaurid ornithopod (Dinosauria, Ornithischia) from the Late Jurassic of Portugal

Epachthosaurus.etymology: From Greek epachthes (heavy/burdensome) + sauros (lizard): 'heavy lizard', likely referring to its robust build as a large titanosaur.
Epachthosaurus.description: Epachthosaurus was a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur, belonging to Lithostrotia, from the Late Cretaceous of Central and Northern Patagonia in South America.

species.name: Epachthosaurus sciuttoi
species.etymology: Named in honor of Dr. J. C. Sciutto, who reported the dinosaurian locality at the Ocho Hermanos Ranch where the holotype material was found.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales ‘Bernardino Rivadavia’

references.authors: Powell, J. E.
references.title: Epachthosaurus sciuttoi (gen. et sp. nov.), un dinosaurio sauropodo del Cretácico de Patagonia (Provincia de Chubut, Argentina) [Epachthosaurus sciuttoi (gen. et sp. nov.), a sauropod dinosaur from the Cretaceous of Patagonia (Chubut province, Argentina)]
references.journal: Actas del V Congreso Argentino de Paleontologia y Bioestratigrafia, Tucumán, Argentina

Epichirostenotes.etymology: From Greek epi- (above/upon, here meaning 'after in time') + Chirostenotes (the related oviraptorosaurian genus): 'above Chirostenotes', because it lived stratigraphically and temporally after Chirostenotes.
Epichirostenotes.description: Epichirostenotes is a genus of oviraptorosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous. Epichirostenotes is known from an incomplete skeleton found in 1923 at the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, in strata dated to about 72 million years ago. It was first named by Robert M. Sullivan, Steven E. Jasinski and Mark P.A. van Tomme in 2011 and the type species is Epichirostenotes curriei. Its holotype, ROM 43250, had been assigned to Chirostenotes pergracilis by Hans-Dieter Sues in 1997.

species.name: Epichirostenotes curriei
species.etymology: Named in honor of Philip J. Currie for his scholarly work on Late Cretaceous theropod dinosaurs.

references.authors: Sullivan, R. M.; Jasinski, S. E.; M. P. A. Van Tomme
references.title: A new caenagnathid Ojoraptorsaurus boerei, n. gen., n. sp. (Dinosauria, Oviraptorosauria), from the Upper Cretaceous Ojo Alamo Formation (Naashoibito Member), San Juan Basin, New Mexico
references.journal: Fossil Record 3. New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science Bulletin
references.publisher: New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science

Epidexipteryx.etymology: From Greek 'epi' meaning 'upon' or 'over', 'deixi' meaning 'display', and 'pteryx' meaning 'wing' or 'feather', in reference to its ornamental display feathers.
Epidexipteryx.description: Epidexipteryx is a genus of small maniraptoran dinosaurs, known from one fossil specimen in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing. Epidexipteryx represents the earliest known example of ornamental feathers in the fossil record.

species.name: Epidexipteryx hui
species.etymology: Named in memory of paleomammologist Hu Yaoming, using the Latinized genitive '-i' form of his surname.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
holotype.material: Nearly complete skeleton with feather impressions

references.authors: Zhang, Fucheng; Zhou, Zhonghe; Xu, Xing; Wang, Xiaolin; Sullivan, Corwin
references.title: A bizarre Jurassic maniraptoran from China with elongate ribbon-like feathers
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Equijubus.etymology: From Latin equus (horse) + juba (mane): 'horse mane', after the Mazong (horse mane) Mountain region in Gansu, China, where it was discovered.
Equijubus.description: Equijubus is a genus of herbivorous hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) of northwestern China.

species.name: Equijubus normani
species.etymology: Named for British palaeontologist David B. Norman, in honour of his contributions to ornithopod research.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: You, Hai-lu; Luo, Zhe-xi; Shubin, Neil H.; Witmer, Lawrence M.; Tang, Zhi-lu; Tang, Feng
references.title: The earliest-known duck-billed dinosaur from deposits of late Early Cretaceous age in northwest China and hadrosaur evolution

Erketu.etymology: Named after Erketü Tengri, a deity in Mongolian mythology, honouring the region where the dinosaur was found.
Erketu.description: Erketu is a genus of somphospondylan dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, roughly between 96 million and 89 million years ago. It is known from the Bayanshiree Formation of Mongolia, and its fossils were found between 2002 and 2003 during field expeditions. Erketu was first described in 2006 and later on in 2010 due to some cervicals that were left behind in the expedition. This genus represents the first sauropod described from the Bayanshiree Formation. The elongated cervical vertebrae indicate that it probably had the longest neck relative to its body size of any sauropod.

species.name: Erketu ellisoni
species.etymology: Named for Mick Ellison, senior principal paleoartist at the American Museum of Natural History and close friend of describer Mark Norell.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Ksepka, Daniel T.; Norell, Mark A.
references.title: Erketu Ellisoni, a Long-necked Sauropod from Bor Guvé (Dornogov Aimag, Mongolia)
references.publisher: American Museum of Natural History (BioOne sponsored)

Erliansaurus.etymology: From Erlian (the town of Erlian/Erenhot in Inner Mongolia, China, near the discovery site) + Greek sauros (lizard): 'Erlian lizard'.
Erliansaurus.description: Erliansaurus is a genus of therizinosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Nei Mongol, Iren Dabasu Formation.

species.name: Erliansaurus bellamanus
species.etymology: From Latin 'bellus' meaning 'beautiful' and 'manus' meaning 'hand', in reference to the exquisite preservation of the forelimb in the holotype.

holotype.institution: Long Hao Institute of Geology and Palaeontology

references.authors: Xu, X.; Zhang, Z.-H.; P. C. Sereno, X.-J. Zhao, X.-W. Kuang, J. Han, L. Tan
references.title: A new therizinosauroid (Dinosauria, Theropoda) from the Upper Cretaceous Iren Dabasu Formation of Nei Mongol

Erlikosaurus.etymology: Named after Erlik, the god of the underworld in Turkic and Mongolian mythology, + Greek sauros (lizard): 'Erlik's lizard'.
Erlikosaurus.description: Erlikosaurus is a genus of therizinosaurid that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period. The fossils, a skull and some post-cranial fragments, were found in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia in 1972, dating to around 96 and 89 million years ago. These remains were later described by Altangerel Perle and Rinchen Barsbold in 1980, naming the new genus and species Erlikosaurus andrewsi. It represents the second therizinosaur taxon from this formation (after Segnosaurus), with the most complete skull among members of this peculiar family of dinosaurs.

species.name: Erlikosaurus andrewsi
species.etymology: Named for Roy Chapman Andrews, the American paleontologist who led the American Asiatic Expeditions to Central Asia from 1922 to 1930.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Barsbold, R.; Perle, A.
references.title: Segnosauria, a new infraorder of carnivorous dinosaurs

Erythrovenator.etymology: From Greek erythros (ερυθρός), 'red', + Latin venator, 'hunter'; means 'red hunter', likely referring to the red mudstone in which the fossil was found
Erythrovenator.description: Erythrovenator is a genus of basal theropod dinosaurs from the Late Triassic of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. The genus contains a single species, Erythrovenator jacuiensis.

species.name: Erythrovenator jacuiensis
species.etymology: Named for the Jacuí River in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, near where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Laboratório de Estratigrafia e Paleobiologia, Universidade Federal de Santa Maria

references.journal: Journal of South American Earth Sciences

Eshanosaurus.etymology: Named for Eshan County in Yunnan Province, China, where the fossil was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Eshanosaurus.description: Eshanosaurus is a genus of a dinosaur from the early Jurassic Period. It is known only from a fossil partial lower jawbone, found in China. It may be a therizinosaurian, and if so the earliest known coelurosaur.

species.name: Eshanosaurus deguchiianus
species.etymology: Named for Hikaru Deguchi, who convinced describer Xu Xing that he should study dinosaurs.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
holotype.material: Partial lower jaw

references.authors: Xu, Xing; Zhao, Xijin; Clark, James M.
references.title: A new therizinosaur from the Lower Jurassic lower Lufeng Formation of Yunnan, China

Eucamerotus.etymology: From Greek eu- (well/good) + kamara (chamber/vault) + -otos (pertaining to): 'well-chambered', referring to the hollow pneumatic cavities in its vertebrae.
Eucamerotus.description: Eucamerotus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Wessex Formation (Wealden) of the Isle of Wight, England. The type specimen, part of a vertebra (one of the bones of the spine), was discovered in the autumn of 1869 by John Hulke. After confirming its point of origin with the Rev. William Fox, Hulke presented his find to the Geological Society of London in 1870. Two years later, he assigned to it the name Eucamerotus, though did not provide a species name. Eucamerotus was subsequently treated as a junior synonym of two existing sauropods, Pelorosaurus and Ornithopsis. In 1995, William T. Blows gave a species name, creating the combination Eucamerotus foxi. While the validity of the genus has continued to be questioned, a 2011 publication found it to be a valid genus of titanosauriform. Comparisons with the fossils of other macronarians suggests it may have reached up to 15 m (49 ft) in length.

species.name: Eucamerotus foxi
species.etymology: Named for the Rev. William Fox, the clergyman who identified the origin of the holotype vertebra from the Isle of Wight.

references.authors: Marsh, O. C.
references.title: Classification of the Dinosauria

Eucnemesaurus.etymology: From Greek eu- (good/well) + kneme (tibia/shin) + sauros (lizard): 'good tibia lizard', referring to its robust tibiae.
Eucnemesaurus.description: Eucnemesaurus is a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur genus usually considered to be a synonym of Euskelosaurus. Recent study by Yates (2006), however, indicates that it is valid and the same animal as putative "giant herrerasaurid" Aliwalia.

synonyms.name: Aliwalia
synonyms.reason: Tentatively treated as a junior synonym of Eucnemesaurus; very recent (2026) research suggests Aliwalia may be a distinct genus, pending broader confirmation.

species.name: Eucnemesaurus fortis
species.etymology: From Latin 'fortis' meaning 'strong', reflecting the robust nature of the described material.

holotype.institution: Ditsong National Museum of Natural History

references.authors: Van Hoepen, E. C. N.
references.title: Contributions to the knowledge of the reptiles of the Karroo Formation. 6. Further dinosaurian material in the Transvaal Museum

Euhelopus.etymology: From Greek 'helos' meaning 'swamp' and Greek 'pous' meaning 'foot', giving 'true marsh-foot' (prefix 'eu-' meaning 'true' was added by Romer in 1956 when renaming from Helopus); the name refers to the marshy area of the finds and to Swedish swamp shoes (truga) which Wiman said resembled the animal's wide feet.
Euhelopus.description: Euhelopus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived between 143 and 133 million years ago during the Berriasian and Valanginian ages of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Shandong Province in China. It was a large quadrupedal herbivore. Like sauropods such as brachiosaurids and titanosaurs, Euhelopus had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs. This discovery was paleontologically significant because it represented the first dinosaur scientifically investigated from China — seen in 1913, rediscovered in 1922, excavated in 1923, and studied by T'an during the same year.

synonyms.name: Helopus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Helopus (Aves).

species.name: Euhelopus zdanskyi
species.etymology: Named for Otto Zdansky, the Austrian student who excavated the holotype and a second skeleton from Shandong Province, China, in 1923.

Euoplocephalus.etymology: From Greek 'eu' meaning 'well', 'hoplon' meaning 'weapon' or 'armor', and 'kephale' meaning 'head', meaning 'well-armored head'.
Euoplocephalus.description: Euoplocephalus is a genus of large herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaurs, living during the Late Cretaceous of Canada. It has only one named species, Euoplocephalus tutus.

synonyms.name: Stereocephalus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Stereocephalus (Insecta).

species.name: Euoplocephalus tutus
species.etymology: From Latin 'tutus' meaning 'safely protected', referring to the extensive bony armour covering the animal's body.

references.authors: Lambe, L. M.
references.title: Note on the parietal crest of Centrosaurus apertus and a proposed new generic name for Stereocephalus tutus

Europasaurus.etymology: From Europa (Europe, named after the Phoenician princess in Greek mythology) + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'Europe lizard', referring to its discovery in Germany
Europasaurus.description: Europasaurus is a genus of dwarf sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Süntel Formation of Lower Saxony, Germany. The type and only species, Europasaurus holgeri, is notable for being among the smallest known adult sauropods, likely the result of insular dwarfism on the Late Jurassic European archipelago.

species.name: Europasaurus holgeri
species.etymology: Named for Holger Lüdtke, the private fossil collector who discovered the first sauropod tooth at the Langenberg quarry in Germany in 1998.

holotype.material: Partial skeleton including vertebrae, limb bones

references.authors: Sander, P. M.; Mateus, O.; T. Laven, N. Knótschke
references.title: Bone histology indicates insular dwarfism in a new Late Jurassic sauropod dinosaur

Europatitan.etymology: From 'Europa' (Europe), referring to its discovery in Iberia, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant', meaning 'European giant'.
Europatitan.description: Europatitan is an extinct genus of somphospondylan sauropod from the Early Cretaceous Castrillo de la Reina Formation of Iberia, known from a relatively complete specimen discovered in the early 2000s. It contains a single species: the type species, Europatitan eastwoodi.

species.name: Europatitan eastwoodi
species.etymology: Named for actor and director Clint Eastwood, whose film The Good, the Bad and the Ugly was shot near Salas de los Infantes, Spain, close to where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Museo de Dinosaurios de Salas de los Infantes
holotype.material: Disarticulated carcass cataloged as MDS-OTII,1 through MDS-OTII-32

Europelta.etymology: From Europa (Europe, where it was found) + Greek pelte (shield): 'Europe's shield', reflecting its nodosaurid armour and European origin.
Europelta.description: Europelta is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from Spain that lived during the Early Cretaceous (early Albian stage, ~113.0 Ma) in what is now the lower Escucha Formation of the Teruel Province. The type and only species, Europelta carbonensis, is known from two associated partial skeletons, and represents the most complete ankylosaur known from Europe. Europelta was named in 2013 by James I. Kirkland and colleagues. Europelta has an estimated length of 5 metres (16 feet) and weight of 1.3 tonnes (2,866 lbs), making it the largest member of the clade Struthiosaurini.

species.name: Europelta carbonensis
species.etymology: From Latin 'carbo' meaning 'coal', honouring the Sociedad Anónima Minera Catalano-Aragonesa (SAMCA Group) for providing access to the fossil locality in the open-pit Santa María coal mine.

Eustreptospondylus.etymology: From Ancient Greek eu- (well) + streptos (twisted) + spondylos (vertebra): 'well-twisted vertebra', referring to the morphology of its vertebrae.
Eustreptospondylus.description: Eustreptospondylus is an extinct genus of megalosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Callovian and Oxfordian stages of the Jurassic period (some time between 166 and 154 million years ago) in southern England, at a time when Europe was a series of scattered islands due to tectonic movement that raised the sea-bed and flooded the lowland.

species.name: Eustreptospondylus oxoniensis
species.etymology: Named for Oxford, England (Latin 'Oxonia'), the city near which the holotype skeleton was discovered.

holotype.institution: Oxford University Museum of Natural History

Falcarius.etymology: From Latin falcarius (sickle cutter or scythe-bearer): 'sickle cutter', likely alluding to its therizinosaur affinities and large curved claws.
Falcarius.description: Falcarius is a genus of primitive therizinosaur dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now North America. Its remains were first collected in the Cedar Mountain Formation in 1999, with subsequent findings made during the 2000s. The genus is known from multiple specimens ranging from immature to fully-grown individuals.

species.name: Falcarius utahensis
species.etymology: Named for Utah, the US state where the holotype and hundreds of associated specimens were recovered from the Cedar Mountain Formation.

Ferganasaurus.etymology: From Fergana (the Fergana Valley in Kyrgyzstan, where it was found) + Greek sauros (lizard): 'Fergana Valley lizard'.
Ferganasaurus.description: Ferganasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in the Balabansai Formation of Kyrgyzstan, which dates to the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic. It was formally described in 2003 by Alifanov and Averianov as the type species Ferganasaurus verzilini. It is believed to be similar to Rhoetosaurus.

species.etymology: Named in honor of Prof. Nikita N. Verzilin, who found the holotype in 1966.

Ferganocephale.etymology: From Fergana (the Fergana Valley region of Central Asia, near Kyrgyzstan where it was found) + Greek kephale, 'head'; means 'Fergana head'
Ferganocephale.description: Ferganocephale is a dubious genus of neornithischian dinosaur. It was from the Middle Jurassic Balabansai Svita of Kyrgyzstan. The type and only species is F. adenticulatum.

Ferrisaurus.etymology: From Latin 'ferrum' meaning 'iron' and Ancient Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'iron lizard', referring to the discovery along a rail line.
Ferrisaurus.description: Ferrisaurus is a genus of leptoceratopsid ceratopsian dinosaur from the Sustut Basin (Tango Creek Formation) in British Columbia, Canada. The type and only species is Ferrisaurus sustutensis. It is the first non-avian dinosaur described from British Columbia.

species.name: Ferrisaurus sustutensis
species.etymology: Named for the Sustut Group and Sustut Basin in British Columbia, Canada, where the holotype was discovered.

Fona.etymology: From a word meaning 'the origin' in the language of the Ute people, whose ancestral territory includes Utah where the fossil was found; means 'the origin'
Fona.description: Fona is an extinct genus of thescelosaurine thescelosaurid ornithischian dinosaurs from the 'mid'-Cretaceous Cedar Mountain Formation (Mussentuchit Member) of Utah, United States. The genus contains a single species, F. herzogae, known from several partial skeletons and skulls. Based on anatomical similarities to the closely related and similarly aged Oryctodromeus, Fona was likely a semi-fossorial animal, likely spending a significant amount of time in underground burrows. It also represents the oldest known definitive thescelosaurine.

species.name: Fona herzogae
species.etymology: Named for Lisa Herzog, discoverer of the Mini Troll locality from which several Fona specimens are known, in recognition of her contributions to fossil conservation.

Foraminacephale.etymology: From Latin foramina (holes/openings) + Greek kephale (head): 'foramina head', referring to the many small pits (foramina) on the surface of its pachycephalosaurid dome.
Foraminacephale.description: Foraminacephale is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from Late Cretaceous (Campanian stage) deposits of Canada.

species.name: Foraminacephale brevis
species.etymology: From Latin 'brevis' meaning 'short', originally applied when the species was named Stegoceras brevis by Lawrence Lambe in 1918.

Foskeia.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'phōs' meaning 'light' and 'boskein' meaning 'to forage', referring to its small size and presumed herbivorous habits.
Foskeia.description: Foskeia is an extinct genus of rhabdodontomorph ornithopod dinosaurs known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian to Aptian ages) Castrillo de la Reina Formation of Spain. The genus contains a single species, Foskeia pelendonum, known from fossils of multiple individuals of different ontogenetic stages. Before its formal description, it had been nicknamed the "Vegagete ornithopod."

Fosterovenator.description: Fosterovenator is a genus of ceratosaur dinosaur known from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of Wyoming. Fostoria.etymology: Named for Robert Foster, the miner who discovered the bone bed at the Sheepyard opal field.
Fostoria.description: Fostoria is a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur from the Griman Creek Formation of New South Wales, Australia. The type and only species, Fostoria dhimbangunmal was described in 2019.

species.name: Fostoria dhimbangunmal
species.etymology: From 'dhimbangunmal' meaning 'sheep yard' in the Yuwaalaraay, Yuwaalayaay, and Gamilaraay languages of Australia.

Fruitadens.etymology: From Fruita (the city of Fruita, Colorado, USA, where fossils were found) + Latin dens (tooth): 'Fruita teeth'.
Fruitadens.description: Fruitadens is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur. The name means "Fruita teeth", in reference to Fruita, Colorado (USA), where its fossils were first found. It is known from partial skulls and skeletons from at least four individuals of differing biological ages, found in Tithonian (Late Jurassic) rocks of the Morrison Formation in Colorado. Fruitadens is one of the smallest known ornithischian dinosaur, with young adults estimated at 65 to 75 cm (26 to 30 in) in length and 0.5 to 0.75 kg (1.1 to 1.7 lb) in weight. It is interpreted as an omnivore and represents one of the latest-surviving heterodontosaurids.

species.etymology: Named for Paul Haaga Jr., Heather Haaga, Blythe Haaga, Paul Haaga III, and Catalina Haaga, in recognition of their support for the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County.

Fujianvenator.etymology: From Fujian (Fujian Province, China, where it was discovered) + Latin venator (hunter): 'Fujian hunter'.
Fujianvenator.description: Fujianvenator is an extinct genus of anchiornithid theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Nanyuan Formation of Fujian Province, China. The genus contains a single species, F. prodigiosus, known from a partial articulated skeleton. It is suggested to possibly have had a terrestrial or wading lifestyle.

Fukuiraptor.etymology: From Fukui (Fukui Prefecture, Japan, where it was found) + Latin raptor (thief/robber): 'thief of Fukui'.
Fukuiraptor.description: Fukuiraptor is a genus of medium-sized megaraptoran theropod dinosaur of the Early Cretaceous epoch (either Barremian or Aptian) that lived in what is now Japan. Fukuiraptor is known from the Kitadani Formation and possibly also the Sebayashi Formation. Fukuiraptor may have been one of the basalmost members of Megaraptora, or a sister taxon to Australovenator.

Fukuisaurus.description: Fukuisaurus is a genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Japan. The type species is Fukuisaurus tetoriensis, which was named and described in 2003.

species.name: Fukuisaurus tetoriensis

Fukuititan.etymology: From Fukui (Fukui Prefecture, Japan, where it was found) + Greek titan (giant): 'giant from Fukui prefecture'.
Fukuititan.description: Fukuititan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous (either Barremian or Aptian age) in the Kitadani Formation in what is now Japan. The genus contains a single species, Fukuititan nipponensis. The discovery of Fukuititan shed light on Japanese titanosauriforms, which are generally very poorly-known.

species.name: Fukuititan nipponensis
species.etymology: From Latin 'nipponensis' meaning 'from Japan', after Nippon, a name for Japan, where the holotype was discovered.

Fukuivenator.etymology: From Fukui (Fukui Prefecture, Japan, where it was found) + Latin venator (hunter): 'hunter of Fukui Prefecture'.
Fukuivenator.description: Fukuivenator is an extinct genus of maniraptoran theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Kitadani Formation of Japan.

species.etymology: From Latin 'paradoxus' meaning 'paradoxical', referring to the unusual combination of primitive and advanced traits exhibited by the species.

Fulengia.etymology: An anagram of the genus name Lufengosaurus, itself named for the Lufeng Formation of China where the fossils were found.
Fulengia.description: Fulengia is a dubious genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic Lufeng Formation of China. The type species, F. youngi, was described by Carroll and Galton in 1977. It is a nomen dubium and may be the same animal as Lufengosaurus (from which it is anagramized). It was originally thought to be a lizard.

Fulgurotherium.description: Fulgurotherium is a dubious genus of ornithischian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) Griman Creek Formation. It lived in what is now Australia.

Furcatoceratops.etymology: Forked horned face; from Latin furcatus (forked) and Greek keras (horn) and ops (face)
Furcatoceratops.description: Furcatoceratops is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Judith River Formation of Montana. The type species is Furcatoceratops elucidans.

Fushanosaurus.etymology: Fushan lizard; named after the Fushan Museum in China where its remains are stored, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Fushanosaurus.description: Fushanosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Shishugou Formation from Xinjiang Province in China. The type and only species is Fushanosaurus qitaiensis (Chinese: 奇台傅山龙; pinyin: Qítái Fùshānlóng). It is solely known from the holotype specimen FH000101, a complete right femur.

Fusuisaurus.etymology: From Fusui (the county in Guangxi, China where it was discovered) + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'Fusui lizard'
Fusuisaurus.description: Fusuisaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China. Fragmentary postcranial remains of this animal have been discovered in 2001 in the Xinlong Formation of Guangxi, and consist of the left ilium, left pubis, anterior caudals, most of the dorsal ribs, and distal end of the left femur. This sauropod has been described as a basal titanosauriform. The type species is F. zhaoi, named in honour of Chinese paleontologist Zhao Xijin.

Futalognkosaurus.etymology: Giant chief lizard; from the Mapuche words futa (giant) and lognko (chief), combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Futalognkosaurus.description: Futalognkosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur. The herbivorous Futalognkosaurus lived approximately 93.5 to 85.8 million years ago in the Portezuelo Formation, in what is now Argentina, of the Coniacian stage of the late Cretaceous Period. The fish and fossilized leaf debris on the site, together with other dinosaur remains, suggest a warm tropical climate in Patagonia during this period.

Fylax.description: Fylax is a genus of hadrosauroid ornithopod from the Late Cretaceous Figuerola Formation of Spain. The genus contains a single species, Fylax thyrakolasus, known from a nearly complete left dentary.

The type species is known from one of the well-preserved diplodocid fossils, a nearly complete skeleton with an associated skull.

Galleonosaurus.description: Galleonosaurus is a genus of basal ornithopod dinosaur from the Wonthaggi Formation of the Gippsland region of Victoria, Australia. The type and only species is Galleonosaurus dorisae.

Gallimimus.etymology: Chicken mimic; from Latin gallus (chicken) and mimus (mimic), referring to similarities between its neck vertebrae and those of Galliformes
Gallimimus.description: Gallimimus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous period. Several fossils in various stages of growth were discovered by Polish-Mongolian expeditions in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia during the 1960s; a large skeleton discovered in this region was made the holotype specimen of the new genus and species Gallimimus bullatus in 1972. The generic name means "chicken mimic", referring to the similarities between its neck vertebrae and those of the Galliformes. The specific name is derived from bulla, a golden capsule worn by Roman youth, in reference to a bulbous structure at the base of the skull of Gallimimus. At the time it was named, the fossils of Gallimimus represented the most complete and best preserved ornithomimid ("ostrich dinosaur") material yet discovered, and the genus remains one of the best known members of the group.

Galvesaurus.description: Galvesaurus, or Galveosaurus (meaning "Galve lizard"), is a genus of brachiosaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic period. Fossils of the only known species, G. herreroi, were found in Galve, Spain, hence its generic name. The specific name herreroi honours the discoverer, José María Herrero. Some researchers suggest that the taxon might represent a junior synonym of the Portuguese genus Lusotitan.

Gandititan.etymology: Combines 'Gan' referencing Ganzhou City, the Chinese word 'di' meaning 'Earth' (also the first syllable of 'dizhi', meaning 'geology'), and 'titan' referencing the pre-Olympian giants of Greek mythology; the specific name cavocaudatus combines Latin 'cavum' (cavity) and 'cauda' (tail), alluding to the caudal vertebrae morphology.
Gandititan.description: Gandititan is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Zhoutian Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, G. cavocaudatus, known from a partial skeleton.

species.name: Gandititan cavocaudatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'cavum' meaning 'cavity' and 'cauda' meaning 'tail', alluding to the distinctive pattern of cavities seen in the caudal vertebrae.

Gannansaurus.etymology: Gannan lizard; named after the Gannan region (Ganzhou Basin) of Jiangxi Province, China, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Gannansaurus.description: Gannansaurus is an extinct genus of somphospondylan sauropod dinosaur known from the latest Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of Ganzhou Basin, Jiangxi Province of southern China. It is known from specimen GMNH F10001 which consists of a single, nearly complete dorsal vertebra and a mid-caudal vertebra. Gannansaurus was first named by Lü Junchang, Yi Laiping, Zhong Hui and Wei Xuefang in 2013 and the type species is Gannansaurus sinensis. Gannansaurus shares some characters with Euhelopus, indicating that it is more closely related to it rather than to other titanosauriforms.

species.name: Gannansaurus sinensis
species.etymology: From Latin 'sinensis' meaning 'of China', referring to the country where the specimens were found.

Ganzhousaurus.etymology: Ganzhou lizard; named after Ganzhou City in Jiangxi Province, China, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Ganzhousaurus.description: Ganzhousaurus is an extinct genus of oviraptorid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of Nankang County, Ganzhou City of Jiangxi Province, southern China. It was found in a Maastrichtian deposit and contains a single species, Ganzhousaurus nankangensis. It is distinguished by a combination of primitive and derived features.

Gargoyleosaurus.etymology: Gargoyle lizard; named for its gargoyle-like appearance, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Gargoyleosaurus.description: Gargoyleosaurus is one of the earliest ankylosaurs known from reasonably complete fossil remains. Garrigatitan.etymology: Garrigue giant; named after garrigue, the type of scrubland habitat in the region of France where it was found, combined with Titan from Greek mythology
Garrigatitan.description: Garrigatitan is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of the Grès à Reptiles Formation in France. The genus contains a single species, Garrigatitan meridionalis.

Garudimimus.etymology: Garuda mimic; named after Garuda, the divine bird from Hindu and Buddhist mythology, combined with Latin mimus (mimic)
Garudimimus.description: Garudimimus is a genus of ornithomimosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous. The genus is known from a single specimen found in 1981 by a Soviet-Mongolian paleontological expedition in the Bayanshiree Formation and formally described in the same year by Rinchen Barsbold; the only species is Garudimimus brevipes. Several interpretations about the anatomical traits of Garudimimus were made in posterior examinations of the specimen, but most of them were criticized during its comprehensive redescription in 2005. Extensive undescribed ornithomimosaur remains at the type locality of Garudimimus may represent additional specimens of the genus.

species.name: Garudimimus brevipes
species.etymology: From Latin 'brevis' meaning 'short' and 'pes' meaning 'foot', referring to the short metatarsus of the holotype specimen.

Garumbatitan.etymology: Garumba giant; named after the Garumba river near the discovery site in Spain, combined with Titan from Greek mythology
Garumbatitan.description: Garumbatitan is an extinct genus of somphospondylan sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Arcillas de Morella Formation of Spain. The genus contains a single species, G. morellensis, known from multiple partial skeletons.

species.name: Garumbatitan morellensis
species.etymology: Named for the Arcillas de Morella Formation and the nearby town of Morella in Castelló, Spain, where some of the first Spanish dinosaur remains were discovered.

Gasosaurus.etymology: From English 'gasoline' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', named for the gasoline company whose workers discovered the fossils.
Gasosaurus.description: Gasosaurus is a genus of tetanuran theropod that lived approximately 171.6 to 161.2 million years ago during the middle of the Jurassic Period. The name "Gasosaurus" is derived from the English "gasoline" and the Greek σαῦρος (sauros) ("lizard / generic reptile"). Only one species is currently recognised, G. constructus, from which the specific name honours the gasoline company that found the Dashanpu fossil quarry in Sichuan Province, China, now named as the Lower Shaximiao Formation.

species.name: Gasosaurus constructus
species.etymology: From Latin 'constructus' meaning 'built' or 'constructed', honoring the gas facility construction project during which the fossils were discovered in Sichuan Province, China.

Gasparinisaura.etymology: Gasparini's lizard; named in honor of Argentine palaeontologist Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Gasparinisaura.description: Gasparinisaura is a genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous. The first fossils of Gasparinisaura were found in 1992 near Cinco Saltos in Río Negro Province, Argentina. The type species, Gasparinisaura cincosaltensis, was named and described in 1996 by Rodolfo Coria and Leonardo Salgado. The generic name honors Argentine palaeontologist Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini. The specific name refers to Cinco Saltos.

Gastonia.description: Gastonia is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of North America, around 139 to 125.77 million years ago. It is often considered a nodosaurid closely related to Polacanthus. Gastonia has a sacral shield and large shoulder spikes.

Geminiraptor.etymology: Twin seizer; from Latin gemini (twins) and raptor (seizer), referring to the twin geologists Marina and Celina Suarez who discovered the fossil site
Geminiraptor.description: Geminiraptor is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Early Cretaceous period. Geminiraptor was a small, ground-dwelling bipedal carnivorous paravian. The type species of Geminiraptor is G. suarezarum.

Genusaurus.etymology: Knee lizard; from Latin genu (knee) and Greek sauros (lizard), referring to distinctive features of the knee region
Genusaurus.description: Genusaurus is a genus of abelisaurid theropod from the Early Cretaceous. Its fossils were found in France. Genusaurus is believed to have lived during the Albian stage, around 112-100 million years ago.

Genyodectes.etymology: Jaw bite; from Greek genys (jaw) and dektes (bite)
Genyodectes.description: Genyodectes and dektes ("bite")) is a genus of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous (Aptian) of South America. The holotype material (MLP 26–39, Museo de La Plata, La Plata, Argentina) was collected from the Cerro Barcino Formation, Cañadón Grande, Departamento Paso de Indios in the Chubut Province of Argentina and consists of an incomplete snout, including the premaxillae, portions of both maxillas, the right and left dentary, many teeth, a fragment of the left splenial, and parts of the supradentaries. These elements are generally poorly preserved and some are in articulation. The premaxilla of Genyodectes possesses relatively large and protruding teeth, similar to those of Ceratosaurus. The specific name, serus, means "late". In 2016 it was estimated to be 6.25 meters (20.5 ft) in length and 790 kg (1,740 lb) in weight.

Geranosaurus.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'geranos' meaning 'crane' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', giving 'crane lizard'; the name refers to the bird-like limb bones, while the specific name atavus is Latin for 'ancestor', referencing its position as an early ornithischian.
Geranosaurus.description: Geranosaurus is a genus of heterodontosaurid ornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic, between 191.1 and 187.5 million years ago. It is known from a single species, G. atavus, that was named in 1911 by Robert Broom for partial jaws found during road-cutting in South Africa. The genus name is likely derived from the word for "crane" in reference to the bird-like limb bones, while the species name means "ancestor" likely in reference to its position as an early ornithischian. The limited material and poor preservation of Geranosaurus have rendered it difficult to diagnose, with authors accepting it as a dubious name though differentiable from its relative Heterodontosaurus, the only other heterodontosaurid known from the Clarens Formation.

species.name: Geranosaurus atavus
species.etymology: From Latin 'atavus' meaning 'ancestor', likely referencing its position as one of the earliest known ornithischian dinosaurs.

Gideonmantellia.etymology: Named after Gideon Mantell, the 19th-century English geologist and paleontologist who first described Iguanodon; the -ia suffix is a Latinized honorific form
Gideonmantellia.description: Gideonmantellia is an extinct genus of basal ornithopod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian stage) Camarillas Formation of Galve, Province of Teruel, Spain. It contains a single species, Gideonmantellia amosanjuanae.

Giganotosaurus.etymology: From Greek gigas/gigantos, 'giant', + Greek notos, 'south/southern', + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'giant southern lizard', referring to its enormous size and South American origin
Giganotosaurus.description: Giganotosaurus is a genus of large theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Argentina, during the early Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 99.6 to 95 million years ago. The holotype specimen was discovered in the Candeleros Formation of Patagonia in 1993 and is almost 70% complete. The animal was named Giganotosaurus carolinii in 1995; the genus name translates to "giant southern lizard", and the specific name honors the discoverer, Ruben Carolini. A dentary bone, a tooth, and some tracks, discovered before the holotype, were later assigned to this animal. The genus attracted much interest and became part of a scientific debate about the maximum sizes of theropod dinosaurs.

Gigantoraptor.description: Gigantoraptor is a genus of large oviraptorosaurian dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period. It is known from the Iren Dabasu Formation of Inner Mongolia, where the first remains were found in 2005.

Gigantspinosaurus.etymology: From Latin gigas/giganteus, 'enormous', + Latin spina, 'spine', + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'giant-spined lizard', referring to its massive shoulder spines
Gigantspinosaurus.description: Gigantspinosaurus is a genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) Upper Shaximiao Formation of China. The type species is Gigantspinosaurus sichuanensis. It was a moderately sized member of the group, measuring up to 4.2 metres (14 ft) in length.

Gilmoreosaurus.etymology: Charles Whitney Gilmore's lizard; named in honor of American paleontologist Charles Whitney Gilmore, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Gilmoreosaurus.description: Gilmoreosaurus is a genus of hadrosauromorphan dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Asia. The type species is Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis, known from the Iren Dabasu Formation of Inner Mongolia, dating to 96 million years ago. Additional specimens have been described as distinct species, including G. atavus from the Khodzhakul Formation of Uzbekistan, and G. arkhangelskyi from the Bissekty Formation, also of Uzbekistan. However, these are based on very fragmentary remains, and their classification is dubious. An additional species, G. kysylkumense, also from the Bissekty Formation, is sometimes included, though it has also been referred to the related genus Bactrosaurus.

Giraffatitan.etymology: Titanic giraffe; from the animal name giraffe and Greek Titan, referring to its enormous size and giraffe-like long neck
Giraffatitan.description: Giraffatitan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the late Jurassic Period (Kimmeridgian–Tithonian stages) in what is now Lindi Region, Tanzania. Only one species is known, G. brancai, named in honor of German paleontologist Wilhelm von Branca, who was a driving force behind the expedition that discovered it in the Tendaguru Formation. Giraffatitan brancai was originally described by German paleontologist Werner Janensch as a species of the North American sauropod Brachiosaurus from the Morrison Formation, as Brachiosaurus brancai. Recent research shows that the differences between the type species of Brachiosaurus and the Tendaguru material are so large that the African material should be placed in a separate genus.

Glacialisaurus.etymology: From Latin glacialis, 'icy' or 'frozen', + Greek sauros, 'lizard'; means 'icy lizard' or 'frozen lizard', referring to its discovery in Antarctica
Glacialisaurus.description: Glacialisaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic period of Antarctica. It is known from two specimens; the holotype (name-bearing specimen), a partial tarsus (ankle) and metatarsus, and a partial left femur (thigh bone). The fossils were collected by a team led by paleontologist William R. Hammer during a 1990–91 field expedition to the central region of the Transantarctic Mountains. They come from sedimentary rocks of the Hanson Formation and date to the Pliensbachian stage of the Early Jurassic, around 186 to 182 million years ago.

Glishades.etymology: Concealed in mud; from Latin glis (mud) and Greek Hades (lord of the underworld, meaning unseen), referring to being found in sedimentary strata
Glishades.description: Glishades is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous in North America. It is based on AMNH 27414, two partial premaxillae discovered in the Upper Cretaceous rocks of the upper Two Medicine Formation in Montana, dated to about 74.5 million years ago. Cladistic analysis conducted by Prieto-Márquez suggests that Glishades is a non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroid, probably a sister taxon to Bactrosaurus johnsoni. The type species is Glishades ericksoni. In 2012, Campione et al. suggest the holotype specimen of Glishades might actually be an indeterminate juvenile saurolophine hadrosaurid and consider it to be a nomen dubium.

Glyptodontopelta.description: Glyptodontopelta is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from New Mexico that lived during the Late Cretaceous (lower to upper Maastrichtian, 69 to 66 Ma) in what is now the Naashoibito member of the Ojo Alamo Formation. The type and only species, Glyptodontopelta mimus, is known from numerous specimens that consist of osteoderms, a dentary, supraorbital and bone fragments. It was named in 2000 by Tracy Ford. Edmontonia australis is a junior synonym of Glyptodontopelta.

Gnathovorax.etymology: From Greek gnathos (jaw) and Latin vorax (voracious, devouring); meaning 'devouring jaw', referring to its predatory nature
Gnathovorax.description: Gnathovorax is a genus of herrerasaurid saurischian dinosaur from the Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. The type and only species is Gnathovorax cabreirai, described by Pacheco et al. in 2019. The type specimen comprises a mostly complete and well-preserved articulated skeleton (considered one of the best herrerasaurid skeletons ever discovered), which fossilized in close association with rhynchosaur and cynodont remains. The discovery of this superb specimen has shed light onto poorly understood aspects of herrerasaurid anatomy such as endocranial soft tissues.

Gobihadros.etymology: From the Gobi Desert (where it was found) combined with hadros (Greek for 'bulky' or 'stout'), the root of Hadrosauridae; meaning 'Gobi hadrosaur'
Gobihadros.description: Gobihadros is a genus of basal hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now the Bayanshiree Formation (dated to the Cenomanian-Santonian) of Mongolia. It contains only the type species Gobihadros mongoliensis, which has an estimated length of 7.5 m (25 ft).

species.name: Gobihadros mongoliensis
species.etymology: Named for Mongolia, reflecting the provenance of the holotype from the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia.

Gobiraptor.etymology: From the Gobi Desert (where it was found) combined with Latin raptor (thief, plunderer); meaning 'Gobi thief'
Gobiraptor.description: Gobiraptor is a genus of oviraptorid maniraptoran dinosaur from the Maastrichtian-aged Nemegt Formation of Mongolia. The type and only species is Gobiraptor minutus, known from a single incomplete specimen—the holotype MPC-D 102/111. It has been found not to be closely related to the other oviraptorids it shared its environment with.

species.name: Gobiraptor minutus

Gobisaurus.etymology: From the Gobi Desert (where it was found) combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'Gobi lizard'
Gobisaurus.description: Gobisaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous basal ankylosaurid ankylosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of China (Nei Mongol Zizhiqu). The genus is monotypic, containing only the species Gobisaurus domoculus.

species.name: Gobisaurus domoculus
species.etymology: From Latin 'domoculus' meaning 'hidden from view', referring to the specimen having been largely overlooked for three decades after its discovery.

Gobititan.etymology: Named for the Gobi Desert region where the fossils were found, combined with the Titans of Greek mythology, in reference to the animal's large body size.
Gobititan.description: Gobititan is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Aptian faunal stage of the Early Cretaceous. The name of this genus is derived from the Gobi Desert region and the Titans of Greek mythology, which is a reference to its large body size. The specific name shenzhouensis, is derived from "Shenzhou", an ancient name for China.

Gobivenator.etymology: From the Gobi Desert (where it was found) combined with Latin venator (hunter); meaning 'Gobi hunter'
Gobivenator.description: Gobivenator is an extinct genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur known from the late Campanian Djadokhta Formation of central Gobi Desert, Mongolia. It contains a single species, Gobivenator mongoliensis. G. mongoliensis is known from a single individual, which represents the most complete specimen of a Late Cretaceous troodontid currently known.

Gojirasaurus.description: Gojirasaurus is a genus of coelophysoid theropod dinosaur named after the giant monster movie character Godzilla. It lived in the Late Triassic Period, containing a single known species, Gojirasaurus quayi.

Gondwanatitan.etymology: Gondwana Titan; named after Gondwana, the ancient supercontinent, combined with Titan from Greek mythology
Gondwanatitan.description: Gondwanatitan was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur. Gondwanatitan was found in Brazil, at the time part of the southern supercontinent Gondwana, in the late Cretaceous Period (70 mya). Like some other sauropods, Gondwanatitan was tall and ate tough shoots and leaves from the tops of trees. Its closest relative was Aeolosaurus. The type species is Gondwanatitan faustoi, formally described by Kellner and de Azevedo in 1999.

Gongbusaurus.etymology: Named for the imperial Chinese ministry of public works (gong bu), honouring the Tang dynasty poet Du Fu who served in that ministry after 760 AD as a 'junior consultant' (shi yi), combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Gongbusaurus.description: Gongbusaurus is a genus of ornithischian, perhaps ornithopod, dinosaur that lived between about 160 and 157 million years ago, in the Late Jurassic period. A small herbivore, it is very poorly known. Two species have been assigned to it, but as the original name is based on teeth, there is no concrete evidence to connect the two species. Its fossils have been found in China.

species.etymology: Named for the rank of shi yi ('junior consultant') held by the Tang dynasty poet Du Fu while working in Sichuan for the imperial ministry of public works; the epithet also puns on a secondary meaning of 'register of lost objects', alluding to the teeth being found separately among the collected bones.

Gongpoquansaurus.etymology: Gongpoquan reptile; named after Gongpoquan in the Mazongshan area of Gansu Province, China, where the specimen was collected
Gongpoquansaurus.description: Gongpoquansaurus is an extinct genus of basal hadrosauroid dinosaur that was not formally named until 2014, while the name was a nomen nudum for many years previously. It is known from IVPP V.11333, a partial skull and postcranial skeleton. It was collected in 1992 at locality IVPP 9208–21, from the Albian Zhonggou Formation (Xinminpu Group), in Mazongshan, Gansu Province, China. The specimen was first described and named by Lü Junchang in 1997 as the third species of Probactrosaurus, Probactrosaurus mazongshanensis. Following its description, several studies found it to be less derived than the type species of Probactrosaurus in relation to Hadrosauridae. In 2014, the species was formally redescribed, and the describers erected Gongpoquansaurus.

species.name: Gongpoquansaurus mazongshanensis

Gongxianosaurus.etymology: Named for Gongxian County in Sichuan Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Gongxianosaurus.description: Gongxianosaurus is a genus of basal sauropod dinosaur from the early Jurassic Period (Sinemurian-Pliensbachian stage). The only species is Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis. Based on four fragmentary to complete specimens found in the Ziliujing Formation, China (Sichuan Province), it is one of the most completely known early sauropods. The skeleton is known in large part, missing both the hand and the majority of the skull. Gongxianosaurus was firstly named and described in a short note published in 1998; however, a comprehensive description has yet to be published. Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis was named for the place it was found, near the village Shibei in Gong County (珙县; Pinyin: Gǒng Xiàn).

synonyms.reason: Treated as a synonym of Gongxianosaurus pending a formal description.

species.name: Gongxianosaurus shibeiensis
species.etymology: Named for the village of Shibei in Gong County, Sichuan Province, China, near where the fossils were found.

Gonkoken.etymology: Similar to a wild duck or swan; from the Aonikenk (Tehuelche) language of Patagonia
Gonkoken.description: Gonkoken is an extinct genus of hadrosauroid ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Dorotea Formation of Chilean Patagonia. The genus contains a single species, Gonkoken nanoi, known from disarticulated bones of multiple individuals.

Gorgosaurus.etymology: From Greek gorgos (dreadful, fierce) and sauros (lizard); meaning 'dreadful lizard'
Gorgosaurus.description: Gorgosaurus is a genus of tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in western North America during the Late Cretaceous Period (Campanian), between about 76.5 and 75 million years ago. Fossil remains have been found in the Canadian province of Alberta and the U.S. state of Montana. Paleontologists recognize only the type species, G. libratus, although other species have been erroneously referred to the genus.

species.name: Gorgosaurus libratus
species.etymology: From Latin 'libratus', the past participle of 'librare' meaning 'to balance', likely referring to the animal's balanced build.

Goyocephale.etymology: From Mongolian goyo (decorated, ornate) and Ancient Greek kephale (head); meaning 'decorated head'
Goyocephale.description: Goyocephale is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurian ornithischian that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous about 76 million years ago. It was first described in 1982 by Altangerel Perle, Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska for a disarticulated skeleton with most of a skull, part of the forelimb and hindlimb, some of the pelvic girdle, and some vertebrae. Perle et al. named the remains Goyocephale lattimorei, from the Mongolian гоё (goyo), meaning "decorated", and the Ancient Greek κεφαλή (kephale), for head. The species name honours Owen Lattimore.

Graciliraptor.description: Graciliraptor is a genus of microraptorian dromaeosaurid dinosaur from the early Cretaceous Period. Its fossil, holotype IVPP V 13474, was found in Beipiao, Liaoning Province, China. The type species is Graciliraptor lujiatunensis, named and described in 2004 by Xu Xing and Wang Xiaoling. The generic name is derived from Latin gracilis (meaning "graceful") and raptor (meaning "thief"). The specific name refers to the village of Lujiatun where the fossil site is located.

Gravitholus.etymology: From Latin gravis (heavy) and tholus (dome); meaning 'heavy dome', referring to its thick skull roof
Gravitholus.description: Gravitholus was a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from the late Cretaceous period (Campanian stage, around 75 million years ago). It was a pachycephalosaur, and like other pachycephalosaurids the skull roof formed a thick dome made of dense bone, which may have been used in head-butting contests over mates or territory. It lived in what is now Alberta, Canada, and was described in 1979 by W. P. Wall and Peter Galton. The type species is Gravitholus albertae.

It contains one species, Gremlin slobodorum, named in 2023 by Michael J. Ryan and colleagues from a frontal bone found in the Oldman Formation of Alberta. It can be distinguished from other leptoceratopsids by a ridge on the frontal that runs transversely from the midline of the skull outwards to the top end of the orbit.

Gryposaurus.etymology: From Greek grypos (hook-nosed, curved) and sauros (lizard); meaning 'hooked-nosed lizard', referring to its arched nasal profile

Named species of Gryposaurus are known from the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada, and two formations in the United States: the Lower Two Medicine Formation in Montana and the Kaiparowits Formation of Utah. A possible additional species from the Javelina Formation in Texas may extend the temporal range of the genus to 66 million years ago.

Paul estimated it at around 2 meters long (6.6 ft) and 10 kg (22 lbs), whereas in 2020 Molina-Pérez and Larramendi listed it at 3 meters (10 ft) and 35 kg (77 lbs).

Gualicho.description: Gualicho is an enigmatic genus of theropod dinosaurs. The type species is Gualicho shinyae. It lived in what is now northern Patagonia, on what was then a South American island continent split off from the supercontinent Gondwana. The fossils were found in the Huincul Formation, dating to the late Cenomanian-early Turonian age of the upper Cretaceous Period, around 91 million years ago.

Gwyneddosaurus.etymology: Named for Gwynedd (the historical Welsh region name applied to Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, where the fossils were found), combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Gwyneddosaurus.description: Gwyneddosaurus is a possibly invalid genus of extinct aquatic tanystropheid reptile. The type species, G. erici was described in 1945 by Wilhelm Bock, who identified it as a coelurosaurian dinosaur related to Podokesaurus (at the time, "podokesaurids" were thought to be coelurosaurians). Its remains were found in the Upper Triassic Lockatong Formation of Montgomery County, eastern Pennsylvania, and the holotype includes skull fragments, several vertebra, ribs, gastralia, partial shoulder and hip bones, and several forelimb and hindlimb elements found in soft shale, while the paratype includes a femur and a tibia. The type specimen is ANSP 15072 and it was discovered by Bock's four-year-old son while the paratype is only listed as ?(ASNP coll.). It was not a large animal; the type skeleton was estimated by Bock as 18 centimetres (7.1 in) long, and its thigh bone was only 23 millimeters long (0.91 in).

Hadrosaurus.etymology: From Greek hadros (bulky, stout) and sauros (lizard); meaning 'bulky lizard'
Hadrosaurus.description: Hadrosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaurs that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous Period in what is now the Woodbury Formation in New Jersey about 83.6 to 77.9 million years ago. The holotype specimen was found in fluvial marine sedimentation, meaning that the corpse of the animal was transported by a river and washed out to sea. Haplocanthosaurus.description: Haplocanthosaurus is a genus of diplodocoid sauropod dinosaur. Two species, H. delfsi and H. priscus, are known from incomplete fossil skeletons. The type species is H. priscus, named in 1903 John Bell Hatcher , and the referred species H. delfsi was discovered by a young college student named Edwin Delfs in Colorado, United States and described by Jack McIntosh and Michael Williams in 1988. Homalocephale.etymology: From Greek homalos (even, flat) and kephale (head); meaning 'even head' or 'flat-headed', referring to its flat skull roof unlike other pachycephalosaurs
Homalocephale.description: Homalocephale is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of what is now the Nemegt Formation, Mongolia. The genus was described in 1974 by Halszka Osmólska and Teresa Maryańska, and consists of a single species, H. calathocercos. Though Homalocephale has been regarded as a synonym (and juvenile form) of Prenocephale, juvenile specimens of the latter indicate that they were distinct. Homalocephale was 1.8 m (5.9 ft) long and possibly an omnivore.

species.name: Homalocephale calathocercos

Hoplitosaurus.etymology: Hoplite lizard; named after the hoplite, a type of heavily armed ancient Greek soldier, in reference to its armored body, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Hoplitosaurus.description: Hoplitosaurus was a genus of armored dinosaur related to Polacanthus. It was named from a partial skeleton found in the Barremian (Early Cretaceous) Lakota Formation of Custer County, South Dakota. It is an obscure genus which has been subject to some misinterpretation of its damaged remains. Although there was a push to synonymize it with Polacanthus in the late 1980s-early 1990s, Hoplitosaurus has been accepted as a valid albeit poorly known genus in more recent reviews.

Huabeisaurus.etymology: Named for North China (Huabei, meaning 'north China' in Chinese) combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'North China lizard'.
Huabeisaurus.description: Huabeisaurus was a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian to Maastrichtian stages, around 99.7–70.6 million years ago) of what is present-day northern China. The type species, Huabeisaurus allocotus, was first described by Pang Qiqing and Cheng Zhengwu in 2000. It is known from numerous remains found in the 1990s, which include teeth, partial limbs and vertebrae. Due to its relative completeness, Huabeisaurus represents a significant taxon for understanding sauropod evolution in Asia. Huabeisaurus comes from Kangdailiang and Houyu, Zhaojiagou Town, Tianzhen County, Shanxi province, China. The holotype was found in the unnamed upper member of the Huiquanpu Formation, which is Late Cretaceous (?Cenomanian–?Campanian) in age based on ostracods, charophytes, and fission-track dating.

Hualianceratops.etymology: From Chinese hua (ornamental) and lian (face), combined with Greek ceratops (horned face); meaning 'ornamental-faced horned face'
Hualianceratops.description: Hualianceratops is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur that lived about 160 million years ago in the Late Jurassic epoch in what is now western China. The single species, H. wucaiwanensis was described in 2015. Its size has been compared to that of a spaniel.

species.name: Hualianceratops wucaiwanensis

Huallasaurus.etymology: Duck lizard; from hualla, the Mapudungun word for duck, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Huallasaurus.description: Huallasaurus is an extinct genus of saurolophine hadrosaur from the Late Cretaceous Los Alamitos Formation of Patagonia in Argentina. The type and only species is H. australis. Originally named as a species of Kritosaurus in 1984, it was long considered a synonym of Secernosaurus before being recognized as its own distinct genus in a 2022 study, different from other members of Kritosaurini.

species.etymology: From Latin 'australis' meaning 'southern', after the discovery of the holotype in southern Argentina.

Huanansaurus.etymology: From Chinese Huanan (Southern China) combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'Southern China lizard'
Huanansaurus.description: Huanansaurus is an extinct genus of oviraptorid dinosaur that lived approximately 72 million years ago, between the Campanian and Maastrichtian, during the latter part of the Cretaceous period in what is now China, in the Nanxiong Formation.

Huanghetitan.description: Huanghetitan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the early Cretaceous Period. It was a basal titanosauriform which lived in what is now Gansu, China.

Huashanosaurus.etymology: Huashan Mountain lizard; named after Huashan Mountain in China, combined with Greek sauros (lizard)
Huashanosaurus.description: Huashanosaurus is an extinct genus of eusauropod sauropod dinosaurs known from the Early–Middle Jurassic Wangmen Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, Huashanosaurus qini, known from a fragmentary partial skeleton.

Huaxiagnathus.etymology: From Chinese 'Hua Xia' (華夏), a traditional word for China, and Greek 'gnathos' meaning 'jaw', hence 'China jaw'.
Huaxiagnathus.description: Huaxiagnathus is an extinct genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of China. The genus contains a single species, Huaxiagnathus orientalis, known from two immature individuals from the Yixian Formation. Huaxiagnathus may represent an earlier ontogenetic stage of the tyrannosauroid Sinotyrannus from the younger Jiufotang Formation.

Huaxiazhoulong.etymology: Combines the Chinese words 'Huaxia' (an ancient name for China), 'zhou' meaning 'armour', and 'long' meaning 'dragon'; the specific name shouwen is Chinese pinyin for 'painted in the shape of a beast'.
Huaxiazhoulong.description: Huaxiazhoulong is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Tangbian Formation of Jiangxi Province, China. The genus contains a single species, H. shouwen, known from a partial skeleton.

Huayangosaurus.etymology: From Huayang (華陽), an alternate historical name for Sichuan Province, China, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'Huayang lizard'
Huayangosaurus.description: Huayangosaurus is a genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of China. The name derives from "Huayang" (華陽), an alternate name for Sichuan (the province where it was discovered), and "saurus", meaning "lizard". It lived during the Bathonian to Callovian stages, around 165 million years ago, some 20 million years before its famous relative, Stegosaurus appeared in North America. At only approximately 4 metres (13 ft) long, it was also much smaller than its famous cousin. Found in the Lower Shaximiao Formation, Huayangosaurus shared the local Middle Jurassic landscape with the sauropods Shunosaurus, Datousaurus, Omeisaurus and Protognathosaurus, the ornithopod Xiaosaurus and the carnivorous Gasosaurus.

Huayracursor.etymology: From Quechua huayra (wind) and Latin cursor (runner); meaning 'wind runner'
Huayracursor.description: Huayracursor is an extinct genus of early sauropodomorph dinosaurs known from the Late Triassic (Carnian age) Santo Domingo Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Huayracursor jaguensis, known from a partial articulated skeleton.

species.name: Huayracursor jaguensis

Hudiesaurus.etymology: Butterfly lizard; from Chinese hudie (butterfly) and Greek sauros (lizard)
Hudiesaurus.description: Hudiesaurus is an extinct genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day China during the Late Jurassic period. It was described by Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming in 1997. The genus contains a single species, Hudiesaurus sinojapanorum, named based on a single vertebra. However, he also assigned teeth and limb bones from a nearby locality to H. sinojapanorum. These fossils were unearthed by the Sino-Japanese Silk Road Expedition near Qiketai in Shanshan, Xinjiang province in rock layers coming from the Kalaza Formation. This formation dates to between the Late Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic, 154 to 143 million years ago. Dong believed that the vertebra was a dorsal (trunk) vertebra, but later analysis suggested that it is one of the last cervical (neck) vertebrae. In 2021, the limb bones were assigned to a distinct genus of sauropod, Rhomaleopakhus, and the teeth were classified as an indeterminate eusauropod.

Huehuecanauhtlus.etymology: From Nahuatl 'huehuetl' meaning 'ancient' and 'canauhtli' meaning 'duck', giving 'ancient duck', in reference to its hadrosauroid (duck-billed) affinities; the specific name tiquichensis honors the town of Tiquicheo, Michoacán.
Huehuecanauhtlus.description: Huehuecanauhtlus is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian stage) of Michoacán, western Mexico. It contains a single species, Huehuecanauhtlus tiquichensis.
