Huinculsaurus.etymology: Named after the Huincul Formation of Argentina where it was found, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'Huincul lizard'
Huinculsaurus.description: Huinculsaurus is an extinct genus of noasaurid dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Huinculsaurus montesi, known from five partial vertebrae.

Hulsanpes.description: Hulsanpes is a genus of halszkaraptorine theropod dinosaurs that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia, about 75-72 million years ago. The remains were found in 1970 and formally described in 1982 by Halszka Osmólska, who noted that the genus is represented by an immature individual. Hulsanpes represents the first record of the basal dromaeosaurid subfamily Halszkaraptorinae.

Hungarosaurus.etymology: From Latin Hungaria (Hungary) and Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'Hungarian lizard'
Hungarosaurus.description: Hungarosaurus is an extinct genus of nodosaurid ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (Santonian) Csehbánya Formation of the Bakony Mountains, western Hungary. The type (and only) species is H. tormai, and represents the most completely known ankylosaur from the Cretaceous of Europe. Hungarosaurus walked on four legs and its body was covered with hundreds of osteoderms. The length of mature specimens was about 4–4.8 metres (13–16 ft).

Hylaeosaurus.description: Hylaeosaurus is a herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur that lived about 136 million years ago, in the late Valanginian stage of the early Cretaceous period of England. It was found in the Grinstead Clay.

Hypacrosaurus.etymology: Near the highest lizard; from Ancient Greek hypo- (less or under) and akros (high or topmost), combined with sauros (lizard), because it was almost but not quite as large as Tyrannosaurus
Hypacrosaurus.description: Hypacrosaurus is an extinct genus of duckbill dinosaur similar in appearance to Corythosaurus. Like Corythosaurus, it had a tall, hollow rounded crest, although not as large and straight. It is known from the remains of two species that spanned 75.0 to 69.5 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada, and Montana, United States, and is the latest hollow-crested duckbill known from good remains in North America. It was an obscure genus until the discovery in the 1990s of nests, eggs, and hatchlings belonging to H. stebingeri.

Hypnovenator.description: Hypnovenator is an extinct genus of troodontid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Albian) Ohyamashimo Formation of Japan. The genus contains a single species, Hypnovenator matsubaraetoheorum, known from a partial skeleton. Hypnovenator is the only troodontid currently known from Japan, and it represents the oldest definitive member of the subgroup Troodontinae.

Hypselosaurus.etymology: From Greek hypsilos (high, lofty) and sauros (lizard); meaning 'highest lizard'
Hypselosaurus.description: Hypselosaurus is a dubious genus of titanosaurian sauropod that lived in southern France during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago in the early Maastrichtian. Hypselosaurus was first described in 1846, but was not formally named until 1869, when Phillip Matheron named it under the binomial Hypselosaurus priscus. The holotype specimen includes a partial hindlimb and a pair of caudal vertebrae, and two eggshell fragments were found alongside these bones. Because of the proximity of these eggshells to the fossil remains, many later authors, including Matheron and Paul Gervais, have assigned several eggs from the same region of France all to Hypselosaurus, although the variation and differences between these eggs suggest that they do not all belong to the same taxon. Hypselosaurus has been found in the same formation as the dromaeosaurids Variraptor and Pyroraptor, the ornithopod Rhabdodon, and the ankylosaurian Rhodanosaurus, as well as indeterminate bones from other groups.

Iani.etymology: Named after Ianus (Janus), the two-faced Roman god of transitions and change, symbolizing the transitional nature of this dinosaur at a time of major faunal change
Iani.description: Iani is an extinct genus of rhabdodontomorph iguanodontian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah, United States. The genus contains a single species, I. smithi, known from a partial skeleton including the skull. Its discovery serves as a link between the genus Tenontosaurus and the Rhabdodontidae, with both along with Iani being members of the clade Rhabdodontomorpha.

species.name: Iani smithi
species.etymology: Named for Joshua Aaron Smith and his paleontological contributions.

holotype.institution: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences

references.authors: Zanno, Lindsay E.; Gates, Terry A.; Avrahami, Haviv M.; Tucker, Ryan T.; Makovicky, Peter J.
references.title: An early-diverging iguanodontian (Dinosauria: Rhabdodontomorpha) from the Late Cretaceous of North America

Iberospinus.etymology: Iberian spine; from Iberia (the Iberian Peninsula, where it was found in Portugal) and Latin spina (spine), referring to its spinosaurid neural spines
Iberospinus.description: Iberospinus is an extinct genus of spinosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Papo Seco Formation of Portugal. The genus contains a single species, I. natarioi, known from several assorted bones belonging to one individual. Iberospinus represents one of five known spinosaurid taxa from the Iberian Peninsula, the others being Camarillasaurus, Protathlitis, Riojavenatrix, and Vallibonavenatrix. It is important for its implications of the geographical origin of Spinosauridae and the suggested presence of potentially semi-aquatic lifestyle earlier in the evolution of this clade.

species.name: Iberospinus natarioi
species.etymology: Named for Carlos Natário, the discoverer of the holotype.

references.authors: Mateus, Octávio; Estraviz-López, Darío
references.title: A new theropod dinosaur from the early cretaceous (Barremian) of Cabo Espichel, Portugal: Implications for spinosaurid evolution

Ibirania.etymology: Named for Ibirá municipality in São Paulo, Brazil (also derived from Tupi 'ybyrá' meaning 'tree'), combined with a modified form of Greek 'plania' meaning 'wanderer'. The species name is from Latin 'parvus' meaning 'small'.
Ibirania.description: Ibirania is a genus of dwarf saltasaurine titanosaur dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian to Campanian) São José do Rio Preto Formation (Bauru Basin) of Southeast Brazil. The type species is Ibirania parva. It is one of the smallest sauropods known to date, comparable in size to the titanosaur Magyarosaurus.

species.name: Ibirania parva
species.etymology: From Latin 'parvus' meaning 'small', after the nanism (dwarfism) seen in the taxon.

Ichthyovenator.etymology: From Greek ichthys (fish) and Latin venator (hunter); meaning 'fish hunter', referring to its inferred piscivorous lifestyle
Ichthyovenator.description: Ichthyovenator is a genus of spinosaurid dinosaur that lived in what is now Laos, sometime between 120 and 113 million years ago, during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous period. It is known from fossils collected from the Grès supérieurs Formation of the Savannakhet Basin, the first of which were found in 2010, consisting of a partial skeleton without the skull or limbs. This specimen became the holotype of the new genus and species Ichthyovenator laosensis, and was described by palaeontologist Ronan Allain and colleagues in 2012. The generic name, meaning "fish hunter", refers to its assumed piscivorous lifestyle, while the specific name alludes to the country of Laos. In 2014, it was announced that more remains from the dig site had been recovered; these fossils included teeth, more vertebrae (backbones) and a pubic bone from the same individual.

species.etymology: Named for Laos, the country where the holotype was discovered.

Igai.etymology: Named for Igai, a mysterious 'lord of the oasis' worshipped around the Dakhla and Kharga Oases of Egypt during the Old Kingdom.
Igai.description: Igai is a genus of titanosaur from the Late Cretaceous Quseir Formation of Kharga Oasis, Egypt. The type species is Igai semkhu.

species.name: Igai semkhu
species.etymology: From Ancient Egyptian 'semekh' meaning 'to forget', referring both to the specimen's convoluted history and the relatively recent start of Late Cretaceous non-marine vertebrate paleontology in continental Africa.

Ignavusaurus.etymology: From Latin 'ignavus' meaning 'coward' and Ancient Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', giving 'coward's lizard'; the name refers to the type locality Ha Ralekoala, which literally means 'the place of the father of the coward' in the local language.
Ignavusaurus.description: Ignavusaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic in what is now Lesotho. Its fossils were found in the Upper Elliot Formation which is probably Hettangian in age (around 200 million years ago). It was described on the basis of a partial, well preserved articulated skeleton. The type species, I. rachelis, was described in 2010 by Spanish palaeontologist F. Knoll.

species.name: Ignavusaurus rachelis
species.etymology: Named for Spanish palaeontologist Raquel López-Antónanzas.

references.authors: KNOLL, F.
references.title: A primitive sauropodomorph from the upper Elliot Formation of Lesotho

Iguanacolossus.etymology: Named for the reptile genus Iguana (in reference to the iconic iguana-like teeth of iguanodontians) combined with Latin 'colossus' meaning 'colossal' or 'giant', in reference to the large body size of the specimen.
Iguanacolossus.description: Iguanacolossus is a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Early Cretaceous period. It is known from UMNH VP 20205, the associated holotype with a large partial skeleton of a single individual.

species.name: Iguanacolossus fortis
species.etymology: From Latin 'fortis' meaning 'mighty', in reference to the large body size of the specimen.

Iguanodon.etymology: Iguana tooth; from the iguana (a modern lizard) and Greek odous/odontos (tooth), named for the resemblance of its teeth to those of the iguana
Iguanodon.description: A genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Europe. Iguanodon was one of the first dinosaurs ever scientifically described and is one of the founding members of the group Dinosauria. It is notable for its large thumb spike, which was originally mistakenly placed on its nose in early reconstructions.

features: Large conical thumb spike
Robust build with ability to walk bipedally or quadrupedally
Broad, blunt snout with a horny beak

diagnostic_features: Large conical thumb spike (manual digit I ungual)
Laterally compressed, leaf-shaped teeth with denticulate margins
Robust fifth finger that could oppose the others

Iliosuchus.etymology: From the ilium (hip bone) and Greek Souchos (the crocodile god); meaning "crocodile-hipped"
Iliosuchus.description: Iliosuchus is a genus of theropod dinosaur known from Bathonian-aged (168.3-166.1 mya) rocks of England. It was perhaps 2 metres (6.6 ft) long.

Ilokelesia.etymology: From Mapuche 'ilo' meaning 'flesh' and 'kelesio' meaning 'lizard', giving 'flesh lizard'; the specific name reflects the Aguada Grande locality where the fossil was found.
Ilokelesia.description: Ilokelesia is an extinct genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs, preserved in the layers of the earliest Late Cretaceous of the Huincul Formation (Neuquén Group) in Neuquén Province, Argentina. The only known specimen, consisting of fragmentary elements of the skull and skeleton, was described by Rodolfo Coria and Leonardo Salgado in late 1998.

Imperobator.etymology: From Latin 'imperobator' meaning 'powerful warrior'. The species name refers to Antarctica, the continent where it was found.
Imperobator.description: Imperobator is a genus of probable unenlagiid paravian theropod dinosaurs, that lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in what is now James Ross Island in Antarctica. Imperobator is one of only two non-avian theropods known from Antarctica, crossing over to the landmass when it was part of Gondwana. The only described specimen was found in 2003 by an expedition launched by the University of California Museum of Paleontology and initially described as a dromaeosaur in 2007. The fossil was formally described as a new genus in 2019, and later searches reported more fossils from the site including teeth and skull bones.

Inawentu.etymology: Meaning "imitator"; language not specified in the article
Inawentu.description: Inawentu is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, I. oslatus, known from a partial articulated skeleton including the skull. The square-shaped jaw of Inawentu demonstrates convergent characteristics with rebbachisaurids.

Incisivosaurus.etymology: Named for its unusually large incisiform front teeth combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'incisor lizard'.
Incisivosaurus.description: Incisivosaurus is a genus of small, probably herbivorous theropod dinosaurs from the early Cretaceous Period of what is now the People's Republic of China. The first specimen to be described (by Xu et al. in 2002), IVPP V13326, is a skull that was collected from the lowermost levels (the fluvial Lujiatun beds) of the Yixian Formation (dating to the Barremian stage about 126 million years ago) in the Sihetun area, near Beipiao City, in western Liaoning Province. The most significant, and highly unusual, characteristic of this dinosaur is its apparent adaptation to an herbivorous or omnivorous lifestyle. It was named for its prominent, rodent-like front teeth, which show wear patterns commonly found in plant-eating dinosaurs. The specific name gauthieri honors Dr. Jacques Gauthier, a pioneer of the phylogenetic method of classification.

Indosaurus.description: Indosaurus is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now India, about 69 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian division of the Late Cretaceous.

Indosuchus.etymology: From India (where it was found) and Greek suchos (crocodile); meaning 'Indian crocodile'
Indosuchus.description: Indosuchus is a genus of abelisaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period (Maastrichtian, 70 to 66 million years ago) of what is now India. Like most theropods, Indosuchus was a bipedal carnivore. It was about 7 metres (23 ft) long, weighed about 1.2 tonnes (1.3 short tons), and had a crested skull, flattened on the top.

Ingentia.etymology: From Latin 'ingentia' meaning 'enormous' or 'gigantic', in reference to the animal's large size for its age in the fossil record.
Ingentia.description: Ingentia is a genus of early sauropodiform dinosaur, sometimes considered a basal sauropod, from the Late Triassic (late Norian-Rhaetian) of Argentina. The type specimen of Ingentia, PVSJ 1086, was discovered in the Quebrada del Barro Formation of northwestern Argentina. It was described in 2018 by Cecilia Apaldetti, Ricardo Nestor Martínez, Ignacio Alejandro Cerda, Diego Pol and Oscar Alcober who named the type and only species Ingentia prima, meaning "first huge one", as the taxon was one of the first very large sauropodomorphs to evolve, along with its close relative Lessemsaurus. A second specimen, PVSJ 1087, was referred, containing five tail vertebrae, both ulnae and radii, a left calfbone and a right foot.

Inosaurus.description: Inosaurus is a dubious genus of extinct theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous age "Continental intercalaire" and Echkar Formation of Niger and possibly from the Late Cretaceous age Baharija Formation of Egypt. The type, and only species, is I. tedreftensis.

Invictarx.etymology: From Latin 'invictus' meaning 'invincible' or 'unconquerable' and 'arx' meaning 'fortress', in reference to the well-armoured nature of ankylosaurs. The species name is from Greek 'Zephyrus' meaning 'western wind'.
Invictarx.description: Invictarx is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from New Mexico that lived during the Late Cretaceous (lower Campanian, 78.5 Ma) in what is now the upper Allison Member of the Menefee Formation. The type and only species, Invictarx zephyri, is known from three isolated, incomplete postcranial skeletons. It was named in 2018 by Andrew T. McDonald and Douglas G. Wolfe. Invictarx shares similarities with Glyptodontopelta from the Naashoibito member of the Ojo Alamo Formation, New Mexico.

Irisosaurus.description: Irisosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropodiform sauropodomorph dinosaur, from the Fengjiahe Formation of China. The type species, Irisosaurus yimenensis was formally described in 2020. It was the sister taxon to Mussaurus.

Irritator.etymology: From English/Latin irritation; named to reflect the frustration of paleontologists who discovered the skull had been heavily damaged and altered by fossil dealers
Irritator.description: Irritator is a genus of spinosaurid dinosaur that lived in what is now Brazil during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous Period, about 113 to 110 million years ago. It is known from a nearly complete skull found in the Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin. Fossil dealers had acquired this skull and sold it to the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart. In 1996, the specimen became the holotype of the type species Irritator challengeri. The genus name comes from the word "irritation", reflecting the feelings of paleontologists who found the skull had been heavily damaged and altered by the collectors. The species name is a homage to the fictional character Professor Challenger from Arthur Conan Doyle's novels.

Isaberrysaura.etymology: Named for Isabel Valdueza Berry, who reported the fossil site, combined with Greek 'saura' meaning 'lizard'.
Isaberrysaura.description: Isaberrysaura is an extinct genus of stegosaurian ornithischian dinosaurs from the Middle Jurassic Los Molles Formation of Patagonia, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, I. mollensis, described by Salgado in 2017 based on a single specimen. Although initially classified as a basal neornithischian, subsequent analyses have allied it with the Stegosauria as the morphology of its skull resembles those of other members of the group.

Isanosaurus.etymology: Named for Isan, the northeastern region of Thailand, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name honours P. Attavipach, a supporter of paleontological research in Thailand.
Isanosaurus.description: Isanosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from Thailand. It was originally dated to approximately 219-199 million years ago during the Late Triassic (late Norian to Rhaetian stages), which would make it one of the oldest known sauropods. Its age was later considered uncertain, and may be Early Jurassic or even as young as Late Jurassic. The only species is Isanosaurus attavipachi. Though important for the understanding of sauropod origin and early evolution, Isanosaurus is poorly known. Exact relationships to other early sauropods remain unresolved.

Isasicursor.description: Isasicursor is an extinct genus of elasmarian ornithopod dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous Chorrillo Formation of Santa Cruz Province, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Isasicursor santacrucensis. It was a contemporary of the titanosaur sauropod Nullotitan, which was described in the same paper.

Ischioceratops.description: Ischioceratops is an extinct genus of small herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur that lived approximately 77.3-73.5 million years ago during the latter part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now China.

Isisaurus.description: Isisaurus is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Lameta Formation of India and Pab Formation of Pakistan. The genus contains a single species, Isisaurus colberti.

species.name: Isisaurus colberti
species.etymology: Named for Edwin Harris Colbert, the American vertebrate palaeontologist.

holotype.material: Partial skeleton cataloged as ISI R 335/1 through 335/65

references.authors: Wilson, Jeffrey A.; Upchurch, Paul
references.title: A revision ofTitanosaurusLydekker (dinosauria ‐ sauropoda), the first dinosaur genus with a ‘Gondwanan’ distribution

Issi.etymology: From Kalaallisut (Greenlandic) meaning 'cold', in reference to it being the most northerly basal sauropodomorph ever discovered. The species name 'saaneq' means 'bone' in Kalaallisut.
Issi.description: Issi is a plateosaurid dinosaur from the Late Triassic Fleming Fjord Formation of Greenland. It contains one species, Issi saaneq; the full binomial name means "cold bone". Fossils of Issi were previously assigned to the species Plateosaurus trossingensis, but new finds allowed for a reassessment of that material that showed that it possessed features thought to be exclusive to Brazilian sauropodomorphs such as Unaysaurus and Macrocollum. This ultimately led to the designation of Issi as a distinct genus in 2021. This taxon is the first non-avian dinosaur described from Greenland.

species.name: Issi saaneq
species.etymology: From Kalaallisut (Greenlandic) 'saaneq' meaning 'bone', together with the genus name forming 'cold bone', a reference to the northernmost location where a basal sauropodomorph has been found.

location.locality: Iron Cake site, northern flank of Macknight Bjerg

references.authors: Beccari, Victor; Mateus, Octávio; Wings, Oliver; Milàn, Jesper; Clemmensen, Lars B.
references.title: Issi saaneq gen. et sp. nov.—A New Sauropodomorph Dinosaur from the Late Triassic (Norian) of Jameson Land, Central East Greenland

Istiorachis.etymology: From Greek histion (sail) and rhachis (spine); meaning "sail spine", referring to the notably elongated vertebral neural spines
Istiorachis.description: Istiorachis is an extinct genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian age) Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, England. The genus contains a single species, Istiorachis macarthurae, known from a partial postcranial skeleton including several vertebrae, incomplete ribs, and part of the pelvis. Its vertebral neural spines are notably elongated, giving the animal a 'sail-backed' appearance.

species.name: Istiorachis macarthurae
species.etymology: Named for Dame Ellen MacArthur, sailor and Isle of Wight native who set the world record for the fastest solo non-stop circumnavigation of the globe in 2005.

location.locality: 100 m east of Grange Chine (bed L11)

references.authors: Lockwood, Jeremy A. F.; Martill, David M.; Maidment, Susannah C. R.
references.title: The origins of neural spine elongation in iguanodontian dinosaurs and the osteology of a new sail‐back styracosternan (Dinosauria, Ornithischia) from the Lower Cretaceous Wealden Group of England

Itapeuasaurus.etymology: Named for Itapeua, the beach locality in Maranhão, Brazil where the fossils were discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'Itapeua lizard'.
Itapeuasaurus.description: Itapeuasaurus is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Alcântara Formation (Itapecuru Group) of Maranhão in Brazil. The type and only species is Itapeuasaurus cajapioensis. It is the most complete Cenomanian-aged diplodocoid known from South America and it is also the first reported Cenomanian-aged rebbachisaurid discovered in South America.

species.name: Itapeuasaurus cajapioensis
species.etymology: Named for Cajapió, the municipality in Maranhão, Brazil, near where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Universidade Federal do Maranhão (UFMA), Campus do Bacanga
holotype.material: Partial skeleton cataloged as UFMA 1.10.1960-1, 3-5, 8

references.authors: Lindoso, Rafael Matos; Medeiros, Manuel Alfredo Araújo; Carvalho, Ismar de Souza; Pereira, Agostinha Araújo; Mendes, Ighor Dienes; Iori, Fabiano Vidoi; Sousa, Eliane Pinheiro; Arcanjo, Silvia Helena Souza; Silva, Taciane Costa Madeira
references.title: A new rebbachisaurid (Sauropoda: Diplodocoidea) from the middle Cretaceous of northern Brazil

Itemirus.etymology: Named for the Itemir locality in Uzbekistan where the fossils were discovered.
Itemirus.description: Itemirus is a genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Turonian aged Bissekty Formation of the Late Cretaceous period of Uzbekistan.

species.name: Itemirus medullaris
species.etymology: From Latin 'medullaris' meaning 'of the marrow' or 'of the medulla', referring to the medulla oblongata, the part of the brain encased by the partial braincase holotype.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Kurzanov, S. M.
references.title: Brain-case structure in the carnosaur Itemirus n. gen. and some aspects of the cranial anatomy of dinosaurs

Iuticosaurus.etymology: Named after the Jutes (Iuti in Latin), the Germanic people associated with the Isle of Wight; meaning "Jute lizard"
Iuticosaurus.description: Iuticosaurus is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of the Isle of Wight. Two species have been named: I. valdensis and I. lydekkeri. I. valdensis was found in the Wessex Formation and I. lydekkeri in the younger Upper Greensand.

species.name: Iuticosaurus lydekkeri
species.etymology: Named for Richard Lydekker, the British palaeontologist who first described the fossil vertebrae.

references.authors: Le Loeuff, J.
references.title: European titanosaurids

Iyuku.etymology: From the Xhosa word for 'hatchling', in reference to the immature status of the specimens. The species name honours South African paleontologist Mike Raath.
Iyuku.description: Iyuku is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Kirkwood Formation of South Africa. The type species is Iyuku raathi.

species.name: Iyuku raathi
species.etymology: Named for Mike Raath, South African palaeontologist.

references.authors: Forster, Catherine A.; de Klerk, William J.; Poole, Karen E.; Chinsamy‐Turan, Anusuya; Roberts, Eric M.; Ross, Callum F.
references.title: Iyuku raathi, a new iguanodontian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Kirkwood Formation, South Africa

Jaculinykus.etymology: Named after Jaculus (a mythical jumping serpent) combined with Greek onyx/nykus (claw); meaning "Jaculus claw", referring to the hypertrophied first digit
Jaculinykus.description: Jaculinykus is an extinct genus of alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Baruungoyot Formation of Mongolia. The genus contains a single species, J. yaruui, known from a nearly complete articulated skeleton including bones of the skull. Jaculinykus is notable for its unique hand, which has a hypertrophied first digit and greatly reduced second digit, which is intermediate between the tridactyl hand of Shuvuuia and monodactyl hand of Linhenykus.

species.name: Jaculinykus yaruui
species.etymology: From Mongolian 'yaruu' meaning 'speedy' or 'hasty', in reference to the animal's presumed agility.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Center, Mongolian Academy of Sciences
holotype.material: Nearly complete skeleton with most of the skull

references.authors: Kubo, Kohta; Kobayashi, Yoshitsugu; Chinzorig, Tsogtbaatar; Tsogtbaatar, Khishigjav
references.title: A new alvarezsaurid dinosaur (Theropoda, Alvarezsauria) from the Upper Cretaceous Baruungoyot Formation of Mongolia provides insights for bird-like sleeping behavior in non-avian dinosaurs

Jainosaurus.etymology: Named after Indian paleontologist Sohan Lal Jain, who made significant contributions to the study of Indian dinosaurs, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'Jain's lizard'
Jainosaurus.description: Jainosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur of India and wider Asia, which lived in the Maastrichtian (approximately 68 million years ago). It is thought to have been about the same size as its contemporary relative Isisaurus, measuring 18 metres (59 ft) long and weighing 15 metric tons (17 short tons). The humerus of the type specimen is 134 centimetres long.

species.name: Jainosaurus septentrionalis
species.etymology: From Latin 'septentrionalis' meaning 'northern', a reference to the fact that the species was discovered in the Northern Hemisphere, in contrast to the southern origins implied by the genus name Antarctosaurus under which it was first described.

references.authors: Hunt, A. P.; Lockley, M. G.; S. G. Lucas, C. A. Meyer
references.title: The global sauropod fossil record

Jakapil.etymology: From 'Ja-Kapïl', a Puelchean word meaning 'shield bearer', in reference to its thyreophoran armor. The species name 'kaniukura' means 'crest stone' in Mapudungun.
Jakapil.description: Jakapil is a genus of basal thyreophoran dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian-aged) Candeleros Formation of Argentina. The type species is Jakapil kaniukura.

species.name: Jakapil kaniukura
species.etymology: From Mapudungun 'kaniukura' meaning 'crest stone', in reference to the uniquely deep jaw of the animal.

references.authors: Riguetti, Facundo J.; Apesteguía, Sebastián; Pereda-Suberbiola, Xabier
references.title: A new Cretaceous thyreophoran from Patagonia supports a South American lineage of armoured dinosaurs
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Jaklapallisaurus.etymology: Named after Jaklapal village in Telangana, central India, near where the fossils were discovered, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'Jaklapal lizard'
Jaklapallisaurus.description: Jaklapallisaurus is a genus of unaysaurid sauropodomorph dinosaur. It lived during the Late Triassic period (late Norian to earliest Rhaetian) in what is now Telangana, central India. The genus is monotypic, only including the species Jaklapallisaurus asymmetricus.

species.name: Jaklapallisaurus asymmetrica
species.etymology: From Latin 'asymmetricus' meaning 'asymmetrical', referring to the highly asymmetrical astragalus of this species in distal view.

holotype.material: Partial skeleton cataloged as ISI R273/1-3

references.authors: Novas, Fernando E.; Ezcurra, Martin D.; Chatterjee, Sankar; Kutty, T. S.
references.title: New dinosaur species from the Upper Triassic Upper Maleri and Lower Dharmaram formations of Central India
references.journal: Earth and Environmental Science Transactions of the Royal Society of Edinburgh

Janenschia.etymology: Named in honor of German paleontologist Werner Janensch, who conducted extensive research on dinosaurs from the Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania
Janenschia.description: Janenschia is a genus of large herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (around 155 to 145 million years ago) Tendaguru Formation of Lindi Region, Tanzania.

synonyms.name: Nteregosaurus
synonyms.reason: Informal name used for material now considered referable to Janenschia.

species.name: Janenschia robusta
species.etymology: From Latin 'robustus' meaning 'robust' or 'sturdy', inspired by the heavy build of the animal.

references.authors: Wild, R.
references.title: Janenschia n. g. robusta (E. Fraas 1908) pro Tornieria robusta (E. Fraas 1908) (Reptilia, Saurischia, Sauropodomorpha) [Janenschia n. g. robusta (E. Fraas 1908) for Tornieria robusta (E. Fraas 1908) (Reptilia, Saurischia, Sauropodomorpha)]
references.journal: Stuttgarter Beiträge zur Naturkunde, Serie B (Geologie und Paläontologie)

Jaxartosaurus.etymology: Named after the Jaxartes (ancient Greek name for the Syr Darya river in Kazakhstan); meaning "Jaxartes lizard"
Jaxartosaurus.description: Jaxartosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur similar to Corythosaurus which lived during the Late Cretaceous. Its fossils were found in Kazakhstan.

species.name: Jaxartosaurus aralensis
species.etymology: Named for the Aral Sea, near the discovery locality in Kazakhstan.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Riabinin, A. N.
references.title: O nakhodke shlemonosnykh form Dinosauria verkhnemelovykh otlozheniyakh yuzhnogo Kazakhstana [The discovery of crested forms of Upper Cretaceous dinosaurs in southern Kazakhstan]

Jeholosaurus.etymology: Named after Jehol, a historical province in northeastern China (western Liaoning and northern Hebei), combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'Jehol lizard'
Jeholosaurus.description: Jeholosaurus is a genus of small neornithischian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous-aged Yixian Formation of what is now China.

species.name: Jeholosaurus shangyuanensis
species.etymology: Named for the geographical area of Shangyuan, where the fossil site is located.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: Xu, X.; Wang, X.-L.; H.-L. You
references.title: A primitive ornithopod from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning

Jeyawati.etymology: From the Zuni language meaning "grinding mouth"
Jeyawati.description: Jeyawati is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur which lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous. The type species, J. rugoculus, was described in 2010, based on fossils recovered in the U.S. state of New Mexico. The holotype, MSM P4166, was discovered in the Moreno Hill Formation.

species.name: Jeyawati rugoculus
species.etymology: From Latin 'ruga' meaning 'wrinkle' and 'oculus' meaning 'eye', in reference to the rough texture of the lateral surface of the postorbital bone.

references.authors: Mcdonald †, Andrew T.; Wolfe, Douglas G.; Kirkland, James I.
references.title: A new basal hadrosauroid (Dinosauria: Ornithopoda) from the Turonian of New Mexico

Jianchangosaurus.etymology: Named after Jianchang County, Liaoning Province, China, where the type specimen was discovered; meaning "lizard from Jianchang County"
Jianchangosaurus.description: Jianchangosaurus is a genus of therizinosaurian dinosaur that lived approximately 126 million years ago during the early part of the Cretaceous Period from the Yixian Formation in what is now China. The type specimen, a juvenile, was discovered in Jianchang County, in the western part of Liaoning Province. It was described in 2013 by a team of palaeontologists from the Henan Museum, who determined that it was among the most basal therizinosaurs.

species.name: Jianchangosaurus yixianensis
species.etymology: Named for the Yixian Formation, where the specimen was found.

holotype.material: Nearly complete skeleton

references.authors: Pu, Hanyong; Kobayashi, Yoshitsugu; Lü, Junchang; Xu, Li; Wu, Yanhua; Chang, Huali; Zhang, Jiming; Jia, Songhai
references.title: An Unusual Basal Therizinosaur Dinosaur with an Ornithischian Dental Arrangement from Northeastern China

Jiangjunosaurus.etymology: Named after Jiangjunmiao ('temple of the general'), an abandoned town near the discovery site in Xinjiang, China, with Chinese jiangjun meaning 'general', combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning 'general's temple lizard'
Jiangjunosaurus.description: Jiangjunosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaurs from the Oxfordian-age (Upper Jurassic) Shishugou Formation of the Junggar Basin, Xinjiang, China.

species.name: Jiangjunosaurus junggarensis
species.etymology: Named for the Junggar Basin of Xinjiang, China, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: Jia, C.; Forster, C. A.; X. Xu, J. M. Clark
references.title: The first stegosaur (Dinosauria, Ornithischia) from the Upper Jurassic Shishugou Formation of Xinjiang, China

Jiangshanosaurus.etymology: Named for Jiangshan County in Zhejiang Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Jiangshanosaurus.description: Jiangshanosaurus is a genus of herbivorous titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur that lived in China approximately 92-88 million years ago, during the Turonian and Coniacian stages of the Late Cretaceous.

species.name: Jiangshanosaurus lixianensis
species.etymology: Named for Lixian Village, the locality in Jiangshan County, Zhejiang, China, where the holotype was excavated.

references.authors: Tang, F.; Kang, X.-M.; Z.-S. Jin, F. Wei, W.-T. Wu
references.title: A new sauropod dinosaur of Cretaceous from Jingshan, Zhejiang province

Jiangxisaurus.etymology: Named after Jiangxi Province of southern China, where the specimen was found
Jiangxisaurus.description: Jiangxisaurus is an extinct genus of oviraptorid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of southern China.

species.name: Jiangxisaurus ganzhouensis
species.etymology: Named for Ganzhou, the city in Jiangxi Province, southern China, where the specimen was discovered.

references.authors: Wei, X.; Pu, H.; L. Xu, D. Liu, J. Lü
references.title: A new oviraptorid dinosaur (Theropoda: Oviraptorosauria) from the Late Cretaceous of Jiangxi Province, southern China

Jiangxititan.etymology: Named for Jiangxi Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'.
Jiangxititan.description: Jiangxititan is an extinct genus of somphospondylan titanosauriform dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, J. ganzhouensis, known from several articulated vertebrae with ribs. Originally described as a titanosaur, Jiangxititan was later suggested to be a non-titanosaurian somphospondylan.

species.name: Jiangxititan ganzhouensis
species.etymology: Named for Ganzhou City in Jiangxi Province, southern China, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Natural History Museum of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region

references.authors: Mo, Jin-You; Fu, Qiong-Yao; Yu, Yi-Lun; Xu, Xing
references.title: A New Titanosaurian Sauropod from the Upper Cretaceous of Jiangxi Province, Southern China

Jianianhualong.etymology: Named after Jianianhua (the company that funded the research) combined with Chinese long (dragon); meaning "Jianianhua dragon"
Jianianhualong.description: Jianianhualong is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China. It contains a single species, Jianianhualong tengi, named in 2017 by Xu Xing and colleagues based on an articulated skeleton preserving feathers. The feathers at the middle of the tail of Jianianhualong are asymmetric, being the first record of asymmetrical feathers among the troodontids. Despite aerodynamic differences from the flight feathers of modern birds, the feathers in the tail vane of Jianianhualong could have functioned in drag reduction whilst the animal was moving. The discovery of Jianianhualong supports the notion that asymmetrical feathers appeared early in the evolutionary history of the Paraves.

species.name: Jianianhualong tengi
species.etymology: Named for Ms. Teng Fangfang, who acquired the specimen and made it available for study.

holotype.material: Nearly complete articulated skeleton preserving feathers, missing only the end of the tail

references.authors: Xu, Xing; Currie, Philip; Pittman, Michael; Xing, Lida; Meng, Qingjin; Lü, Junchang; Hu, Dongyu; Yu, Congyu
references.title: Mosaic evolution in an asymmetrically feathered troodontid dinosaur with transitional features
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Jinbeisaurus.etymology: Named for Jinbei, the northern part of Shanxi Province in China, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'northern Shanxi Province lizard'.
Jinbeisaurus.description: Jinbeisaurus is an extinct genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaurs from the Upper Cretaceous Huiquanpu Formation of Shanxi Province in China. The type and only species is Jinbeisaurus wangi. It is the first non-avian theropod named from Shanxi.

species.name: Jinbeisaurus wangi
species.etymology: Named in honor of Mr. Suozhu Wang for his contributions to the vertebrate paleontology of Shanxi Province, including organizing field explorations and discovering many Mesozoic reptile fossils within the province.

references.authors: Wu, Xiao-Chun; Shi, Jian-Ru; Dong, Li-Yang; Carr, Thomas D.; Yi, Jian; Xu, Shi-Chao
references.title: A new tyrannosauroid from the Upper Cretaceous of Shanxi, China

Jinfengopteryx.etymology: From Chinese Jinfeng (golden phoenix, the queen of birds in Chinese folklore) and Ancient Greek pteryx (feather, wing); meaning 'golden phoenix feather'
Jinfengopteryx.description: Jinfengopteryx is a genus of maniraptoran dinosaur. It was found in the Qiaotou Member of the Huajiying Formation of Hebei Province, China, and is therefore of uncertain age. The Qiaotou Member may correlate with the more well-known Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation, and so probably dates to around 122 Ma (122 million years) ago.

species.name: Jinfengopteryx elegans
species.etymology: From Latin 'elegans' meaning 'elegant', describing the delicate nature of the fossil and its well-preserved feathers.

holotype.institution: Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences-Institute of Geology
holotype.material: Complete skeleton with feather impressions

references.authors: Ji, Q.; Ji, S. -A.; J. -C. Lü, H. -L. You, W. Chen, Y. -Q. Liu, Y. -X. Liu
references.title: First avialan bird from China

Jingiella.etymology: Named for the Jing region or Jingia locality in Guangxi, China (diminutive '-ella' suffix), originally named 'Jingia' before a nomenclatural amendment.
Jingiella.description: Jingiella is an extinct genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Dongxing Formation of Guangxi, China. The genus contains a single species, J. dongxingensis, known from vertebrae and limb bones. The original description of Jingiella referred to it using the name "Jingia" which was preoccupied by a moth genus named in 1983, and an amendment was published shortly thereafter, establishing Jingiella as the new replacement name.

species.name: Jingiella dongxingensis
species.etymology: Named for Dongxing City in Guangxi, southern China, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Dongxing Municipal Bureau of Natural Resources

references.authors: Ren, Xin-Xin; Wang, Xu-Ri; Ji, Yan-Nan; Guo, Zhen; Ji, Qiang
references.title: The first mamenchisaurid from the Upper Jurassic Dongxing Formation of Guangxi, southernmost China

Jingshanosaurus.etymology: Named after the town of Jingshan ("Golden Hill") near the fossil locality in Lufeng County, Yunnan, China; meaning "Jingshan lizard"
Jingshanosaurus.description: Jingshanosaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaurs from the early Jurassic period (201.4 to 196.5 million years ago, Hettangian age) of China. The type and only species is Jingshanosaurus xinwaensis. Its maximum weight was around 4.3 t (4.7 short tons) with an adult femur length of 845 mm (33.3 in). The genus grew up to 5 m (16 ft) long.

synonyms.name: Chuxiongosaurus
synonyms.reason: Possible junior subjective synonym of Jingshanosaurus; identification is tentative. Per Olshevsky's Dinosaur Genera List.

species.name: Jingshanosaurus xinwaensis
species.etymology: Named for Xinwa Village, about 6 km from Jingshan Town in northeast Lufeng, Yunnan Province, China.

references.authors: Zhang, Y.; Yang, Z.
references.title: A new complete osteology of Prosauropoda in Lufeng Basin, Yunnan, China
references.journal: Yunnan Publishing House of Science and Technology, Kunming, China

Jintasaurus.etymology: Named for Jinta County in Gansu, China, where the fossils were discovered, combined with Chinese 'long' meaning 'dragon', hence 'Jinta County dragon'.
Jintasaurus.description: Jintasaurus is a genus of hadrosauriform dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous of what is now Jiuquan, Gansu, northwestern China. The type species is J. meniscus, described by Hai-Lu You and Da-Qing Li in 2009. The holotype and only known specimen includes the postorbital skull, lacking the jugal and quadratojugal, whose discovery supports the theory that hadrosaurs originated in Asia.

species.name: Jintasaurus meniscus
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'meniskos' meaning 'crescent', referring to the crescentic paroccipital process and occipital condyle of the specimen.

holotype.institution: The Fossil Research and Development Center of the Third Geology and Mineral Resources Exploration Academy of Gansu Provincial Bureau of Geo-exploration and Mineral Development

references.authors: You, Hai-Lu; Li, Da-Qing
references.title: A new basal hadrosauriform dinosaur (Ornithischia: Iguanodontia) from the Early Cretaceous of northwestern China

Jinyunpelta.etymology: Named after Jinyun County, Zhejiang, China combined with Greek pelta (shield); meaning "Jinyun shield"
Jinyunpelta.description: Jinyunpelta is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurine thyreophoran dinosaur from the Cretaceous Liangtoutang Formation of Jinyun County, Zhejiang, China; it has one species, the type species J. sinensis. This species is the basalmost ankylosaur known to have had a proper tail club.

species.name: Jinyunpelta sinensis
species.etymology: From Latin 'sinensis' meaning 'from China', referring to the country of discovery.

references.authors: Zheng, Wenjie; Jin, Xingsheng; Azuma, Yoichi; Wang, Qiongying; Miyata, Kazunori; Xu, Xing
references.title: The most basal ankylosaurine dinosaur from the Albian–Cenomanian of China, with implications for the evolution of the tail club
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Jinzhousaurus.etymology: Named for the town of Jinzhou in Liaoning, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Jinzhousaurus.description: Jinzhousaurus is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur of the Early Cretaceous of China. The type species is Jinzhousaurus yangi. The generic name refers to the town Jinzhou. The specific name honours Yang Zhongjian is the founder of Chinese paleontology. It was first described by Wang Xiao-lin and Xu Xing in 2001.

species.name: Jinzhousaurus yangi
species.etymology: Named for Yang Zhongjian, the founder of Chinese paleontology.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Jiutaisaurus.etymology: Named for Jiutai, the discovery site in Jilin, China, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'Jiutai lizard'.
Jiutaisaurus.description: Jiutaisaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Quantou Formation of Jilin, China. The formation dates from the Early - Late Cretaceous boundary. The type species, Jiutaisaurus xidiensis, was described by Wu et al. in 2006, and is based on eighteen vertebrae. It probably lived alongside Changchunsaurus and Helioceratops.

species.name: Jiutaisaurus xidiensis
species.etymology: Named for Xidi Village in Jiutai, Jilin, China, where the holotype was recovered.

references.authors: Wu, W.-h.; Dong, Z.-m.; Y.-w. Sun, C.-t. Li, T. Li
references.title: [A new sauropod dinosaur from the Cretaceous of Jiutai, Jilin, China]

Joaquinraptor.etymology: Named after San Joaquín, a locality in Chubut Province, Argentina, near where the fossils were found, combined with Latin raptor (thief); meaning 'Joaquín thief'
Joaquinraptor.description: Joaquinraptor is an extinct genus of megaraptorid theropod dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous Lago Colhué Huapi Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Joaquinraptor casali, representing the youngest (most recent) definitive megaraptoran. It is known from a partially articulated, incomplete skeleton including vertebrae and bones of the skull, forelimbs and hindlimbs, and pectoral girdle, making it one of the most completely known members of the Megaraptora. It was likely at least 7 metres (23 ft) long.

Its skeleton demonstrates a unique combination of anatomical traits seen in both earlier-diverging (basal) tyrannosauroids and the later-diverging (derived) tyrannosaurids.

The type specimen was excavated from the Ukhaa Tolgod locality of the Djadochta Formation, dating to about 75 million years ago. It is believed to have been about twice the size of the contemporaneous Shuvuuia. However, unlike Shuvuuia, which is known from many well preserved specimens, and although Ukhaa Tolgod has been thoroughly explored, Kol is known only from one complete foot, suggesting that it must have been relatively rare in that ecosystem.

species.name: Kol ghuva
species.etymology: From Mongolian 'ghuva' meaning 'beautiful', complementing the generic name 'kol' meaning 'foot' in Mongolian.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences
holotype.material: One complete foot

references.authors: Turner, Alan H.; Nesbitt, Sterling J.; Norell, Mark A.

references.publisher: American Museum of Natural History (BioOne sponsored)

Koleken.etymology: From Teushen, a language of central Patagonia, meaning 'coming from clay and water', in reference to the estuarine sedimentary environment where it was found. The species name honours Inakayal, a chief of the Tehuelche people.
Koleken.description: Koleken is a genus of carnotaurin abelisaurid from the Maastrichtian La Colonia Formation in the Chubut Province of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Koleken inakayali, known from one immature specimen about 4.97 metres (16.3 ft) long and six years old in minimum age.

species.name: Koleken inakayali
species.etymology: Named for Inakayal, one of the last chiefs of the Tehuelche people, the native inhabitants of central Patagonia, where the holotype was found.

holotype.material: Partial skull and postcranial skeleton

references.authors: Pol, Diego; Baiano, Mattia Antonio; Černý, David; Novas, Fernando E.; Cerda, Ignacio A.; Pittman, Michael
references.title: A new abelisaurid dinosaur from the end Cretaceous of Patagonia and evolutionary rates among the Ceratosauria

Koparion.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'koparion' (small surgical knife), referring to the small, blade-like shape of the known tooth fossil
Koparion.description: Koparion is a genus of small coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur, from the late Jurassic Period (Kimmeridgian stage), of Utah. It contains the single named species Koparion douglassi which is known only from a single isolated tooth.

species.name: Koparion douglassi
species.etymology: Named for Earl Douglass, who in the early twentieth century excavated the Dinosaur National Monument quarry near where the holotype tooth was discovered.

holotype.material: Single maxillary tooth crown (root missing)

references.title: Koparion douglassi, a new dinosaur from the Morrison Formation (Upper Jurassic) of Dinosaur National Monument; the oldest troodontid (Theropoda: Maniraptora)

Koreaceratops.etymology: From 'Korea' (referring to South Korea, where it was discovered) combined with Greek 'keras' (horn) and 'ops' (face); meaning 'Korean horned face'
Koreaceratops.description: Koreaceratops is a genus of basal ceratopsian dinosaur discovered in Albian-aged (Early Cretaceous) rocks of South Korea.

species.name: Koreaceratops hwaseongensis
species.etymology: Named for Hwaseong City, South Korea, where the type specimen was found incorporated into the Tando seawall.

holotype.institution: Geological Museum of Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources

references.title: The first ceratopsian dinosaur from South Korea
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Koreanosaurus.etymology: From 'Koreano-' (pertaining to Korea) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Korean lizard'
Koreanosaurus.description: Koreanosaurus is a genus of orodromine neornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous of what is now South Korea. One species has been described, Koreanosaurus boseongensis.

species.name: Koreanosaurus boseongensis
species.etymology: Named for Boseong, the locality on the southern coast of the Korean Peninsula where the holotype and referred specimens were recovered.

holotype.institution: Korea Dinosaur Research Center, Chonnam National University
holotype.material: Partial upper skeleton lacking the skull

Koshisaurus.etymology: Named for 'Koshi', an old Japanese regional name for the area including Fukui Prefecture where the fossils were discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Koshisaurus.description: Koshisaurus is a monospecific genus of basal hadrosauroid from the Kitadani Formation in Japan. The discovery of the genus suggests that hadrosauroids had higher diversity along the eastern margin of Asia in the Early Cretaceous. "Koshi" means an old Japanese regional name including Fukui prefecture where fossils of the genus were discovered.

species.name: Koshisaurus katsuyama
species.etymology: Named for Katsuyama, a city in Fukui Prefecture, Japan, where fossils of the genus were discovered.

references.authors: SHIBATA, MASATERU; AZUMA, YOICHI
references.title: New basal hadrosauroid (Dinosauria: Ornithopoda) from the Lower Cretaceous Kitadani Formation, Fukui, central Japan

Kosmoceratops.etymology: From Greek kosmos (ornate/decorated) combined with ceratops (horned face); meaning "ornate horned face", referring to the elaborate skull ornamentation
Kosmoceratops.description: Kosmoceratops is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur that lived in North America about 76–75.9 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period. Specimens were discovered in Utah in the Kaiparowits Formation of the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument in 2006 and 2007, including an adult skull and postcranial skeleton and partial subadults. In 2010, the adult was made the holotype of the new genus and species Kosmoceratops richardsoni; the generic name means "ornate horned face", and the specific name honors Scott Richardson, who found the specimens. The find was part of a spate of ceratopsian discoveries in the early 21st century, and Kosmoceratops was considered significant due to its elaborate skull ornamentation.

species.name: Kosmoceratops richardsoni
species.etymology: Named in honor of Scott Richardson, who found the specimens.

references.authors: Sampson, Scott D.; Loewen, Mark A.; Farke, Andrew A.; Roberts, Eric M.; Forster, Catherine A.; Smith, Joshua A.; Titus, Alan L.
references.title: New Horned Dinosaurs from Utah Provide Evidence for Intracontinental Dinosaur Endemism

Kotasaurus.etymology: Named for the Kota Formation of Telangana, India, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'Kota Formation lizard'. The species name refers to Yamanpalli, the village near the discovery site.
Kotasaurus.description: Kotasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic period (Sinemurian–Pliensbachian). The only known species is Kotasaurus yamanpalliensis. It was discovered in the Kota Formation of Telangana, India and shared its habitat with the related Barapasaurus. So far the remains of at least 12 individuals are known. The greater part of the skeleton is known, but the skull is missing, with the exception of two teeth. Like some sauropods, it had a tail club that would have been used for intraspecific combat or interspecific defense.

species.name: Kotasaurus yamanpalliensis
species.etymology: Named for Yamanpalli, the village in Telangana, India near which the fossil material was discovered.

references.authors: Yadagiri, P.
references.title: A new sauropod Kotasaurus yamanpalliensis from Lower Jurassic Kota Formation of India
references.journal: Records of the Geological Survey of India

Kritosaurus.etymology: From Greek kritos (separated) and sauros (lizard); meaning "separated lizard", referring to the arrangement of the cheek bones in the type skull
Kritosaurus.description: Kritosaurus is an incompletely known genus of hadrosaurid (duck-billed) dinosaur. It lived about 74.5-66 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous of North America. The name means "separated lizard" (referring to the arrangement of the cheek bones in an incomplete type skull), but is often mistranslated as "noble lizard" in reference to the presumed "Roman nose" (in the original specimen, the nasal region was fragmented and disarticulated, and was originally restored flat).

synonyms.name: Nectosaurus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Nectosaurus (Reptilia).

species.name: Kritosaurus navajovius
species.etymology: Named for the Navajo people and their territory in the American Southwest, where the type specimen was collected in San Juan County, New Mexico.

location.locality: west of Chaco Canyon, Ojo Alamo

references.authors: Brown, B.
references.title: The Cretaceous Ojo Alamo beds of New Mexico with description of the new dinosaur genus Kritosaurus
references.journal: Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History

Kryptops.etymology: From Greek kryptos (covered/hidden) and ops (face); meaning "covered face", referring to the heavily textured surface of the maxilla
Kryptops.description: Kryptops is an extinct genus of possibly chimeric abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of Niger. It is known from a partial maxilla (upper jaw bone) found at the Gadoufaoua locality in the western Ténéré Desert, in rocks of the Aptian–Albian-age Elrhaz Formation. The fossils were collected in 2000 by a University of Chicago expedition to Niger led by American paleontologist Paul Sereno. They were then described in 2008 by Sereno and Steve Brusatte. The genus contains a single species, Kryptops palaios. Sereno and Brusatte referred several postcranial remains to Kryptops, but later studies have shown that these elements belong to an allosauroid theropod, leaving Kryptops to be only known from the incomplete maxilla.

species.name: Kryptops palaios
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'palaios' meaning 'old', in reference to the ancient age of the fossils relative to other known members of the Abelisauridae.

holotype.material: Partial maxilla (MNN GAD1-1) and initially associated postcranial elements MNN GAD1-2 through MNN GAD1-8; postcranials now regarded as allosauroid

references.authors: Sereno, Paul C.; Brusatte, Stephen L.
references.title: Basal Abelisaurid and Carcharodontosaurid Theropods from the Lower Cretaceous Elrhaz Formation of Niger
references.publisher: Polska Akademia Nauk Instytut Paleobiologii (Institute of Paleobiology, Polish Academy of Sciences)

Kulceratops.etymology: Named for the Khodzhakul Formation where the fossils were found, with 'kul' meaning 'lake' in the local language, combined with Greek 'keratops' meaning 'horned face'; the specific name kulensis also references the formation.
Kulceratops.description: Kulceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous. It lived in the late Albian stage. It is one of the few ceratopsians known from this period. However, the fossils from this genus have been sparse: only jaw and tooth fragments have been found so far.

species.name: Kulceratops kulensis
species.etymology: Named for the Khodzhakul Formation of Uzbekistan, from which the holotype was recovered, with the Uzbek word 'kul' meaning 'lake'.

holotype.institution: Chernyshev Central Museum of Geological Exploration

references.authors: Nessov, L. A.
references.title: Dinozavri severnoi Yevrazii: Novye dannye o sostave kompleksov, ekologii i paleobiogeografii [Dinosaurs of northern Eurasia: new data about assemblages, ecology, and paleobiogeography]
references.journal: Institute for Scientific Research on the Earth's Crust, St. Petersburg State University, St. Petersburg

Kulindadromeus.etymology: From the Kulinda fossil sites in Russia combined with Greek 'dromeus' (runner); meaning 'Kulinda runner'
Kulindadromeus.description: Kulindadromeus is a genus of basal neornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic. The first Kulindadromeus fossil was found in Russia. Its feather-like integument is evidence for protofeathers being basal to Ornithischia and possibly Dinosauria as a whole, rather than just to Coelurosauria, as previously suspected.

synonyms.name: Daurosaurus
synonyms.reason: Based on material reportedly stolen from the Kulindadromeus type locality; rejected by the original describing team.

synonyms.name: Lepidocheirosaurus
synonyms.reason: Described from the same formation as Kulindadromeus, alongside Daurosaurus and Kulindapteryx; now widely treated as a junior synonym.

species.name: Kulindadromeus zabaikalicus
species.etymology: Named for Zabaykalsky Krai in Russia, where the Kulinda fossil sites are located, with the Latin suffix '-icus' meaning 'pertaining to'.

references.title: A Jurassic ornithischian dinosaur from Siberia with both feathers and scales
references.publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

Kunbarrasaurus.etymology: From Wulguru language kunbarra (shield) combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "shield lizard"
Kunbarrasaurus.description: Kunbarrasaurus is an extinct genus of small ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Australia. The genus contains a single species, K. ieversi.

species.name: Kunbarrasaurus ieversi
species.etymology: Named for Ian Ivers, the property manager of Marathon Station near Richmond, Queensland, who originally discovered the holotype specimen.

references.authors: Leahey, Lucy G.; Molnar, Ralph E.; Carpenter, Kenneth; Witmer, Lawrence M.; Salisbury, Steven W.
references.title: Cranial osteology of the ankylosaurian dinosaur formerly known asMinmisp. (Ornithischia: Thyreophora) from the Lower Cretaceous Allaru Mudstone of Richmond, Queensland, Australia

Kundurosaurus.etymology: Named for Kundur, the type locality in Amur Region, Far Eastern Russia, combined with Ancient Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; the specific name nagornyi honors V.A. Nagorny, who discovered the Kundur locality in 1990.
Kundurosaurus.description: Kundurosaurus is an extinct genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur known from the latest Cretaceous (probably late Maastrichtian stage) of Amur Region, Far Eastern Russia. It contains a single species, Kundurosaurus nagornyi.

species.name: Kundurosaurus nagornyi
species.etymology: Named for V.A. Nagorny of the Far Eastern Institute of Mineral Resources, who discovered the Kundur fossil locality in 1990.

holotype.institution: Amur Natural History Museum of the Institute of Geology and Nature Management, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Godefroit, Pascal; Bolotsky, Yuri L.; Lauters, Pascaline
references.title: A New Saurolophine Dinosaur from the Latest Cretaceous of Far Eastern Russia

Kuru.etymology: Named for Kurukullā, a deity venerated in Tibetan Buddhism associated with major life transitions (explicitly not in reference to the prion disease of the same name).
Kuru.description: Kuru kulla (, after Kurukullā, a Tibetan Buddhist deity) is an extinct species of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia. K. kulla is the only species in the genus Kuru, known from a fragmentary skeleton including a partial skull.

synonyms.name: Airakoraptor
synonyms.reason: Informal name for a dromaeosaurid taxon reported at a 1992 Society of Vertebrate Paleontology conference; the specimen was ultimately formally described as Kuru kulla.

Kurupi.description: Kurupi itaata is an extinct species of abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Marília Formation of Brazil. It is the only species in the genus Kurupi.
Kurupi.etymology: Named for Kurupi, a god of fertility and sexuality from Guaraní mythology; chosen to reference the discovery of the holotype near a love hotel ('Motel Paraíso' / 'Paradise Motel').

species.name: Kurupi itaata
species.etymology: From the Tupi 'ita' meaning 'rock' and 'ata' meaning 'hard', in reference to the heavily cemented rocks in which the holotype was found.

Kuszholia.etymology: From Kazakh qus joly (Milky Way, literally "bird road"); meaning "Milky Way bird"
Kuszholia.description: Kuszholia is the name given to a genus of primitive birds or bird-like dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous.

Labocania.etymology: Named after the La Bocana Roja Formation in Baja California, Mexico, where the type specimen was likely recovered
Labocania.description: Labocania is an extinct genus of theropod dinosaur of disputed affinities, known from the Late Cretaceous of Mexico. Initially regarded as an indeterminate theropod, later studies have mentioned possible affinities with tyrannosaurids, abelisaurids, or carcharodontosaurids. More recent research based on additional fossil material found support for a position within the tyrannosaurine clade Teratophoneini. Two species have been proposed: L. anomala (the type species), likely from the La Bocana Roja Formation, and L. aguillonae from the Cerro del Pueblo Formation.

species.name: Labocania anomala
species.etymology: From Latin 'anomala' meaning 'anomalous', in reference to the distinctive and unusual morphology of the type specimen that set it apart from other theropods.

holotype.institution: Colección Paleontológica de Coahuila, Museo del Desierto (MUDE)

references.authors: Molnar, R. E.
references.title: A distinctive theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Baja California (Mexico)

Laevisuchus.etymology: From Latin 'laevis' (light or smooth) and Greek 'Soukhos' (the ancient Egyptian crocodile god); meaning 'light crocodile'
Laevisuchus.description: Laevisuchus is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous. Its remains were discovered by Charles Alfred Matley near Jabalpur in Maastrichtian "Carnosaur Bed" deposits in the Lameta Formation in Madhya Pradesh, central India, and were named and described by paleontologists Friedrich von Huene and Matley in 1933.

synonyms.name: Jubbulpuria
synonyms.reason: Material previously assigned to Jubbulpuria tenuis is now attributed to Laevisuchus, with apparent differences explained by serial position within the vertebral column.

species.name: Laevisuchus indicus
species.etymology: From Latin 'indicus' meaning 'Indian', referring to India, where the fossil remains were discovered in the Lameta Formation.

references.title: The Cretaceous Saurischia and Ornithischia of the Central Provinces of India

Laiyangosaurus.etymology: Named for Laiyang, a city in Shandong Province, China where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'Laiyang lizard'.
Laiyangosaurus.description: Laiyangosaurus is a genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid from the Late Cretaceous Jingangkou Formation of China. It is known from one species, L. youngi, found in the Laiyang Basin within the province of Shandong.

species.name: Laiyangosaurus youngi
species.etymology: Named for Yang Zhongjian (C.C. Young), the pioneering Chinese vertebrate paleontologist.

Lajasvenator.etymology: Named after the city of Las Lajas in Neuquén, Argentina combined with Latin venator (hunter); meaning "Las Lajas hunter"
Lajasvenator.description: Lajasvenator is a genus of carcharodontosaurid dinosaur from the Mulichinco Formation from Neuquén Province in Argentina. The type and only species is Lajasvenator ascheriae. It was probably one of the smaller known Carcharodontosaurids, being slightly more than half the length of Concavenator, about 3.5 m (11 ft).

species.name: Lajasvenator ascheriae
species.etymology: Named for Susana Ascheri, in recognition of her kindness in allowing the researchers to work on her land.

references.authors: Coria, Rodolfo A.; Currie, Philip J.; Ortega, Francisco; Baiano, Mattia A.

Lambeosaurus.etymology: Named for Canadian paleontologist Lawrence M. Lambe, with the Greek suffix '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Lambeosaurus.description: Lambeosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of western North America. The first skull of Lambeosaurus found was used by palaeontologist Lawrence M. Lambe to justify the creation of the new genus Stephanosaurus, although it was not part of the latter's original material. Its incomplete nature led William A. Parks to name Lambeosaurus lambei for this skull in 1923 to honour Lambe. Multiple species of Lambeosaurus have been named since, including L. clavinitialis and L. magnicristatus in 1935, and L. laticaudus in 1981 which was later moved to its own genus Magnapaulia. It has also been identified that some species earlier identified as belonging to Tetragonosaurus and Corythosaurus are now considered juveniles of Lambeosaurus. It is the eponymous member of the subfamily Lambeosaurinae and tribe Lambeosaurini. Lambeosaurins, which also includes Corythosaurus and Hypacrosaurus from western North America, are understood to be some of the most specialized ornithopods.

synonyms.name: Procheneosaurus
synonyms.reason: Holds species P. praeceps and P. cranibrevis (originally Tetragonosaurus); both are now interpreted as juveniles of Lambeosaurus lambei.

species.etymology: Named for Lawrence Morris Lambe, a Canadian paleontologist who described numerous Cretaceous dinosaurs from Alberta in the early twentieth century.

Lametasaurus.etymology: Named after the Lameta Formation of India where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Lameta lizard'
Lametasaurus.description: Lametasaurus , is a chimeric genus of dinosaur known from the Lameta Formation of Jabalpur, India. The type species is L. indicus. The weight estimate of Lametasaurus, on the basis of the robust tibia, is 3,600 kg (7,900 lb), similar morphology can be seen in the tibia of Pycnonemosaurus, which indicates similar weight estimates.

species.name: Lametasaurus indicus
species.etymology: From Latin 'indicus' meaning 'Indian', referring to India, where the type material was excavated from the Lameta Formation near Jabalpur.

references.authors: Matley, C. A.
references.title: Note on an armoured dinosaur from the Lameta beds of Jubbulpore
references.journal: Records of the Geological Survey of India

Lamplughsaura.etymology: Named in honor of Pamela Lamplugh Robinson, a British paleontologist, combined with Greek 'saura' (lizard); meaning 'Lamplugh's lizard'
Lamplughsaura.description: Lamplughsaura is an extinct genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Sinemurian-aged (Early Jurassic) Dharmaram Formation of India. The genus contains a single species, Lamplughsaura dharmaramensis, known from several partial skeletons of a large quadrupedal animal up to 10 metres (33 ft) long. It has been classified as either a basal sauropod or more basal sauropodomorph.

species.name: Lamplughsaura dharmaramensis
species.etymology: Named for the Dharmaram Formation of the Pranhita-Godavari Basin in India, from which the holotype and referred specimens were recovered.

Lanzhousaurus.etymology: Named for Lanzhou, the capital of Gansu Province, China, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'Lanzhou lizard'.
Lanzhousaurus.description: Lanzhousaurus is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur that lived in the Gansu region of what is now China during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian). Described by You, Ji, and Li in 2005, the type and only species is Lanzhousaurus magnidens, known from a partial skeleton recovered from the Hekou Group. It has been estimated to be about 10 meters (33 ft) in length and 6 metric tons (6.6 short tons) in weight.

species.name: Lanzhousaurus magnidens
species.etymology: From Latin 'magnus' meaning 'great' and 'dens' meaning 'tooth', referring to the exceptionally large teeth that distinguish this genus.
