references.authors: You, H.; Ji, Q.; D. Li
references.title: Lanzhousaurus magnidens gen. et sp. nov. from Gansu Province, China: the largest-toothed herbivorous dinosaur in the world

Laosaurus.etymology: From Greek laas (stone or fossil) and sauros (lizard); meaning "stone or fossil lizard"
Laosaurus.description: Laosaurus is a genus of neornithischian dinosaur. The type species, Laosaurus celer, was first described by O.C. Marsh in 1878 from remains discovered in the Upper Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Morrison Formation of Wyoming. The validity of this genus is doubtful because it is based on fragmentary fossils. A second species also from the Morrison Formation, L. gracilis, and a species from the Upper Cretaceous Allison Formation of Alberta, Canada, L. minimus, are also considered dubious.

species.name: Laosaurus celer
species.etymology: From Latin 'celer' meaning 'swift' or 'fast', in reference to the inferred agility of this small ornithischian.

holotype.institution: Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History

references.authors: Marsh, O. C.
references.title: Notice of new dinosaurian reptiles

Lapampasaurus.etymology: Named after La Pampa Province of Argentina, where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'La Pampa lizard'
Lapampasaurus.description: Lapampasaurus is an extinct genus of hadrosaurid known from the Late Cretaceous Allen Formation (late Campanian or early Maastrichtian stage) of La Pampa Province, Argentina. It contains a single species, Lapampasaurus cholinoi. The generic name refers to the Argentine province of La Pampa. The specific name honours the late collector José Cholino. The material includes cervical, dorsal, sacral and caudal vertebrae, the forelimb girdle, and the partial hindlimb.

species.name: Lapampasaurus cholinoi
species.etymology: Named for the late collector José Cholino, who contributed to the recovery of fossil material from the Allen Formation of La Pampa Province, Argentina.

references.authors: Coria, Rodolfo A.; Riga, Bernardo González; Casadío, Silvio
references.title: Un Nuevo Hadrosáurido (Dinosauria, Ornithopoda) de la Formación Allen, Provincia de la Pampa, Argentina

Laplatasaurus.etymology: Named for La Plata, Argentina, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'La Plata lizard'. The species name refers to the Araucanos (Mapuche) people.
Laplatasaurus.description: Laplatasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in South America, with the holotype and only known specimen found in the Anacleto Formation.

species.name: Laplatasaurus araukanicus
species.etymology: Named for the Araucanos (Mapuche), the indigenous people of Patagonia and central Chile, in whose traditional territory the type material was found.

synonyms.name: Titanosaurus araukanicus
synonyms.reason: Originally described as Titanosaurus araukanicus; the genus name was preoccupied, and the species was reassigned to Laplatasaurus.

references.authors: Huene, F. v.
references.title: Short review of the present knowledge of the Sauropoda

Lapparentosaurus.etymology: Named in honor of French paleontologist Albert-Félix de Lapparent, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Lapparent's lizard'
Lapparentosaurus.description: Lapparentosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic. Its fossils were found in Madagascar (Isalo III Formation). It contains one species, Lapparentosaurus madagascariensis. The genus and species were named by José Bonaparte in 1986. The classification of Lapparentosaurus is controversial, as it exhibits a combination of characteristics of basal sauropods and titanosauriforms.

species.name: Lapparentosaurus madagascariensis
species.etymology: Named for Madagascar, the island nation where the fossil material was discovered in the Isalo III Formation.

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.
references.title: The early radiation and phylogenetic relationships of the Jurassic sauropod dinosaurs, based on vertebral anatomy
references.journal: The Beginning of the Age of Dinosaurs: Faunal Change Across the Triassic–Jurassic Boundary. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge

Laquintasaura.etymology: Named for the La Quinta Formation where it was discovered, combined with the feminine Greek suffix for lizard.
Laquintasaura.description: Laquintasaura is a genus of Venezuelan ornithischian dinosaur containing a single species, Laquintasaura venezuelae. It is known for being one of the most primitive ornithischians in the fossil record, as well as the first dinosaur to have been identified from Venezuela. The name is derived from the La Quinta Formation, where it was discovered, and the feminine Greek suffix for lizard, with the specific name referring to the country of Venezuela. It is known from hundreds of fossil elements, all derived from a single extensive bonebed locality. Initially discovered by French palaeontologists, numerous expeditions have been conducted to excavate from the bonebed, largely led by Marcelo R Sánchez-Villagra. Once thought to represent remains of Lesothosaurus, it was formally named in a 2014 study; much of the abundant material was not yet prepared at the time and research remains ongoing.

species.name: Laquintasaura venezuelae
species.etymology: Named for Venezuela, the country where the holotype bonebed in the La Quinta Formation is located, honoring the country and its people.

holotype.institution: Museo de Biología de la Universidad del Zulia

references.authors: Barrett, Paul M.; Butler, Richard J.; Mundil, Roland; Scheyer, Torsten M.; Irmis, Randall B.; Sánchez-Villagra, Marcelo R.
references.title: A palaeoequatorial ornithischian and new constraints on early dinosaur diversification
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

Latirhinus.etymology: From Latin latus (broad) and Greek rhis (nose); meaning "broad nose"
Latirhinus.description: Latirhinus is an extinct genus of lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mexico. The type species, Latirhinus uitstlani, was named in 2012 on the basis of a partial skeleton from the Campanian-age Cerro del Pueblo Formation. The specific name uitstlani means "southern" in the Náhuatl language of Mexico, a reference to the species' southern occurrence in the Cretaceous landmass Laramidia.

species.name: Latirhinus uitstlani
species.etymology: From the Náhuatl language of Mexico, 'uitstlani' meaning 'southern', in reference to the species' occurrence in the southern part of the Late Cretaceous landmass Laramidia.

holotype.institution: Instituto de Geología, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México

references.authors: Prieto-Márquez, Albert; Serrano Brañas, Claudia Inés
references.title: Latirhinus uitstlani, a ‘broad-nosed’ saurolophine hadrosaurid (Dinosauria, Ornithopoda) from the late Campanian (Cretaceous) of northern Mexico

Lavocatisaurus.etymology: Named for French paleontologist René Lavocat combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'René Lavocat's lizard'. The species name refers to Agrio del Medio, the locality where it was found.
Lavocatisaurus.description: Lavocatisaurus is a genus of sauropod in the family Rebbachisauridae from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian) Rayoso Formation of the Neuquén Basin, northern Patagonia, Argentina.

species.name: Lavocatisaurus agrioensis
species.etymology: Named for Agrio del Medio, the locality in Neuquén Province, Argentina from which the holotype and referred specimens were recovered.

location.locality: 3 km south of Agrio del Medio

holotype.institution: Museo Provincial de Ciencias Naturales "Dr, Prof. Juan A. Olsacher"

references.authors: Canudo, José; Carballido, Jose; Salgado, Leonardo; Garrido, Alberto
references.title: A new rebbachisaurid sauropod from the Aptian–Albian, Lower Cretaceous Rayoso Formation, Neuquén, Argentina
references.publisher: Polska Akademia Nauk Instytut Paleobiologii (Institute of Paleobiology, Polish Academy of Sciences)

Leaellynasaura.etymology: Named after Leaellyn Rich, the daughter of paleontologists Tom Rich and Patricia Vickers-Rich, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Leaellyn's lizard"
Leaellynasaura.description: Leaellynasaura is a genus of small herbivorous ornithischian dinosaurs from the late Aptian to early Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, around 118-110 million years ago. It was first discovered in Dinosaur Cove, Australia. The only known species is Leaellynasaura amicagraphica. It was described in 1989, and named after Leaellyn Rich, the daughter of the Australian palaeontologist couple Tom Rich and Patricia Vickers-Rich who discovered it. The specific name, amicagraphica, translates to "friend writing" and honours both the Friends of the Museum of Victoria and the National Geographic Society for their support of Australian paleontology.

species.name: Leaellynasaura amicagraphica
species.etymology: From Latin 'amicus' meaning 'friend' and Greek 'graphikos' relating to writing or imagery, translating as 'friend writing', honoring both the Friends of the Museum of Victoria and the National Geographic Society for their support of Australian paleontology.

holotype.material: Partial skull

references.authors: Rich, T. H.; Vickers-Rich, P.
references.title: Polar dinosaurs and biotas of the Early Cretaceous of southeastern Australia

Ledumahadi.etymology: From Sesotho meaning 'giant thunderclap', in reference to the animal's enormous size. The species name 'mafube' means 'dawn' in Sesotho.
Ledumahadi.description: Ledumahadi is a genus of lessemsaurid sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation in Free State Province, South Africa. The type and only species is L. mafube, known from a singular incomplete postcranial specimen. A quadruped, it was one of the first giant sauropodomorphs, reaching a weight of around 12 tonnes (13 short tons), despite not having evolved columnar limbs like its later huge relatives.

species.name: Ledumahadi mafube
species.etymology: From Sesotho 'mafube' meaning 'dawn', referring to the early appearance of this giant sauropodomorph at the dawn of sauropod evolution in the Early Jurassic.

holotype.institution: Evolutionary Studies Institute (formerly Bernard Price Institute for Palaeontological Research), University of the Witwatersrand

references.authors: McPhee, Blair W.; Benson, Roger B.J.; Botha-Brink, Jennifer; Bordy, Emese M.; Choiniere, Jonah N.
references.title: A Giant Dinosaur from the Earliest Jurassic of South Africa and the Transition to Quadrupedality in Early Sauropodomorphs

Leinkupal.etymology: From Mapudungun 'lein' (vanishing) and 'kupal' (family); meaning 'vanishing family', in reference to it being the last known diplodocid
Leinkupal.description: Leinkupal is a genus of diplodocine sauropod known from the Early Cretaceous (Late Berriasian to Early Valanginian stage) of the Bajada Colorada Formation, southeastern Neuquén Basin in the Neuquén Province of Argentina. It contains a single species, Leinkupal laticauda.

species.name: Leinkupal laticauda
species.etymology: From Latin 'latus' meaning 'wide' and 'cauda' meaning 'tail', referring to the broad caudal vertebrae that characterize the holotype.

holotype.institution: Museo Municipal ‘Ernesto Bachman’, Villa El Chocón

references.authors: Gallina, Pablo A.; Apesteguía, Sebastián; Haluza, Alejandro; Canale, Juan I.
references.title: A Diplodocid Sauropod Survivor from the Early Cretaceous of South America

Leonerasaurus.etymology: Named after the Las Leoneras Formation in Argentina, where the fossil was found; meaning "Las Leoneras lizard"
Leonerasaurus.description: Leonerasaurus is a basal genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur. Currently, there is only one species known, named L. taquetrensis by Diego Pol, Alberto Garrido and Ignacio A. Cerda in 2011. The fossil, an incomplete subadult individual, was found in the Las Leoneras Formation in Argentina. This formation is probably Early Jurassic in age. Leonerasaurus was a small non-sauropod sauropodomorph, showing an unusual combination of basal and derived characters. This indicates that the evolution of early sauropodomorphs witnessed a great degree of convergent evolution.

species.name: Leonerasaurus taquetrensis
species.etymology: Named for the Sierras de Taquetrén in Central Patagonia, where the Las Leoneras Formation crops out.

references.authors: Pol, Diego; Garrido, Alberto; Cerda, Ignacio A.
references.title: A New Sauropodomorph Dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of Patagonia and the Origin and Evolution of the Sauropod-type Sacrum

Lepidus.description: Lepidus is a genus of extinct theropod from the Upper Triassic of the United States. It lived in the Otis Chalk localities of the Dockum Group in Texas, from 231 to 223 million years ago.

species.name: Lepidus praecisio
species.etymology: From Latin 'praecisio' meaning 'fragment' or 'scrap'.

holotype.institution: Texas Memorial Museum, Austin, Texas, USA (used for collections now housed in the Vertebrate Paleontology Collections at the Jackson School Museum of Earth History, Austin, Texas, USA), now called the Texas Science and Natural History Museum
holotype.material: Articulated distal ends of left tibia and fibula and left astragalocalcaneum

references.authors: Nesbitt, Sterling; EZCURRA, MARTÍN
references.title: The early fossil record of dinosaurs in North America: A new neotheropod from the base of the Upper Triassic Dockum Group of Texas
references.publisher: Polska Akademia Nauk Instytut Paleobiologii (Institute of Paleobiology, Polish Academy of Sciences)

Leptoceratops.etymology: From Greek 'leptos' (small or slender), 'keras' (horn), and 'ops' (face); meaning 'small horn face'
Leptoceratops.description: Leptoceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America. First found in Alberta in 1910, the type species Leptoceratops gracilis was named in 1914 by Barnum Brown for a partial skull and skeleton of two individuals found in the Scollard Formation of Alberta. Additional specimens found in the Scollard include one complete and two mostly complete skeletons together, uncovered in 1947 by Charles M. Sternberg. Specimens from Montana that were among the earliest referred to Leptoceratops have since been moved to their own genera Montanoceratops and Cerasinops, while new specimens of L. gracilis include bonebed remains from the Hell Creek Formation of Montana and a partial skeleton from the Lance Formation of Wyoming. Together with related taxa, Leptoceratops is the eponymous genus of the family Leptoceratopsidae. Leptoceratops is known from more than ten individuals, all from Maastrichtian deposits of Alberta, Montana and Wyoming, representing the entire skeleton.

species.name: Leptoceratops gracilis
species.etymology: From Latin 'gracilis' meaning 'slender', reflecting the slender build of the holotype specimen.

location.locality: 3 miles above Tolman Ferry (190 ft level)

references.authors: Brown, B.
references.title: Leptoceratops, a new genus of Ceratopsia from the Edmonton Cretaceous of Alberta
references.journal: Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History

Leptorhynchos.etymology: From Greek 'leptos' meaning 'slender' or 'thin' and 'rhynchos' meaning 'beak' or 'snout', referring to a slender beak.
Leptorhynchos.description: Leptorhynchos is an extinct genus of caenagnathid theropod from the Late Cretaceous of what is now the US state of Texas, although it has been suggested to also exist in Alberta and South Dakota. The type species is L. gaddisi, and it is currently the only widely accepted valid species. The generic name of Leptorhynchos comes from the Greek "leptos" meaning "small" and "rhynchos" meaning "beak". The specific epithet is in honor of the Gaddis family, who owned the land on which the holotype was discovered.

species.name: Leptorhynchos gaddisi
species.etymology: Named in honor of the Gaddis family, who owned the land on which the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Texas Memorial Museum, Austin, Texas, USA (used for collections now housed in the Vertebrate Paleontology Collections at the Jackson School Museum of Earth History, Austin, Texas, USA), now called the Texas Science and Natural History Museum
holotype.material: Single fused mandible

references.authors: Longrich, Nicholas R.; Barnes, Ken; Clark, Scott; Millar, Larry
references.title: Caenagnathidae from the Upper Campanian Aguja Formation of West Texas, and a Revision of the Caenagnathinae

references.publisher: Bulletin of the Peabody Museum of Natural History

Leshansaurus.etymology: Named after Leshan, the city in Sichuan Province, China, near where fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Leshan lizard'
Leshansaurus.description: Leshansaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Shaximiao Formation of what is now China. It was described in 2009 by a team of Chinese paleontologists. The type species is Leshansaurus qianweiensis. Fossils of Leshansaurus were discovered in strata from the Shangshaximiao Formation, a formation rich in dinosaur fossils. Li et al. referred this taxon to Sinraptoridae – a group of carnosaurian theropods, but it may belong to Megalosauridae instead.

species.name: Leshansaurus qianweiensis
species.etymology: Named for Qianwei County in Sichuan, China, where the holotype fossils were found.

references.authors: Li, F.; Peng, G.; Y. Yong, S. Jiang, D. Huang
references.title: A new carnosaur from the Late Jurassic of Qianwei, Sichuan, China

Lesothosaurus.etymology: Named after Lesotho, the country in southern Africa where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'lizard from Lesotho'
Lesothosaurus.description: Lesothosaurus is a monospecific genus of ornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic in what is now South Africa and Lesotho. It was named by paleontologist Peter Galton in 1978, the name meaning "lizard from Lesotho". The genus has only one valid species, Lesothosaurus diagnosticus. Lesothosaurus is one of the most completely-known early ornithischians, based on numerous skull and postcranial fossils from the Upper Elliot Formation. It had a simpler tooth and jaw anatomy than later ornithischians, and may have been omnivorous in some parts of the year.

synonyms.name: Stormbergia
synonyms.reason: Now generally treated as a junior synonym of Lesothosaurus.

species.name: Lesothosaurus diagnosticus
species.etymology: From Greek 'diagnostikos' meaning 'distinguished', in reference to Lesothosaurus being a distinct member of Fabrosauridae.

references.authors: Galton, Peter M.
references.title: Fabrosauridae, the basal family of ornithischian dinosaurs (Reptilia: Ornithopoda)
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Lessemsaurus.etymology: Named in honor of Don Lessem, a writer of popular science books about dinosaurs, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; the specific name sauropoides means 'sauropod-like', referencing its sauropodiform affinities.
Lessemsaurus.description: Lessemsaurus is an extinct genus of sauropodiform dinosaur that lived in the Norian-aged (Upper Triassic) Los Colorados Formation of what is now Argentina.

species.name: Lessemsaurus sauropoides
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek '-oides' meaning 'resembling', combined with 'sauro-' (lizard/sauropod), meaning 'resembling a sauropod', in reference to its sauropod-like characteristics.

holotype.institution: Colección de Paleontologia de Vertebrados de la Fundación Instituto Miguel Lillo
holotype.material: Partial skeleton cataloged as PVL 4822-1/1 through 4822-1/7 and 4822-1/10

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.
references.title: Evolución de las vértebras presacras en Sauropodomorpha [Evolution of the presacral vertebrae in Sauropodomorpha]

Levnesovia.etymology: Named in honor of the late Russian paleontologist Lev Nessov; the suffix '-ia' is a standard Latinized honorific formation
Levnesovia.description: Levnesovia is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Turonian) Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan. It was related to Bactrosaurus. The type species is L. transoxiana. The genus name honours the late Russian paleontologist Lev Nessov, and the specific name refers to the ancient region Transoxiana. It is known from partial skulls, maxillae, dentaries and numerous bones of the postcranial skeleton.

species.name: Levnesovia transoxiana
species.etymology: Named for Transoxiana, the ancient region of Central Asia where the fossils were found, corresponding to modern Uzbekistan.

holotype.institution: National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution

references.authors: Sues, Hans-Dieter; Averianov, Alexander
references.title: A new basal hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Uzbekistan and the early radiation of duck-billed dinosaurs
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

Leyesaurus.etymology: Named for the Leyes family of Balde de Leyes, who discovered the holotype, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name refers to the Marayes-El Carrizal Basin where the holotype was found.
Leyesaurus.description: Leyesaurus is an extinct genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur known from the San Juan Province, northwestern Argentina.

species.name: Leyesaurus marayensis
species.etymology: Named for the Marayes-El Carrizal Basin in San Juan Province, Argentina, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: División de Paleontología de Vertebrados del Museo de Ciencias Naturales y Universidad Nacional de San Juan

references.authors: Apaldetti, Cecilia; Martinez, Ricardo N.; Alcober, Oscar A.; Pol, Diego
references.title: A New Basal Sauropodomorph (Dinosauria: Saurischia) from Quebrada del Barro Formation (Marayes-El Carrizal Basin), Northwestern Argentina

Liaoceratops.etymology: From 'Liaoning' (the Chinese province where it was discovered) combined with Greek 'keras' (horn) and 'ops' (face); meaning 'Liaoning horned face'
Liaoceratops.description: Liaoceratops, meaning "Liaoning horned face", is a ceratopsian dinosaur believed to be an early relative of the horned ceratopsids. It lived in the Early Cretaceous, 126 million years ago. It was discovered in China by a team of American and Chinese scientists. Liaoceratops was much smaller than its later relatives, but offers a glimpse into the early evolution of this group of dinosaurs.

species.name: Liaoceratops yanzigouensis
species.etymology: Named for Yanzigou, the town in Liaoning Province, China, near where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: Xu, Xing; Makovicky, Peter J.; Wang, Xiao-lin; Norell, Mark A.; You, Hai-lu
references.title: A ceratopsian dinosaur from China and the early evolution of Ceratopsia
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Liaoningosaurus.etymology: Named after Liaoning Province, China, where the fossil was found; meaning "Liaoning lizard"
Liaoningosaurus.description: Liaoningosaurus is an unusual genus of basal ankylosaurid dinosaur from the Liaoning Province, China that lived during the Early Cretaceous (late Barremian to early Aptian stages, ~125.4 to 118.9 Ma) in what is now the Yixian and Jiufotang Formation. The type and only species, Liaoningosaurus paradoxus, is known from more than 20 specimens, represented by juvenile individuals. It was named in 2001 by Xu, Wang and You.

species.name: Liaoningosaurus paradoxus
species.etymology: From Latin 'paradoxus' meaning 'paradoxical' or 'contrary to expectation', in reference to the suite of highly unusual traits this dinosaur possesses for an ankylosaur.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: Xu, Xing; Wang, Xiao-Lin; You, Hai-Lu
references.title: A juvenile ankylosaur from China
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Liaoningotitan.etymology: Named after Liaoning Province, China combined with Greek titan (giant); meaning "Liaoning giant"
Liaoningotitan.description: Liaoningotitan is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Yixian Formation in Liaoning, China. A redescription of the holotype proposed affinities of Liaoningotitan with the Euhelopodidae.

species.name: Liaoningotitan sinensis
species.etymology: From Latin 'sinensis' meaning 'from China', referring to the country where the holotype was found.

references.authors: Zhou, C.-f.; Wu, W.-h.; T. Sekiya, Z.-m. Dong
references.title: [A new titanosauriformes dinosaur from Jehol Biota of western Liaoning, China]

Liaoningvenator.etymology: Named after Liaoning Province, China combined with Latin venator (hunter); meaning "Liaoning hunter"
Liaoningvenator.description: Liaoningvenator is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China. It contains a single species, L. curriei, named after paleontologist Phillip J. Currie in 2017 by Shen Cai-Zhi and colleagues from an articulated, nearly complete skeleton, one of the most complete troodontid specimens known. Shen and colleagues found indicative traits that placed Liaoningvenator within the Troodontidae. These traits included its numerous, small, and closely packed teeth, as well as the vertebrae towards the end of its tail having shallow grooves in place of neural spines on their top surfaces.

species.name: Liaoningvenator curriei
species.etymology: Named for paleontologist Phillip J. Currie, honored in the genitive Latin '-i' suffix.

holotype.material: Nearly complete, well-preserved articulated skeleton

references.authors: Shen, C.-z.; Zhao, B.; C.-l. Gao, J.-c. Lü, M. Kundrát
references.title: A new troodontid dinosaur (Liaoningvenator curriei gen. et sp. nov.) from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation in western Liaoning Province

Ligabueino.etymology: Named for Italian doctor and fossil enthusiast Giancarlo Ligabue, its discoverer, with the diminutive '-ino' suffix in Italian meaning 'little one', hence 'Ligabue's little one'.
Ligabueino.description: Ligabueino is a genus of abelisauroid theropod dinosaur named after its discoverer, Italian doctor Giancarlo Ligabue. It is known only from an extremely fragmentary specimen, measuring 79 cm (2.6 ft) long, found in the La Amarga Formation. In spite of initial reports that it was an adult, the unfused vertebrae indicate that the specimen was a juvenile. It was a theropod and lived during the Early Cretaceous Period (Barremian to early Aptian), in what is now Patagonia. Contrary to initial classifications that placed it as a member of the Noasauridae, Carrano and colleagues found in 2011 that it could only be placed with any confidence in the group Abelisauroidea. In 2024, Ligabueino was recovered as a sister taxon of Berthasauridae and Abelisauroidea.

species.name: Ligabueino andesi
species.etymology: Named for the Andes mountains of South America, where the holotype was found in Patagonia, Argentina, in the genitive form 'andesi' meaning 'of the Andes'.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales ‘Bernardino Rivadavia’

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.
references.title: Cretaceous tetrapods of Argentina

Ligabuesaurus.etymology: Named in honor of Giancarlo Ligabue, an Italian explorer and naturalist who supported paleontological research.
Ligabuesaurus.description: Ligabuesaurus is a genus of somphospondylan sauropod from the Early Cretaceous Lohan Cura Formation of what is now Argentina. The type species, Ligabuesaurus leanzai, was described in 2006, based on a partial skeleton with a skull. The generic name, Ligabuesaurus, honors Giancarlo Ligabue, while the specific name, leanzai, honors the geologist Dr. Héctor A. Leanza, who discovered the skeleton in the Lohan Cura Formation.

species.name: Ligabuesaurus leanzai
species.etymology: Named for geologist Dr. Héctor A. Leanza, who discovered the skeleton in the Lohan Cura Formation of Patagonia, Argentina.

references.authors: Bonaparte, José F.; González Riga, Bernardo J.; Apesteguía, Sebastián
references.title: Ligabuesaurus leanzai gen. et sp. nov. (Dinosauria, Sauropoda), a new titanosaur from the Lohan Cura Formation (Aptian, Lower Cretaceous) of Neuquén, Patagonia, Argentina

Liliensternus.etymology: Named for German paleontologist Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern, who collected early specimens of this dinosaur.
Liliensternus.description: Liliensternus is an extinct genus of basal neotheropod dinosaur that lived approximately 210 million years ago during the latter part of the Triassic Period in what is now Germany. Liliensternus was a bipedal, ground-dwelling carnivore, that could grow up to 5.15 m (16.9 ft) long; however, this size estimate is based on specimens now believed to be subadults, and possible fragmentary remains indicate an adult length of 7 to 9 meters. It is the best represented Triassic theropod from Europe and one of the largest known.

species.name: Liliensternus liliensterni
species.etymology: Named for Count Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern, an amateur paleontologist and medical doctor who discovered the holotype specimens in Germany and founded a paleontological museum in his castle.

holotype.material: Partial and fragmentary skeletons of at least two individuals including skull elements, lower jaws, vertebrae, and appendicular skeleton

references.authors: Welles, S. P.
references.title: Dilophosaurus wetherilli (Dinosauria, Theropoda): osteology and comparisons

Limaysaurus.etymology: Named after the Rio Limay, which borders the fossil locality in northwestern Patagonia; meaning "Limay lizard"
Limaysaurus.description: Limaysaurus is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaurs which lived during the late Cretaceous period, about 99.7 to 94 million years ago, in the Cenomanian, in what is now South America (northwestern Patagonia). It is represented by a single species, L. tessonei.

species.name: Limaysaurus tessonei
species.etymology: Named for Lieto Francisco Tessone, who discovered the first and most complete holotype specimen in 1988 in Neuquén Province, Argentina.

references.title: Lower Cretaceous rebbachisaurid sauropods from Cerro Aguada del León (Lohan Cura Formation), Neuquén Province, northwestern Patagonia, Argentina

Limusaurus.etymology: From Latin 'limus' meaning 'mud' or 'mire' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'mire lizard', referring to the specimens appearing to have died after being mired in mud.
Limusaurus.description: Limusaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now China during the Late Jurassic, around 161 to 157 million years ago. The type and only species Limusaurus inextricabilis was described in 2009 from specimens found in the Upper Shishugou Formation in the Junggar Basin of China. The genus name consists of the Latin words for "mud" and "lizard", and the species name means "impossible to extricate", both referring to these specimens possibly dying after being mired. Limusaurus was a small, slender animal, about 1.7 m (5 ft 7 in) in length and 15 kg (33 lb) in weight, which had a long neck and legs but very small forelimbs (with reduced first and fourth fingers). It underwent a drastic morphological transformation as it aged: while juveniles were toothed, these teeth were completely lost and replaced by a beak with age. Several of these features were convergently similar to the later ornithomimid theropods as well as the earlier non-dinosaurian shuvosaurids.

species.name: Limusaurus inextricabilis
species.etymology: From Latin 'inextricabilis' meaning 'impossible to extricate', referring to the specimens' likely fate of dying after becoming mired in mud pits created by the footprints of giant sauropods.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

Lingwulong.etymology: From 'Lingwu' (the city in Ningxia, China near the discovery site) and Chinese 'long' (dragon); meaning 'Lingwu dragon'
Lingwulong.description: Lingwulong is a genus of diplodocoid sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of what is now Lingwu, Yinchuan, Ningxia, China. The type and only species is L. shenqi, known from several partial skeletons. It is one of the earliest neosauropods ever discovered, as well as the only definitive diplodocoid from east Asia.

species.name: Lingwulong shenqi
species.etymology: From Mandarin Chinese 'shenqi' (神奇) meaning 'amazing' or 'magical', reflecting the unexpected discovery of a diplodocoid sauropod in East Asia, a group never before identified in the region.

Lingyuanosaurus.etymology: Named for the county-level city of Lingyuan in Liaoning Province, China, where it was discovered, combined with Ancient Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; the specific name sihedangensis also references the discovery locality, the town of Sihedang.
Lingyuanosaurus.description: Lingyuanosaurus is a genus of therizinosaurian theropod from the Early Cretaceous of Liaoning Province, China. The type and only species is L. sihedangensis. It was uncovered within one of the formations that make up the Jehol biota, although the exact geological formation — and therefore also its precise geological age — is unknown.

species.name: Lingyuanosaurus sihedangensis
species.etymology: Named for Sihedang, the town near the type locality in Liaoning Province, China.

Linhenykus.etymology: Named for Linhe, a city near the fossil discovery site in Inner Mongolia, combined with Greek 'nykus' meaning 'claw'.
Linhenykus.description: Linhenykus is an extinct genus of alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Inner Mongolia, China. It is the most basal known member of the Parvicursorinae. The genus gets its name from Linhe, a city near the site where the fossil was first found and Greek nykus, "claw". The specific name is derived from Greek monos, "single", and daktylos, "finger", a reference to the fact that it is the only known non-avian dinosaur to have had but a single digit.

species.name: Linhenykus monodactylus
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'monos' meaning 'single' and 'daktylos' meaning 'finger', referring to the fact that Linhenykus is the only known non-avian dinosaur with a single functional digit on each forelimb.

Linheraptor.etymology: Named for Linhe, a city in Inner Mongolia near the fossil discovery site, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief' or 'plunderer'.
Linheraptor.description: Linheraptor is a genus of dromaeosaurid dinosaur which lived in what is now China in the Late Cretaceous. It was named by Xu Xing and colleagues in 2010, and contains the species Linheraptor exquisitus. This bird-like dinosaur was less than 2 m (6.5 ft) long and was found in Inner Mongolia. It is known from a single, nearly complete skeleton.

species.name: Linheraptor exquisitus
species.etymology: From Latin 'exquisitus' meaning 'exquisite' or 'excellent', referring to the exceptionally well-preserved nature of the holotype skeleton.

Linhevenator.description: Linhevenator is a genus of short-armed troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Bayan Mandahu Formation of Bayan Mandahu, Inner Mongolia, China.

Lirainosaurus.etymology: From Basque lirain (slender) combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "slender lizard"
Lirainosaurus.description: Lirainosaurus is a genus of titanosaur sauropod which lived in what is now Spain. The type species, Lirainosaurus astibiae, was described by Sanz, Powell, Le Loeuff, Martinez, and Pereda-Suberbiola in 1999. It was a relatively small sauropod, measuring 4 metres (13 ft) long, possibly up to 6 metres (20 ft) long for the largest individuals, and weighed about 2–4 metric tons (2.2–4.4 short tons).

species.name: Lirainosaurus astibiae
species.etymology: Named in honor of Dr. Humberto Astibia, leader of the research at the outcrop in Lano.

Lishulong.description: Lishulong is a genus of sauropodiform dinosaur from the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian–Toarcian) Lufeng Formation of China. The type and only species is Lishulong wangi.

species.name: Lishulong wangi
species.etymology: Named for Wang Zheng-Ju, discoverer of Lufengpithecus and contributor to vertebrate paleontology in Lufeng, China, honored in the genitive Latin '-i' suffix.

Liubangosaurus.etymology: Named after Liubang village, the holotype locality in Guangxi Province, China; meaning "Liubang lizard"
Liubangosaurus.description: Liubangosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now China. Liubangosaurus is known from the holotype NHMG 8152, five complete and articulated middle-caudal dorsal vertebrae that were collected from the Xinlong Formation in Fusui County, Guangxi Province. The type species is L. hei, which honors He Wenjian, who discovered the site where Liubangosaurus was discovered.

Llukalkan.etymology: From Mapuche llukalkan meaning "one who causes fear" or "one who scares"

Lohuecotitan.etymology: Named for Lo Hueco, the fossil site in Spain where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'.
Lohuecotitan.description: Lohuecotitan is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which lived during the Late Cretaceous in Spain. The only species known in the genus is Lohuecotitan pandafilandi, described and named in 2016.

Lokiceratops.etymology: Named for Loki, the Norse god, combined with Greek 'ceratops' meaning 'horned face' (from 'keras' meaning 'horn' and 'ops' meaning 'face'), hence 'Loki horned face'. The species name 'rangiformis' means 'reindeer-shaped' in reference to its elaborate ornamentation.
Lokiceratops.description: Lokiceratops is an extinct genus of centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Judith River Formation of Montana, United States. The genus contains a single species, L. rangiformis, known from most of the skull and a partial skeleton. Four other ceratopsians are known from the same stratigraphic interval as Lokiceratops—more than in any other locality—suggesting that this clade was very diverse during the Late Cretaceous of northern Laramidia.

species.name: Lokiceratops rangiformis
species.etymology: From Latin 'rangiformis' meaning 'reindeer-shaped', referencing the mammal genus Rangifer (caribou or reindeer) whose antlers are bilaterally asymmetrical like the frill ornamentations of Lokiceratops.

holotype.institution: Dinosaur Forest and Museum of Evolution, Knuthenborg Safaripark

Loncosaurus.etymology: Meaning uncertain; either from Araucanian 'lonco' meaning 'chief' or Greek 'lonche' meaning 'lance', combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Loncosaurus.description: Loncosaurus is an extinct genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina. The type (and only known) species is Loncosaurus argentinus, described by the famous Argentinian paleontologist Florentino Ameghino, but is considered a dubious name. Details on this animal are often contradictory, befitting a genus that was long confused for a theropod.

Lophorhothon.etymology: From Greek 'lophos' meaning 'crested' and 'rhothon' meaning 'nose', giving the meaning 'crested nose', referring to the nasal crest of the holotype.
Lophorhothon.description: Lophorhothon is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Alabama, and possibly Georgia and North Carolina. It was the first dinosaur genus discovered in Alabama, in the United States.

Lophostropheus.etymology: From Greek 'lophè' meaning 'crest' and 'stropheus' meaning 'pertaining to the vertebrae', giving the meaning 'crest vertebrae', referring to the prominent dorsal and ventral laminae on the cranial cervical vertebrae.
Lophostropheus.description: Lophostropheus is an extinct genus of coelophysoid theropod dinosaur that lived approximately 205.6 to 196.5 million years ago during the boundary between the Late Triassic Period and the Early Jurassic Period, in what is now Normandy, France. Lophostropheus is one of the few dinosaurs that may have survived the Triassic–Jurassic extinction event.

Loricatosaurus.etymology: From Latin loricatus (armored) combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "armored lizard"
Loricatosaurus.description: Loricatosaurus is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur known from Callovian-aged (Middle Jurassic) rocks of England and France.

species.name: Loricatosaurus priscus
species.etymology: From Latin 'priscus' meaning 'ancient' or 'of former times', reflecting the prehistoric nature of the animal when originally named Stegosaurus priscus by Baron Franz Nopcsa in 1911.

Loricosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'lorica' meaning 'armor' or 'cuirass' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'armor lizard', in reference to the bony armor associated with this titanosaur.
Loricosaurus.description: Loricosaurus is a genus of sauropod represented by a single species, L. scutatus. It is a titanosaur that lived near the end of the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 71 million years ago in the early Maastrichtian, being found in the province of Neuquen, Argentina in the Allen Formation. Due to the presence of armor, at first it was believed that it was an ankylosaur, but today it is considered to be that of a titanosaur.

species.etymology: From Latin 'australis' meaning 'southern', referring to the southern location of the Neuquén Province of Argentina where the holotype fossils were discovered.

Losillasaurus.etymology: Named after Losilla, the village near the fossil locality in Valencia, Spain; meaning "Losilla lizard"
Losillasaurus.description: Losillasaurus is a genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic and possibly Early Cretaceous (Kimmeridgian-?Berriasian) of southeastern Spain. The type species, Losillasaurus giganteus, was discovered in the Villar del Arzobispo Formation in Valencia, and formally described by Casanovas, Santafé, and Sanz in 2001. The holotype material is from a subadult and includes part of a skull; complete cervical, dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae as well as several fragments; skeletal elements from the limbs including a humerus, ulna, radius, and metacarpal; sternal plates; and from the pelvis: the ilium, ischium, and pubis. The genus is characterized by the dimension and shape of the neural spine of the proximal caudal vertebrae. The humerus is 143 centimetres (56 in) long, which despite being from a subadult specimen is within 20% of the size of Paralititan. The size estimation proposed by Francisco Gascó in his master thesis is 15–18 m (49–59 ft) in length and 12–15 t (13–17 short tons) in body mass.

species.name: Losillasaurus giganteus
species.etymology: From Latin 'giganteus' meaning 'gigantic', referring to the large size of this sauropod, whose humerus alone measures 143 centimetres.

Lourinhanosaurus.etymology: Named for Lourinhã, the town in Portugal near where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'Lourinhã lizard'. The species name honours Portuguese paleontologist Miguel Telles Antunes.
Lourinhanosaurus.description: Lourinhanosaurus was a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic Period (Kimmeridgian/Tithonian) in Portugal. It is one of many large predators discovered at the Lourinhã Formation and probably competed with coeval Torvosaurus gurneyi, Allosaurus europaeus, and Ceratosaurus.

species.etymology: Named for Portuguese paleontologist Miguel Telles Antunes, honored in the genitive Latin '-i' suffix.

Lourinhasaurus.etymology: Named after Lourinhã, the municipality in Portugal associated with the fossil-bearing formation, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'lizard from Lourinhã'
Lourinhasaurus.description: Lourinhasaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur dating from Late Jurassic strata of Estremadura, Portugal. The genus is monotypic, containing one species, Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis. The type specimen for this species was discovered near the town of Alenquer, near an abandoned mill. The specimen is housed at the Geological Museum of Lisbon. The research history of Lourinhasaurus is not without controversies, with referred specimens later being interpreted as not belonging to the genus (such as the type specimen of Supersaurus (=Dinheirosaurus) lourinhanensis). Lourinhasaurus means "lizard from Lourinhã" literally translated, despite the fact that the type specimen wasn't found in the Lourinhã municipality.

Luanchuanraptor.etymology: Named after Luanchuan, Henan Province, China combined with Latin raptor (thief/seizer); meaning "Luanchuan thief"
Luanchuanraptor.description: Luanchuanraptor is a genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of China. Lucianovenator.etymology: Named for Don Luciano Leyes, who first reported the fossil remains, combined with Latin 'venator' meaning 'hunter'.
Lucianovenator.description: Lucianovenator is an extinct genus of coelophysid theropod dinosaur which lived in Argentina during the Triassic. The genus name Lucianovenator translates to "Luciano's hunter", in reference to Don Luciano Leyes, who first reported the remains. The species name bonoi refers to Tulio del Bono, a local scientific authority who collaborated on the describers' research. It is one of the few neotheropods known from South America.

The type species is L. liudianensis. Holtz estimated it at 1.5 meters (4.9 ft) and around 2.27–9.1 kilograms (5.0–20.1 lb). Lurdusaurus.etymology: From Latin 'lurdus' meaning 'heavy' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'heavy lizard', in reference to its massive proportions. The species name 'arenatus' is Latin for 'sandy', as it was found in a desert.
Lurdusaurus.description: Lurdusaurus is a genus of massive and unusually shaped iguanodont dinosaur from the Elrhaz Formation in Niger. It contains one species, L. arenatus. The formation dates to the Early Cretaceous, roughly 112 million years ago.

synonyms.name: Gravisaurus
synonyms.reason: Informal name; never met ICZN requirements for formal publication and is treated as referable to Lurdusaurus. Per Olshevsky's Dinosaur Genera List.

species.name: Lurdusaurus arenatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'arenatus' meaning 'sandy', because the holotype was found in a desert environment at the Gadoufaoua site of Niger.

references.authors: Taquet, Philippe; Russell, Dale A.
references.title: A massively-constructed iguanodont from Gadoufaoua, lower Cretaceous of Niger

Lusotitan.etymology: From 'Luso-' (the Latin term for an inhabitant of Lusitania, i.e., Portugal) combined with Greek 'Titan' (a mythological giant); meaning 'Portuguese titan' or 'Lusitanian titan'
Lusotitan.description: Lusotitan is a genus of herbivorous brachiosaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of Portugal.

species.name: Lusotitan atalaiensis
species.etymology: Named for Atalaia, the site in Portugal where the holotype fossils were discovered.

holotype.institution: Museu Geológico do Instituto Geológico e Mineiro

references.authors: Antunes, Miguel Telles; Mateus, Octávio
references.title: Dinosaurs of Portugal

Lusovenator.etymology: From Latin Luso- (Portuguese, referring to Lusitania/Portugal) combined with Latin venator (hunter); meaning "Portuguese hunter"
Lusovenator.description: Lusovenator is a genus of carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Praia de Amoreira Porto-Novo Member and the Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous (Tithonian-Berriasian) Assenta Member of the Lourinhã Formation in present-day Portugal. It includes one species, Lusovenator santosi.

species.name: Lusovenator santosi
species.etymology: Named for José Joaquim dos Santos, who discovered the holotype during the 1980s and later donated his fossil collection to the Sociedade de História Natural.

location.locality: cliffs north of Praia de Valmitão

holotype.material: Partial postcranial skeleton: odontoid, atlantal intercentrum, cervical vertebra, isolated cervical neural spines, dorsal vertebrae, sacral fragments, caudal vertebrae, chevrons, rib fragments, right ilium, both pubes and ischia

references.authors: Malafaia, Elisabete; Mocho, Pedro; Escaso, Fernando; Ortega, Francisco
references.title: A new carcharodontosaurian theropod from the Lusitanian Basin: evidence of allosauroid sympatry in the European Late Jurassic

Lycorhinus.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'lykos' (wolf) and 'rhinos' (nose); meaning 'wolf nose', referring to the shape of the snout or teeth
Lycorhinus.description: Lycorhinus is a genus of heterodontosaurid ornithischian dinosaur from the Early Jurassic (Hettangian to Sinemurian ages) strata of the Elliot Formation located in the Cape Province, South Africa.

synonyms.name: Lanasaurus
synonyms.reason: Additional material allowed direct comparison and demonstrated that Lanasaurus is referable to Lycorhinus.

species.name: Lycorhinus angustidens
species.etymology: From Latin 'angustus' meaning 'narrow' and 'dens' meaning 'tooth', referring to the narrow teeth of the holotype jaw.

location.locality: Buck Camp, Golden Gate Highlands NP

references.authors: Haughton, S. H.
references.title: The fauna and stratigraphy of the Stormberg Series
references.journal: Annals of the South African Museum

Lythronax.etymology: From Greek 'lythron' (λύθρον) meaning 'gore' and 'anax' (ἄναξ) meaning 'king', hence 'gore king'. The species name is from Greek 'argestes' (ἀργεστής), Homer's name for the wind from the southwest, referring to where the specimen was found in North America.
Lythronax.description: Lythronax is a genus of tyrannosaurid dinosaur that lived in North America around 81.9-81.5 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period. The only known specimen was discovered in Utah in the Wahweap Formation of the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument in 2009, and it consists of a partial skull and skeleton. In 2013, it became the basis of the new genus and species Lythronax argestes; the generic name Lythronax means "gore king", and the specific name argestes originates from the Greek poet Homer's name for the wind from the southwest, in reference to the specimen's geographic provenance in North America.

species.name: Lythronax argestes
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'argestes', a name used by the poet Homer for the wind from the southwest, in reference to where the specimen was found within North America.

holotype.material: Partial skull and skeleton including skull bones, dorsal rib, caudal chevron, both pubic bones, left tibia, fibula, and left second and fourth metatarsals

references.authors: Loewen, Mark A.; Irmis, Randall B.; Sertich, Joseph J. W.; Currie, Philip J.; Sampson, Scott D.
references.title: Tyrant Dinosaur Evolution Tracks the Rise and Fall of Late Cretaceous Oceans

Machairasaurus.etymology: From Greek 'makhaira' (short scimitar or curved blade) and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'scimitar lizard', referring to the sabre-like hand claws
Machairasaurus.description: Machairasaurus is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur which was found in the Bayan Mandahu Formation, China, dating to the late Cretaceous period.

species.name: Machairasaurus leptonychus
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'leptos' meaning 'slender' and 'onyx' meaning 'claw', referring collectively to the sabre-like hand claws of the animal.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: LONGRICH, NICHOLAS R.; CURRIE, PHILIP J.; ZHI-MING, DONG
references.title: A new oviraptorid (Dinosauria: Theropoda) from the Upper Cretaceous of Bayan Mandahu, Inner Mongolia

Machairoceratops.etymology: From Greek machairis (bent sword) combined with ceratops (horned face); meaning "bent sword horned face", referring to the two forward-curving frill horns
Machairoceratops.description: Machairoceratops , previously known as the "Wahweap centrosaurine B", is an extinct genus of centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Wahweap Formation (late Campanian stage) of Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument, southern Utah, United States.

species.name: Machairoceratops cronusi
species.etymology: Named for Cronus, the Greek god who deposed his father Uranus using a curved bladed weapon, alluding to the forward-curving horns on the frill of this ceratopsian.

holotype.material: Partial skull including eyesocket horncores, left jugal, nearly complete braincase, left squamosal, and parietal bone complex

references.authors: Lund, Eric K.; O’Connor, Patrick M.; Loewen, Mark A.; Jinnah, Zubair A.
references.title: A New Centrosaurine Ceratopsid, Machairoceratops cronusi gen et sp. nov., from the Upper Sand Member of the Wahweap Formation (Middle Campanian), Southern Utah

Macrocollum.etymology: From Greek 'makros' (long) and Latin 'collum' (neck); meaning 'long neck', referring to the animal's elongated neck
Macrocollum.description: Macrocollum is a genus of unaysaurid sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic period (early Norian) in what is now Brazil. It is one of the oldest dinosaurs known.

species.name: Macrocollum itaquii
species.etymology: Named for José Jerundino Machado Itaqui, one of the principal figures behind the creation of the Centro de Apoio à Pesquisa Paleontológica da Quarta Colônia (CAPPA/UFSM).

holotype.institution: Centro de Apoio à Pesquisa Paleontológica da Quarta Colônia, Universidade Federal de Santa Maria

references.authors: Müller, Rodrigo Temp; Langer, Max Cardoso; Dias-da-Silva, Sérgio
references.title: An exceptionally preserved association of complete dinosaur skeletons reveals the oldest long-necked sauropodomorphs

Macrogryphosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'makros' meaning 'large', 'gryphos' meaning 'enigmatic', and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'big enigmatic lizard'. The species name 'gondwanicus' refers to the ancient continent of Gondwana.
Macrogryphosaurus.description: Macrogryphosaurus is a genus of elasmarian dinosaur from the Coniacian age Upper Cretaceous Sierra Barrosa Formation (Neuquén Group) of Argentina in Patagonia. It was described by Jorge Calvo and colleagues in 2007, with M. gondwanicus as the type and only species.

species.name: Macrogryphosaurus gondwanicus
species.etymology: Named for Gondwana, the ancient southern supercontinent, reflecting the South American provenance of this ornithopod.

references.authors: Calvo, J. O.; Porfiri, J. D.; F. E. Novas
references.title: Discovery of a new ornithopod dinosaur from the Portezuelo Formation (Upper Cretaceous), Neuquén, Patagonia, Argentina
references.journal: Arquivos do Museu Nacional, Rio de Janeiro

Macrurosaurus.etymology: From Greek makros (large) and oura (tail); meaning "large-tailed lizard"
Macrurosaurus.description: Macrurosaurus is the name given to a genus of dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous. It was a titanosauriform which lived in what is now England. The type species, M. semnus, was named in 1876. A second species, M. platypus, may also exist.

species.name: Macrurosaurus semnus
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'semnos' meaning 'stately' or 'impressive', an allusion to the imposing size inferred from the large caudal vertebrae.

references.authors: Seeley, Harry G.
references.title: Discovery of Dakosaurus in England

Magnamanus.etymology: From Latin 'magna' (large) and 'manus' (hand); meaning 'large hand', likely referring to its broad hand morphology
Magnamanus.description: Magnamanus is an extinct genus of herbivorous iguanodontian dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Spain in the Golmayo Formation. It contains a single species, Magnamanus soriaensis.

species.name: Magnamanus soriaensis
species.etymology: Named for Soria, the Spanish province where the holotype skeleton was excavated at the Zorralbo I site.

holotype.material: Partial skeleton cataloged as MNS 200/132, 2001/122, 2002/95, 2003/69, and 2004/54

references.authors: Fuentes Vidarte, C.; Meijide Calvo, M.; F. Meijide Fuentes, M. Meijide Fuentes
references.title: Un nuevo dinosaurio estiracosterno (Ornithopoda: Ankylopollexia) del Cretácico Inferior de España [A new styracosternan dinosaur (Ornithopoda: Ankylopollexia) from the Lower Cretaceous of Spain]

Magnapaulia.etymology: From Latin 'magnus' meaning 'large' and the first name of Paul G. Haaga Jr., president of the board of trustees of the Los Angeles County Museum of Natural History, honoring his support of the institution.
Magnapaulia.description: Magnapaulia is a genus of herbivorous lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) El Gallo Formation of Baja California, northwestern Mexico. It contains a single species, Magnapaulia laticaudus, which was first described in 1981 as a possible species of Lambeosaurus by William J. Morris, and was given its own genus in 2012 by Prieto-Márquez and colleagues.

species.name: Magnapaulia laticaudus
species.etymology: From Latin 'latus' meaning 'broad' and 'cauda' meaning 'tail', referring to the tall, laterally broad tail of this hadrosaurid.

holotype.institution: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County

references.authors: Prieto-Márquez, Albert; Chiappe, Luis M.; Joshi, Shantanu H.
references.title: The Lambeosaurine Dinosaur Magnapaulia laticaudus from the Late Cretaceous of Baja California, Northwestern Mexico

Magnosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'magnus' (large) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'large lizard'
Magnosaurus.description: Magnosaurus was a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of England. It is based on fragmentary remains and has often been confused with or included in Megalosaurus.

species.name: Magnosaurus nethercombensis
species.etymology: Named for Nethercomb, the village near Sherborne in Dorset, England, where the holotype partial skeleton was found.

holotype.institution: Oxford University Museum of Natural History
holotype.material: Partial lower jaw

references.authors: Huene, F. v.
references.title: Die fossile Reptil-Ordnung Saurischia, ihre Entwicklung und Geschichte [The fossil reptile order Saurischia, their development and history]
references.journal: Monographien zur Geologie und Palaeontologie, serie 1

Magyarosaurus.etymology: From Hungarian 'Magyar' meaning 'Hungarian' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; named for Hungary, the country that controlled the Transylvanian region where it was found at the time of discovery.
Magyarosaurus.description: Magyarosaurus is a genus of dwarf sauropod dinosaur from late Cretaceous Period (early to late Maastrichtian) in today's Transylvania. It is one of the smallest-known adult sauropods, measuring less than 3 m (9.8 ft) long and weighing less than 1,000 kg (2,200 lb). The type and only species is Magyarosaurus dacus. It has been found to be a close relative of Rapetosaurus in the family Saltasauridae in the sauropod clade Titanosauria in a 2005 study.

species.name: Magyarosaurus dacus
species.etymology: Named for the Dacians, the ancient people who inhabited the Transylvanian region of present-day Romania approximately two thousand years ago.

references.authors: Huene, F. v.
references.title: Die fossile Reptil-Ordnung Saurischia, ihre Entwicklung und Geschichte [The fossil reptile order Saurischia, their development and history]
references.journal: Monographien zur Geologie und Palaeontologie, serie 1

Mahakala.etymology: Named after Mahakala, a deity common to Hinduism and Buddhism.
Mahakala.description: Mahakala is a genus of halszkaraptorine theropod dinosaur from the Campanian-age (about 80 million years ago) Upper Cretaceous Djadokhta Formation of Ömnögovi, Mongolia. It is based on a partial skeleton found in the Gobi Desert. Mahakala was a small dromaeosaurid, and its skeleton shows features that are also found in early troodontids and avialans. Despite its late appearance, it is among the most basal dromaeosaurids. Its small size, and the small size of other basal deinonychosaurians, suggests that small size appeared before flight capability in birds.

species.name: Mahakala omnogovae
species.etymology: Named for Ömnögovi (South Gobi Province) of Mongolia, where the holotype was discovered, with the genitive Latin suffix '-ae' meaning 'of'.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Turner, Alan H.; Pol, Diego; Clarke, Julia A.; Erickson, Gregory M.; Norell, Mark A.
references.title: A Basal Dromaeosaurid and Size Evolution Preceding Avian Flight
references.publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

Mahuidacursor.etymology: From Mapudungun 'mahuida' meaning 'mountain' and Latin 'cursor' meaning 'runner'; translates as 'mountain runner'.
Mahuidacursor.description: Mahuidacursor is a genus of basal ornithopod dinosaur from the Santonian Bajo de la Carpa Formation of the Neuquén Basin in northern Patagonia, Argentina. The type and only species is M. lipanglef.

species.name: Mahuidacursor lipanglef
species.etymology: From the Mapuche 'lipang' meaning 'arm' and 'lef' meaning 'lightly', in reference to the gracile nature of the specimen, particularly the slender architecture of its forelimbs.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino Urquiza, Rincón de los Sauces

references.authors: Cruzado-Caballero, Penélope; Gasca, José M.; Filippi, Leonardo S.; Cerda, Ignacio A.; Garrido, Alberto C.
references.title: A new ornithopod dinosaur from the Santonian of Northern Patagonia (Rincón de los Sauces, Argentina)

Maiasaura.etymology: From Greek 'maia' (good mother) and 'saura' (the feminine form of sauros, lizard); meaning 'good mother lizard' or 'good mother reptile', referring to evidence of parental care
Maiasaura.description: Maiasaura is a large herbivorous saurolophine hadrosaurid ("duck-billed") dinosaur genus that lived in the area currently covered by the state of Montana and the Canadian province of Alberta, in the Upper Cretaceous (mid to late Campanian), from 86.3 to 70.6 million years ago. Maiasaura is the state fossil of Montana.

species.name: Maiasaura peeblesorum
species.etymology: Named for the families of John and James Peebles, on whose land the holotype and associated nesting site were discovered in Montana.

holotype.institution: Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History

references.authors: Horner, John R.; Makela, Robert
references.title: Nest of juveniles provides evidence of family structure among dinosaurs
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Maip.etymology: Named for Maip, a malicious being in Aonikenk (Tehuelche) mythology described as 'the shadow of death' that 'kills with cold wind', from the indigenous traditions of Patagonia.
Maip.description: Maip is a genus of large megaraptorid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) Chorrillo Formation of Santa Cruz, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, M. macrothorax, known from an incomplete, disarticulated skeleton. Maip may represent the largest megaraptorid known from South America, and possibly the world.

species.name: Maip macrothorax
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'makros' meaning 'large' and Latin 'thorax' meaning 'chest', in reference to the notably large thoracic cavity of this megaraptorid.

references.authors: Aranciaga Rolando, Alexis M.; Motta, Matias J.; Agnolín, Federico L.; Manabe, Makoto; Tsuihiji, Takanobu; Novas, Fernando E.
references.title: A large Megaraptoridae (Theropoda: Coelurosauria) from Upper Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of Patagonia, Argentina
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Majungasaurus.etymology: Named after Mahajanga (formerly Majunga), a city and region in northwestern Madagascar where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Mahajanga lizard'
Majungasaurus.description: Majungasaurus is a genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in Madagascar from 70 to 66 million years ago, at the end of the Cretaceous Period, making it one of the last-known non-avian dinosaurs that went extinct during the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event. The genus contains a single species, Majungasaurus crenatissimus. This dinosaur is also called Majungatholus, a name which is considered a junior synonym of Majungasaurus.

synonyms.name: Majungatholus
synonyms.reason: Initially erected as a separate genus due to the lack of overlapping material; subsequently recognized as referable to Majungasaurus.

species.name: Majungasaurus crenatissimus
species.etymology: From Latin 'crenatus' meaning 'notched' combined with the superlative suffix '-issimus' meaning 'most', referring to the numerous serrations on both the front and rear edges of the teeth.

holotype.material: Partial skull and skeleton (ICZN Opinion 2269, 2011)

references.authors: Lavocat, R.
references.title: Sur une portion de mandibule de théropode provenant du Crétacé supérieur de Madagascar [On a portion of theropod mandible from the Upper Cretaceous of Madagascar]
references.journal: Bulletin du Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle, Paris, 2e série

Malarguesaurus.etymology: Named after the Malargüe Department of Mendoza Province, Argentina, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Malargüe lizard'.
Malarguesaurus.description: Malarguesaurus is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mendoza Province, Argentina. Its fossils, consisting of tail vertebrae, chevrons, ribs, and limb bones, were found in the upper Turonian-lower Coniacian Portezuelo Formation of the Neuquén Group. The type species, described by González Riga et al. in 2008, is M. florenciae.

species.name: Malarguesaurus florenciae
species.etymology: Named in honor of Florencia Fernandez Favaron, who collaborated in years of fieldwork and found the first fossil remains of this species.

location.locality: Quebrada Norte Quarry, Paso de las Bardas

holotype.institution: Instituto Argentino de Nivologia Glaciologia y Ciencias Ambientales

references.authors: González Riga, Bernardo J.; Previtera, Elena; Pirrone, Cecilia A.
references.title: Malarguesaurus florenciae gen. et sp. nov., a new titanosauriform (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the Upper Cretaceous of Mendoza, Argentina

Malawisaurus.etymology: Named for Malawi, the African country where its fossils were discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Malawisaurus.description: Malawisaurus is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur. It is known from the Dinosaur Beds of northern Malawi, which probably date to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous. The type species is M. dixeyi and the specific name honours Frederick Augustus Dixey.

species.name: Malawisaurus dixeyi
species.etymology: Named for Frederick Augustus Dixey, honoring his contributions to the discovery and study of fossils in Malawi.

references.authors: Jacobs, L. L.; Winkler, D. A.; W. R. Downs, E. M. Gomani
references.title: New material of an Early Cretaceous titanosaurid sauropod dinosaur from Malawi

Maleevus.etymology: Named in honor of Soviet paleontologist Evgeny Maleev; the suffix '-us' is a standard Latinized honorific formation
Maleevus.description: Maleevus is an extinct genus of herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaur from the late Cretaceous, around 90 million years ago (possibly 98-83 Ma), of Mongolia.

synonyms.name: Syrmosaurus
synonyms.reason: Has a complex reassignment history (Talarurus, Pinacosaurus, Maleevus); tentatively treated as a synonym of Maleevus pending further research.

species.name: Maleevus disparoserratus
species.etymology: From Latin 'dispar' meaning 'unequal' and 'serratus' meaning 'serrated', referring to the unequal serrations observed on the teeth of the holotype jaw bones.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Tumanova, T. A.
references.title: Pantsirnyye dinozavry Mongolii [The armored dinosaurs of Mongolia]

Malefica.etymology: From Latin 'malefica', meaning 'witch' or 'sorceress', referring to its discovery in Bruja Canyon ('bruja' being Spanish for 'witch').
Malefica.description: Malefica is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Aguja Formation of Texas. The type and only species is Malefica deckerti.

species.name: Malefica deckerti
species.etymology: Named for Frank Deckert, the specimen's discoverer and former superintendent of Big Bend National Park.

holotype.institution: Texas Memorial Museum, Austin, Texas, USA (used for collections now housed in the Vertebrate Paleontology Collections at the Jackson School Museum of Earth History, Austin, Texas, USA), now called the Texas Science and Natural History Museum

references.authors: Prieto-Márquez, Albert; Wagner, Jonathan R.
references.title: A new ‘duck-billed’ dinosaur (Ornithischia: Hadrosauridae) from the upper Campanian of Texas points to a greater diversity of early hadrosaurid offshoots

Mamenchisaurus.etymology: Named after Mamenchi (a transliteration of the Chinese place name for a ferry crossing, Maming Creek), where the first fossils were found near Yibin, Sichuan, China, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Mamenchi lizard'
Mamenchisaurus.description: Mamenchisaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaurs known for their remarkably long necks, which made up nearly half the total body length. Numerous species have been assigned to the genus; however, the validity of these assignments has been questioned. Fossils have been found in the Sichuan Basin and Yunnan Province in China. Several species from the Upper Shaximiao Formation, whose geologic age is uncertain, have been described. However, evidence suggests this formation to be no earlier than the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic. M. sinocanadorum dates to the Oxfordian stage (161.2 to 158.7 mya), and M. anyuensis to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous (around 114.4 mya). Most species were medium-large to large sauropods, measuring roughly 15 to 26 meters (49 to 85 ft) in length—possibly up to 35 meters (115 ft), based on two undescribed vertebrae.

synonyms.name: Moshisaurus
synonyms.reason: Informal name; never met ICZN requirements for formal publication and is treated as referable to Mamenchisaurus. Per Olshevsky's Dinosaur Genera List.

species.name: Mamenchisaurus constructus
species.etymology: From Latin 'constructus' meaning 'constructed' or 'built', chosen because the holotype fossil was discovered during construction work on the Yitang Highway in Sichuan Province, China.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: Young, C.-C.
references.title: On a new sauropod from Yiping, Szechuan, China

Mandschurosaurus.etymology: Named for Manchuria (Mandschuria in German), the region of China where its fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Mandschurosaurus.description: Mandschurosaurus is an extinct genus of hadrosaurids based on material from the Late Cretaceous of China and possibly also the Early Cretaceous of Laos. It was the first dinosaur genus named from China.

species.name: Mandschurosaurus amurensis
species.etymology: Named for the Amur River in China, on whose banks the holotype skeleton was collected.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
holotype.material: Fragmentary postcranial remains

references.authors: Riabinin, A. N.
references.title: Mandschurosaurus amurensis nov. gen. nov. sp., verkhnemelovoy dinozavr s. r. Amura [Mandschurosaurus amurensis nov. gen, nov. sp., a hadrosaurian dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of the Amur River]

Manidens.etymology: From Latin 'manus' (hand) and 'dens' (tooth), referring to the hand-shaped form of the posterior lower teeth.
Manidens.description: Manidens is an extinct genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of Patagonia. It is a sister taxon of the closely related Pegomastax from South Africa. Fossils have been found in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation in Chubut Province, Argentina, considered to be originally dated to the Bajocian, latter were found to be from Toarcian beds.

species.name: Manidens condorensis
species.etymology: Named for the village of Cerro Cóndor in Chubut Province, Argentina, located near the Queso Rallado site where the holotype was found.

references.authors: Pol, Diego; Rauhut, Oliver W. M.; Becerra, Marcos
references.title: A Middle Jurassic heterodontosaurid dinosaur from Patagonia and the evolution of heterodontosaurids
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Mansourasaurus.etymology: Named for Mansoura University in Egypt, the institution whose paleontologists discovered and described it, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Mansourasaurus.description: Mansourasaurus is a genus of herbivorous lithostrotian sauropod dinosaur from the Quseir Formation of Egypt. The type and only species is Mansourasaurus shahinae.

species.name: Mansourasaurus shahinae
species.etymology: Named for Mona Shahin, one of the founders of the Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center in Egypt.

location.locality: north of road between Mut and Balat

holotype.institution: Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center, Department of Geology

references.authors: Sallam, Hesham M.; Gorscak, Eric; O’Connor, Patrick M.; El-Dawoudi, Iman A.; El-Sayed, Sanaa; Saber, Sara; Kora, Mahmoud A.; Sertich, Joseph J. W.; Seiffert, Erik R.; Lamanna, Matthew C.
references.title: New Egyptian sauropod reveals Late Cretaceous dinosaur dispersal between Europe and Africa
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Mantellisaurus.etymology: Named for Gideon Mantell, the English geologist and paleontologist who first described Iguanodon, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Mantellisaurus.description: Mantellisaurus is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur that lived in the Barremian and early Aptian ages of the Early Cretaceous Period of Europe. Its remains are known from Belgium (Bernissart), England, Spain and Germany. The type and only species is M. atherfieldensis. Formerly known as Iguanodon atherfieldensis, the new genus Mantellisaurus was erected for the species by Gregory Paul in 2007. According to Paul, Mantellisaurus was more lightly built than Iguanodon and more closely related to Ouranosaurus, making Iguanodon in its traditional sense paraphyletic. It is known from many complete and almost complete skeletons. The genus name honours Gideon Mantell, the discoverer of Iguanodon.

synonyms.name: Heterosaurus
synonyms.reason: Initially described as its own genus in 1850 and later reassigned to Iguanodon; subsequent study placed the material in Mantellisaurus.

synonyms.name: Vectisaurus
synonyms.reason: Now generally interpreted as a juvenile individual of Mantellisaurus.

synonyms.name: Proplanicoxa
synonyms.reason: Originally referred to Vectisaurus valdensis and later re-erected as Proplanicoxa; with Vectisaurus now considered a juvenile of Mantellisaurus, Proplanicoxa is also treated as a junior synonym.

synonyms.name: Dollodon
synonyms.reason: Possible junior subjective synonym of Mantellisaurus; identification is tentative. Per Olshevsky's Dinosaur Genera List.

species.name: Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis
species.etymology: Named for Atherfield, a village on the southwest shore of the Isle of Wight, England, where the holotype fossil was discovered.

synonyms.name: Mantellodon
synonyms.reason: M. carpenteri is now considered referable to Mantellisaurus atherfieldensis.

Mapusaurus.etymology: From Mapudungun 'mapu' (earth or land) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'earth lizard'
Mapusaurus.description: Mapusaurus is a genus of giant carcharodontosaurid carnosaurian dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Cenomanian–Turonian ages of the Late Cretaceous. It is known from a bonebed of between seven and nine specimens, excavated from the strata of the Huincul Formation between 1997 and 2001 as part of the Argentinian-Canadian Dinosaur Project. In 2006, Rodolfo Coria and Philip J. Currie scientifically described Mapusaurus. Only one species of Mapusaurus, M. roseae, has been described, named after the rose-colored rocks in which it was discovered and sponsor Rose Letwin.

species.name: Mapusaurus roseae
species.etymology: Named for both the rose-colored rocks in which the fossils were found and for Rose Letwin, who sponsored the expeditions that recovered the specimens.

Maraapunisaurus.etymology: From Ute 'maraapuni' meaning 'it is very large' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', giving the meaning 'very large lizard', named for the enormous estimated size of the specimen.
Maraapunisaurus.description: Maraapunisaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of western North America. It contains one species, Maraapunisaurus fragillimus, which was originally named Amphicoelias fragillimus. It has sometimes been estimated to be the largest dinosaur specimen ever discovered. Based on surviving descriptions of a single fossil bone, scientists have produced numerous size estimates over the years; the largest estimate M. fragillimus to have been the longest known animal at 58 metres (190 ft) in length with a mass of 150 tonnes (150 long tons; 170 short tons). However, because the only fossil remains were lost at some point after being studied and described in the 1870s, evidence survived only in contemporary drawings and field notes.

species.name: Maraapunisaurus fragillimus
species.etymology: From Latin 'fragillimus', the superlative of 'fragilis' meaning 'very fragile', chosen by Cope to describe the extreme delicateness of the bone produced by very thin vertebral laminae.

Marmarospondylus.description: Marmarospondylus is a dubious genus of sauropod dinosaur from Middle Jurassic deposits in the English Midlands.

Marshosaurus.etymology: Named for Othniel Charles Marsh, the pioneering American paleontologist, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Marshosaurus.description: Marshosaurus is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur, belonging to the family Piatnitzkysauridae, from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of Utah and possibly Colorado.

species.name: Marshosaurus bicentesimus
species.etymology: Named in honor of the bicentennial of the United States of America, as the species was described around the time of the 1976 American bicentennial celebrations.

Martharaptor.etymology: Named in honor of Martha C. Hayden, the paleontologist assistant who helped discover the Hayden-Corbett site in the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah where the specimen was found, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief'.
Martharaptor.description: Martharaptor is a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Utah. They can be distinguished from other therizinosauroids by means of several features of the skeleton (particularly the hands and feet) which were intermediate between early therizinosaurs such as Falcarius and Beipiaosaurus, and more "advanced" members of the group like therizinosaurids. The deep and homogeneous hand claws clearly differ from the case in early therizinosauroids, but the foot has not yet acquired the robust morphology of therizinosaurids.

species.name: Martharaptor greenriverensis
species.etymology: Named for Green River, the city in Utah near which the holotype was excavated from the Cedar Mountain Formation.
