Masiakasaurus.etymology: From Malagasy 'masiaka' meaning 'vicious' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'vicious lizard'.
Masiakasaurus.description: Masiakasaurus is a genus of small predatory theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of Madagascar. In Malagasy, masiaka means "vicious"; thus, the genus name means "vicious lizard". The type species, Masiakasaurus knopfleri, was named after the musician Mark Knopfler, whose music inspired the expedition crew. It was named in 2001 by Scott D. Sampson, Matthew Carrano, and Catherine A. Forster. Unlike most theropods, the front teeth of Masiakasaurus projected forwards instead of straight down. This unique dentition suggests that they had a specialized diet, perhaps including fish and other small prey. Other bones of the skeleton indicate that Masiakasaurus were bipedal, with much shorter forelimbs than hindlimbs. It was a small theropod, reaching 1.8–2.1 m (5.9–6.9 ft) long and weighing 20 kg (44 lb). Masiakasaurus lived from 72.1 to 66 million years ago, along with animals such as Majungasaurus, Rapetosaurus, and Rahonavis. Masiakasaurus was a member of the group Noasauridae, small predatory ceratosaurs found primarily in South America.

species.name: Masiakasaurus knopfleri
species.etymology: Named for Mark Knopfler, the guitarist and singer-songwriter of Dire Straits, whose music inspired and accompanied the expedition crew during fieldwork in Madagascar.

Massospondylus.etymology: From Greek 'massos' meaning 'longer' and 'spondylos' meaning 'vertebra', referring to what Richard Owen identified as elongated tail vertebrae.
Massospondylus.description: Massospondylus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of southern Africa. It was described by Richard Owen in 1854 from remains discovered in South Africa, and is thus one of the first dinosaurs to have been named. The name Massospondylus means 'longer vertebra', alluding to what Owen identified as tail vertebrae; these vertebrae are now known to be from the neck. Although the original fossils were destroyed in London during The Blitz, a plethora of specimens have since been assigned to the genus, making it one of the best-known sauropodomorphs from the Early Jurassic. The genus lived during the Hettangian, Sinemurian, and Pliensbachian ages, which lasted from ca. 201 to 184 million years ago. Most fossils come from the upper Elliot and Clarens formations of South Africa and Lesotho, but the genus is also found in the Forest Sandstone and the Mpandi Formation of Zimbabwe. Material from the US, India, and Argentina was previously assigned to the genus, but the US and Argentinian specimens are now assigned to their own genera (Sarahsaurus and Adeopapposaurus). Because of their great abundance, Massospondylus fossils have been used to date rocks, and a biozone, the Massospondylus Range Zone, is named after the genus.

Matheronodon.etymology: Named after French paleontologist Philippe Matheron, combined with Greek 'odon' (tooth); meaning 'Matheron's tooth'.
Matheronodon.description: Matheronodon is a genus of rhabdodontid ornithopod dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of the Grès à Reptiles Formation in France. The genus contains a single species, M. provincialis, which is known from a single maxilla and associated teeth. It was named by Pascal Godefroit and colleagues in 2017. The teeth of Matheronodon are large but few in number. The teeth are also in an unusual arrangement, emerging alternatingly from one of a pair of fused tooth sockets in its mouth. In life, the teeth would have functioned like a pair of scissors, allowing Matheronodon to feed on the tough leaves of monocot plants.

species.etymology: From Latin 'provincialis' meaning 'of the province', referring to Provence, the region of southeastern France where all known specimens were found.

Megalosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'megas' (big, tall, or great) and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'great lizard'.
Megalosaurus.description: Megalosaurus is an extinct genus of large carnivorous theropod dinosaurs of the Middle Jurassic Epoch (Bathonian stage, 166 million years ago) of southern England. Although fossils from other areas have been assigned to the genus, the only certain remains of Megalosaurus come from Oxfordshire and date to the late Middle Jurassic.

Megapnosaurus.description: Megapnosaurus is an extinct genus of coelophysid theropod dinosaur that lived approximately 188 million years ago during the early part of the Jurassic Period in what is now Africa. The species was a small to medium-sized, lightly built, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore, that could grow up to 2.2 m (7.2 ft) long and weigh up to 13 kg (29 lb).

Megaraptor.etymology: From Greek 'megas' (large) and Latin 'raptor' (one who seizes or thief); meaning 'large thief' or 'large raptor'
Megaraptor.description: Megaraptor is a genus of large theropod dinosaur, the type genus and namesake of the clade Megaraptora and family Megaraptoridae. Its fossils have been discovered in the Patagonian Portezuelo Formation of Argentina, South America, dating to the Turonian and Coniacian ages of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 90–88 million years ago. One species of Megaraptor, M. namunhuaiquii, has thus been named, known from seven partial or fragmentary skeletons, with only two including skull elements.

It is represented by several partial skeletons from a single locality within the Coniacian (lower Upper Cretaceous) Sierra Barrosa Formation in the south of Mendoza Province, northern Neuquén Basin, Argentina.

It walked on two legs, had short front arms, a characteristic ceratopsian frill and beak-like mouth, and was around 60 cm (2.0 ft) long. It was one of the most primitive ceratopsians, or horned dinosaurs, along with Psittacosaurus, which was also discovered in Mongolia.

Microraptor.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' (small) and Latin 'raptor' (one who seizes); meaning 'small thief' or 'small raptor'
Microraptor.description: Microraptor is a genus of small, four-winged dromaeosaurid dinosaurs. Numerous well-preserved fossil specimens have been recovered from Liaoning, China. They date from the early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation (Aptian stage), 125 to 120 million years ago. Three species have been named (M. zhaoianus, M. gui, and M. hanqingi), though further study has suggested that all of them represent variation in a single species, which is properly called M. zhaoianus. Cryptovolans, initially described as another four-winged dinosaur, is usually considered to be a synonym of Microraptor.

Microvenator.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' meaning 'small' and Latin 'venator' meaning 'hunter'; translates as 'small hunter', named for its small size.
Microvenator.description: Microvenator is a genus of oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Cloverly Formation in what is now south central Montana. The holotype fossil is an incomplete skeleton, most likely a juvenile with a length of 1.3 m (4.3 ft), and consequently, the adult size remains uncertain. Microvenator is primitive and may be the "sister taxon to all other oviraptorosaurs."

Mierasaurus.etymology: Named for Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, an eighteenth-century Spanish cartographer and explorer of the American Southwest, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Mierasaurus.description: Mierasaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Utah, United States. The taxon was first described and named in 2017 by Rafael Royo-Torres and colleagues, from a mostly complete skeleton including a disarticulated partial skull and mandible, teeth, multiple vertebrae from along the length of the body, both scapulae, radius and ulna bones, a left manus, a complete pelvis, both femora and the entire left hindlimb. Additionally, they referred a lower jaw and femur from juvenile individuals, which were found nearby, to the genus. Collectively, Mierasaurus is among the most completely known North American sauropods. The genus name honours Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, the first European scientist to enter what is now Utah. The type species for Mierasaurus is Mierasaurus bobyoungi, named after Robert Glen Young, a paleontologist who researched the Early Cretaceous of Utah.

Migmanychion.etymology: From Greek 'meigma' (mixture) and 'nychion' (claw); meaning 'claw mixture', referring to the mix of claw features in the specimen.
Migmanychion.description: Migmanychion is an extinct genus of maniraptoran theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Longjiang Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, M. laiyang, known from an incomplete left forelimb.

Minimocursor.etymology: From Latin 'minimus' meaning 'the smallest' and 'cursor' meaning 'runner'; translates as 'smallest runner', referring to the small size of the holotype.
Minimocursor.description: Minimocursor is a genus of basal neornithischian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Phu Kradung Formation of Thailand. The type species is Minimocursor phunoiensis.

Minotaurasaurus.etymology: Named after the Minotaur of Greek mythology (the bull of Minos) combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Minos's bull reptile'.
Minotaurasaurus.description: Minotaurasaurus is a monospecific genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian stage, ~75-71 Ma) in what is now the Djadochta Formation. The type and only species, Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani, is known from two skulls, a cervical vertebra and a cervical half ring. It was named and described in 2009 by Clifford Miles and Clark Miles. The holotype of Minotaurasaurus has been suspected to be illegally exported out of Mongolia. It has been suggested to be a synonym of Tarchia but more recent publications consider it as a distinct genus.

Minqaria.etymology: From Arabic 'minqaria' meaning 'beak', a reference to the beak-like nature of the hadrosaurid jaw.
Minqaria.description: Minqaria is a genus of lambeosaurine dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco. The genus contains a single species, Minqaria bata, known from a partial skull.

species.name: Minqaria bata

Miragaia.description: Miragaia is a genus of long-necked stegosaurid dinosaur. Its fossils have been found in Upper Jurassic rocks in Portugal (Lourinhã Formation, Sobral Unit) and possibly also Wyoming and Utah, United States (Morrison Formation). Miragaia has the longest neck known for any stegosaurian, which included at least seventeen vertebrae. Some researchers consider this taxon to be a junior synonym of Dacentrurus.

Mirischia.description: Mirischia is an extinct genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Albian stage (Early Cretaceous Period) of northeastern Brazil.

Moabosaurus.etymology: Named for Moab, Utah, the city near the Dalton Wells Quarry where the fossils were collected, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Moabosaurus.description: Moabosaurus is a genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah, United States.

Mochlodon.description: Mochlodon is a genus of rhabdodontid dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of Austria and Hungary. It lived during the Late Cretaceous (85-80 Ma) and two species have been named, M. suessi and M. vorosi, although the latter has been regarded as a junior synonym of the ceratopsian Ajkaceratops.

Mongolostegus.etymology: From 'Mongol' (Mongolia, where it was found) and Greek 'stegos' (roof); meaning 'Mongolian roof', referencing Mongolia and its classification as a stegosaur.
Mongolostegus.description: Mongolostegus is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian–Albian ages) Dzunbain Formation of Mongolia. The genus contains a single species, Mongolostegus exspectabilis, known from a fragmentary single specimen representing the first stegosaur named from Mongolia. It is one of the youngest known stegosaurs, along with Yanbeilong and an unnamed species from the Hekou Group of China. In contrast to these taxa, which are members of the late-diverging stegosaur subfamily Stegosaurinae, Mongolostegus may have affinities to more basal taxa such as the Huayangosauridae.

Monkonosaurus.description: Monkonosaurus is a dubious genus of herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic/Early Cretaceous-aged Loe-ein Formation of Tibet (or the Early Cretaceous Lura Formation of China). Some sources place it as alive during the Oxfordian - Albian stages, around 163 - 100 million years ago, although Monkonosaurus was probably only alive during the Late Jurassic (163 – 152.1 ± 0.9 million years ago), making it among the earliest known stegosaurs along with Chungkingosaurus and Bashanosaurus.

Monolophosaurus.description: Monolophosaurus is an extinct genus of tetanuran theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Shishugou Formation in what is now Xinjiang, China. It was named for the single crest on top of its skull. Monolophosaurus was a mid-sized theropod at about 5–5.5 metres (16–18 ft) long and weighed 475 kilograms (1,047 lb).

Mononykus.description: Mononykus is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia, specifically the Nemegt Formation. Mononykus was a very small theropod, estimated around 1 to 1.2 metres (3.3 to 3.9 ft) in length with a weight of 3.5 kilograms (7.7 lb). As in Shuvuuia, Mononykus likely developed a shaggy feathering. It was lightly built with long, thin legs and highly reduced and specialized forelimbs that were likely used for foraging termite mounds or other insect colonies.

Muttaburrasaurus.etymology: Named for Muttaburra, a town in Queensland, Australia near where the fossil was discovered, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Muttaburrasaurus.description: Muttaburrasaurus was a genus of herbivorous iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur that lived in what is now north-eastern Australia sometime between 112 and 103 million years ago during the early Cretaceous period. It has been recovered in some analyses as a member of the iguanodontian clade Rhabdodontomorpha, or alternately as a member of Elasmaria. After Kunbarrasaurus, it is Australia's most completely known dinosaur from skeletal remains. It was named after Muttaburra, the site in Queensland, Australia, where it was found. The dinosaur was selected from twelve candidates to become the official fossil emblem of the State of Queensland.

species.name: Muttaburrasaurus langdoni
species.etymology: Named for Doug Langdon, the grazier who discovered the holotype specimen at Rosebery Downs Station near Muttaburra, Queensland, in 1963.

references.authors: Bartholomai, A.; Molnar, R. E.

Muyelensaurus.etymology: Named after 'Muyelen', an indigenous name for the Colorado River in Argentina, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Muyelen lizard'.
Muyelensaurus.description: Muyelensaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina. It was more slender than other titanosaurs. Fossils have been recovered in the Neuquén province of Patagonia and were originally assigned to the Portezuelo Formation but further research showed that these layers belong to the Plottier Formation. The type species is M. pecheni. The name Muyelensaurus first appeared in a 2007 paper by Argentine paleontologists Jorge Calvo of the Universidad Nacional del Comahue and Bernardo González Riga of the Laboratorio de Paleovertebrados, and Brazilian paleontologist Juan Porfiri of the Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro.

species.name: Muyelensaurus pecheni

Mymoorapelta.etymology: Named after the Mygatt-Moore Quarry (combining the names of its discoverers) combined with Greek 'pelta' (shield); meaning 'shield from the Mygatt-Moore Quarry'.
Mymoorapelta.description: Mymoorapelta is a nodosaurid ankylosaur from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian-Tithonian, around 155 to 150 million years ago) Morrison Formation (Brushy Basin Member) of western Colorado and central Utah, USA. The animal is known from a single species, Mymoorapelta maysi, and few specimens are known. The most complete specimen is the holotype individual from the Mygatt-Moore Quarry, which includes osteoderms, a partial skull, vertebrae, and other bones. It was initially described by James Kirkland and Kenneth Carpenter in 1994. Along with Gargoyleosaurus, it is one of the earliest known nodosaurids.

species.name: Mymoorapelta maysi
species.etymology: Named for Chris Mays, president of the Dinamation International Corporation and Society, who funded the initial excavation of the Mygatt-Moore Quarry where the holotype was found.

Naashoibitosaurus.etymology: From Navajo naʼashǫ́ʼii bitooh, meaning 'creek lizard'; named after the Naashoibito Member of the Kirtland Formation where the specimen was thought to have been found
Naashoibitosaurus.description: Naashoibitosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived about 73 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous, and was found in the Kirtland Formation of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico, United States. Only a partial skeleton has been found to date. It was first described as a specimen of Kritosaurus by Jack Horner, and has been intertwined with the taxon since its description.

Nambalia.etymology: Derived from Nambal village, located near the discovery site in Telangana, central India
Nambalia.description: Nambalia is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur. It lived during the Late Triassic period (late Norian to earliest Rhaetian) in what is now Telangana, central India. It is known from the holotype ISI R273, parts 1–3, partially articulated postcranial material and from the paratypes ISI R273, parts 4-29, including partial postcrania of at least two individuals of different sizes found closely associated and one of them is nearly the same size as the holotype.

species.name: Nambalia roychowdhurii
species.etymology: Named for Dr. Roy Chowdhuri, honoring his research on the Triassic vertebrate faunas of India.

Nankangia.etymology: Named after Nankang County (now Nankang District), Ganzhou City, Jiangxi Province, China, where the specimen was found
Nankangia.description: Nankangia is an extinct genus of caenagnathoid oviraptorosaurian dinosaur known from the Upper Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of Nankang County, Ganzhou City of Jiangxi Province, southeastern China. It contains a single species, Nankangia jiangxiensis. N. jiangxiensis coexisted with at least four other caenagnathoids, including but not limited to Corythoraptor, Banji, Ganzhousaurus and Jiangxisaurus. The relatively short dentary and non-downturned mandibular symphysis of Nankangia suggest that it may have been more herbivorous than carnivorous. Its diet consisted of leaves and seeds.

species.name: Nankangia jiangxiensis
species.etymology: Named for Jiangxi Province, China, where the holotype site is located.

Nanningosaurus.description: Nanningosaurus is a genus of hadrosauromorph dinosaur from the upper Late Cretaceous of the Nalong Basin, Guangxi, China.

Nanosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'nanos' (small or dwarf) and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'small or dwarf lizard'.
Nanosaurus.description: Nanosaurus is an extinct genus of neornithischian dinosaur that lived about 155 to 148 million years ago, during the Late Jurassic in North America. Its fossils are known from the Morrison Formation of the south-western United States. The type and only species, Nanosaurus agilis, was described and named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877. The taxon has a complicated taxonomic history, largely the work of Marsh and Peter M. Galton, involving the genera Laosaurus, Hallopus, Drinker, Othnielia, and Othnielosaurus, the latter three now being considered to be synonyms of Nanosaurus. It had historically been classified as a hypsilophodont or fabrosaur, types of generalized small bipedal herbivore, but more recent research has abandoned these groupings as paraphyletic and Nanosaurus is today considered a basal member of Neornithischia.

Nanshiungosaurus.etymology: Named after Nanxiong (formerly romanized as Nanshiung), a city in Guangdong Province, China, where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Nanxiong's lizard'.
Nanshiungosaurus.description: Nanshiungosaurus is a genus of therizinosaurid that lived in what is now Asia during the Late Cretaceous of South China. The type species, Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus, was first discovered in 1974 and described in 1979 by Dong Zhiming. It is represented by a single specimen preserving most of the cervical and dorsal vertebrae with the pelvis. A supposed and unlikely second species, "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini, was found in 1992 and described in 1997. It is also represented by vertebrae but this species however, differs in geological age and lacks authentic characteristics compared to the type, making its affinity to the genus unsupported.

species.name: Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus
species.etymology: From Latin 'brevis' meaning 'short' and 'spina' meaning 'spine', in reference to the relatively short vertebral spines of the holotype.

Nanuqsaurus.etymology: From Inupiaq 'nanuq' (polar bear) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'polar bear lizard', referring to its Arctic Alaska discovery locality.
Nanuqsaurus.description: Nanuqsaurus is a genus of tyrannosaurine theropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Latest Campanian age) Prince Creek Formation of the North Slope of Alaska. It contains a single species, Nanuqsaurus hoglundi, known from a partial skull and multiple undescribed postcranial and teeth elements.

Nanyangosaurus.etymology: Named for Nanyang, a city in Henan Province, China near where it was found, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Nanyangosaurus.description: Nanyangosaurus is a genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur belonging to the Hadrosauromorpha that lived in the Late Cretaceous of present-day Henan Province, China.

Narambuenatitan.etymology: Refers to Puesto Narambuena, the locality in northern Patagonia, Argentina, where the fossil was found, combined with Greek Titan (a giant)
Narambuenatitan.description: Narambuenatitan is a genus of lithostrotian titanosaur sauropod from late Cretaceous (lower-middle Campanian stage) deposits of northern Patagonia of Argentina. Narambuenatitan is known from the holotype MAU-Pv-N-425, an incomplete skeleton. It was collected in 2005 and 2006 from the Anacleto Formation (Neuquén Group) in northern Patagonia. It was first named by Leonardo S. Filippi, Rodolfo A. García and Alberto C. Garrido in 2011 and the type species Narambuenatitan palomoi. The generic name refers to Puesto Narambuena. The specific name honours the discoverer, Salvador Palomo.

Narindasaurus.etymology: Named after Narinda Bay in northwestern Madagascar, where its fossils were collected, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Narinda Bay lizard'.
Narindasaurus.description: Narindasaurus is a genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Isalo III Formation of Madagascar. The type and only species is Narindasaurus thevenini. The only known specimen of the genus was first described in 1907, but it was not formally named as a distinct species until 2020.

Nasutoceratops.etymology: From Latin 'nasutus' meaning 'large-nosed' and Latinized Greek 'ceratops' meaning 'horned face'; translates as 'large-nosed horned face', referring to its distinctive enlarged nasal region.
Nasutoceratops.description: Nasutoceratops is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous period, about 76.0–75.5 million years ago. The first known specimens were discovered in Utah in the Kaiparowits Formation of the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument (GSENM) from 2006 onwards, including a subadult skull with both a partial postcranial skeleton and rare skin impressions, and two other partial skulls. In 2013, the subadult was made the holotype of the new genus and species Nasutoceratops titusi; the generic name means "large-nosed horned face", and the specific name honors the paleontologist Alan L. Titus for his work at the GSENM. The dinosaur was noted for its large nose in news reports, and later featured in Jurassic World films.

Natovenator.etymology: From Latin nato ('to swim') and venator ('hunter'), meaning 'swimming hunter', reflecting the proposed semi-aquatic lifestyle of this halszkaraptorine
Natovenator.description: Natovenator is a genus of halszkaraptorine dromaeosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia. The genus is known from a single species, N. polydontus. Natovenator is crucial to the understanding of halszkaraptorines due to it providing more support for the semi-aquatic lifestyle that has been proposed for this clade. This discovery is important as the semi-aquatic lifestyles of halszkaraptorines (mainly Halszkaraptor) was contested in early 2022.

Navajoceratops.etymology: Named after the Navajo people of the American Southwest, combined with Greek 'keras' (horn) and 'ops' (face); meaning 'Navajo horned face'.
Navajoceratops.description: Navajoceratops is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of what is now North America. The genus contains a single species, N. sullivani, named after Robert M. Sullivan, leader of the expeditions that recovered the holotype.

Nebulasaurus.etymology: From Latin 'nebulae' meaning 'misty cloud', in reference to Yunnan Province (meaning 'southern misty cloudy province') where the fossil was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Nebulasaurus.description: Nebulasaurus is an extinct genus of basal eusauropod dinosaur known from the early Middle Jurassic Zhanghe Formation (Aalenian or Bajocian stage) of Yunnan Province, China. It is known only from the holotype braincase LDRC-v.d.1. A phylogenetic analysis found Nebulasaurus to be a sister taxon to Spinophorosaurus from the Middle Jurassic of Africa. This discovery is significant paleontologically because it represents a clade of basal eusauropods previously unknown from Asia.

Nedcolbertia.description: Nedcolbertia is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian-aged) Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah. The type and only described species so far is N. justinhofmanni, known from at least three partial skeletons.

Neimongosaurus.description: Neimongosaurus is a genus of herbivorous therizinosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Cretaceous period. Its fossils are known from the strata of the Iren Dabasu Formation. It is known from two specimens, discovered in 1999 by researchers from the Ministry of Land and Resources and described two years later. One species, N. yangi, is known, named after Chinese palaeontologist Yang Zhongjian.

Nemegtomaia.etymology: Named for the Nemegt Basin of Mongolia where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'maia' meaning 'good mother', in reference to the brooding behavior of oviraptorids.
Nemegtomaia.description: Nemegtomaia is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur from what is now Mongolia that lived in the Late Cretaceous Period, about 72 to 70 million years ago. The first specimen was found in 1996, and became the basis of the new genus and species N. barsboldi in 2004. The original genus name was Nemegtia, but this was changed to Nemegtomaia in 2005, as the former name was preoccupied. The first part of the generic name refers to the Nemegt Basin, where the animal was found, and the second part means "good mother", in reference to the fact that oviraptorids are known to have brooded their eggs. The specific name honours the palaeontologist Rinchen Barsbold. Two more specimens were found in 2007, one of which was found on top of a nest with eggs, but the dinosaur had received its genus name before it was found associated with eggs.

Nemegtonykus.description: Nemegtonykus is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous ( Maastrichtian) Nemegt Formation of Mongolia. The type and only species is Nemegtonykus citus. It is the second alvarezsaurid known from the Nemegt Formation, preceded by Mononykus.

Nemegtosaurus.etymology: Named for the Nemegt Basin in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia where the skull was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Nemegtosaurus.description: Nemegtosaurus was a sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now Mongolia. Measuring an estimated 12–13 m (39–43 ft) long and weighing 20 t (44,000 lb), it was named after the Nemegt Basin in the Gobi Desert, where the remains — a single skull — were found. The skull resembles diplodocoids in being long and low, with pencil-shaped teeth. However, recent work has shown that Nemegtosaurus is in fact a titanosaur, closely related to animals such as Saltasaurus, Alamosaurus, and Rapetosaurus.

It has never been formally given a species name, but is often seen as N. praecursor, which actually comes from a different animal. Often in the past, it had been assigned to the wastebasket taxon Pelorosaurus, but restudy has suggested that it could be related to Turiasaurus, a roughly contemporaneous giant Spanish sauropod. It is only known from six teeth.

Neovenator.etymology: From Latin neo- ('new') and venator ('hunter'), meaning 'new hunter'
Neovenator.description: Neovenator is an extinct genus of carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaur. It is known primarily from several skeletons found in the Early Cretaceous (Hauterivian–Barremian) Wessex Formation on the south coast of the Isle of Wight, southern England. The first remains of Neovenator were discovered in 1978 alongside those of the ornithopod Brighstoneus, after the collapse of part of Grange Chine. In 1996, Steve Hutt, David Martill and Michael Barker named the genus Neovenator. One species is known: the type species, N. salerii, after the Salero family who owned the site on which its remains were discovered.

Neuquenraptor.etymology: Meaning 'Neuquén thief'; from Neuquén Province, Argentina, where it was found, combined with Latin raptor ('thief' or 'plunderer')
Neuquenraptor.description: Neuquenraptor is a genus of unenlagiine theropod dinosaurs that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Portezuelo Formation of Argentina. It is one of the first dromaeosaurids found in the Southern Hemisphere.

synonyms.name: Araucanoraptor
synonyms.reason: Informal name reported at a 1997 Society of Vertebrate Paleontology conference; the taxon was ultimately formally described as Neuquenraptor.

species.name: Neuquenraptor argentinus
species.etymology: Named for Argentina, the country where the holotype was discovered, with the Latin suffix '-inus' meaning 'of' or 'from'.

references.authors: Novas, Fernando E.; Pol, Diego
references.title: New evidence on deinonychosaurian dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Neuquensaurus.etymology: Named for the Neuquén Province and Neuquén River of Argentina where its fossils were recovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Neuquensaurus.description: Neuquensaurus is a genus of saltasaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous, about 80 million years ago in Argentina in South America. Its fossils were recovered from outcrops of the Anacleto Formation around Cinco Saltos, near the Neuquén river from which its name is derived.

species.name: Neuquensaurus australis
species.etymology: From Latin 'australis' meaning 'southern', in reference to the South American provenance of the fossils.

Nevadadromeus.etymology: Named after Nevada, the US state where it was found, combined with Greek 'dromeus' (runner); meaning 'Nevada runner'.
Nevadadromeus.description: Nevadadromeus is an extinct genus of small thescelosaurine ornithischian dinosaur, from the Willow Tank Formation of Nevada, United States. The genus contains a single species, N. schmitti, which represents the first non-avian dinosaur named from Nevada.

species.name: Nevadadromeus schmitti
species.etymology: Named for geologist James G. Schmitt, who initially described the geology of the Willow Tank Formation where the holotype was found.

Ngwevu.etymology: From Xhosa 'ngwevu' meaning 'grey' and 'intloko' meaning 'skull', giving the combined meaning 'grey skull'.
Ngwevu.description: Ngwevu is a genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Lower Jurassic of South Africa. The genus contains one species, Ngwevu intloko.

species.name: Ngwevu intloko
species.etymology: From Xhosa 'intloko' meaning 'skull', referring to the grey-coloured skull of the holotype; the full genus-plus-species name together means 'grey skull' in Xhosa.

holotype.institution: Evolutionary Studies Institute (formerly Bernard Price Institute for Palaeontological Research), University of the Witwatersrand

Nhandumirim.etymology: From Tupi nhandú ('rhea') and mirim ('small'), meaning 'small rhea'
Nhandumirim.description: Nhandumirim is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Carnian age of Late Triassic Brazil. It is currently considered a saturnaliid sauropodomorph. The type and only species, Nhandumirim waldsangae, is known from a single immature specimen including vertebrae, a chevron, pelvic material, and a hindlimb found in the Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul.

species.name: Nhandumirim waldsangae
species.etymology: Named for Waldsanga (also called Cerro da Alemoa or Sanga do Mato), the historically significant Triassic fossil site in Santa Maria, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Departamento de Biologia, Faculdade de Filosofia, Ciências e Letras de Ribeirão Preto, Universidade de São Paulo

references.authors: Marsola, Júlio C. A.; Bittencourt, Jonathas S.; Butler, Richard J.; Da Rosa, Átila A. S.; Sayão, Juliana M.; Langer, Max C.
references.title: A new dinosaur with theropod affinities from the Late Triassic Santa Maria Formation, south Brazil

Niebla.etymology: From Spanish 'niebla' meaning 'mist', referring to the foggy days during the excavation of the fossil.
Niebla.description: Niebla antiqua is an extinct species of abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of Río Negro province, Argentina. Niebla antiqua is the only species in the genus Niebla, known from a partial, non-articulated skeleton. The holotype, found in the Allen Formation, represents an adult individual about nine years old in minimum age.

species.name: Niebla antiqua
species.etymology: From Latin 'antiqua' meaning 'ancient' or 'old'.

Nigersaurus.etymology: Named after Niger, the African country where it was discovered, combined with Latin 'saurus' (lizard); meaning 'Niger reptile'.
Nigersaurus.description: Nigersaurus is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived during the middle Cretaceous period, about 115 to 105 million years ago. It was discovered in the Elrhaz Formation in an area called Gadoufaoua, in Niger. Fossils of this dinosaur were first described in 1976, but it was only named Nigersaurus taqueti in 1999 after further and more complete remains were found and described. The genus name means "Niger reptile", and the specific name honours the palaeontologist Philippe Taquet, who discovered the first remains.

species.name: Nigersaurus taqueti
species.etymology: Named for Philippe Taquet, the French paleontologist who led the first expeditions to Niger that recovered the earliest remains of this dinosaur.

references.authors: Sereno, Paul C.; Beck, Allison L.; Dutheil, Didier B.; Larsson, Hans C. E.; Lyon, Gabrielle H.; Moussa, Bourahima; Sadleir, Rudyard W.; Sidor, Christian A.; Varricchio, David J.; Wilson, Gregory P.; Wilson, Jeffrey A.

Ningyuansaurus.etymology: Derived from Ningyuan, an ancient name for Xingcheng City in western Liaoning Province, China, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'
Ningyuansaurus.description: Ningyuansaurus is a pennaraptoran dinosaur genus. It contains the single species Ningyuansaurus wangi, known from a fossil specimen from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation (Aptian stage, 124.6 Ma ago) of Jianchang, western Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China. It was originally thought to be the basalmost species of oviraptorosaur, based on its long skull and a greater number of teeth in comparison to any other known oviraptorosaur. However, later research showed that it is a member of Halszkaraptorinae. The generic name Ningyuansaurus is derived from Ningyuan, an ancient name for Xingcheng City. The specific name honors Wang Qiuwu, the private owner of the specimen who donated it for scientific study. The specimen is now in the Confuciusornis Museum in Xingcheng.

species.name: Ningyuansaurus wangi
species.etymology: Named for Wang Qiuwu, the private owner of the specimen who donated it for scientific study.

holotype.material: No specimen ID assigned

references.authors: Ji, Q.; Lü, J.-c.; X.-f. Wei, X.-r. Wang
references.title: A new oviraptorosaur from the Yixian Formation of Jianching, western Liaoning Province, China

Ninjatitan.etymology: Named for 'Ninja', a nickname of Argentine palaeontologist Sebastian Apesteguia, combined with Latin 'titan' meaning 'giant'; translates as 'Ninja giant'.
Ninjatitan.description: Ninjatitan is an exinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Berriasian–Valanginian age) Bajada Colorada Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Ninjatitan zapatai, which was named and described in 2021 based on a partial postcranial skeleton discovered in 2014. Its generic name comes from a nickname of Argentine palaeontologist Sebastian Apesteguia, and the specific name comes from technician Rogelio Zapata.

species.name: Ninjatitan zapatai
species.etymology: Named for Rogelio Zapata, the technician involved in the preparation and recovery of the holotype specimen.

holotype.institution: Museu de les Mines de Cercs

references.authors: Gallina, Pablo Ariel; Canale, Juan Ignacio; Carballido, José Luis
references.title: The Earliest Known Titanosaur Sauropod Dinosaur

Niobrarasaurus.etymology: Named after the Niobrara Formation of Kansas where its fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Niobrara lizard'.
Niobrarasaurus.description: Niobrarasaurus is an extinct genus of nodosaurid ankylosaurian dinosaur which lived during the Late Cretaceous, around 87 to 82 million years ago. Its fossils were found in the Smoky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Formation, in western Kansas, which would have been near the middle of the Western Interior Seaway during the Late Cretaceous. It was probably closely related to Nodosaurus.

species.name: Niobrarasaurus coleii
species.etymology: Named for Virgil Cole, the geologist who discovered and excavated the holotype specimen in 1930.

holotype.institution: Sternberg Museum of Natural History, Fort Hays State University

references.authors: Carpenter, Kenneth; Dilkes, David; Weishampel, David B.
references.title: The Dinosaurs of the Niobrara Chalk Formation (Upper Cretaceous, Kansas)

Nipponosaurus.etymology: Named for Nippon (Japan), the country that controlled Sakhalin Island where the fossils were found at the time of description, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Nipponosaurus.description: Nipponosaurus is a lambeosaurine hadrosaur from sediments of the Yezo Group, in Sinegorsk on the island of Sakhalin, which was part of Japan at the time of the species' classification. The type and only species is N. sachalinensis, known only from a single juvenile specimen discovered in 1934 and named in 1936, by Takumi Nagao, with further material of the same individual found in 1937. Since then, the taxon has been largely ignored, and its validity has been doubted, with synonymy with other Asian hadrosaurs or status as a nomen dubium being suggested. Redescriptions from 2004 and 2017, however, have supported recognition as a distinct species. Dating the only specimen has been difficult, but based on associated mollusc taxa, the species likely lived sometime in the upper Santonian or lower Campanian, around 80 million years ago.

species.name: Nipponosaurus sachalinensis
species.etymology: Named for Sakhalin, the island where the holotype was found during construction of a colliery hospital in 1934.

references.authors: Nagao, T.
references.title: Nipponosaurus sachalinensis: a new genus and species of trachodont dinosaur from Japanese Saghalien
references.journal: Journal of the Faculty of Science, Hokkaido Imperial University, series 4, Geology and Mineralogy

Noasaurus.etymology: Named after the Noroeste Argentino (northwestern Argentina) region, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Northwestern Argentina lizard'.
Noasaurus.description: Noasaurus is a genus of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Maastrichtian (Late Cretaceous) of Argentina. The type and only species is N. leali. The fragmentary holotype specimen of Noasaurus, PVL 4061, consisting of a few cranial and postcranial bones, was discovered from strata from the Lecho Formation of Southern Salta in 1975 by a team led by José Fernando Bonaparte. When described by Bonaparte and in PhD student Jaime Powell in 1980, it was believed to be a coelurosaur theropod and assigned to a family of its own; this family, Noasauridae, still exists, though has been reassigned to Ceratosauria.

species.name: Noasaurus leali
species.etymology: Named for Juan Carlos Leal, the discoverer of the El Brete fossil site in Argentina where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Colección de Paleontologia de Vertebrados de la Fundación Instituto Miguel Lillo

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.; Powell, J. E.
references.title: A continental assemblage of tetrapods from the Upper Cretaceous beds of El Brete, northwestern Argentina (Sauropoda-Coelurosauria-Carnosauria-Aves)
references.journal: Mémoires de la Société Géologique de France, Nouvelle Série

Nodocephalosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'nodus' (knob), Greek 'kephale' (head), and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'knob headed lizard', referring to the nodular ornamentation on its skull.
Nodocephalosaurus.description: Nodocephalosaurus is a monospecific genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur from New Mexico that lived during the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian to early Maastrichtian stage, 73.49 to 72 Ma) in what is now the De-na-zin member of the Kirtland Formation. The type and only species, Nodocephalosaurus kirtlandensis, is known only from a partial skull. It was named in 1999 by Robert M. Sullivan. Nodocephalosaurus has an estimated length of 4.5 metres (15 feet) and weight of 1.5 tonnes (3,306 lbs). It is closely related and shares similar cranial anatomy to Akainacephalus.

species.name: Nodocephalosaurus kirtlandensis
species.etymology: Named for the Kirtland Formation of New Mexico, the geological formation from which the holotype was recovered.

references.authors: Sullivan, Robert M.
references.title: Nodocephalosaurus kirtlandensis, gen. et sp. nov., a new ankylosaurid dinosaur (Ornithischia: Ankylosauria) from the Upper Cretaceous Kirtland Formation (upper Campanian), San Juan Basin, New Mexico

Nodosaurus.etymology: From Latin nodus ('knob' or 'node') and Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'knobbed lizard', in reference to the knobby armour on its body
Nodosaurus.description: Nodosaurus is a genus of herbivorous nodosaurid ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous, the fossils of which were found in Niobrara County, Wyoming, in the Lance Formation.

species.name: Nodosaurus textilis
species.etymology: From Latin 'textilis' meaning 'woven' or 'textile-like', referring to the textile-like appearance of the osteoderms on the animal's back.

holotype.institution: Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History

references.authors: Marsh, O. C.
references.title: Notice of gigantic horned Dinosauria from the Cretaceous

Nomingia.etymology: Named after the Nomingiin Gobi (one of the 'Thirty-Three Gobis' of the Gobi Desert) where the holotype was found
Nomingia.description: Nomingia is a genus of oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Bugin Tsav Beds of Mongolia.

species.name: Nomingia gobiensis
species.etymology: gobiensis refers to the Gobi Desert

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Barsbold, R.; Osmólska, H.; M. Watabe, P. J. Currie, K. Tsogtbaatar
references.title: A new oviraptorosaur (Dinosauria, Theropoda) from Mongolia: the first dinosaur with a pygostyle

Nopcsaspondylus.etymology: Named for Baron Franz Nopcsa, the paleontologist who first described the fossil material, combined with Greek 'spondylos' meaning 'vertebra'; translates as 'Nopcsa's vertebra'.
Nopcsaspondylus.description: Nopcsaspondylus is a dubious genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Cenomanian-aged (Upper Cretaceous) Candeleros Formation of Neuquén, Argentina. It is based on a now-lost back vertebra described by Nopcsa in 1902 but not named at the time. The specimen had a small vertebral body and large hollows, now known to be typical of rebbachisaurids.

species.name: Nopcsaspondylus alarconensis
species.etymology: Named for Barda Alarcón, the locality in Neuquén, Argentina, where the holotype vertebra was discovered.

holotype.institution: Paläontologisches Institut und Museum der Universität Wien
holotype.material: Single dorsal vertebra figured by Nopcsa (1902); never formally catalogued

references.title: The sauropod diversity of the La Amarga Formation (Barremian), Neuquén (Argentina)

Normanniasaurus.etymology: Derived from Normannia, the Latin name for Normandy (northwestern France, where the bones were discovered), and Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Normandy lizard'
Normanniasaurus.description: Normanniasaurus is an extinct genus of basal titanosaur sauropod known from the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) Poudingue Ferrugineux of Seine-Maritime, northwestern France.

species.name: Normanniasaurus genceyi
species.etymology: Named for Pierre Gencey, who discovered the remains in July 1990.

location.locality: Northern side of Cap de la Hève, Bléville

references.authors: Le Loeuff, J.; Suteethorn, S.; E. Buffetaut
references.title: A new sauropod dinosaur from the Albian of Le Havre (Normandy, France)

Notatesseraeraptor.etymology: From Latin 'nota' (feature), 'tesserae' (mosaic tiles), and 'raptor' (thief); meaning 'feature mosaic tile thief', referencing the mixture of features from dilophosaurids and coelophysoids.
Notatesseraeraptor.description: Notatesseraeraptor is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic of what is now Switzerland. It was found in the Gruhalde Member of the Klettgau Formation. It was an early member of Neotheropoda with affinities to Dilophosaurus and Averostra. The new genus and species Notatesseraeraptor frickensis was named by Marion Zahner and colleagues in 2019.

species.name: Notatesseraeraptor frickensis
species.etymology: Named for the municipality of Frick in the Aargau, Switzerland, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.material: Partial postcranial skeleton (SMF 06-1) and cranium (SMF 09-2) of a juvenile to subadult individual

references.authors: Zahner, Marion; Brinkmann, Winand
references.title: A Triassic averostran-line theropod from Switzerland and the early evolution of dinosaurs
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Nothronychus.etymology: From Greek 'nothros' meaning 'slothful' and 'onyx' meaning 'claw'; translates as 'slothful claw', a reference to its therizinosaur-like elongated claws and presumed slow-moving herbivorous habits.
Nothronychus.description: Nothronychus is a genus of therizinosaurid theropod dinosaurs that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous period. The type species, Nothronychus mckinleyi, was described by James Kirkland and Douglas G. Wolfe in 2001. It was recovered near New Mexico's border with Arizona, in an area known as the Zuni Basin, from rocks assigned to the Moreno Hill Formation, dating to the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous. A second specimen, described in 2009 as a second species, Nothronychus graffami, was found in the Tropic Shale of Utah, dating to between one million and 500,000 years older than N. mckinleyi.

species.name: Nothronychus mckinleyi
species.etymology: Named for rancher Bobby McKinley, on whose land the fossil findings were made.

references.authors: Kirkland, James I.; Wolfe, Douglas G.
references.title: First definitive therizinosaurid (Dinosauria; Theropoda) from North America

Notoceratops.etymology: From Greek 'notos' (southern), 'keras' (horn), and 'ops' (face); meaning 'southern horned face', referring to its discovery in the southern part of South America.
Notoceratops.description: Notoceratops is a dubious genus of extinct ornithischian dinosaur. The genus was described based on an incomplete, toothless left dentary (now lost) from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia (in Argentina), probably dating to the Campanian or Maastrichtian. Initially classified as a putative ceratopsian found in the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation, the lost fragmentary holotype precludes confident referral of this taxon within ornithischians, with some researchers suggesting that it belongs to a hadrosaur instead.

species.name: Notoceratops bonarelli
species.etymology: Named for Guido Bonarelli (1871–1951), who advised Augusto Tapia in his study of the find.

holotype.institution: División de Paleontología de Vertebrados del Museo de Ciencias Naturales y Universidad Nacional de San Juan
holotype.material: Unnamed specimen; originally at Dirección General de Minas de Buenos Aires

references.title: Una mandibula de Dinosaurioa procedente de Patagonia [A dinosaur mandible from Patagonia]
references.journal: Physis, Revista de la Sociedad Argentina de Ciencias Naturales

Notocolossus.etymology: From Greek notos (νότος, 'south wind') and kolossos (κολοσσός, 'giant statue'), meaning 'giant of the south', referring to its southern hemisphere provenance and enormous size
Notocolossus.description: Notocolossus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from late Cretaceous strata of Mendoza Province, Argentina.

species.name: Notocolossus gonzalezparejasi
species.etymology: Named for Jorge González Parejas, who studied the dinosaur fossils of Mendoza Province for two decades.

holotype.institution: Universidad Nacional de Cuyo, Laboratorio de Dinosaurios

Notohypsilophodon.etymology: From Greek 'notos' meaning 'south wind' (indicating its southern provenance in South America) combined with the genus name Hypsilophodon, indicating its similarity to that ornithopod.
Notohypsilophodon.description: Notohypsilophodon is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina. It was described as the only "hypsilophodont" known from South America, although this assessment is not universally supported, and Gasparinisaura is now believed to have been a basal euornithopod as well.

species.name: Notohypsilophodon comodorensis
species.etymology: Named for Comodoro Rivadavia, the nearest city to the discovery site.

references.title: Notohypsilophodon comodorensis gen. et sp. nov. un Hypsilophodontidae (Ornitischia: Ornithopoda) del Cretácico Superior de Chubut, Patagonia central, Argentina [Notohypsilophodon comodorensis gen. et sp. nov., a Hypsilophodontidae (Ornithischia: Ornithopoda) from the Upper Cretaceous of Chubut, central Patagonia, Argentina]

Nqwebasaurus.etymology: From Xhosa 'Nqweba', the local name for the Kirkwood district in the Eastern Cape of South Africa where the specimen was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Nqwebasaurus.description: Nqwebasaurus is a probable ornithomimosaurian theropod from the Early Cretaceous of South Africa. The genus contains a single species, Nqwebasaurus thwazi, representing the oldest known coelurosaur in Africa and the evidence for basal coelurosaurian dinosaurs inhabiting Gondwana since the earliest Cretaceous period.

species.name: Nqwebasaurus thwazi
species.etymology: From the ancient Xhosa word 'thwazi' meaning 'fast runner'.

references.authors: de Klerk, W. J.; Forster, C. A.; S. D. Sampson, A. Chinsamy, C. F. Ross
references.title: A new coelurosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of South Africa

Nullotitan.etymology: Named in honor of geologist Francisco Nullo, combined with Greek 'titan' (giant); meaning 'Nullo's giant'.
Nullotitan.description: Nullotitan is an extinct genus of lithostrotian titanosaur dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Chorrillo Formation of Santa Cruz Province, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Nullotitan glaciaris. It was a contemporary of the ornithopod Isasicursor, which was described in the same paper.

species.name: Nullotitan glaciaris
species.etymology: From Latin 'glaciaris' meaning 'of ice' or 'icy', referring to the Perito Moreno Glacier, which is visible from the discovery site.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales ‘Bernardino Rivadavia’

Nuthetes.etymology: From Koine Greek 'nouthetes' meaning 'one who admonishes' or 'a monitor', referring to the similarity of its teeth to those of a modern monitor lizard.
Nuthetes.description: Nuthetes is a genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur, either a dromaeosaurid or tyrannosauroid, known only from fossil teeth and jaw fragments found in rocks of the middle Berriasian age (Early Cretaceous) in the Cherty Freshwater Member of the Lulworth Formation in England and also the Angeac-Charente bonebed in France. If it was a dromaeosaurid, Nuthetes would have been a small predator.

species.name: Nuthetes destructor
species.etymology: From Latin 'destructor' meaning 'destroyer', a reference to the adaptations of the teeth for piercing, cutting, and lacerating prey.

Obelignathus.etymology: Named for Obelix, the fictional character from the Asterix and Obelix cartoon, combined with Greek 'gnathos' meaning 'jaw'; refers to the robust morphology of the holotype dentary likened to the strength of that character.
Obelignathus.description: Obelignathus is an extinct genus of rhabdodontomorph ornithopod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous 'Grès à Reptiles' Formation of France. The genus contains a single species, O. septimanicus, known from a right dentary. The species was initially classified as a species of the coeval Rhabdodon.

species.name: Obelignathus septimanicus
species.etymology: Named for Septimania, a historic region of France corresponding to Languedoc, where the type locality in Montouliers is located, with the Latin suffix '-icus' meaning 'of' or 'pertaining to'.

holotype.institution: Le Musée des Dinosaures Espéraza-Aude (Dinosaur Museum Espéraza), Espéraza, Department  Aude, Region  Languedoc-Roussillon-Midi-Pyrénées

references.title: Exploring the diversity and disparity of rhabdodontomorph ornithopods from the Late Cretaceous European archipelago

Oblitosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'oblitus' (forgotten or obsolete) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'forgotten lizard', referring to how its fossils were long overlooked.
Oblitosaurus.description: Oblitosaurus is a genus of ankylopollexian ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Villar del Arzobispo Formation of Spain. The type species is Oblitosaurus bunnueli.

species.name: Oblitosaurus bunnueli
species.etymology: Named for Spanish filmmaker Luis Buñuel.

holotype.institution: Museo de la Fundación Conjunto Paleontológico de Teruel-Dinópolis
holotype.material: Partial skeleton cataloged as CPT-1440, CPT-1444, and MAP-8290 through MAP-8299

references.authors: Sánchez-Fenollosa, Sergio; Verdú, Francisco J; Cobos, Alberto

Oceanotitan.etymology: From Latin 'oceanus' meaning 'ocean', because the fossil was found at the base of a coastal cliff overlooking the Atlantic Ocean, combined with 'Titan' from Greek mythology meaning 'giant'.
Oceanotitan.description: Oceanotitan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur known from the Upper Jurassic (latest Kimmeridgian stage, about 149 million years ago) Lourinhã Formation of Portugal. It is represented by a single specimen consisting of several tail vertebrae and appendicular bones. It contains one species, Oceanotitan dantasi. Oceanotitan is classified as possibly one of the earliest members of the Somphospondyli, a group of sauropods that includes the titanosaurs.

species.name: Oceanotitan dantasi
species.etymology: Named for Portuguese paleontologist Pedro Dantas, who was a major contributor to Portuguese vertebrate paleontology towards the end of the 20th century.

location.locality: cliffs north of Praia de Valmitão

references.authors: Mocho, Pedro; Royo-Torres, Rafael; Ortega, Francisco
references.title: A new macronarian sauropod from the Upper Jurassic of Portugal

Ohmdenosaurus.etymology: Named after the village of Ohmden in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, near where the specimen was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Ohmden lizard'
Ohmdenosaurus.description: Ohmdenosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic epoch in what is now Germany. The only specimen – a tibia (shinbone) and ankle – was discovered in rocks of the Posidonia Shale near the village of Ohmden. The specimen, which was originally identified as a plesiosaur, is exhibited in a local museum, the Urweltmuseum Hauff. In the 1970s, it caught the attention of German palaeontologist Rupert Wild, who recognised it as the remains of a sauropod. Wild named Ohmdenosaurus in a 1978 publication; the only known species is Ohmdenosaurus liasicus.

species.name: Ohmdenosaurus liasicus
species.etymology: From Latin 'liasicus' meaning 'of the Lias', referring to the Lias, an old name for the Lower Jurassic of Europe, in which the holotype was found.

holotype.material: Tibia, astragalus, and calcaneus; originally identified as a plesiosaur, later recognised as a sauropod by Wild (1978). No formal catalogue number known in the published literature

references.authors: Wild, R.
references.title: Ein Sauropoden-Rest (Reptilia, Saurischia) aus dem Posidonienschiefer (Lias, Toarcium) von Holzmaden [A new sauropod (Reptilia, Saurischia) from the Posidonienschiefer (Lias, Toarcian) of Holzmaden]
references.journal: Stuttgarter Beiträge zur Naturkunde, Serie B (Geologie und Paläontologie)

Ojoceratops.description: Ojoceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur which lived in what is now New Mexico, United States. Ojoceratops fossils have been recovered from strata of the Ojo Alamo Formation (Naashoibito Member), dating to the late Cretaceous period (late Maastrichtian age, 66 million years ago). The type species is Ojoceratops fowleri.

references.authors: Sullivan, R. M.; Lucas, S. G.
references.title: A new chasmosaurine (Ceratopsidae, Dinosauria) from the Upper Cretaceous Ojo Alamo Formation (Naashoibito Member), San Juan Basin, New Mexico
references.journal: New Perspectives on Horned Dinosaurs: The Royal Tyrrell Museum Ceratopsian Symposium. Indiana University Press, Bloomington

Ojoraptorsaurus.etymology: Combines a reference to the Ojo Alamo Formation (where it was found) with Latin raptor ('plunderer') and Latinised Greek sauros ('lizard'); meaning 'Ojo Alamo plunderer lizard'
Ojoraptorsaurus.description: Ojoraptorsaurus is a dubious genus of oviraptorosaurian dinosaur from the late Cretaceous. Ojoraptorsaurus is only known from pubic bones found at the Naashoibito Member of the Ojo Alamo Formation dating to the late Maastrichtian, about 66 million years ago. It was first named by Robert M. Sullivan, Steven E. Jasinski and Mark P.A. van Tomme in 2011 and the type species is Ojoraptorsaurus boerei. The generic name combines a reference to the formation with a Latin raptor, "plunderer", and a Latinised Greek saurus, "lizard". The specific name honours oceanographer Arjan Boeré who found the specimen.

species.name: Ojoraptorsaurus boerei
species.etymology: Named for oceanographer Arjan Boeré, who found the specimen.

references.authors: Sullivan, R. M.; Jasinski, S. E.; M. P. A. Van Tomme
references.title: A new caenagnathid Ojoraptorsaurus boerei, n. gen., n. sp. (Dinosauria, Oviraptorosauria), from the Upper Cretaceous Ojo Alamo Formation (Naashoibito Member), San Juan Basin, New Mexico
references.journal: Fossil Record 3. New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science Bulletin
references.publisher: New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science

Oksoko.etymology: From Öksökö, a mythical two-headed bird in Yakut (Sakha) folklore of Siberia
Oksoko.description: Oksoko is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Nemegt Formation of Omnogov Province, Mongolia. The type and only species is Oksoko avarsan. It is notable for having only two functional fingers, having lost the third manual digit, suggesting a trend toward digit reduction within oviraptorosaurs.

species.name: Oksoko avarsan
species.etymology: From the Mongolian word 'avarsan' meaning 'rescued', given that specimens of the genus were redeemed from fossil poachers.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Center, Mongolian Academy of Sciences
holotype.material: Block assemblage of three individuals (subcatalogued MPC-D 102/110a, 102/110b, 102/110c): skulls, cervical vertebrae, pelvis, hindlimbs, caudal vertebrae, forelimb material

references.authors: Funston, Gregory F.; Chinzorig, Tsogtbaatar; Tsogtbaatar, Khishigjav; Kobayashi, Yoshitsugu; Sullivan, Corwin; Currie, Philip J.
references.title: A new two-fingered dinosaur sheds light on the radiation of Oviraptorosauria

Olorotitan.etymology: From Latin olor ('swan'), referencing the swan-like elongated neck and crest of this hadrosaur, combined with Greek Titan (a giant); meaning 'giant swan'
Olorotitan.description: Olorotitan is a monotypic genus of lambeosaurine duck-billed dinosaur, containing a single species, O. arharensis. It was among the last non-avian dinosaurs to go extinct during the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, having lived from the middle to late Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period. The remains were found in the Udurchukan Formation beds of Kundur, Arkharinsky District, Amur Oblast, Eastern Russia, in the vicinity of the Amur River.

species.name: Olorotitan arharensis
species.etymology: Named for Arhara County in Russia, where the fossil was found.

holotype.institution: Amur Natural History Museum of the Institute of Geology and Nature Management, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Godefroit, Pascal; Bolotsky, Yuri; Alifanov, Vladimir
references.title: A remarkable hollow-crested hadrosaur from Russia: an Asian origin for lambeosaurines

Omeisaurus.etymology: Named after Mount Emei (Omei) in Sichuan Province, China, where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Omei lizard'.
Omeisaurus.description: Omeisaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Middle to Late Jurassic Period (Bathonian-Oxfordian stage) of what is now China. Its name comes from Mount Emei, where it was discovered in the lower Shaximiao Formation of Sichuan Province.

species.name: Omeisaurus junghsiensis
species.etymology: Named for the Junghsi locality in Sichuan, China, where the holotype was collected.

references.authors: Young, C. C.
references.title: On a New Sauropoda, with Notes on Other Fragmentary Reptiles from Szechuan
references.journal: Bulletin of the Geological Society of China

Ondogurvel.etymology: From Mongolian 'ondo' meaning 'egg' and 'gurvel' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'egg lizard'.
Ondogurvel.description: Ondogurvel is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Barun Goyot Formation in southern Mongolia. The type and only species is O. alifanovi, known from a partial skeleton consisting of fragments of two last dorsal vertebrae, three anterior sacral vertebrae, right ilium, left and right pubis and ischium, articulated right tibia, fibula, metatarsals II and IV, and phalanges IV-1 and IV-2, right carpometacarpus, left and right manual phalanx II-1, right femur, left pedal phalanx II-1, and fragments of unidentified phalanges.

species.name: Ondogurvel alifanovi
species.etymology: Named for the late Russian paleontologist Vladimir Alifanov, who found the holotype specimen in 1999.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Averianov, Alexander O.; Lopatin, Alexey V.
references.title: A new alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Gobi Desert, Mongolia

Oohkotokia.etymology: From Blackfoot 'ooh'kotoka' meaning 'large stone' and Latin suffix '-ia' meaning 'derived from', giving the meaning 'child of stone', referring to its extensive body armor; the name also honors the Blackfoot people on whose land the specimen was found.
Oohkotokia.description: Oohkotokia is a genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae. It is known from the upper levels of the Two Medicine Formation (late Campanian stage, about 74 Ma ago) of Montana, United States. The discovery of Oohkotokia supports that Ankylosaurine dinosaurs existed and flourished continuously in Montana and/or Alberta throughout the late Campanian and early Maastrichtian stages in the Late Cretaceous period. It was a large, heavily built, quadrupedal, herbivore, that could grow up to 5 metres (16 ft) long and weigh up to 2 metric tons (2.2 short tons).

species.name: Oohkotokia horneri
species.etymology: Named for John R. Horner of the Museum of the Rockies, who collected the type specimen.

references.authors: Penkalski, Paul
references.title: A new ankylosaurid from the late Cretaceous Two Medicine Formation of Montana, USA
references.publisher: Polska Akademia Nauk Instytut Paleobiologii (Institute of Paleobiology, Polish Academy of Sciences)

Opisthocoelicaudia.etymology: From Greek 'opisthen' (behind/posterior), 'koilos' (hollow), Latin 'cauda' (tail), and Latin '-ia' (suffix); meaning 'hollow-backed tail', referring to the opisthocoelouos (posteriorly hollowed) tail vertebrae.
Opisthocoelicaudia.description: Opisthocoelicaudia is a genus of sauropod dinosaur of the Late Cretaceous Period discovered in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia. The type species is Opisthocoelicaudia skarzynskii. A well-preserved skeleton lacking only the head and neck was unearthed in 1965 by Polish and Mongolian scientists, making Opisthocoelicaudia one of the best known sauropods from the Late Cretaceous. Tooth marks on this skeleton indicate that large carnivorous dinosaurs had fed on the carcass and possibly had carried away the now-missing parts. To date, only two additional, much less complete specimens are known, including part of a shoulder and a fragmentary tail. A relatively small sauropod, Opisthocoelicaudia measured about 11.4–13 m (37–43 ft) in length. Like other sauropods, it would have been characterised by a small head sitting on a very long neck and a barrel shaped trunk carried by four column-like legs. The name Opisthocoelicaudia means "posterior cavity tail", alluding to the unusual, opisthocoel condition of the anterior tail vertebrae that were concave on their posterior sides. This and other skeletal features lead researchers to propose that Opisthocoelicaudia was able to rear on its hindlegs.

species.name: Opisthocoelicaudia skarzynskii
species.etymology: Named for Wojciech Skarżyński, the person who prepared the type specimen.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences
holotype.material: Originally catalogued as ZPAL MgD-I/48 at the Institute of Paleobiology, Warsaw; later repatriated to Mongolia

references.authors: Borsuk-Bialynicka, M.
references.title: A new camarasaurid sauropod Opisthocoelicaudia skarzynskii gen. n., sp. n. from the Upper Cretaceous of Mongolia

Oplosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'hoplon' (weapon or armor) and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'armed or weapon lizard' or 'armoured lizard'.
Oplosaurus.description: Oplosaurus was a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous (Barremian stage) Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, England. It is known from a single tooth usually referred to the contemporaneous "wastebasket taxon" Pelorosaurus, although there is no solid evidence for this.

species.name: Oplosaurus armatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'armatus' meaning 'armed', referring either to the weapons of the teeth or to the presumed armored nature of the animal, paralleling the Greek generic name.

references.authors: Gervais, Paul
references.title: Liste des ouvrages et mémoires de zoologie et d'anatomie comparée
references.book: Liste des ouvrages et mémoires de zoologie et d'anatomie comparée

Orkoraptor.etymology: From Aoniken 'Orr-Korr', the local name for the La Leona River near the fossil site, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief'; translates as 'Toothed River thief'.
Orkoraptor.description: Orkoraptor is a genus of medium-sized megaraptoran theropod dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of Argentina. It is known from incomplete fossil remains including parts of the skull, teeth, tail vertebrae, and a partial tibia. The specialized teeth resemble those of some maniraptoriform theropods, namely the deinonychosaurs and compsognathids. This and other anatomical features led the authors who described it (Novas, Ezcurra, and Lecuona) to suggest that it was a maniraptoran coelurosaur. However, subsequent studies found it to be a megaraptoran. Found in the Cerro Fortaleza Formation of Southern Patagonia, it is one of the southernmost carnivorous dinosaurs known from South America.

species.name: Orkoraptor burkei
species.etymology: Named for Coleman Burke, an amateur paleontologist who supported the expedition that collected the original fossils.

references.authors: Novas, Fernando E.; Ezcurra, Martín D.; Lecuona, Agustina
references.title: Orkoraptor burkei nov. gen. et sp., a large theropod from the Maastrichtian Pari Aike Formation, Southern Patagonia, Argentina

Ornatops.etymology: From Latin 'ornatus' (ornate) and Greek 'ops' (face); meaning 'ornate face'.
Ornatops.description: Ornatops is a genus of brachylophosaurin saurolophine hadrosaur from the Late Cretaceous Menefee Formation of New Mexico, United States. The genus contains a single species, Ornatops incantatus.

species.name: Ornatops incantatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'incantatus' meaning 'enchanted', a reference to New Mexico's nickname the 'Land of Enchantment', where the holotype was found.

references.authors: McDonald, Andrew T.; Wolfe, Douglas G.; Freedman Fowler, Elizabeth A.; Gates, Terry A.
references.title: A new brachylophosaurin (Dinosauria: Hadrosauridae) from the Upper Cretaceous Menefee Formation of New Mexico

Ornitholestes.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'ornis' (bird) and 'lestes' (robber); meaning 'bird robber'.
Ornitholestes.description: Ornitholestes is a small theropod dinosaur of the late Jurassic (Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation, middle Kimmeridgian age, about 154 million years ago) of Western Laurasia (the area that was to become North America).

species.name: Ornitholestes hermanni
species.etymology: Named for Adam Hermann, the head preparator at the American Museum of Natural History, who directed the restoration and mounting of the skeleton.

references.authors: Osborn, H. F.
references.title: Ornitholestes hermanni, a new compsognathoid dinosaur from the Upper Jurassic
references.journal: Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History

Ornithomimoides.etymology: From Greek 'ornis' (bird), 'mimos' (mimic), and '-oides' (resembling); meaning 'bird mimic-like', indicating resemblance to ornithomimosaurs.
Ornithomimoides.description: Ornithomimoides is a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur, from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage, sometime between 70 and 66 mya) Lameta Formation of India. Two species have been identified, the type species O. mobilis and O. barasimlensis, were named by von Huene in 1932 and were described by Matley in 1933 though they are known only from isolated vertebrae. O. barasimlensis is known from five dorsal vertebrae, and O. mobilis from four smaller vertebrae, found at the same location.

species.name: Ornithomimoides mobilis
species.etymology: From Latin 'mobilis' meaning 'mobile' or 'agile'.

references.authors: Huene, F. v.; Matley, C. A.
references.title: The Cretaceous Saurischia and Ornithischia of the Central Provinces of India
references.journal: Palaeontologica Indica (New Series), Memoirs of the Geological Survey of India

Ornithomimus.etymology: From Greek ornitho- (ὄρνις/ὀρνίθ-, 'bird') and mimos (μῖμος, 'mimic' or 'imitator'), meaning 'bird mimic'
Ornithomimus.description: Ornithomimus is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaurs from the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous in western North America. Ornithomimus was a swift, bipedal dinosaur which was covered in feathers and equipped with a small toothless beak that may indicate an omnivorous diet. It is usually classified into two species: the type species, Ornithomimus velox, and a referred species, Ornithomimus edmontonicus.

species.name: Ornithomimus velox
species.etymology: From Latin 'velox' meaning 'swift'.

Ornithopsis.etymology: From Greek 'ornis' (bird) and 'opsis' (likeness or appearance); meaning 'bird-likeness'.
Ornithopsis.description: Ornithopsis is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England and possibly Germany. The type species, which is the only species seen as valid today, is O. hulkei, which is only known from fragmentary remains.

species.name: Ornithopsis hulkei
species.etymology: Named for John Whitaker Hulke, the colleague of Harry Govier Seeley who first described the vertebrae.

holotype.material: Lectotype designated by Naish & Martill (2001)

Orodromeus.etymology: From Greek 'oros' (mountain) and 'dromeus' (runner); meaning 'Mountain Runner', referring to the Egg Mountain site where it was discovered and its cursorial habits.
Orodromeus.description: Orodromeus is a genus of herbivorous orodromine thescelosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America. Only one species is known, the type species Orodromeus makelai.

species.name: Orodromeus makelai
species.etymology: Named for Robert Makela, who discovered the fossil remains during excavations at Egg Mountain, Montana.

Orosaurus.description: Orosaurus is a dubious genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic of South Africa, containing a single species, O. capensis.

synonyms.reason: Coined by Lydekker (1889) as a replacement name when Orosaurus was incorrectly believed to be preoccupied; Orosaurus retains priority.

species.etymology: Named for the Cape region of South Africa, where the holotype was discovered.

Orthogoniosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'orthos' (straight), 'gonia' (angle), and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'straight angled lizard', referring to the straight posterior edge of its type tooth.
Orthogoniosaurus.description: Orthogoniosaurus is a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (late Maastrichtian) Lameta Formation of Jabalpur, India. It is based on one small, fragmentary tooth, with the preserved section measuring 2.7 cm (1.1 in) long.

species.name: Orthogoniosaurus matleyi
species.etymology: Named in honor of Charles Alfred Matley, a British geologist who discovered the fossil material in the Lameta Formation of Jabalpur, India, between 1917 and 1919.

references.journal: Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, New Series

Oryctodromeus.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'oruktēs' meaning 'digger' and 'dromaios' meaning 'runner'; translates as 'digging runner', reflecting its unique status as the first non-avian dinosaur with evidence of burrowing behavior.
Oryctodromeus.description: Oryctodromeus is an extinct genus of small orodromine thescelosaurid dinosaur. Fossils are known from the Late Cretaceous Blackleaf Formation of southwestern Montana and the Wayan Formation of southeastern Idaho, USA, both of the Cenomanian stage, roughly 105-96 million years ago. A member of the small, presumably fast-running herbivorous family Thescelosauridae, Oryctodromeus is the first non-avian dinosaur published that shows evidence of burrowing behavior.

species.name: Oryctodromeus cubicularis
species.etymology: From Latin 'cubicularis' meaning 'of the lair' or 'of the chamber', referring to the burrowing lifestyle of the animal; together with the genus name it translates as 'digging runner of the lair'.

Osmakasaurus.etymology: From Lakota 'osmaka' (canyon) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'canyon lizard'.
Osmakasaurus.description: Osmakasaurus is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur which lived in the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian age) Chilson Member of the Lakota Formation in what is now Buffalo Gap of South Dakota, United States. This genus was named by Andrew T. McDonald in 2011 and the type species is O. depressus.

Ostromia.etymology: Named in honour of John Ostrom, the influential American paleontologist who identified the holotype specimen as an Archaeopteryx
Ostromia.description: Ostromia is a genus of anchiornithid theropod dinosaur containing a single species, Ostromia crassipes. Recovered from the Late Jurassic Painten Formation of Germany, it was named by Christian Foth and Oliver Rauhut in 2017.

species.name: Ostromia crassipes
species.etymology: From Latin 'crassipes' meaning 'thick-footed', combining 'crassus' ('thick') and 'pes' ('foot'), derived from the original name Pterodactylus crassipes given in 1857.

Ouranosaurus.etymology: From Tuareg 'ouranou' meaning 'brave' or 'valiant' (the local name for the monitor lizard) and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', giving the meaning 'brave lizard' or 'valiant lizard'.
Ouranosaurus.description: Ouranosaurus is a genus of herbivorous basal hadrosauriform dinosaur that lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous of modern-day Niger and Cameroon. Ouranosaurus measured about 7–8.3 metres (23–27 ft) long and weighed 2.2 metric tons (2.4 short tons). Two rather complete fossils were found in the Elrhaz Formation, Gadoufaoua deposits, Agadez, Niger, in 1965 and 1970, with a third indeterminate specimen known from the Koum Formation of Cameroon. The animal was named in 1976 by French paleontologist Philippe Taquet, the type species being Ouranosaurus nigeriensis. The generic name is a combination of ourane, a word with multiple meanings, and sauros, the Greek word for lizard. The specific epithet nigeriensis alludes to Niger, its country of discovery (in Latin, the adjectival suffix -iensis means "originating from"). As such, Ouranosaurus nigeriensis could be interpreted as "brave lizard originating from Niger".

species.name: Ouranosaurus nigeriensis
species.etymology: Named for Niger, the country of discovery, with the Latin suffix '-iensis' meaning 'originating from'.

references.authors: Taquet, P.
references.title: Il giacimento di Gadoufaoua [The locality of Gadoufaoua]

Overoraptor.etymology: From Spanish 'overo' (piebald, a coat pattern with irregular patches), combined with Latin 'raptor' (thief); meaning 'piebald thief'.
Overoraptor.description: Overoraptor is an extinct genus of paravian theropod of uncertain affinities from the Late Cretaceous Huincul Formation of Argentinian Patagonia. The genus contains a single species, O. chimentoi, known from several bones of the hands, feet, and hips alongside some vertebrae.

species.name: Overoraptor chimentoi
species.etymology: Named for Roberto Nicolás Chimento, who initially discovered the remains.
