Overosaurus.etymology: Named after the Cerro Overo locality in Patagonia, Argentina, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Overo lizard".
Overosaurus.description: Overosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaurs, containing only a single species, Overosaurus paradasorum. This species lived approximately 86 to 84 million years ago during the latter part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now Patagonia (in southern Argentina). Overosaurus paradasorum was relatively small compared to other sauropods from Patagonia, like the saltasaurids and other aeolosaurines, estimated as approximately 10 m (33 ft). It was a ground-dwelling herbivore.

species.name: Overosaurus paradasorum
species.etymology: Named for the Parada family, who found the specimen and provided logistical support during fieldwork, with the Latin genitive plural suffix '-orum'.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino Urquiza, Rincón de los Sauces

Oviraptor.etymology: From Latin ovum ('egg') and raptor ('thief'), meaning 'egg thief', based on the initial (later revised) interpretation that it was stealing eggs
Oviraptor.description: Oviraptor is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period. The first remains were collected from the Djadokhta Formation of Mongolia in 1923 during a paleontological expedition led by Roy Chapman Andrews, and in the following year the genus and type species Oviraptor philoceratops were named by Henry Fairfield Osborn. The genus name refers to the initial thought of egg-stealing habits, and the specific name was intended to reinforce this view indicating a preference over ceratopsian eggs. Despite the fact that numerous specimens have been referred to the genus, Oviraptor is only known from a single partial skeleton regarded as the holotype, as well as a nest of about fifteen eggs and several small fragments from a juvenile.

synonyms.name: Fenestrosaurus
synonyms.reason: Osborn previously reported the taxon as 'Fenestrosaurus philoceratops'; the designation was later discredited and the specimen is referable to Oviraptor.

species.name: Oviraptor philoceratops
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'philos' meaning 'lover of' and 'keratops' meaning 'horned face', intended to convey a fondness for ceratopsian eggs, based on the initial mistaken interpretation that the holotype was stealing eggs from a Protoceratops nest.

holotype.material: Partial skull and skeleton

Owenodon.etymology: Named for Richard Owen, the British paleontologist who first described the specimen, combined with Greek 'odon' meaning 'tooth'.
Owenodon.description: Owenodon is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur known from a partial lower jaw discovered in Early Cretaceous-aged rocks of Dorset, United Kingdom, and possibly also Romania and Spain. The first and only definitive specimen was found in the Lulworth Formation of the Purbeck Limestone Group, dating to the middle Berriasian stage.

species.name: Owenodon hoggii
species.etymology: Named for naturalist A. J. Hogg, who originally collected the fossil mandible.

Ozraptor.etymology: From "Oz", informal name for Australia, combined with Latin raptor (thief); meaning "Australian thief".
Ozraptor.description: Ozraptor is a genus of possibly abelisauroid theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic (Bajocian) Colalura Sandstone of Australia, known from fragmentary remains.

species.name: Ozraptor subotaii
species.etymology: Named for the fictional character Subotai, the swift-running thief and archer from the 1982 film Conan the Barbarian.

Pachycephalosaurus.etymology: From Greek pachys (παχύς, 'thick'), kephalon (κεφαλή, 'head'), and sauros (σαῦρος, 'lizard'), meaning 'thick-headed lizard'
Pachycephalosaurus.description: Pachycephalosaurus is a genus of pachycephalosaurid ornithischian dinosaur. The type species, P. wyomingensis, is the only known definitive species. The possibly synonymous taxon, Stygimoloch, might represent a distinct genus or a second species, P. spinifer. It lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now western North America. Remains have been excavated in Montana, South Dakota, Wyoming, and Alberta. Mainly known from a single skull and a few extremely thick skull roofs (at 22 cm (8.7 in) thick), Pachycephalosaurus is estimated to have reached 4.5 m (15 ft) long and weighed 370–450 kg (820–990 lb). More complete fossils would come to be found in the following years.

synonyms.name: Tylosteus
synonyms.reason: Formally rejected by ICZN in favor of Pachycephalosaurus, which became a conserved name.

synonyms.name: Dracorex

Pachyrhinosaurus.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'pachys' meaning 'thick', 'rhino' meaning 'nose', and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'thick-nosed lizard', named for the distinctive bony mass on its snout.
Pachyrhinosaurus.description: Pachyrhinosaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of North America. The first examples were discovered by Charles M. Sternberg in Alberta, Canada, in 1946, and named in 1950. Over a dozen partial skulls and a large assortment of other fossils from various species have been found in Alberta and Alaska.

species.name: Pachyrhinosaurus canadensis
species.etymology: Named for Canada, where the holotype specimens were discovered in Alberta.

Pachysuchus.etymology: From Greek pachys (παχύς, 'thick') and Latin/Greek suchos (from Σοῦχος, 'crocodile'), meaning 'thick crocodile', a reference to the robust snout
Pachysuchus.description: Pachysuchus is a dubious extinct genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of China.

Padillasaurus.etymology: Named for Carlos Bernardo Padilla, founder of the Centro de Investigaciones Paleontológicas in Villa de Leyva, Colombia, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Padillasaurus.description: Padillasaurus is an extinct genus of titanosauriform sauropod known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian stage) Paja Formation in Colombia. It contains a single species, Padillasaurus leivaensis, known only from a single partial axial skeleton. Initially described as a brachiosaurid, it was considered to be the first South American brachiosaurid ever discovered and named. Before its discovery, the only known brachiosaurid material on the continent was very fragmentary and from the Jurassic period. However, a more recent study finds it to be a basal somphospondylan.

species.etymology: Named for Villa de Leyva, the Colombian town near which the holotype vertebrae were discovered.

Palaeopteryx.etymology: From Greek palaios (ancient) and pteryx (wing); meaning "ancient wing".
Palaeopteryx.description: Palaeopteryx is an extinct genus of dubious paravian theropod dinosaur from the Morrison Formation of Colorado. The type species is P. thomsoni.

Palaeoscincus.etymology: From Greek 'palaios' meaning 'ancient' and 'skinkos' meaning 'lizard' (related to skink); translates as 'ancient lizard'.
Palaeoscincus.description: Palaeoscincus is a dubious genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur based on teeth from the mid-late Campanian-age Upper Cretaceous Judith River Formation of Montana. Like several other dinosaur genera named by Joseph Leidy (Deinodon, Thespesius, and Trachodon), it is an historically important genus with a convoluted taxonomy that has been all but abandoned by modern dinosaur paleontologists. Because of its wide use in the early 20th century, it was somewhat well known to the general public, often through illustrations of an animal with the armor of Edmontonia and the tail club of an ankylosaurid.

Paludititan.etymology: From Latin palus ('marsh' or 'swamp') and Greek Titan (a giant), meaning 'marsh titan', referring to the marshy paleoenvironment where it was found in Romania
Paludititan.description: Paludititan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which lived in the area of present Romania during the Late Cretaceous. It existed in the island ecosystem known as Hațeg Island.

Pampadromaeus.description: Pampadromaeus is an extinct genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaurs known from the Late Triassic (Carnian) Santa Maria Formation of the Paraná Basin in Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil.

Pamparaptor.etymology: Named for the Pampas region of South America where it was found, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief'; translates as 'thief of the Pampas'.
Pamparaptor.description: Pamparaptor is an extinct genus of paravian theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Portezuelo Formation of the Neuquén province in Argentine Patagonia. Its precise classification is uncertain, but the authors who described this taxon have argued that it is a dromaeosaurid. The genus contains a single species, P. micros (from the Greek word for "small"), which is known from a single specimen consisting of a mostly complete and fully-articulated left foot, which preserves the iconic dromaeosaur-like "killing claw".

Panamericansaurus.description: Panamericansaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of Argentina. The holotype is very similar to known fossil material of Aeolosaurus, which Panamericansaurus is thought to be closely related to.

Pandoravenator.description: Pandoravenator is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian to Tithonian) of central Patagonia (Chubut Province). Fossils in the form of a fragmentally preserved postcranial skeleton of this dinosaur were discovered and scientifically described in 2017 by paleontologists Oliver Rauhut and Diego Pol as the type species P. fernandezorum.

Panguraptor.etymology: Named after Pangu, the Chinese creator deity (also evoking the supercontinent Pangaea), combined with Latin raptor (seizer, robber); meaning "Pangu plunderer".
Panguraptor.description: Panguraptor is a genus of coelophysid theropod dinosaur known from fossils discovered in Lower Jurassic rocks of southern China. The type and only known species is Panguraptor lufengensis. The generic name refers to the deity Pangu but also to the supercontinent Pangaea for which in a geological context the same characters are used: 盘古. Raptor means "seizer", "robber" in Latin. The specific name is a reference to the Lufeng Formation. It was described in 2014 by You Hai-Lu and colleagues.

Panoplosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'panoplos' meaning 'fully armored' or 'well-armored' and '-saurus' meaning 'lizard', referring to its extensive armor plating.
Panoplosaurus.description: Panoplosaurus is a genus of armoured dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada. Few specimens of the genus are known, all from the middle Campanian of the Dinosaur Park Formation, roughly 76 to 75 million years ago. It was first discovered in 1917, and named in 1919 by Lawrence Lambe, named for its extensive armour, meaning "well-armoured lizard". Panoplosaurus has at times been considered the proper name for material otherwise referred to as Edmontonia, complicating its phylogenetic and ecological interpretations, at one point being considered to have existed across Alberta, New Mexico and Texas, with specimens in institutions from Canada and the United States. The skull and skeleton of Panoplosaurus are similar to its relatives, but have a few significant differences, such as the lumpy form of the skull osteoderms, a completely fused shoulder blade, and regularly shaped plates on its neck and body lacking prominent spines. It was a quadrupedal animal, roughly 5 m (16 ft) long and 1,600 kg (3,500 lb) in weight. The skull has a short snout, with a very domed surface, and bony plates directly covering the cheek. The neck had circular groups of plates arranged around the top surface, both the forelimb and hindlimb were about the same length, and the hand may have only included three fingers. Almost the entire surface of the body was covered in plates, osteoderms and scutes of varying sizes, ranging from large elements along the skull and neck, to smaller, round bones underneath the chin and body, to small ossicles that filled in the spaces between other, larger osteoderms.

Panphagia.etymology: From Greek 'pan' meaning 'all' and 'phagein' meaning 'to eat', referring to its interpreted omnivorous diet as a basal sauropodomorph.
Panphagia.description: Panphagia is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur described in 2009. It lived around 231 million years ago, during the Carnian age of the Late Triassic period in what is now northwestern Argentina. Fossils of the genus were found in the La Peña Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin. The name Panphagia comes from the Greek words pan, meaning "all", and phagein, meaning "to eat", in reference to its inferred omnivorous diet. Panphagia is one of the earliest known dinosaurs, and is an important find which may mark the transition of diet in early sauropodomorph dinosaurs.

Pantydraco.description: Pantydraco is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic of the United Kingdom (Wales). It is based on a partial juvenile skeleton once thought to belong to Thecodontosaurus. Only one valid species of Pantydraco is recognised: P. caducus.

Papiliovenator.description: Papiliovenator is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Bayan Mandahu Formation of Inner Mongolia, China. The type and only species is Papiliovenator neimengguensis.

Paralitherizinosaurus.description: Paralitherizinosaurus is an extinct genus of therizinosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Osoushinai Formation of Hokkaido, Japan. The genus contains a single species, Paralitherizinosaurus japonicus, known from a partial right hand and cervical vertebra. Paralitherizinosaurus represents the youngest therizinosaur known from Japan.

Paralititan.etymology: From Greek parali (tidal, of the sea) and titan (giant); meaning "tidal giant".
Paralititan.description: Paralititan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day Egypt during the Late Cretaceous period. It was described by American paleontologist Joshua B. Smith and colleagues in 2001. The genus contains a single species, Paralititan stromeri, named based on a fragmentary skeleton including vertebrae and limb bones. These fossils were unearthed by an American expedition to the Bahariya Oasis in western Egypt in rock layers of the Bahariya Formation. This formation dates to the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, which lasted 101 to 94 million years ago. An incomplete dorsal (back) vertebra that had been described by German paleontologist Ernst Stromer in 1932 was also assigned to Paralititan. However, this vertebra had been destroyed during the Bombing of Munich in World War II.

Paranthodon.description: Paranthodon is a genus of stegosaurian dinosaur that lived in what is now South Africa during the Early Cretaceous, between 139 and 131 million years ago. Discovered in 1845, it was one of the first stegosaurians found. Its only remains, a partial skull, isolated teeth, and fragments of vertebrae, were found in the Kirkwood Formation.

Pararhabdodon.etymology: From Greek 'para' meaning 'near' or 'beside' combined with the genus name Rhabdodon (meaning 'fluted tooth'); translates as 'near fluted tooth', indicating its close relationship to Rhabdodon.
Pararhabdodon.description: Pararhabdodon is a genus of tsintaosaurin hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Maastrichtian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Tremp Group of Spain. The first remains were discovered from the Sant Romà d'Abella fossil locality and assigned to the genus Rhabdodon, and later named as the distinct species Pararhabdodon isonensis in 1993. Known material includes assorted postcranial remains, mostly vertebrae, as well as maxillae from the skull. Specimens from other sites, including remains from France, a maxilla previously considered the distinct taxon Koutalisaurus kohlerorum, an additional maxilla from another locality, the material assigned to the genera Blasisaurus and Arenysaurus, and the extensive Basturs Poble bonebed have been considered at different times to belong to the species, but all of these assignments have more recently been questioned. It was one of the last non-avian dinosaurs known from the fossil record that went extinct during the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.

Parasaurolophus.description: A genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America. Parasaurolophus is best known for its large, elaborate cranial crest that extends back from the skull in a long, curved tube. The hollow crest likely functioned as a resonating chamber for producing sounds and for visual display.

Paraxenisaurus.etymology: From Greek para (near, beside) and xenos (strange) and sauros (lizard); meaning "strange lizard".
Paraxenisaurus.description: Paraxenisaurus is an extinct genus of ornithomimosaurian theropod from the Late Cretaceous Cerro del Pueblo Formation of Coahuila in Mexico. The genus contains a single species, P. normalensis, which is known from a few bones of tail, hips, hands, and feet. The specific epithet was given in honor of the Benemérita Normal School of Coahuila, a teacher training institution, where the fossils were reposited. It is a member of the family Deinocheiridae and is the only member of that clade known from Laramidia.

species.name: Paraxenisaurus normalensis
species.etymology: Named in honor of the Benemérita Normal School (Escuela Normal) of Coahuila, Mexico, the teacher-training institution where the holotype fossils were reposited.

holotype.material: Partial postcranial skeleton

Pareisactus.etymology: From Greek pareisaktos (intruder); referring to the specimen being found as a single element among hundreds of hadrosaurid bones.
Pareisactus.description: Pareisactus is a genus of rhabdodontid ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (lower Maastrichtian) Conquès Member of the Tremp Formation in the Southern Pyrenees of Spain. The type and only species is P. evrostos, known only from a single scapula.

species.name: Pareisactus evrostos
species.etymology: From Greek 'evrostos' meaning 'robust', in reference to the great mediolateral thickness of the proximal scapula and the massive build of the deltoid ridge.

references.authors: PÁRRAGA, JAVIER; PRIETO-MÁRQUEZ, ALBERT
references.title: Pareisactus evrostos, a new basal iguanodontian (Dinosauria: Ornithopoda) from the Upper Cretaceous of southwestern Europe

Parksosaurus.etymology: Named after Canadian paleontologist William A. Parks, who discovered the specimen, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Parks's lizard'
Parksosaurus.description: Parksosaurus is a genus of neornithischian dinosaur from the early Maastrichtian-aged (Upper Cretaceous) Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, Canada. It is based on most of a partially articulated skeleton and partial skull, showing it to have been a small, bipedal, herbivorous dinosaur. It is one of the few described non-hadrosaurid ornithopods from the end of the Cretaceous in North America, existing around 70 million years ago.

species.name: Parksosaurus warreni
species.etymology: Named for Mrs. H. D. Warren, who financially supported the research that led to the description of the holotype specimen.

references.authors: Sternberg, C. M.

Paronychodon.etymology: From Greek 'para' meaning 'beside', 'onyx' meaning 'claw', and 'odon' meaning 'tooth'; translates as 'beside claw tooth', referring to the claw-like nature of the tooth.
Paronychodon.description: Paronychodon is an extinct theropod dinosaur genus. It is a tooth taxon, often considered dubious because of the fragmentary nature of the fossils, which include "buckets" of teeth from many disparate times and places but no other remains, and should be considered a form taxon.

species.name: Paronychodon lacustris
species.etymology: From Latin 'lacustris' meaning 'belonging to a lake' or 'lake-dwelling', referencing the marshy, lacustrine environment of the Judith River Formation where the holotype was found.

Parvicursor.etymology: From Latin parvus (small) and cursor (runner); meaning "small runner".
Parvicursor.description: Parvicursor is a genus of very small alvarezsaurid maniraptoran dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of Mongolia. It had long, slender legs adapted for fast running.

species.name: Parvicursor remotus
species.etymology: From Latin 'remotus' meaning 'remote', 'deviating', or 'far from', likely referring to the phylogenetic distance of P. remotus from other Alvarezsauridae or its unique, specialized, or 'deviating' features that set it apart from other small dinosaurs found in the same region.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Karhu, A. A.; Rautian, A. S.

Patagonykus.etymology: Named for Patagonia, the region of Argentina where it was found, combined with Greek 'onyx' meaning 'claw'; translates as 'Patagonian claw'.
Patagonykus.description: Patagonykus is a genus of alvarezsauroid theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Argentina. It was discovered in exposures of the Portezuelo Formation (Turonian-Coniacian) of the Rio Neuquén Subgroup in the Neuquén Basin, Neuquén Province. The holotype consists of an incomplete but well-preserved skeleton, lacking a skull, but including many vertebrae, the coracoids, a partial forelimb, pelvic girdle, and hindlimbs. Patagonykus has been classed with the Alvarezsauridae, a family which includes such taxa as the Mongolian Mononykus and the also Argentinian Alvarezsaurus. In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 1 meter (3.3 ft) and its weight at 3.5 kilograms (7.7 lb).

species.name: Patagonykus puertai
species.etymology: Named in honor of Pablo Puerta, Argentine fossil hunter and preparator.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales ‘Bernardino Rivadavia’

Patagopelta.etymology: Named after Patagonia, the region in Argentina where it was found, combined with Latin pelta (shield); meaning "Patagonian shield".
Patagopelta.description: Patagopelta is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (upper Campanian–lower Maastrichtian) Allen Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, P. cristata, known from several partial skeletons, isolated bones, and osteoderms. While originally described as a member of the family Nodosauridae, later discoveries provided support for parankylosaurian affinities. Patagopelta is a small armored dinosaur, comparable in size to the 'dwarf' nodosaurid Struthiosaurus, at about 2 m (6.6 ft) long. It is larger, more robust, and more heavily armored than other paranklyosaurs such as Stegouros.

species.name: Patagopelta cristata
species.etymology: From Latin 'cristata' meaning 'crested', referring to the large crests on the cervical osteoderms and femur of the holotype.

references.authors: Riguetti, Facundo; Pereda-Suberbiola, Xabier; Ponce, Denis; Salgado, Leonardo; Apesteguía, Sebastián; Rozadilla, Sebastián; Arbour, Victoria
references.title: A new small-bodied ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of North Patagonia (Río Negro Province, Argentina)

Patagosaurus.etymology: Named for Patagonia, the region of Argentina where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Patagonia lizard'.
Patagosaurus.description: Patagosaurus is an extinct genus of eusauropod dinosaur from the middle Toarcian of Patagonia, Argentina. It was first found in deposits of the Cañadón Asfalto Formation, which date to around 178 million years ago. Although originally twelve specimens were assigned to the taxon, at least one of them may belong to a different genus. Patagosaurus probably lived alongside genera such as Piatnitzkysaurus, Condorraptor, and Volkheimeria.

species.name: Patagosaurus fariasi
species.etymology: Named for Ricardo Farias, on whose land in the Cañadón Asfalto region of Patagonia the initial discovery was made.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales ‘Bernardino Rivadavia’

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.
references.title: Dinosaurs: A Jurassic Assemblage from Patagonia
references.publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

Patagotitan.etymology: Named for Patagonia, the region of Argentina where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant', referencing its enormous size.
Patagotitan.description: Patagotitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) Cerro Barcino Formation in Chubut Province, Patagonia, Argentina. The genus contains a single species known from at least six young adult individuals, Patagotitan mayorum, which was first announced in 2014 and then named in 2017 by José Carballido and colleagues. Originally thought to be the largest known titanosaur and land animal overall, preliminary studies and press releases suggested that Patagotitan had an estimated length of 37 m (121 ft) and an estimated weight of 69 tonnes (76 short tons). Later research revised the length estimate down to 31 m (102 ft) and weight estimates down to approximately 50–60 tonnes (55–66 short tons), suggesting that Patagotitan was of a similar size to, if not smaller than, its closest relatives Argentinosaurus and Puertasaurus. Still, Patagotitan is one of the best-known titanosaurs, and so its interrelationships with other titanosaurs have been relatively consistent in phylogenetic analyses. This led to its use in a re-definition of the group Colossosauria by Carballido and colleagues in 2022.

species.name: Patagotitan mayorum
species.etymology: Named for the Mayo family, owners of the La Flecha ranch in Chubut Province, Argentina, where the holotype and paratype specimens were excavated.

references.authors: Carballido, José L.; Pol, Diego; Otero, Alejandro; Cerda, Ignacio A.; Salgado, Leonardo; Garrido, Alberto C.; Ramezani, Jahandar; Cúneo, Néstor R.; Krause, Javier M.
references.title: A new giant titanosaur sheds light on body mass evolution among sauropod dinosaurs
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

Pawpawsaurus.etymology: Named for the Paw Paw Formation in Texas where it was discovered, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Pawpawsaurus.description: Pawpawsaurus, meaning "Pawpaw Lizard", is a nodosaurid ankylosaur from the Cretaceous (late Albian) of Tarrant County, Texas, discovered in May 1992. The only species yet assigned to this taxon, Pawpawsaurus campbelli, is based on a complete skull (lacking mandibles) from the marine Paw Paw Formation (Washita Group).

species.name: Pawpawsaurus campbelli
species.etymology: Named for Cameron Campbell, who discovered the holotype skull in the Paw Paw Formation of Tarrant County, Texas, in May 1992.

holotype.institution: Schuler Museum of Paleontology, Southern Methodist University

Pectinodon.etymology: From Latin pecten ('comb') and Greek odon (ὀδών, 'tooth'), meaning 'comb tooth', referring to the comb-like serrations on the rear edge of its teeth
Pectinodon.description: Pectinodon is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaurs from the end of the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period (66 mya). It currently contains a single valid species, Pectinodon bakkeri (sometimes classified as Troodon bakkeri), known only from teeth.

species.name: Pectinodon bakkeri
species.etymology: Named for Robert Thomas Bakker, the paleontologist honored by Kenneth Carpenter when the species was named in 1982.

holotype.institution: University of Colorado Museum of Natural History

Pedopenna.etymology: From Latin pedo- (pes/pedis, 'foot') and penna ('feather' or 'quill'), meaning 'foot feather', referring to the long pennaceous feathers on the metatarsus
Pedopenna.description: Pedopenna (meaning "foot feather") is a genus of small, feathered, maniraptoran dinosaur from the Daohugou Beds in China. It is possibly older than Archaeopteryx, though the age of the Daohugou Beds where it was found is debated. A majority of studies suggest that the beds probably date from between the late Middle Jurassic (168 million years ago) and early Late Jurassic Period (164-152 million years ago).

species.name: Pedopenna daohugouensis
species.etymology: Named for Daohugou, the locality in China where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

Pegomastax.etymology: From Greek pego- (πηγός, 'strong' or 'stout') and mastax (μάσταξ, 'jaw' or 'mouth'), meaning 'strong jaw', referring to its robust lower jaw
Pegomastax.description: Pegomastax is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic of South Africa. The only known specimen was discovered in a 1966–1967 expedition in Transkei District of Cape Province, but was not described until 2012 when Paul Sereno named it as the new taxon Pegomastax africana. The genus name is derived from the Greek for "strong jaw", and the species name describes the provenance of Africa; it was originally spelled africanus, was corrected to africana to align with the gender of the genus name.

species.name: Pegomastax africanus
species.etymology: From Latin 'africanus' meaning 'pertaining to Africa', after South Africa, the country where the holotype was discovered.

references.title: Taxonomy, morphology, masticatory function and phylogeny of heterodontosaurid dinosaurs

Peishansaurus.etymology: Named after Beishan (Peishan in older romanisation), meaning 'Northern Mountains' in Chinese (Chinese: 北山, Běishān), in Gansu Province where the specimen was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'
Peishansaurus.description: Peishansaurus was a genus of ornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period (late Santonian-Campanian stages), roughly 85-72 million years ago.

species.name: Peishansaurus philemys
species.etymology: From Greek 'phileo' meaning 'to love' and 'emys' meaning 'water turtle', meaning 'lover of turtles', in reference to the co-occurrence of the turtle Peishanemys latipons at the same site.

Pelecanimimus.etymology: From Latin pelecanus (pelican) and mimus (mimic); meaning "pelican mimic", referring to the long snout and throat pouch.
Pelecanimimus.description: Pelecanimimus is an extinct genus of basal ("primitive") ornithomimosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Spain. It is notable for possessing more teeth than any other member of the Ornithomimosauria (or any other theropod), most of which were toothless.

species.name: Pelecanimimus polyodon
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'polys' meaning 'many' and 'odous' meaning 'tooth', referring to the exceptionally large number of teeth (approximately 220) possessed by this ornithomimosaur.

Pellegrinisaurus.etymology: Named after Pellegrini Lake (Lago Pellegrini) in Río Negro Province, Argentina, where the holotype was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Pellegrini lizard'
Pellegrinisaurus.description: Pellegrinisaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous period. The holotype was found in the Allen Formation, Argentina.

species.name: Pellegrinisaurus powelli
species.etymology: Named for Jaime E. Powell, the assistant who helped discover the holotype at Pellegrini Lake, Argentina.

Pendraig.etymology: From Middle Welsh 'pen' meaning 'chief' or 'head' and 'draig' meaning 'dragon'; translates as 'chief dragon', a poetic reference to its discovery in Wales.
Pendraig.description: Pendraig is a genus of coelophysoid theropod dinosaur from South Wales. It contains one species, Pendraig milnerae, named after Angela Milner. The specimen was discovered in the Pant-y-Ffynnon quarry. In life it would have measured 1 m (3.3 ft) in length.

species.name: Pendraig milnerae
species.etymology: Named for Angela Milner, the paleontologist who rediscovered the lost holotype fossils in the collections of the Natural History Museum, London.

Penelopognathus.etymology: From Greek penelops (wild duck) and gnathos (jaw); meaning "wild duck jaw".
Penelopognathus.description: Penelopognathus is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur which lived in the Early Cretaceous Bayin-Gobi Formation in what is now China. The discovery of this taxon contributes to the hypothesis that hadrosauroids originated in Asia.

species.name: Penelopognathus weishampeli
species.etymology: Named for David Weishampel, the paleontologist honored by the describers Godefroit, Li, and Shang when the species was named in 2005.

Pentaceratops.etymology: From Greek 'pente' meaning 'five', 'keras' meaning 'horn', and 'ops' meaning 'face'; translates as 'five-horned face', referring to the five horn-like projections on its skull.
Pentaceratops.description: Pentaceratops is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsid dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of what is now North America. Fossils of this animal were first discovered in 1921, but the genus was named in 1923 when its type species, Pentaceratops sternbergii, was described. Pentaceratops lived around 76–73 million years ago, its remains having been mostly found in the Kirtland Formation in the San Juan Basin in New Mexico. Another species, P. aquilonius, was named by Nick W. Longrich in 2014, but it is debated if it belongs to that genus or a separate taxon. About a dozen skulls and skeletons have been uncovered, so anatomical understanding of Pentaceratops is fairly complete. One exceptionally large specimen later became its own genus, Titanoceratops, due to its more derived morphology, similarities to Triceratops, and lack of unique characteristics shared with Pentaceratops.

species.name: Pentaceratops sternbergii
species.etymology: Named for Charles Hazelius Sternberg, who discovered the holotype skull in the Kirtland Formation of New Mexico in 1922.

Perijasaurus.etymology: Named after the Serranía del Perijá mountain range in Colombia where the fossil was discovered, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Perija lizard".
Perijasaurus.description: Perijasaurus is a genus of basal eusauropod sauropod dinosaur from the "Girón-type redbeds" of the La Quinta Formation of Cesar Department, north-eastern Colombia. The type species is Perijasaurus lapaz. It lived during the Toarcian-Aalenian boundary around 175 million years ago (early to middle Jurassic period).

species.etymology: Named for La Paz, a town in Cesar Department, Colombia, near where the holotype was discovered, and also evoking the Spanish word 'paz' meaning 'peace', in reference to the peace agreement that allowed the describers to conduct fieldwork in the region.

Petrobrasaurus.etymology: Named after Petrobras, the Brazilian state oil company that operated in the region where the fossil was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Petrobras lizard'
Petrobrasaurus.description: Petrobrasaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur. It is a titanosaur which lived during the upper Cretaceous period (Coniacian-Santonian age) in what is now Rincón de los Sauces, Patagonia, Argentina. It is known from the holotype MAU-Pv-PH-449 — a partial disarticulated skeleton recovered from the Plottier Formation (Neuquén Basin), Argentina. This genus was named by Leonardo S. Filippi, José Ignacio Canudo, Leonardo J. Salgado, Alberto C. Garrido, Rodolfo A. Garcia, Ignacio A. Cerda and Alejandro Otero in 2011, and the type species is Petrobrasaurus puestohernandezi. The generic name is derived from "Petrobras" (oil company) and saurus, "lizard". The specific name refers to the Puesto Hernández oil field, where the fossil remains were found.

species.name: Petrobrasaurus puestohernandezi
species.etymology: Named for the Puesto Hernández oil field in Neuquén, Argentina, where the holotype fossil remains were found.

Petrustitan.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'pétra' meaning 'stone/rock' (referring to the rocky outcrops of the type locality, Sânpetru) and 'titán' meaning 'giant', a common suffix used when naming titanosaurian sauropods.
Petrustitan.description: Petrustitan is a eutitanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of Romania. The type and only species is P. hungaricus, originally assigned to the genus Magyarosaurus.

species.name: Petrustitan hungaricus
species.etymology: From Latin 'hungaricus' meaning 'Hungarian', referring to Hungary, the country of origin, as the fossil was originally assigned to the Hungarian-named genus Magyarosaurus.

Phaedrolosaurus.etymology: From Greek phaedros (elated, bright, gleaming) and sauros (lizard); meaning "elated lizard".
Phaedrolosaurus.description: Phaedrolosaurus is a dubious genus of coelurosaurian (perhaps dromaeosaurid) theropod dinosaur, based on an isolated and non-diagnostic tooth from the Early Cretaceous Lianmuqin Formation of Wuerho, in the autonomous region of Xinjiang, China.

Philovenator.etymology: From Greek philos (loving) and Latin venator (hunter); literally meaning "love hunter".
Philovenator.description: Philovenator is an extinct genus of troodontid paravian dinosaurs from the Wulansuhai Formation (dated to the Campanian age, sometime between 75 and 71 million years ago) of Inner Mongolia, China. Its specific name honors Phillip J. Currie.

Phuwiangosaurus.etymology: Named after the Phu Wiang area of Thailand where the fossil was discovered, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Phu Wiang lizard".
Phuwiangosaurus.description: Phuwiangosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian-Hauterivian) Sao Khua Formation of Thailand. The type species, P. sirindhornae, was described by Martin, Buffetaut, and Suteethorn in a 1993 press release and was formally named in 1994. The species was named to honor Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn of Thailand, who was interested in the geology and palaeontology of Thailand, while the genus was named after the Phu Wiang area, where the fossil was discovered. The precise affinities of Phuwiangosaurus among titanosauriform sauropods are uncertain, though several studies have classified it as a euhelopodid.

species.name: Phuwiangosaurus sirindhornae
species.etymology: Named for Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn of Thailand, who was known for her interest in the geology and palaeontology of the country.

Phuwiangvenator.etymology: Named for the Phu Wiang mountains in Thailand where the holotype was discovered, combined with Latin 'venator' meaning 'hunter'.
Phuwiangvenator.description: Phuwiangvenator is an extinct genus of megaraptoran theropod that lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now Thailand. It contains only the type species, P. yaemniyomi. The generic name of Phuwiangvenator comes from the Phu Wiang mountains, where the holotype was discovered, and the Latin word "venator" meaning hunter. The specific name, "yaemniyomi", is in honor of Sudham Yaemniyom, who was a historical paleontologist from Thailand and the first person to discover fossils there.

species.etymology: Named for Sudham Yaemniyom, a historical paleontologist from Thailand and the first person to discover dinosaur fossils there.

Phyllodon.etymology: From Greek 'phyllon' meaning 'leaf' and 'odon' meaning 'tooth'; translates as 'leaf tooth', named for the leaf-shaped teeth.
Phyllodon.description: Phyllodon is a genus of small ornithischian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Camadas de Guimarota Formation of Leiria, Portugal and possibly also the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian) Chipping Norton Limestone of England. It may have been closely related to contemporaneous ornithischian dinosaurs from North America. This genus is known from teeth and possibly partial lower jaws. The name is also in use for a genus of modern moss, but this is not considered to be a problem because the two organisms are in two different kingdoms.

species.etymology: Named in honor of Siegfried Henkel, a German paleontologist who discovered the Guimarota coal mine lignite beds in Portugal, which yielded the holotype jaw fragment.

Piatnitzkysaurus.etymology: Named after Alejandro Piatnitzky, a Russian-born Argentine geologist, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Piatnitzky's lizard".
Piatnitzkysaurus.description: Piatnitzkysaurus is a genus of tetanuran theropod dinosaur that lived approximately 179 to 177 million years ago during the lower part of the Jurassic Period in what is now Argentina. Piatnitzkysaurus was a moderately large, lightly built, bipedal, ground-dwelling carnivore that could grow over 4 m (13.1 ft) long.

Pilmatueia.etymology: Named after the Pilmatué locality in Neuquén Province, Argentina, where the fossils were discovered.
Pilmatueia.description: Pilmatueia is a genus of diplodocoid sauropods belonging to the family Dicraeosauridae that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Argentina. Its type and only species is Pilmatueia faundezi. Pilmatueia was probably closely related to other South American dicraeosaurids such as Amargasaurus. Like other dicraeosaurids, Pilmatueia was relatively small for a sauropod. The vertebrae of Pilmatueia were more extensively hollowed out by air sacs than in other dicraeosaurids, which otherwise were characterized by a reduction in the air sac system compared to other sauropods. Pilmatueia dates to the Valanginian, an age of the Cretaceous period for which dinosaur faunas are poorly known.

Pinacosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'pinax' meaning 'plank' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'plank lizard', named for the small rectangular plank-like scutes covering its head.
Pinacosaurus.description: Pinacosaurus is a genus of ankylosaurid thyreophoran dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago), mainly in Mongolia and China.

species.name: Pinacosaurus grangeri

Pitekunsaurus.etymology: From Mapudungun pitekun, meaning 'to discover', combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'discovery lizard'
Pitekunsaurus.description: Pitekunsaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Anacleto Formation of Neuquén, Argentina. It was described by L. Filippi and A. Garrido in 2008. The type species is P. macayai. The generic name is derived from Mapudungun pitekun, meaning "to discover", the epitheton honours the discoverer, oil company explorer Luis Macaya, who found the fossil in April 2004.

species.etymology: Named for Luis Macaya, an oil company explorer who discovered the fossil in April 2004.

Piveteausaurus.etymology: Named after French paleontologist Jean Piveteau, who first described the type specimen, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Jean Piveteau's lizard".
Piveteausaurus.description: Piveteausaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur known from a partial skull discovered in the Middle Jurassic (164.7 to 161.2 million years ago) Marnes de Dives of Calvados, northern France. In 2012, Thomas Holtz gave a possible length of 11 metres (36 ft).

Planicoxa.etymology: From Latin 'planus' meaning 'flat' and 'coxa' meaning 'hip', referring to a distinctive flat feature of the hip bones.
Planicoxa.description: Planicoxa is a genus of advanced iguanodontian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of North America. It is known from the partial skeletons of several individual specimens. Its fossils were discovered in Utah, United States.

Plateosauravus.description: Plateosauravus is a basal plateosaurian of uncertain affinities from the Late Triassic Elliot Formation of South Africa.

Plateosaurus.etymology: From Greek platys (broad, flat) and sauros (lizard); probably meaning "broad lizard" (often mistranslated as "flat lizard").
Plateosaurus.description: Plateosaurus is a genus of plateosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic epoch of the Triassic period, around 214 to 204 million years ago, in what is now Central and Northern Europe. Plateosaurus is a basal (early) sauropodomorph dinosaur, a so-called "prosauropod". The type species is Plateosaurus trossingensis; before 2019, that honor was given to Plateosaurus engelhardti, but it was ruled as undiagnostic (i.e. indistinguishable from other dinosaurs) by the ICZN. Currently, there are three valid species; in addition to P. trossingensis, P. longiceps and P. gracilis are also known. However, others have been assigned in the past, and there is no broad consensus on the species taxonomy of plateosaurid dinosaurs. Similarly, there are a plethora of synonyms (invalid duplicate names) at the genus level.

synonyms.name: Pachysaurus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by another lizard genus; replaced by Pachysauriscus (1959), and the underlying material is now considered referable to Plateosaurus.

synonyms.reason: Coined (1961) as a replacement name for the preoccupied Pachysaurus; junior to Pachysauriscus (1959, also a Pachysaurus replacement) and ultimately referable to Plateosaurus.

Platypelta.etymology: From Greek platys (πλατύς, 'flat' or 'broad') and Latin pelta ('small shield'), meaning 'flat shield', referring to the broad, flat armour of this ankylosaurid
Platypelta.description: Platypelta is an extinct genus of herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaurs within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae. It is known from the Late Cretaceous Dinosaur Park Formation (early Late Campanian stage, about 77.5-76.5 Ma ago) of southern Alberta, Canada. The type species is Platypelta coombsi.

Platytholus.etymology: From Greek 'platys' meaning 'flat' or 'broad' and 'tholos' meaning 'dome', referring to the flattened dome on the skull of this pachycephalosaurid.
Platytholus.description: Platytholus is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) Hell Creek Formation of the United States. The genus contains a single species, P. clemensi, known from a partial skull.

Plesiohadros.description: Plesiohadros is an extinct genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur. It is known from a partial skeleton including the skull collected at Alag Teg locality, from the Campanian Alagteeg Formation of southern Mongolia. The type species is Plesiohadros djadokhtaensis.

Pleurocoelus.etymology: From Greek pleurá ('side, rib') and koilos ('hollow'), referring to the deep pleurocoels (lateral hollows) on the vertebrae
Pleurocoelus.description: Pleurocoelus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur named by O. C. Marsh in 1888 from juvenile remains found in the Arundel Formation of Maryland. Pneumatoraptor.etymology: From Greek 'pneuma' meaning 'air' or 'breath', combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief', likely referring to pneumatic (air-filled) features in the bones.
Pneumatoraptor.description: Pneumatoraptor is a genus of small paravian, possibly a dromaeosaurid, dinosaur that lived in Hungary. It is known from a single complete left shoulder girdle (scapulocoracoid) found in the Csehbánya Formation of the Iharkút locality in the Bakony Mountains of western Hungary. This formation dates to the late Cretaceous period (Santonian age) about 85 million years ago.

Podokesaurus.etymology: From Greek podoces (πόδας ὠκύς, podas okys, 'swift-footed'), meaning 'swift-footed lizard', referring to its presumed agility
Podokesaurus.description: Podokesaurus is a genus of coelophysoid dinosaur that lived in what is now the eastern United States during the Early Jurassic Period. The first fossil was discovered by the geologist Mignon Talbot near Mount Holyoke, Massachusetts, in 1910. The specimen was fragmentary, preserving much of the body, limbs, and tail. In 1911, Talbot described and named the new genus and species Podokesaurus holyokensis based on it. The full name can be translated as "swift-footed lizard of Holyoke". This discovery made Talbot the first woman to find and describe a non-bird dinosaur. The holotype fossil was recognized as significant and was studied by other researchers, but was lost when the building it was kept in burned down in 1917; no unequivocal Podokesaurus specimens have since been discovered. It was made state dinosaur of Massachusetts in 2022.

Poekilopleuron.etymology: From Greek poikilos (varied, diverse) and pleuron (rib); meaning "varied ribs".
Poekilopleuron.description: Poekilopleuron is a genus of carnosaurian theropod dinosaur, which lived during the middle Bathonian of the Jurassic, about 168 to 166 million years ago. The genus has been used under many different spelling variants, although only one, Poekilopleuron, is valid. The type species is P. bucklandii, named after William Buckland, and many junior synonyms of it have also been erected. Little material is currently known, as the holotype was destroyed in World War II, although many casts of the material still exist.

Polacanthus.etymology: From Ancient Greek polys (πολύς, 'many') and akantha (ἄκανθα, 'thorn' or 'prickle'), meaning 'many thorns', referring to the numerous spikes on its body
Polacanthus.description: Polacanthus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaurs from the early Cretaceous (130–125 million years ago) of England. Several species have been named in the genus Polacanthus, but only the type species, Polacanthus foxii, is currently seen as valid. There are not many fossil remains of this dinosaur, and some important anatomical features, such as its skull, are poorly known. It grew to about 4–5 metres (13–16 ft) long. Its body was covered with armour plates and spikes. It may be a basal member of the Nodosauridae or part of a separate family, the Polacanthidae.

Fossils of the dinosaur were found in the Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin. The type species, Powellvenator podocitus, was named by Martin Ezcurra in 2017.

Pradhania.etymology: Named in honour of Dhuiya Pradhan, a fossil collector at the Indian Statistical Institute who contributed to paleontological work in India
Pradhania.description: Pradhania is a genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Sinemurian-age (Early Jurassic) Upper Dharmaram Formation of India. It was first named by T. S. Kutty, Sankar Chatterjee, Peter M. Galton and Paul Upchurch in 2007 and the type species is Pradhania gracilis. It was a sauropodomorph of modest size, only about four meters (13 ft) long, and is known from fragmentary remains. It was originally regarded as a basal sauropodomorph but new cladistic analysis performed by Novas et al., 2011 suggests that Pradhania is a massospondylid. Pradhania presents two synapomorphies of Massospondylidae recovered in their phylogenetic analysis.

Prenoceratops.etymology: From Greek prene- (πρηνή, 'bent forwards' or 'prone'), cerat- (κερατ-, 'horn'), and ops (ωψ, 'face'), meaning 'bent or prone-horned face'
Prenoceratops.description: Prenoceratops, (meaning 'bent or prone-horned face' and derived from Greek prene-/πρηνη- meaning 'bent forwards' or 'prone', cerat-/κερατ- meaning 'horn' and -ops/ωψ meaning 'face') is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period. It was a relatively small dinosaur, reaching 1.3 m (4.3 ft) in length and 20 kg (44 lb) in body mass. Its fossils have been found in the upper Two Medicine Formation in the present-day U.S. state of Montana, in Campanian age rock layers that have been dated to 74.3 million years ago. Fossils were also found in the Oldman Formation in the modern day Canadian province of Alberta, dating to around 77 million years ago.

Priconodon.description: Priconodon is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur (perhaps nodosaurid), mainly known from its large teeth. Its remains have been found in the Early Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian age) Arundel Formation of Muirkirk, Prince George's County, Maryland, USA, and possibly the Potomac Group, also located in Maryland. As an ankylosaur, Priconodon would have been a large armored quadrupedal herbivore, though no size estimation has been done due to the scarcity of described remains.

Proa.etymology: From Spanish 'proa' meaning 'prow', alluding to the pointed shape of the animal's predentary bone.
Proa.description: Proa is a genus of basal iguanodont dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Escucha Formation of Aragón, Spain. The type and only species, Proa valdearinnoensis, is known from fragmentary remains and represents an unusual hadrosauriform from the Albian stage.

species.name: Proa valdearinnoensis
species.etymology: Named for Val de Ariño, the traditional name for the coal mines near where the first fossils were found.

holotype.institution: Museo Aragonés de Paleontología, Fundación Conjunto Paleontológico de Teruel-Dinópolis (FCPT-D)

references.authors: MCDONALD, ANDREW T.; ESPÍLEZ, EDUARDO; MAMPEL, LUIS; KIRKLAND, JAMES I.; ALCALÁ, LUIS
references.title: An unusual new basal iguanodont (Dinosauria: Ornithopoda) from the Lower Cretaceous of Teruel, Spain

Probactrosaurus.etymology: From Latin pro (before) and the genus name Bactrosaurus; meaning "before Bactrosaurus", reflecting the hypothesis that it was the direct ancestor of Bactrosaurus.
Probactrosaurus.description: Probactrosaurus is an extinct genus of basal hadrosauroid iguanodontian dinosaur that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous period.

species.name: Probactrosaurus gobiensis
species.etymology: Named for the Gobi Desert of Inner Mongolia, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Rozhdestvensky, A. K.
references.title: Novye igyanodonti ie tsentrallinoy Asii. Phillogeneticheskye y taksonomicheskye veaimoothoshenia poednich Iguanodontidae y rannich Hadrosauridae [New iguanodonts from central Asia. Phylogenetic and taxonomic relationships of late Iguanodontidae and early Hadrosauridae]

Probrachylophosaurus.etymology: From Greek pro- (πρό, 'before' or 'ancestral to') prefixed to Brachylophosaurus, indicating a suspected ancestral relationship; meaning 'before Brachylophosaurus'
Probrachylophosaurus.description: Probrachylophosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in North America. Fossils have been found in rocks of the Judith River Formation in Montana and the Foremost Formation in Alberta, and date to the Campanian age, c. 80.45–79 million years ago. The only recognized species is Probrachylophosaurus bergei. First discovered in Montana in 1981 and not fully excavated until 2008, it was initially suspected to be a new species of Brachylophosaurus. However, in 2015 it was named as a distinct genus, with its name reflecting a suspected ancestral relationship. Both an adult and subadult specimen were originally recognized, and in 2021 fragmentary remains would extend its known range into the Foremost Formation. Thought to be a close relative of the later Brachylophosaurus and Ornatops, and a possible descendant of the older Acristavus, it represents a possible transitional state in brachylophosaurin evolution. Nonetheless, whether this represents a single evolutionary lineage or a series of diverging or convergent branches remains unclear, as does its relation to the genus Maiasaura.

species.name: Probrachylophosaurus bergei
species.etymology: Named for Sam Berge, one of the landowners who donated the holotype fossil to the Museum of the Rockies and supported the research.

references.authors: Freedman Fowler, Elizabeth A.; Horner, John R.
references.title: A New Brachylophosaurin Hadrosaur (Dinosauria: Ornithischia) with an Intermediate Nasal Crest from the Campanian Judith River Formation of Northcentral Montana

Proceratosaurus.etymology: From Greek pro- (πρό, 'before' or 'precursor of') prefixed to Ceratosaurus, as it was originally thought to be closely related to or ancestral to Ceratosaurus; meaning 'before Ceratosaurus'
Proceratosaurus.description: Proceratosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic in what is now England. The holotype and only known specimen consists of a mostly complete skull with an accompanying lower jaw and a hyoid bone, found near Minchinhampton, a town in Gloucestershire. It was originally described in 1910 as a species of Megalosaurus, M. bradleyi, but was moved to its own genus, Proceratosaurus, in 1926. The genus was named for its supposed close relationship with Ceratosaurus, later shown to be erroneous, due to perceived resemblance of Proceratosaurus's incomplete cranial crest to Ceratosaurus's nasal horn.

species.name: Proceratosaurus bradleyi
species.etymology: Named for F. Lewis Bradley, who discovered the holotype skull during excavation for a reservoir near Minchinhampton, England.

references.authors: Huene, F. v.
references.title: On several known and unknown reptiles of the order Saurischia from England and France
references.journal: Annals and Magazine of Natural History, series 9

Procompsognathus.etymology: From Greek pro- (πρό, 'before' or 'precursor of') prefixed to Compsognathus (Greek kompsos 'elegant' + gnathos 'jaw'); meaning 'before Compsognathus' or 'precursor of the elegant jaw'
Procompsognathus.description: Procompsognathus is an extinct genus of coelophysid theropod dinosaur that lived approximately 210 million years ago during the later part of the Triassic Period, in what is now Germany. Procompsognathus was a small-sized, lightly built, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore, that could grow up to 1 m (3.3 ft) long.

species.name: Procompsognathus triassicus
species.etymology: From Latin 'triassicus' meaning 'Triassic', referring to the geologic time period in which the animal lived.

references.authors: Fraas, E.
references.title: Die neuesten Dinosaurierfunde in der schw�bischen Trias
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Prodeinodon.etymology: From Greek pro (before) and the genus name Deinodon; meaning "before Deinodon".
Prodeinodon.description: Prodeinodon is a wastebasket taxon and a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian to Aptian stages) from the Xinlong Formation in the Napai Basin of China and from the Oosh Formation of Mongolia. Two species have been formally identified (with a third informal species), all three known only from tooth fragments, showing no diagnostic features, making them difficult to classify, though they may belong to a carnosaur. At least some of the referred species may represent basal carcharodontosaurid theropods similar to Acrocanthosaurus.

species.name: Prodeinodon mongoliense
species.etymology: Named for Mongolia, where the holotype tooth was collected from the Oosh Formation, with the Latin suffix '-ense' meaning 'from'.

holotype.material: Isolated teeth

references.authors: Osborn, H. F.
references.title: Sauropoda and Theropoda from the Lower Cretaceous of Mongolia

Propanoplosaurus.etymology: From Latin prefix 'pro-' (before) combined with the genus name Panoplosaurus, meaning 'before Panoplosaurus', reflecting that it lived earlier than but resembled Panoplosaurus.
Propanoplosaurus.description: Propanoplosaurus is a genus of herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Patuxent Formation of Maryland, USA. Its type specimen is a natural cast and partial natural mold of a hatchling.

species.name: Propanoplosaurus marylandicus
species.etymology: Named for Maryland, the U.S. state where the holotype was found in the Patuxent Formation, with the Latin suffix '-icus' meaning 'of' or 'from'.

holotype.institution: National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution

references.authors: Stanford, Ray; Weishampel, David B.; Deleon, Valerie B.
references.title: The First Hatchling Dinosaur Reported from the Eastern United States: Propanoplosaurus marylandicus (Dinosauria: Ankylosauria) from the Early Cretaceous of Maryland, U.S.A.

Prosaurolophus.etymology: From Greek pro (before) and the genus name Saurolophus (crested lizard); meaning "before Saurolophus", referring to it being an earlier dinosaur with a similar head crest.
Prosaurolophus.description: Prosaurolophus is a genus of hadrosaurid (or duck-billed) dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America. It is known from the remains of at least 25 individuals, including skulls and skeletons, but this remains obscure. Its fossils have been found in the late Campanian-aged Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, and the roughly contemporaneous Two Medicine Formation in Montana, dating to around 75.7 to 74.1 million years ago. Its most recognizable feature is a small solid crest formed by the nasal bones, sticking up in front of the eyes.

species.name: Prosaurolophus maximus
species.etymology: From Latin 'maximus' meaning 'greatest' or 'largest', referring to the large size of the type specimen.

references.authors: Brown, B.
references.title: A new crested trachodont dinosaur, Prosaurolophus maximus
references.journal: Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History

Protarchaeopteryx.etymology: From Greek protos (before) and the genus name Archaeopteryx; meaning "before Archaeopteryx".
Protarchaeopteryx.description: Protarchaeopteryx is a genus of turkey-sized feathered theropod dinosaur from China. Known from the Jianshangou bed of the Yixian Formation, it lived during the early Aptian age of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 124.6 million years ago. It was probably a herbivore or omnivore, although its hands were very similar to those of small carnivorous dinosaurs. It appears to be one of the most basal members of the Oviraptorosauria, closely related to Incisivosaurus, or a taxon slightly less closely related to birds than oviraptorosaurs were.

species.name: Protarchaeopteryx robusta
species.etymology: From Latin 'robusta' meaning 'robust' or 'strong', referring to the sturdy build of the animal.

references.authors: Ji, Q.; Ji, S.-A.
references.title: [Protarchaeopteryx gen. nov.—a new genus of Archaeopterygidae in China]

Protathlitis.description: Protathlitis is a potentially dubious and chimeric genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Arcillas de Morella Formation of Castellón, Spain. The type and only species is Protathlitis cinctorrensis, known from a partial skeleton. It was originally identified as a basal member of the Baryonychinae. If a spinosaurid identity of the material is correct, its discovery, as well as those of the spinosaurids Camarillasaurus, Iberospinus, Riojavenatrix, and the contemporary Vallibonavenatrix shows that the Iberian Peninsula held a diverse assemblage of these theropods during the Early Cretaceous.

species.name: Protathlitis cinctorrensis
species.etymology: Named for Cinctorres, the town in Castellón, Spain, where the holotype remains were discovered.

holotype.material: Maxillary fragment and caudal vertebrae

references.authors: Santos-Cubedo, Andrés; de Santisteban, Carlos; Poza, Begoña; Meseguer, Sergi
references.title: A new spinosaurid dinosaur species from the Early Cretaceous of Cinctorres (Spain)
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Protoavis.etymology: From Greek protos (first) and Latin avis (bird); meaning "first bird".
Protoavis.description: Protoavis is a problematic taxon known from fragmentary remains from Late Triassic Norian stage deposits near Post, Texas. The animal's true classification has been the subject of much controversy, and there are many different interpretations of what the taxon actually is. When it was first described, the fossils were described as being from a primitive bird which, if the identification is valid, would push back avian origins some 60–75 million years.

species.name: Protoavis texensis
species.etymology: Named for Texas, the US state where the holotype was discovered.

references.authors: Chatterjee, S.
references.title: Cranial anatomy and relationships of a new Triassic bird from Texas
references.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London B

Protognathosaurus.etymology: From Greek protos (first, early) and gnathos (jaw) and sauros (lizard); meaning "early jaw lizard".
Protognathosaurus.description: Protognathosaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Lower Shaximiao Formation in Sichuan, present-day China.

synonyms.name: Protognathus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Protognathus (Insecta).

species.name: Protognathosaurus oxyodon
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'oxys' meaning 'sharp' and 'odon' meaning 'tooth', referring to the sharp replacement teeth visible in the known fossil jaw fragment.

references.authors: Olshevsky, G.
references.title: A revision of the parainfraclass Archosauria Cope, 1869, excluding the advanced Crocodylia

Protohadros.etymology: From Greek 'protos' meaning 'first' and 'hadros' meaning 'thick' (as in Hadrosauridae), meaning 'first hadrosaur.' The specific name byrdi honours discoverer Gary Byrd.
Protohadros.description: Protohadros is a genus of basal hadrosaurid dinosaur from the early Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian stage, approximately 100-93.9 million years ago) of what is now Texas, United States. It is represented by the species Protohadros byrdi, known from a partially complete skull and associated postcranial remains recovered from the Woodbine Formation. Protohadros was one of the earliest derived hadrosaurs in North America.

species.name: Protohadros byrdi
species.etymology: Named for Gary Byrd, the part-time palaeontologist who discovered the first remains of the species in 1994.

holotype.institution: Shuler Museum of Paleontology, Southern Methodist University

references.authors: Head, Jason J.
references.title: A new species of basal hadrosaurid (Dinosauria, Ornithischia) from the Cenomanian of Texas

Pteropelyx.etymology: From Greek pteron (wing) and pelyx (pelvis); meaning "winged pelvis".
Pteropelyx.description: Pteropelyx is a dubious genus of Late Cretaceous hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Judith River Formation of Montana, named by Edward Drinker Cope in 1889. Historically, several species were assigned to it, all based on extremely fragmentary remains, but there is no evidence to support these assignments, making the type species, P. grallipes, the only valid species. Most of these other species' remains likely belong to better-known hadrosaurs, such as Lambeosaurus and Gryposaurus. It is probable that the type material of Pteropelyx, a skeleton lacking a skull, is from Corythosaurus (making Pteropelyx its senior synonym) (Brett-Surman, 1989), but the lack of a skull makes such a synonymy impossible to determine with sure certainty as no certain evidence pertain to prove the organ to be present.

species.name: Pteropelyx grallipes
species.etymology: From Latin 'grallae' meaning 'stilts' and 'pes' meaning 'foot', likely referring to the long-legged proportions of the animal.

references.authors: Cope, E. D.
references.title: Notes on the Dinosauria of the Laramie

Pterospondylus.etymology: From Greek 'pteron' meaning 'wing' and 'spondylos' meaning 'vertebra', meaning 'winged vertebra.' The species name trielbae references the Triassic period and the Elbe River area.
Pterospondylus.description: Pterospondylus is a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur from the Late Triassic. It was a coelophysid theropod which lived in what is now Germany (Trossingen Formation). The type species, Pterospondylus trielbae, (derived from "Tri", in reference to the Triassic period, and "Elba", for the Elbe River area), was described by Jaekel in 1913–14 for a single back vertebra found inside the shell of the Proganochelys turtle. Sometimes, it is aligned with Procompsognathus, or even considered to be synonymous with it, despite being based on a vertebra that is twice the size of the corresponding bone in Procompsognathus. P. trielbae has no diagnostic features and is therefore considered a nomen dubium.

species.name: Pterospondylus trielbae
species.etymology: Combining 'Tri' in reference to the Triassic period during which the animal lived, and 'Elba' for the Elbe River area of Germany where the specimen was found.

references.authors: Jaekel, Otto
references.title: Über die Wirbeltierfunde in der oberen Trias von Halberstadt
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Puertasaurus.etymology: Named for Pablo Puerta, one of the field workers who discovered the fossil specimen, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Puertasaurus.description: Puertasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous Period. It is known from a single specimen recovered from sedimentary rocks of the Cerro Fortaleza Formation in southwestern Patagonia, Argentina, which probably is Campanian or Maastrichtian in age. The only species is Puertasaurus reuili. Described by the paleontologist Fernando Novas and colleagues in 2005, it was named in honor of Pablo Puerta and Santiago Reuil, who discovered and prepared the specimen. It consists of four well-preserved vertebrae, including one cervical, one dorsal, and two caudal vertebrae. Puertasaurus is a member of Titanosauria, the dominant group of sauropods during the Cretaceous.

species.name: Puertasaurus reuili
species.etymology: Named for Santiago Reuil, one of the fossil hunters who discovered and prepared the holotype specimen in Patagonia, Argentina.

references.authors: Novas, Fernando; Salgado, Leonardo; Calvo, Jorge; Agnolin, Federico
references.title: Giant titanosaur (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia
references.journal: Revista del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales

Pukyongosaurus.etymology: Named after Pukyong National University in South Korea, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Pukyong lizard".
Pukyongosaurus.description: Pukyongosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform dinosaur that lived in South Korea during the Early Cretaceous Period (Aptian - Albian). It may have been closely related to Euhelopus, and is known from a series of vertebrae in the neck and back. The characteristics that were originally used to distinguish this genus have been criticized as being either widespread or too poorly preserved to evaluate, rendering the genus an indeterminate nomen dubium among titanosauriforms. A 2022 study noted that Pukyongosaurus is probably a somphospondylan.

species.name: Pukyongosaurus millenniumi
species.etymology: From Latin 'millennium' meaning 'a thousand years', referring to the year 2000 around which the fossil material was described, marking the turn of the millennium.

holotype.material: Partial skeleton cataloged as PKNUG-G 102 through PKNUG-G 109

references.authors: Dong, Z.; Paik, I. S.; H. J. Kim
references.title: A preliminary report on a sauropod from the Hasandong Formation (Lower Cretaceous), Korea
references.journal: Proceedings of the Eighth Annual Meeting of the Chinese Society of Vertebrate Paleontology

Pulanesaura.etymology: From Sesotho 'Pulane' meaning 'rain-maker/bringer' (in reference to the heavy rain conditions during collection) and Latin 'saura' (feminine of sauros) meaning 'lizard'.
Pulanesaura.description: Pulanesaura is an extinct genus of basal sauropodiform known from the Early Jurassic (late Hettangian to Sinemurian) Upper Elliot Formation of the Free State, South Africa. It contains a single species, Pulanesaura eocollum, known from partial remains of at least two subadult to adult individuals.

species.name: Pulanesaura eocollum
species.etymology: From Greek 'eo' meaning 'dawn' and Latin 'collum' meaning 'neck', referring to Pulanesaura being a very basal sauropod that had not yet evolved the characteristically elongated neck of more derived sauropods.

holotype.institution: Evolutionary Studies Institute (formerly Bernard Price Institute for Palaeontological Research), University of the Witwatersrand

references.authors: McPhee, Blair W.; Bonnan, Matthew F.; Yates, Adam M.; Neveling, Johann; Choiniere, Jonah N.
references.title: A new basal sauropod from the pre-Toarcian Jurassic of South Africa: evidence of niche-partitioning at the sauropodomorph–sauropod boundary?
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Punatitan.etymology: Named for the puna, the high-altitude Andean plateau characterized by oxygen-depleted atmosphere, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'; meaning 'puna giant.'
Punatitan.description: Punatitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Ciénaga del Río Huaco Formation of La Rioja, Argentina. It contains one species, Punatitan coughlini.

species.name: Punatitan coughlini
species.etymology: Named for geologist Tim Coughlin, who first reported dinosaur fossils at the discovery locality in La Rioja, Argentina.

location.locality: Quebrada de Santo Domingo (upper section: 170 m bed)

references.title: Two Late Cretaceous sauropods reveal titanosaurian dispersal across South America

Pycnonemosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'pyknos' (dense, thick) + 'nemos' (woodland, forest) + 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'dense forest lizard'.
Pycnonemosaurus.description: Pycnonemosaurus is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur that belonged to the family Abelisauridae. It was found in the Upper Cretaceous red conglomerate sandstones of the Cachoeira do Bom Jardim Formation, Mato Grosso, Brazil, and it lived during the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

species.name: Pycnonemosaurus nevesi
species.etymology: Named for Dr. Iedo Batista Neves, who died in 2000 and who encouraged the pursuit of palaeontological studies, particularly those of describer Alexander Kellner.

holotype.institution: Collection of the Earth Science Museum of the National Department of Mineral Production
holotype.material: Teeth and postcranial fragments

references.authors: Kellner, A. W. A.; Campos, D. d. A.
references.title: On a theropod dinosaur (Abelisauria) from the continental Cretaceous of Brazil
references.journal: Arquivos do Museu Nacional, Rio de Janeiro

Pyroraptor.etymology: From Greek pyr (fire) and Latin raptor (thief); meaning "fire thief", named because the first fossils were found after a forest fire.
Pyroraptor.description: Pyroraptor is an extinct genus of paravian dinosaur, probably a dromaeosaurid or unenlagiid, from the Late Cretaceous Ibero-Armorican island, of what is now southern France. It lived during the late Campanian and early Maastrichtian stages, approximately 72 million years ago. It is known from a single partial specimen that was found in Provence in 1992, after a forest fire. The animal was named Pyroraptor olympius by Allain and Taquet in 2000.

species.name: Pyroraptor olympius
species.etymology: Named for Mont Olympe, the mountain in Provence, France, at the foot of which the animal's remains were unearthed.

references.authors: Allain, Ronan; Taquet, Philippe
references.title: A new genus of Dromaeosauridae (Dinosauria, Theropoda) from the Upper Cretaceous of France

Qantassaurus.etymology: Named after Qantas, the Australian airline, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); honours the national carrier of the country where it was discovered.
Qantassaurus.description: Qantassaurus is a genus of basal two-legged, plant-eating elasmarian ornithischian dinosaur that lived in Australia about 125-112 million years ago, when the continent was still partly south of the Antarctic Circle. It was described by Patricia Vickers-Rich and her husband Tom Rich in 1999 after a find near Inverloch, and named after Qantas, the Australian airline.

species.name: Qantassaurus intrepidus
species.etymology: From Latin 'intrepidus' meaning 'intrepid' or 'fearless', referring to the climatic challenges the small dinosaur faced living within the Antarctic Circle.

references.authors: Rich, T. H.; Vickers-Rich, P.
references.title: The Hypsilophodontidae from southeastern Australia
references.journal: Proceedings of the Second Gondwanan Dinosaur Symposium, National Science Museum Monographs

Qianjiangsaurus.etymology: Named for Qianjiang District, Chongqing Municipality, China, where the type locality is located, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Qianjiang lizard.'
Qianjiangsaurus.description: Qianjiangsaurus is an extinct genus of hadrosauroidean ornithopod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Zhengyang Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, Q. changshengi, known from a partial skeleton. Qianjiangsaurus is one of the few hadrosauroids named from south China, and it indicates important fauna connections between similarly aged formations in Mongolia.

species.name: Qianjiangsaurus changshengi
species.etymology: Named for Changsheng Wang, the discoverer of the Chongqing fossil locality where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Chongqing Laboratory of Geoheritage Protection and Research

references.authors: Dai, Hui; Ma, Qingyu; Xiong, Can; Lin, Yu; Zeng, Hui; Tan, Chao; Wang, Jun; Zhang, Yuguang; Xing, Hai
references.title: A new late-diverging non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroid (Dinosauria: Ornithopoda) from southwest China: Support for interchange of dinosaur faunas across East Asia during the Late Cretaceous

Qianlong.etymology: From Mandarin '黔' (Qian), a name for Guizhou Province, China, and 'long' (龙) meaning 'dragon'; meaning 'Guizhou dragon.' The specific name shouhu means 'guarding' in Mandarin, referencing the associated adult and embryo fossils.
Qianlong.description: Qianlong is an extinct genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic Ziliujing Formation of China. Known from partial skeletons of three mature individuals associated with several eggs, some of which contain embryos, these fossils may represent the oldest leathery eggs currently known.

species.name: Qianlong shouhu
species.etymology: From Mandarin 'shouhu' (守护) meaning 'guarding' or 'protecting', in reference to the discovery of the adult skeleton in close association with fossil eggs containing embryos.

references.authors: Han, Fenglu; Yu, Yilun; Zhang, Shukang; Zeng, Rong; Wang, Xinjin; Cai, Huiyang; Wu, Tianzhuang; Wen, Yingfeng; Cai, Sifu; Li, Chun; Wu, Rui; Zhao, Qi; Xu, Xing
references.title: Exceptional Early Jurassic fossils with leathery eggs shed light on dinosaur reproductive biology

Qianzhousaurus.etymology: Named for Qianzhou, the older name of Ganzhou, China, where the remains were discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Qianzhou lizard.'
Qianzhousaurus.description: Qianzhousaurus is a genus of tyrannosaurid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period. There is currently only one species named, the type species Qianzhousaurus sinensis, which is a member of the tribe Alioramini and most closely related to Alioramus, the only other known alioramin.

species.name: Qianzhousaurus sinensis
species.etymology: From the Greek-derived Latin 'sinensis' meaning 'of China' or 'Chinese', derived from 'Sinai' (Σῖναι), a classical reference to China.

holotype.material: Partial sub-adult individual with nearly complete skull, cervical vertebrae, dorsal vertebrae, caudal vertebrae, scapulocoracoids, partial ilia, and left leg
