references.title: A new clade of Asian Late Cretaceous long-snouted tyrannosaurids
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Qiaowanlong.etymology: Named after Qiaowan, the area in Gansu Province, China where the fossil was found, combined with Chinese long (dragon); meaning "Qiaowan dragon".
Qiaowanlong.description: Qiaowanlong is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur. Fossils belonging to the genus were found in the Yujinzi Basin of what is today Gansu Province, China. The remains come from a geological formation called the Xiagou Formation in the Xinminpu Group, dating to the late Aptian Stage of the Early Cretaceous.

species.name: Qiaowanlong kangxii
species.etymology: Named for the Kangxi Emperor, the second emperor of the Qing dynasty, who was said to have had dreams of the Qiaowan area near where the fossil was discovered.

holotype.institution: The Fossil Research and Development Center of the Third Geology and Mineral Resources Exploration Academy of Gansu Provincial Bureau of Geo-exploration and Mineral Development

references.authors: You, Hai-Lu; Li, Da-Qing
references.title: The first well-preserved Early Cretaceous brachiosaurid dinosaur in Asia
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

Qijianglong.etymology: Named after Qijiang District in Chongqing, China, where fossils were discovered, combined with Chinese 'long' (dragon).
Qijianglong.description: Qijianglong is a genus of herbivorous mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaurs. It is known from the Suining Formation of China, which is of a debated age (reported as Late Jurassic or Early Cretaceous using different methods). The genus contains a single species, Qijianglong guokr, known from a partial skeleton including cranial bones, most of the neck and tail, and other associated elements.

species.name: Qijianglong guokr
species.etymology: Named for Guokr (果壳网), a Chinese scientific social network, meaning 'nutshell' in Chinese.

holotype.institution: Qijiang Petriﬁed Wood and Dinosaur Footprint National Geological Park Museum

references.title: A new sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of China and the diversity, distribution, and relationships of mamenchisaurids

Qingxiusaurus.etymology: Named for Qingxiu, a shortened form of the Chinese phrase meaning 'a picturesque scenery of mountains and water in Guangxi', combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Qingxiu lizard.'
Qingxiusaurus.description: Qingxiusaurus is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Dashi Site of Guangxi, China. The type species, described by Mo et al. in 2008, is Q. youjiangensis. Like other sauropods, Qingxiusaurus would have been a large quadrupedal herbivore. It is known from only limited remains collected in 1991: Two humeri, two sternal plates, and the neural spine of a single vertebra.

species.name: Qingxiusaurus youjiangensis
species.etymology: Named for the Youjiang region of Guangxi, China, where the fossil material was collected.

holotype.institution: Natural History Museum of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region

references.authors: Mo, J.-Y.; Huang, C.-L.; Z.-R. Zhao, W. Wang, X. Xu
references.title: A new titanosaur (Dinosauria: Sauropoda) from the Late Cretaceous of Guangxi, China

Qinlingosaurus.etymology: Named after the Qinling mountain range of Shaanxi Province, China, where the first fossils were recovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard).
Qinlingosaurus.description: Qinlingosaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Asia.

species.name: Qinlingosaurus luonanensis
species.etymology: Named for Luonan County in Shaanxi Province, China, near where the holotype was discovered.

references.authors: Xue, Xiangxu; Zhang, Yunxiang; Bi, Yan; Yue, Leping; Chen, Danling
references.title: The development and environmental changes of the intermontane basins in the eastern part of Qinling Mountains
references.book: The development and environmental changes of the intermontane basins in the eastern part of Qinling Mountains

Qiupalong.etymology: From Chinese 'Qiupa' (the Qiupa Formation where it was found) + 'long' (dragon), meaning 'dragon from the Qiupa Formation'.
Qiupalong.description: Qiupalong is an extinct genus of ornithomimosaurian theropod that was discovered in the Late Cretaceous Qiupa Formation of Henan, China. The genus contains a single species, Q. henanensis, the specific epithet for which was named for the province of Henan. Uniquely, Qiupalong is one of the few Late Cretaceous non-avian dinosaurs known from both Asia and Laramidia. A specimen from Alberta has been referred to the genus without being assigned to the type species or suggested to be similar to it. A fossil of an ornithomimid similar to Qiupalong has also been described from Russian Far East.

species.name: Qiupalong henanensis
species.etymology: Named for Henan Province, China, where the holotype was discovered.

references.authors: Xu, Li; Kobayashi, Yoshitsugu; Lü, Junchang; Lee, Yuong-Nam; Liu, Yongqing; Tanaka, Kohei; Zhang, Xingliao; Jia, Songhai; Zhang, Jiming
references.title: A new ornithomimid dinosaur with North American affinities from the Late Cretaceous Qiupa Formation in Henan Province of China

Qiupanykus.etymology: Named after the Qiupa Formation where the fossil was found, combined with Greek onyx (claw); meaning "claw from the Qiupa Formation".
Qiupanykus.description: Qiupanykus is an extinct genus of alvarezsaurid theropod from the Late Cretaceous Qiupa Formation of Henan Province, China. The type and only species is Q. zhangi, named for Shuancheng Zhang, who assisted in finding the fossils of Qiupanykus.

species.name: Qiupanykus zhangi
species.etymology: Named for Shuancheng Zhang, who assisted in finding the fossils of Qiupanykus in Henan Province, China.

holotype.material: Partial postcranial skeleton including cervical vertebrae, sacral vertebrae, caudal vertebrae, partial ilium and ischium, pubis, articulated right hindlimb, digits, pedal claws

references.authors: Lü, JC; Xu, L; Chang, HL; Jia, SH; Zhang, JM; Gao, DS; Zhang, YY; Zhang, CJ; Ding, F
references.title: A new alvarezsaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Qiupa Formation of Luanchuan, Henan Province, central China

Quaesitosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'quaesitus' (extraordinary, sought-after, unusual) + Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'extraordinary lizard'.
Quaesitosaurus.description: Quaesitosaurus is a genus of nemegtosaurid sauropod containing only the type species, Q. orientalis, described in 1983. It lived from 72 to 71 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous epoch in the Barun Goyot Formation. With long, low and horse-like with frontally located peg-teeth, the skull of Quaesitosaurus is similar enough to the skull of Diplodocus and its kin to have prompted informed speculation that the missing body was built like those of diplodocids.

species.name: Quaesitosaurus orientalis
species.etymology: From Latin 'orientalis' meaning 'eastern', referring to the fossil's origin in Mongolia.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Kurzanov, S. M.; Bannikov, A. F.
references.title: Nouviy sauropod ys uerchnego mela MNR [New sauropod from the Upper Cretaceous of Mongolia]

Quetecsaurus.etymology: From the Milcayac word 'quetec' meaning 'fire', combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'fire lizard.'
Quetecsaurus.description: Quetecsaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of the southern Mendoza Province, western Argentina. It contains a single species, Quetecsaurus rusconii.

species.name: Quetecsaurus rusconii
species.etymology: Named in honor of Carlos Rusconi (1898–1969), a naturalist who worked extensively in Mendoza Province and was Director of the Museo de Ciencias Naturales 'Juan Cornelio Moyano'.

holotype.institution: Universidad Nacional de Cuyo, Laboratorio de Dinosaurios

references.authors: González Riga, B. J.; Ortiz David, L.
references.title: A new titanosaur (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the Upper Cretaceous (Cerro Lisandro Formation) of Mendoza Province, Argentina

Quilmesaurus.etymology: Named for the Quilmes, an indigenous people of northwestern Argentina, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Quilmesaurus.description: Quilmesaurus is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian to Maastrichtian stages) Allen Formation of Argentina. It was a member of Abelisauridae, closely related to genera such as Carnotaurus. The only known remains of this genus are leg bones which share certain similarities to a variety of abelisaurids. However, these bones lack unique features, which may render Quilmesaurus a nomen vanum (more commonly known as a nomen dubium, or "dubious name").

species.name: Quilmesaurus curriei
species.etymology: Named for Dr. Philip John Currie, a Canadian theropod specialist.

references.authors: Coria, R. A.
references.title: New theropod from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia

Qunkasaura.etymology: From 'Qunka' (or 'Kunka'), the old Spanish name that gave rise to Cuenca in Castilla-La Mancha, Spain, where the Lo Hueco site is located, combined with Greek 'saura' meaning 'lizard'.
Qunkasaura.description: Qunkasaura is a genus of saltasauroid titanosaur dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian–Maastrichtian) Lo Hueco site of the Villalba de la Sierra Formation of Spain. The type species is Qunkasaura pintiquiniestra.

species.name: Qunkasaura pintiquiniestra
species.etymology: Named for Queen Pintiquiniestra, a character from Miguel de Cervantes's novel Don Quixote, in a nod to the Spanish provenance of the fossil site at Lo Hueco, Cuenca.

holotype.institution: Museo de las Ciencias de Castilla-La Mancha

references.authors: Mocho, Pedro; Escaso, Fernando; Marcos-Fernández, Fátima; Páramo, Adrián; Sanz, José Luis; Vidal, Daniel; Ortega, Francisco
references.title: A Spanish saltasauroid titanosaur reveals Europe as a melting pot of endemic and immigrant sauropods in the Late Cretaceous
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Rahiolisaurus.etymology: Named after Rahioli, the village in Gujarat, India, near where the fossils were recovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard).
Rahiolisaurus.description: Rahiolisaurus is a genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaur which existed in India during the Late Cretaceous period. It was described in 2010, based on fossils recovered from the Lameta Formation in the Indian state of Gujarat. These fossils include elements from at least seven different individuals and are believed to have been from the Maastrichtian stage, sometime between 70 and 66 million years ago, making it one of the last non-avian dinosaurs known in the fossil record. Despite representing a variety of different growth stages, all recovered fossils from the locality indicate a single species, the type species Rahiolisaurus gujaratensis.

species.name: Rahiolisaurus gujaratensis
species.etymology: Named for Gujarat, the Indian state where the fossils were recovered from the Lameta Formation.

references.authors: Novas, Fernando E.; Chatterjee, Sankar; Rudra, Dhiraj K.; Datta, P.M.
references.title: Rahiolisaurus gujaratensis, n. gen. n. sp., A New Abelisaurid Theropod from the Late Cretaceous of India

Rahonavis.etymology: From Malagasy 'rahona' meaning 'cloud' or 'menace' and Latin 'avis' meaning 'bird', named for its bird-like nature and discovery in Madagascar.
Rahonavis.description: Rahonavis is a genus of bird-like theropod from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian, from about 70 to 66 mya) of what is now northwestern Madagascar. It is known from a partial skeleton (UA 8656) found by Catherine Forster and colleagues in Maevarano Formation rocks at a quarry near Berivotra, Mahajanga Province. Rahonavis was a small predator, at about 70 centimetres (2.3 ft) long and 0.45-2.27 kg (1-5 lbs), with the typical dromaesaurid-like raised sickle claw on the second toe. It was the first coelurosaur discovered in Africa, with Nqwebasaurus being the second.

synonyms.name: Rahona
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Rahona (Lepidoptera).

species.name: Rahonavis ostromi
species.etymology: Named for John Ostrom, the American palaeontologist renowned for his work on dromaeosaurids and the theropod origin of birds.

references.authors: Forster, Catherine A.; Sampson, Scott D.; Chiappe, Luis M.; Krause, David W.
references.title: Genus Correction
references.publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

Rajasaurus.description: Rajasaurus is a genus of carnivorous abelisaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of India, containing one species: Rajasaurus narmadensis. The bones were excavated from the Lameta Formation in the Gujarat state of Western India, probably inhabiting what is now the Narmada River Valley. It was formally described by palaeontologist Jeffrey A. Wilson and colleagues in 2003 based on a partial skeleton comprising the braincase, spine, hip bone, legs, and tail–a first for an Indian theropod. The dinosaur likely measured 6.6 metres (22 ft), and had a single horn on the forehead which was probably used for display and head-butting. Like other abelisaurids, Rajasaurus was probably an ambush predator.

species.name: Rajasaurus narmadensis
species.etymology: Named for the Narmada River in central India, near whose valley the fossils were discovered.

holotype.material: Partial skull and postcranial skeleton

references.authors: Wilson, J. A.; Sereno, P. C.; S. Srivastava, D. K. Bhatt, A. Khosla, A. Sahni
references.title: A new abelisaurid (Dinosauria, Theropoda) from the Lameta Formation (Cretaceous, Maastrichtian) of India
references.journal: Contributions from the Museum of Paleontology, University of Michigan

Rapator.etymology: Problematic etymology — von Huene provided no explanation; 'Rapator' appears rarely in Medieval Latin meaning 'violator', possibly intended as 'plunderer' or 'predator'.
Rapator.description: Rapator is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Griman Creek Formation of New South Wales, Australia, dating to the Cenomanian age of the Cretaceous period. It contains only the type species, Rapator ornitholestoides, which was originally named by Friedrich von Huene in 1932.

species.name: Rapator ornitholestoides
species.etymology: From Greek '-oides' meaning 'resembling', combined with Ornitholestes, a small coelurosaur; the single known hand bone displays a prominent dorsomedial process similar to that of Ornitholestes.

holotype.material: Single left metacarpal (hand bone), opalised

references.authors: Huene, F. v.
references.title: Die fossile Reptil-Ordnung Saurischia, ihre Entwicklung und Geschichte [The fossil reptile order Saurischia, their development and history]
references.journal: Monographien zur Geologie und Palaeontologie, serie 1

Rapetosaurus.etymology: From Malagasy 'rapeto' (a giant mischievous creature in Malagasy folklore) + Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'Rapeto lizard'.
Rapetosaurus.description: Rapetosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in Madagascar from 70 to 66 million years ago, at the end of the Cretaceous Period. Only one species, Rapetosaurus krausei, has been identified. Like other sauropods, Rapetosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore. It is calculated to have reached lengths of 15 m (49 ft) in adulthood.

species.name: Rapetosaurus krausei
species.etymology: Named for David W. Krause, the palaeontologist who led the field team that excavated the holotype in Madagascar from 1993 onwards.

references.authors: Curry Rogers, K. A.; Forster, C. A.
references.title: The last of the dinosaur titans: a new sauropod from Madagascar

Raptorex.description: Raptorex is a controversial genus of tyrannosaurid dinosaur. Its fossil remains consist of a single juvenile specimen probably uncovered in Mongolia, or possibly northeastern China. The type species is R. kriegsteini, described in 2009 by Sereno and colleagues. The genus name is derived from Latin raptor, "robber", and rex, "king". The specific name honours Roman Kriegstein, a survivor of the Holocaust, whose son Henry Kriegstein donated the specimen to the University of Chicago for scientific study.

species.name: Raptorex kriegsteini
species.etymology: Honours Roman Kriegstein, a Holocaust survivor, whose son Henry Kriegstein donated the specimen to the University of Chicago for study

holotype.institution: Long Hao Institute of Geology and Palaeontology

references.authors: Sereno, Paul C.; Tan, Lin; Brusatte, Stephen L.; Kriegstein, Henry J.; Zhao, Xijin; Cloward, Karen
references.title: Tyrannosaurid Skeletal Design First Evolved at Small Body Size
references.publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

Ratchasimasaurus.etymology: Named after Nakhon Ratchasima province in Thailand where the fossil was found, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Nakhon Ratchasima lizard".
Ratchasimasaurus.description: Ratchasimasaurus is a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage) Khok Kruat Formation of Nakhon Ratchasima province in northeastern Thailand. The type and only species is R. suranareae, named after Thao Suranari, a 19th-century war heroine. It was considered by one study to be a nomen dubium, diagnosed with characters widespread in Styracosterna.

species.name: Ratchasimasaurus suranareae
species.etymology: Named for Thao Suranari, a 19th-century Thai war heroine celebrated in Nakhon Ratchasima Province, where the fossil was discovered.

references.authors: SHIBATA, Masateru; JINTASAKUL, Pratueng; AZUMA, Yoichi
references.title: A New Iguanodontian Dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Khok Kruat Formation, Nakhon Ratchasima in Northeastern Thailand

Rativates.etymology: From Latin 'ratis' meaning 'raft' (in reference to the bird group Ratites) and 'vates' meaning 'seer'; the ornithomimids seemingly foretold the future existence of the ratites they resembled.
Rativates.description: Rativates is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaur from the Campanian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, Canada. The type species is Rativates evadens.

species.name: Rativates evadens
species.etymology: From Latin 'evadens' meaning 'evading', referring both to the animal's fleet-footed ability to escape predators and to the specimen's eighty-year evasion of recognition as a distinct species.

references.authors: McFeeters, Bradley; Ryan, Michael J.; Schröder-Adams, Claudia; Cullen, Thomas M.
references.title: A new ornithomimid theropod from the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, Canada

Rayososaurus.etymology: Named after the Rayoso Formation in Neuquén Province, Argentina, where the specimen was excavated, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard).
Rayososaurus.description: Rayososaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur in the family Rebbachisauridae. Rayososaurus was named by Argentinian paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1996. Its type and only accepted species is Rayososaurus agrioensis. The species Limaysaurus tessonei was at one point included in Rayososaurus as Rayososaurus tessonei.

species.name: Rayososaurus agrioensis
species.etymology: Named for the Agrio River near which the holotype was found, in Neuquén Province, Argentina.

location.locality: 3 km south of Agrio del Medio

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales ‘Bernardino Rivadavia’

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.
references.title: Cretaceous tetrapods of Argentina

Rebbachisaurus.etymology: Named for the Aït Rebbach, a Berber tribal group in the Errachidia Province of Morocco near where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Aït Rebbach lizard.'
Rebbachisaurus.description: Rebbachisaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Africa during the Late Cretaceous period, between 99 and 97 million years ago. The only valid species is R. garasbae. However, two other species have been assigned to the genus; R. tessonei, now Limaysaurus tessonei, and the nomen dubium R. tamesnensis. Known from a single, incomplete skeleton, much of R. garasbae's anatomy is unknown. The skeleton, discovered in 1948, was unearthed in the Errachidia Province of Morocco from strata of the Kem Kem Beds.

species.name: Rebbachisaurus garasbae
species.etymology: Named for the Gara Sbaa fossil locality in the Kem Kem Beds of Morocco where the holotype was unearthed.

references.authors: Lavocat, R.
references.title: Sur les dinosauriens du Continental Intercalaire des Kem-Kem de la Daoura [On the dinosaurs from the Continental Intercalaire of the Kem Kem of the Doura]
references.journal: Congrés Géologique International, Comptes Rendus de la Dix-Neuvième Session, Section 13

Regaliceratops.etymology: From Latin regalis (royal) and Greek keras (horn) and ops (face); meaning "Royal horned face".
Regaliceratops.description: Regaliceratops is a monospecific genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from Alberta, Canada that lived during the Late Cretaceous (middle Maastrichtian stage, 68.5 to 67.5 Ma) in what is now the St. Mary River Formation. The type and only species, Regaliceratops peterhewsi, is known only from an adult individual with a nearly complete skull lacking the lower jaw, which was nicknamed "Hellboy". Regaliceratops was named in 2015 by Caleb M. Brown and Donald M. Henderson. Regaliceratops has an estimated length of 5 metres (16 ft) and body mass of 2 metric tons (2.2 short tons). The skull of Regaliceratops displays features more similar to centrosaurines, which suggests convergent evolution in display morphology in ceratopsids.

species.name: Regaliceratops peterhewsi
species.etymology: Named for Peter Hews, the geologist who discovered the type specimen along the Oldman River in southwestern Alberta in 2005.

references.authors: Brown, Caleb M.; Henderson, Donald M.
references.title: A New Horned Dinosaur Reveals Convergent Evolution in Cranial Ornamentation in Ceratopsidae

Regnosaurus.etymology: Named for the Regni, the ancient Roman name for the people of Sussex, England, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Sussex lizard.'
Regnosaurus.description: Regnosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous presumably armored dinosaur known from the early Cretaceous Wealden Formation of England. The genus contains a single species, Regnosaurus northamptoni, known from a single partial jaw bone. Regnosaurus has traditionally been regarded as a stegosaur, possibly related to the Jurassic Huayangosaurus of China. Later research considers it to be a dubious, indeterminate thyreophoran.

species.name: Regnosaurus northamptoni
species.etymology: Named for Spencer Compton, 2nd Marquess of Northampton, who was president of the Royal Society at the time the species was described.

references.authors: Mantell, G. A.
references.title: On the structure of the jaws and teeth of the Iguanodon
references.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London

Rhabdodon.etymology: From Greek rhabdos (fluted, rod-like) and odon (tooth); meaning "fluted tooth".
Rhabdodon.description: Rhabdodon is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur that lived in Europe approximately 72-69 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous. The genus contains a single species, R. priscus. It is similar in build to a very robust "hypsilophodont" (non-iguanodont ornithopod), though all modern phylogenetic analyses find this to be an unnatural grouping, and Rhabdodon to be a basal member of Iguanodontia. It was large amongst its relatives, measuring 4 m (13 ft) long and weighing 250 kg (550 lb), with some specimens possibly reaching up to 6 m (20 ft) long.

species.etymology: From Latin 'priscus' meaning 'ancient' or 'former', indicating the primitive or early nature of the taxon.

references.journal: Mémoires de l'Académie des Sciences, Belles-Lettres, et Arts de Marseille

Rhinorex.etymology: From Greek rhinos ('nose') and Latin rex ('king')
Rhinorex.description: Rhinorex is a genus of kritosaurin hadrosaur from the Late Cretaceous Neslen Formation, in central Utah. Its exact placement in time is uncertain, though it probably dates to 75 million years ago and was discovered in estuarine sediments.

species.name: Rhinorex condrupus
species.etymology: From Latin condo ('bury') and rupes ('cliffs'), referring to discovery in the Book Cliffs of Utah

holotype.institution: Earth Sciences Museum, Brigham Young University

references.title: A new saurolophine hadrosaurid (Dinosauria: Ornithopoda) from the Campanian of Utah, North America

Rhoetosaurus.etymology: Named for Rhoetus, a giant (Titan) in Greek mythology, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Rhoetus lizard.'
Rhoetosaurus.description: Rhoetosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) Walloon Coal Measures of what is now eastern Australia. Rhoetosaurus is estimated to have been about 15 metres (49 ft) long, weighing about 9 tonnes (8.9 long tons; 9.9 short tons). Subsequent authors have sometimes misspelled the name: Rhaetosaurus (de Lapparent & Laverat, 1955); Rheteosaurus (Yadagiri, Prasad & Satsangi, 1979).

species.name: Rhoetosaurus brownei
species.etymology: Named for Arthur Browne, the station manager at Durham Downs who forwarded the first fossil fragments to palaeontologist Heber Longman and thereby enabled the discovery.

references.title: A giant dinosaur from Durham Downs, Queensland

Rhomaleopakhus.etymology: From Greek rhomaleos (strong) and pachys (forearm, thick); meaning "strong forearm".
Rhomaleopakhus.description: Rhomaleopakhus is a genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Kalaza Formation of China. The type and only species is Rhomaleopakhus turpanensis.

species.name: Rhomaleopakhus turpanensis
species.etymology: Named for the Turpan Basin of Xinjiang, China, where the specimen was collected.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.title: Re-assessment of the Late Jurassic eusauropod dinosaur Hudiesaurus sinojapanorum Dong, 1997, from the Turpan Basin, China, and the evolution of hyper-robust antebrachia in sauropods

Riabininohadros.etymology: Named for Russian paleontologist Anatoly Nikolaevich Riabinin, who first described the type material, combined with 'hadros' as in Hadrosauridae; meaning 'Riabinin's hadrosaur.'
Riabininohadros.description: Riabininohadros is an extinct genus of ankylopollexian dinosaur from the Maastrichtian of Crimea. Its type species is Riabininohadros weberi, emended to Riabininohadros weberae. It was originally classified as a species of Orthomerus, until 2015.

species.name: Riabininohadros weberae
species.etymology: Named for Gertruda Weber, who discovered the holotype hindlimb elements near Bakhchysarai, Crimea, in 1934; the feminine ending '-ae' reflects that Weber was a woman.

holotype.institution: Chernyshev Central Museum of Geological Exploration

references.authors: Ulansky, R. E.
references.title: Riabininohadros, novyy rod dlya gadrozavra iz maastrikhta Kryma Rossiya []

Richardoestesia.etymology: Named in honour of palaeontologist Richard Estes, with the Latinised possessive form 'Richardoestesia' combining his first name Richard with his surname Estes.
Richardoestesia.description: Richardoestesia is a morphogenus of theropod dinosaur teeth, originally described from the Late Cretaceous of what is now Canada, the United States, and possibly also Uzbekistan. It currently contains two species, R. gilmorei and R. isosceles, and a possible third, R. asiatica, although it has been classified in its own genus Asiamericana. It has been used as a morphotaxon to describe other theropod teeth widely displaced in time and space from the type species. If all teeth assigned to the genus are truly reflective of the animals biology and taxonomic state (as some teeth go as far back as the Late Jurassic), it would have been one of the longest lasting dinosaur genera, perhaps also being the most widely distributed.

species.name: Richardoestesia gilmorei
species.etymology: Named for Charles Whitney Gilmore, the paleontologist who originally described the jaws as part of Chirostenotes pergracilis.

location.locality: 2.5 miles south of mouth, Sand Creek (200 ft level)

references.authors: Currie, Philip J.; Rigby, J. Keith; Sloan, Robert E.
references.title: Theropod teeth from the Judith River Formation of southern Alberta, Canada

Rinchenia.etymology: Named after Mongolian palaeontologist Byambyn Rinchen, with the Latinised suffix '-ia' forming the genus name.
Rinchenia.description: Rinchenia is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous epoch in what is now Mongolia, Nemegt Formation. The type and only known species, Rinchenia mongoliensis, was originally classified as a species within the genus Oviraptor (named Oviraptor mongoliensis), but a subsequent reexamination found differences significant enough to warrant a separate genus. The name Rinchenia was coined for this new genus, though not formally described in detail.

species.name: Rinchenia mongoliensis
species.etymology: Named for Mongolia, the country where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Barsbold, R.
references.title: Oviraptorosauria

Rinconsaurus.etymology: Named for Rincón de los Sauces, the locality in Neuquén Province, Argentina where it was discovered, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Rinconsaurus.description: Rinconsaurus is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous in what is now Argentina. The type species, Rinconsaurus caudamirus, was described by Calvo and Riga in 2003, and is based on three partial skeletons.

species.name: Rinconsaurus caudamirus
species.etymology: From Latin 'cauda' meaning 'tail' and 'mirus' meaning 'amazing' or 'wonderful', referring to the unusual shape of the tail vertebrae.

holotype.institution: Museo Argentino Urquiza, Rincón de los Sauces
holotype.material: Holotype material distributed across MRS-Pv 26 and MRS-Pv 13

references.authors: Calvo, Jorge O.; González Riga, Bernardo J.
references.title: Rinconsaurus caudamirus gen. et sp. nov., a new titanosaurid (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia, Argentina
references.publisher: SciELO Agencia Nacional de Investigacion y Desarrollo (ANID)

Riojasaurus.etymology: Named after La Rioja Province in Argentina where it was found, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "lizard from La Rioja".
Riojasaurus.description: Riojasaurus was a herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur named after La Rioja Province in Argentina where it was found in the Los Colorados Formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin by José Bonaparte. It lived during the Late Triassic (Norian stage) and grew to about 6.6 metres (22 ft) long. Riojasaurus is the only known riojasaurid to live in South America.

synonyms.name: Strenusaurus
synonyms.reason: Now interpreted as a juvenile specimen of Riojasaurus.

species.name: Riojasaurus incertus
species.etymology: From Latin 'incertus' meaning 'uncertain' or 'doubtful'.

holotype.institution: Colección de Paleontologia de Vertebrados de la Fundación Instituto Miguel Lillo

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.
references.title: Dos nuevas "faunas" de reptiles triasicos de Argentina [Two new reptilian "faunas" of the Argentine Triassic]

Riojavenatrix.etymology: Named for La Rioja Province, Spain, where the fossils were found, combined with Latin 'venatrix' meaning 'huntress'; meaning 'La Rioja huntress.'
Riojavenatrix.description: Riojavenatrix is a genus of spinosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous Enciso Group of La Rioja, Spain. The type species is Riojavenatrix lacustris.

species.name: Riojavenatrix lacustris
species.etymology: From Latin 'lacustris' meaning 'of the lake' or 'from the lake', referring to the lacustrine depositional environment of the Enciso Group where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Centro de Interpretación Paleontológica de La Rioja
holotype.material: Partial skeleton of a single individual cataloged as CPI 1637-1648, 1675-1677

references.journal: Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society

Riparovenator.etymology: From Latin riparius (of the riverbank) and venator (hunter); meaning "riverbank hunter".
Riparovenator.description: Riparovenator is a genus of baryonychine spinosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) period of Britain. The genus contains a single species, Riparovenator milnerae.

species.name: Riparovenator milnerae
species.etymology: Named for Angela Milner, a British palaeontologist who died in August 2021, shortly before the species was formally described.

holotype.institution: Isle of Wight County Museum Service at Dinosaur Isle
holotype.material: Partial skull

references.authors: Barker, Chris T.; Hone, David W. E.; Naish, Darren; Cau, Andrea; Lockwood, Jeremy A. F.; Foster, Brian; Clarkin, Claire E.; Schneider, Philipp; Gostling, Neil J.
references.title: New spinosaurids from the Wessex Formation (Early Cretaceous, UK) and the European origins of Spinosauridae
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Rocasaurus.etymology: Named for General Roca, a city in Río Negro Province, Argentina, near where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'General Roca lizard.'
Rocasaurus.description: Rocasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod that lived in South America. Rocasaurus was discovered in Argentina in 2000, within the Allen Formation which is dated to be middle Campanian to early Maastrichtian in age (75 to 70 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous). This genus grew up to 8 metres (26 ft) long, making it one of the smaller sauropods. It seems to be closely related to saltasaurid dinosaurs, like Saltasaurus and Neuquensaurus. The type species, Rocasaurus muniozi, was formally described by Leonardo Salgado and Azpilicueta in 2000.

species.name: Rocasaurus muniozi
species.etymology: Named for Juan Carlos Muñoz, director of paleontology at the Carlos Ameghino Provincial Museum, in recognition of his support of paleontological research in the region.

references.authors: Salgado, L.; Azpilicueta, C.
references.title: Un nuevo saltasaurino (Sauropoda, Titanosauridae) de la provincia de Río Negro (Formación Allen, Cretácico Superior), Patagonia, Argentina [A new saltasaurine (Sauropoda, Titanosauridae) from Río Negro province (Allen Formation, Upper Cretaceous), Patagonia, Argentina

Ruehleia.etymology: Named for German paleontologist Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern, who collected paleontological material from the region.
Ruehleia.description: Ruehleia is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic period of Germany. The type species is R. bedheimensis, described by Galton in 2001, and is named for the German paleontologist Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern. Discovered in 1952, the holotype consists of one nearly complete skeleton, including cervical (neck), dorsal (back), and caudal (tail) vertebrae; a partial sacrum; a scapulocoracoid; pelvic bones; most limb bones; and a partially complete manus (hands). The fossils were found in the Trossingen Formation of central Germany and date to the Norian stage, around 216 to 208 million years ago.

species.name: Ruehleia bedheimensis
species.etymology: Named after the German town of Bedheim, from where von Lilienstern hailed and near where he worked.

references.authors: Galton, P. M.
references.title: The prosauropod dinosaur Plateosaurus Meyer, 1837 (Saurischia: Sauropodomorpha; Upper Triassic). II. Notes on the referred species

Rugocaudia.etymology: From Latin 'rugosus' (wrinkled, rough) + 'cauda' (tail), meaning 'wrinkled tail' or 'rough-tailed', referring to the texture of the caudal vertebrae.
Rugocaudia.description: Rugocaudia is a potentially dubious genus of early titanosauriform sauropod dinosaurs known from the Early Cretaceous of Montana, United States.

species.name: Rugocaudia cooneyi
species.etymology: Named for J. P. Cooney, the owner of the land in Montana on which the holotype specimen was found.

references.authors: Woodruff, D. Cary
references.title: A new titanosauriform from the Early Cretaceous Cloverly Formation of Montana

Rugops.etymology: From Latin 'ruga' (wrinkle) + Greek 'ops' (face, eye), meaning 'wrinkle face', referring to the pitted and rough surface of the skull.
Rugops.description: Rugops is a monospecific genus of basal abelisaurid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period (Cenomanian stage, approximately 95 million years ago) in what is now the Echkar Formation in Niger. The type and only species, Rugops primus, is known only from a partial skull. It was named and described in 2004 by Paul Sereno, Jeffery Wilson and Jack Conrad. Rugops has an estimated length of 4.4–5.3 metres (14–17 ft) and weight of 410 kilograms (900 lb). The top of its skull bears several pits which correlates with overlaying scale and the front of the snout would have had an armour-like dermis.

species.name: Rugops primus
species.etymology: From Latin 'primus' meaning 'first', referring to Rugops being one of the earliest abelisaurids known with a heavily textured skull.

references.authors: Sereno, Paul C.; Wilson, Jeffrey A.; Conrad, Jack L.
references.title: New dinosaurs link southern landmasses in the Mid–Cretaceous
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series B: Biological Sciences

Ruixinia.etymology: Named in honour of Ruixin Zhang, who made significant contributions to the infrastructure and collection of the Erlianhaote Dinosaur Museum.
Ruixinia.description: Ruixinia is an extinct genus of somphospondylan sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Yixian Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, Ruixinia zhangi, known from a partial articulated skeleton. This specimen preserves the most complete series of caudal vertebrae known from any Asian titanosauriform.

species.name: Ruixinia zhangi
species.etymology: Named for Ruixin Zhang, a contributor to the Erlianhaote Dinosaur Museum, with the Latin genitive '-i' suffix indicating an honorific.

references.authors: Mo, Jinyou; Ma, Feimin; Yu, Yilun; Xu, Xing
references.title: A new titanosauriform sauropod with an unusual tail from the Lower Cretaceous of northeastern China

Rukwatitan.etymology: Named for the Rukwa Rift Basin in Tanzania where it was found, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'.
Rukwatitan.description: Rukwatitan is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur from the Galula Formation in Tanzania. It lived around 100 million years ago, during the middle Cretaceous. The species, which shared features with another southern African species, Malawisaurus dixeyi, measured 30 feet (9.1 m) from the head to the tip of the tail, and had forelimbs that were estimated around 6.5 feet (2.0 m) long. Its fossils were found embedded in a cliff face near Lake Rukwa in the Rukwa Valley, from which it gets its name.

species.name: Rukwatitan bisepultus
species.etymology: From Latin 'bisepultus' meaning 'twice buried', in reference to the holotype being initially entombed in overbank-derived mudstone, with a portion later mobilized by a paleochannel and reburied nearby in channel sandstone.

references.authors: Gorscak, Eric; O'Connor, Patrick M.; Stevens, Nancy J.; Roberts, Eric M.
references.title: The basal titanosaurian Rukwatitan bisepultus (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the middle Cretaceous Galula Formation, Rukwa Rift Basin, southwestern Tanzania

Ruyangosaurus.etymology: Named for Ruyang County in Henan Province, China where it was discovered, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Ruyangosaurus.description: Ruyangosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur recovered from the Early Cretaceous Haoling Formation of China. The type species is R. giganteus, described in 2009 by Lü Junchang et al.

species.name: Ruyangosaurus giganteus
species.etymology: From Latin 'giganteus' meaning 'gigantic', referring to the enormous size of this titanosauriform sauropod.

references.authors: Lü, J.-c.; Xu, L.; S.-h. Jia, X.-l. Zhang, J.-m. Zhang, L.-l. Yang, H.-l. You, Q. Ji
references.title: A new gigantic sauropod dinosaur from the Cretaceous of Ruyang, Henan, China

Saichania.description: Saichania is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of Mongolia and China. The first fossils of Saichania were found in the early 1970s in the Baruungoyot Formation. In 1977, the type species Saichania chulsanensis was named.

synonyms.name: Shanxia
synonyms.reason: Possible junior subjective synonym of Saichania; identification is tentative. Per Olshevsky's Dinosaur Genera List.

species.name: Saichania chulsanensis
species.etymology: Named for Chulsan (also spelled Khulsan), the locality in Mongolia near which the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Maryanska, T.
references.title: Ankylosauridae (Dinosauria) from Mongolia

Saltasaurus.etymology: Named after Salta Province in northwestern Argentina, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'lizard from Salta'.
Saltasaurus.description: Saltasaurus is a genus of saltasaurid dinosaur of the Late Cretaceous period of Argentina. Small among sauropods, though still heavy by the standards of modern creatures, Saltasaurus was characterized by a short neck and stubby limbs. It was the first genus of sauropod known to possess armour of bony plates embedded in its skin. Such small bony plates, called osteoderms, have since been found on other titanosaurians.

synonyms.name: Microcoelus
synonyms.reason: Possible junior subjective synonym of Saltasaurus; identification is tentative. Per Olshevsky's Dinosaur Genera List.

species.name: Saltasaurus loricatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'loricatus' meaning 'protected by armour' or 'clad in mail', referring to the bony osteoderms embedded in the skin of this titanosaur.

holotype.institution: Colección de Paleontologia de Vertebrados de la Fundación Instituto Miguel Lillo

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.; Powell, J. E.
references.title: A continental assemblage of tetrapods from the Upper Cretaceous beds of El Brete, northwestern Argentina (Sauropoda-Coelurosauria-Carnosauria-Aves)
references.journal: Mémoires de la Société Géologique de France, Nouvelle Série

Saltriovenator.etymology: Named for Saltrio, the town in northern Italy where the fossils were found in a marble quarry, combined with Latin 'venator' meaning 'hunter'; meaning 'Saltrio hunter.'
Saltriovenator.description: Saltriovenator is a genus of ceratosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic in what is now Italy. The type and only species is Saltriovenator zanellai; in the past, the species had been known under the informal name "saltriosaur". Although a full skeleton has not yet been discovered, Saltriovenator is thought to have been a large, bipedal carnivore similar to Ceratosaurus.

synonyms.name: Saltriosaurus
synonyms.reason: Latinised form of Dal Sasso's provisional Italian name 'Saltriosauro'; remains an invalid nomen nudum, with the specimen formally described as Saltriovenator.

species.name: Saltriovenator zanellai
species.etymology: Named for Angelo Zanella, the amateur paleontologist who discovered the holotype in the Salnova marble quarry in Saltrio in 1996.

holotype.institution: Museo di Storia Naturale di Milano
holotype.material: Partial skeleton

references.authors: Dal Sasso, Cristiano; Maganuco, Simone; Cau, Andrea
references.title: The oldest ceratosaurian (Dinosauria: Theropoda), from the Lower Jurassic of Italy, sheds light on the evolution of the three-fingered hand of birds

Sanjuansaurus.etymology: Named after San Juan Province in Argentina where it was found, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "San Juan Province lizard".
Sanjuansaurus.description: Sanjuansaurus is a genus of herrerasaurid dinosaur from the Late Triassic (Carnian) Ischigualasto Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina.

species.name: Sanjuansaurus gordilloi
species.etymology: Named for Raul Gordillo, the head fossil preparator and artist of the San Juan Museum.

location.locality: Herrera de la base, La Gallinita

holotype.institution: División de Paleontología de Vertebrados del Museo de Ciencias Naturales y Universidad Nacional de San Juan

references.authors: Alcober, O. A.; Martínez, R. N.
references.title: A new herrerasaurid (Dinosauria, Saurischia) from the Upper Triassic Ischigualasto Formation of northwestern Argentina

Sanpasaurus.etymology: Named for Sanpa (Shanba), the locality in Sichuan, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Sanpa lizard.'
Sanpasaurus.description: Sanpasaurus is a poorly known sauropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of Sichuan, China. The type species, S. yaoi, was described by Chung Chien Young, in 1944. The type remains, IVPP V.156, consists of 20 vertebrae, scapulae, forelimbs, and some hindlimb bones.

species.name: Sanpasaurus yaoi
species.etymology: Named in honor of Mr. Y. Yao, who collected the fossils.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: Young, C. C.
references.title: On the Reptilian Remains from Weiyuan, Szechuan, China
references.journal: Bulletin of the Geological Society of China

Santanaraptor.etymology: Named after the Santana Formation of Brazil where the fossil was found, combined with Latin raptor (thief); meaning "Santana Formation thief".
Santanaraptor.description: Santanaraptor is a genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Early Cretaceous (late Aptian-early Albian), about 112 million years ago.

species.name: Santanaraptor placidus
species.etymology: Named for Placido Cidade Nuvens, who founded the Museu de Paleontologia da Universidade Regional do Cariri in Brazil.

references.authors: Kellner, A. W. A.
references.title: Short note on a new dinosaur (Theropoda, Coelurosauria) from the Santana Formation (Romualdo Member, Albian), northeastern Brazil
references.journal: Boletim do Museu Nacional, Nova Série

Sanxiasaurus.etymology: Named for Sanxia (Three Gorges) of the Yangtze River in China, near the type locality, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Sanxia lizard.'
Sanxiasaurus.description: Sanxiasaurus is a genus of neornithischian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Xintiangou Formation in the Chongqing Municipality of China. The type and only species is S. modaoxiensis. The holotype is a partial postcranial skeleton consisting of 55 bones including two cervical vertebrae, 11 dorsal vertebrae, 4 sacral vertebrae, 18 caudal vertebrae, both humeri, radii, and ulnas, partial right ilium, partial right ischium, both femora and tibiae, left fibula, 3 metatarsi and 4 phalanges. In a phylogenetic analysis, it was found to be a basal neornithischian, more derived than Lesothosaurus and less derived than Hexinlusaurus.

species.name: Sanxiasaurus modaoxiensis
species.etymology: Named for the Modaoxi, a tributary of the Yangtze River near the discovery locality in Yunyang County, Chongqing.

holotype.institution: Chongqing Municipal Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources
holotype.material: Partial skeleton

references.authors: Li, Ning; Dai, Hui; Tan, Chao; Hu, Xufeng; Wei, Zhaoying; Lin, Yu; Wei, Guangbiao; Li, Deliang; Meng, Li; Hao, Baoqiao; You, Hailu; Peng, Guangzhao
references.title: A neornithischian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Xintiangou Formation of Yunyang, Chongqing, China: the earliest record in Asia

Sarahsaurus.etymology: Named in honor of Sarah (Mrs. Ernest) Butler, an Austin philanthropist who helped fund the 'Dino Pit' exhibit at the Austin Nature and Science Center, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Sarahsaurus.description: Sarahsaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur which lived during the Early Jurassic period in what is now northeastern Arizona, United States.

species.name: Sarahsaurus aurifontanalis
species.etymology: From Latin 'aurum' meaning 'gold' and 'fontanalis' meaning 'of the spring', referring to Gold Spring, Arizona, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Texas Memorial Museum, Austin, Texas, USA (used for collections now housed in the Vertebrate Paleontology Collections at the Jackson School Museum of Earth History, Austin, Texas, USA), now called the Texas Science and Natural History Museum

references.authors: Rowe, Timothy B.; Sues, Hans-Dieter; Reisz, Robert R.
references.title: Dispersal and diversity in the earliest North American sauropodomorph dinosaurs, with a description of a new taxon
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

Sarcolestes.etymology: From Ancient Greek sarx (flesh) and lestes (robber); meaning "flesh robber".
Sarcolestes.description: Sarcolestes is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian ornithischian dinosaur from the Oxford Clay of England. The current type and only species is S. leedsi, and the holotype is a single partial left mandible. The genus and species were named in 1893 by Richard Lydekker, who thought they belonged to a theropod.

species.name: Sarcolestes leedsi
species.etymology: Named for Alfred Nicholson Leeds, the collector who discovered the holotype specimen in the Oxford Clay of England.

references.authors: Lydekker, R.
references.title: On the Jaw of a New Carnivorous Dinosaur from the Oxford Clay of Peterborough
references.journal: Quarterly Journal of the Geological Society of London

Sarcosaurus.description: Sarcosaurus is a genus of basal neotheropod dinosaur, roughly 3.5 metres (11 ft) long. It lived in what is now England and maybe Ireland and Scotland during the Hettangian-Sinemurian stages of the Early Jurassic, about 199-196 million years ago. Sarcosaurus is one of the earliest known Jurassic theropods, and one of only a handful of theropod genera from this time period. Along with Dracoraptor hanigani it is one of the two described neotheropods from the lowermost Jurassic of the United Kingdom.

synonyms.name: Liassaurus
synonyms.reason: Informal name given to a specimen thought to be Sarcosaurus woodi in 1995; nomen nudum due to lack of overlapping material with the Sarcosaurus woodi holotype.

species.name: Sarcosaurus woodi
species.etymology: Named for S. L. Wood, who found the partial skeleton near Barrow-on-Soar in the Scunthorpe Mudstone of England.

references.authors: Andrews, Charles W.
references.title: LVI.—On some ramins of a Theropodous dinosaur from the Lower Lias of Barrow-on-Soa
references.journal: Annals and Magazine of Natural History

Sarmientosaurus.etymology: Named after the town of Sarmiento in Chubut Province, Argentina, near where the fossils were discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard).
Sarmientosaurus.description: Sarmientosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur belonging to the Titanosauria. It lived in what is now South America, specifically Argentina, during the Upper Cretaceous Period about 95 million years ago. The type species is Sarmientosaurus musacchioi.

species.name: Sarmientosaurus musacchioi
species.etymology: Named for Eduardo Musacchio, an educator at the Universidad Nacional de la Patagonia San Juan Bosco, in recognition of his contributions to Patagonian paleontology.

references.authors: Martínez, Rubén D. F.; Lamanna, Matthew C.; Novas, Fernando E.; Ridgely, Ryan C.; Casal, Gabriel A.; Martínez, Javier E.; Vita, Javier R.; Witmer, Lawrence M.
references.title: A Basal Lithostrotian Titanosaur (Dinosauria: Sauropoda) with a Complete Skull: Implications for the Evolution and Paleobiology of Titanosauria

Sasayamagnomus.etymology: Named for the Sasayama Basin in Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan, where the fossils were found, combined with Latin 'gnomus' meaning 'gnome'; meaning 'gnome from Sasayama.'
Sasayamagnomus.description: Sasayamagnomus is an extinct genus of neoceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian age) Ohyamashimo Formation of Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan. The genus contains a single species, Sasayamagnomus saegusai. The holotype individual is estimated to reach 80 centimetres (2.6 ft) long, although this specimen is not fully grown.

species.name: Sasayamagnomus saegusai
species.etymology: Named for Haruo Saegusa, a palaeontologist who led dinosaur excavations in the Tamba area and made significant contributions to vertebrate paleontology in Hyogo Prefecture, Japan.

holotype.institution: Museum of Nature and Human Activities

references.authors: Tanaka, Tomonori; Chiba, Kentaro; Ikeda, Tadahiro; Ryan, Michael J.
references.title: A new neoceratopsian (Ornithischia, Ceratopsia) from the Lower Cretaceous Ohyamashimo Formation (Albian), southwestern Japan

Saturnalia.etymology: Named after the ancient Roman festival of Saturn (Saturnalia), held in December, in reference to the festive time of year during which the fossils were collected.
Saturnalia.description: Saturnalia is an extinct genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur known from the Late Triassic Santa Maria Formation of Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil. It contains one species, Saturnalia tupiniquim. It is one of the earliest known dinosaurs.

species.name: Saturnalia tupiniquim
species.etymology: The species name 'tupiniquim' is a word of Guarani origin colloquially used in Portuguese to refer to things of Brazilian origin.

holotype.institution: Museu de Ciências e Tecnologia da Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul

references.authors: Langer, Max C.; Abdala, Fernando; Richter, Martha; Benton, Michael J.
references.title: A sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Upper Triassic (Carman) of southern Brazil
references.journal: Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences - Series IIA - Earth and Planetary Science

Saurolophus.etymology: From Greek sauros (lizard) and lophos (crest); meaning "lizard crest".
Saurolophus.description: Saurolophus is a genus of large hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of North America and Asia, in what is now the Horseshoe Canyon and Nemegt formations respectively (about 70 to 66 million years ago). It is one of the few dinosaur genera known from multiple continents. The type species, S. osborni, was described by Barnum Brown in 1912 from Canadian fossils. A second valid species, S. angustirostris, is represented by numerous specimens from Mongolia, and was described by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky. Saurolophus is distinguished by a spike-like crest which projects up and back from the skull. It was a herbivorous dinosaur which could move either bipedally or quadrupedally.

species.name: Saurolophus osborni
species.etymology: Named in honor of Henry Fairfield Osborn, American paleontologist and president of the American Museum of Natural History, who was a mentor to Barnum Brown.

references.authors: Brown, B.
references.title: A crested dinosaur from the Edmonton Cretaceous
references.journal: Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History

Sauropelta.etymology: From Greek 'sauros' (lizard) + 'pelte' (small shield), meaning 'lizard shield', referring to the bony armour covering the body.
Sauropelta.description: Sauropelta is a genus of nodosaurid dinosaur that existed in the Early Cretaceous Period of North America. One species (S. edwardsorum) has been named. Anatomically, Sauropelta is one of the most well-understood nodosaurids, with fossilized remains recovered in the U.S. states of Wyoming, Montana, and possibly Utah. It is also the earliest known genus of nodosaurine; most of its remains are found in a section of the Cloverly Formation dated to 108.5 million years ago.

synonyms.name: Peltosaurus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Peltosaurus (Squamata).

species.name: Sauropelta edwardsorum
species.etymology: Named in honor of the Edwards family; originally published as 'edwardsi' by Ostrom in 1970, corrected to 'edwardsorum' by Olshevsky in 1991 to adhere to Latin grammatical conventions for naming a species after multiple people.

references.authors: Ostrom, J. H.
references.title: Stratigraphy and paleontology of the Cloverly Formation (Lower Cretaceous) of the Bighorn Basin area, Wyoming and Montana

Saurophaganax.etymology: From Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', 'phagein' meaning 'to eat', and 'anax' meaning 'ruler' or 'lord'; meaning 'lord of lizard-eaters.'
Saurophaganax.description: Saurophaganax is a dubious, chimeric genus of large saurischian dinosaur, possibly a sauropod, from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Morrison Formation of Oklahoma, United States. This taxon was historically considered to represent a species of Allosaurus or very large allosaurid. However, re-examinations of the attributed specimens suggested that it is a chimera of multiple dinosaur genera, since some specimens most likely belong to a diplodocid sauropod, while the other referred specimens could be reassigned to a novel species of Allosaurus.

synonyms.name: Saurophagus
synonyms.reason: Name preoccupied by Saurophagus (Aves).

species.name: Saurophaganax maximus
species.etymology: From Latin 'maximus' meaning 'the largest' or 'greatest', reflecting the exceptional size of this large allosaurid theropod.

references.authors: Chure, D. J.
references.title: A reassessment of the gigantic theropod Saurophagus maximus from the Morrison Formation (Upper Jurassic) of Oklahoma, USA

Sauroplites.etymology: From Greek sauros (lizard) and hoplites (armed foot soldier, hoplite); meaning "saurian hoplite".
Sauroplites.description: Sauroplites is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China.

species.name: Sauroplites scutiger
species.etymology: From Neo-Latin 'scutiger' meaning 'shield bearer', combining Latin 'scutum' ('shield') and 'gerere' ('to bear'), referring to the heavily armoured body of this ankylosaur.

holotype.material: Uncatalogued; specimens last recorded at the AMNH

Sauroposeidon.etymology: From Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard' and Poseidon (Ποσειδών), the Greek god of the sea also associated with earthquakes; meaning 'lizard earthquake god', referencing the notion that the animal's immense weight shook the ground.
Sauroposeidon.description: Sauroposeidon is a genus of sauropod dinosaur known from several incomplete specimens including a bone bed and fossilized trackways that have been found in the U.S. states of Oklahoma, Wyoming, and Texas.

synonyms.name: Paluxysaurus
synonyms.reason: D'Emic and Foreman (2021) re-analysed the material and treated Paluxysaurus as a junior synonym of Sauroposeidon.

species.name: Sauroposeidon proteles
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'proteles' meaning 'perfect before the end', referring to Sauroposeidon's status as the last and most specialized giant sauropod known in North America during the Early Cretaceous.

references.authors: Wedel, Mathew J.; Cifelli, Richard L.; Sanders, R. Kent
references.title: Sauroposeidon proteles, a new sauropod from the early Cretaceous of Oklahoma

Saurornithoides.etymology: From Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', 'ornis' (stem 'ornith') meaning 'bird', and 'eidos' meaning 'form' or 'resemblance', referring to its bird-like skull.
Saurornithoides.description: Saurornithoides is a genus of troodontid maniraptoran dinosaur, which lived during the Late Cretaceous period. These creatures were predators, which could run fast on their hind legs and had excellent sight and hearing. The name is derived from the Greek stems saur~ (lizard), ornith~ (bird) and eides (form), referring to its bird-like skull.

synonyms.name: Ornithoides
synonyms.reason: Osborn mentioned this name in a 1924 popular publication without a description, leaving it an invalid nomen nudum; the formal description used Saurornithoides.

species.name: Saurornithoides mongoliensis
species.etymology: Named for Mongolia, where the holotype was discovered in the Djadochta Formation.

references.authors: Osborn, H. F.
references.title: Three new Theropoda, Protoceratops zone, central Mongolia

Saurornitholestes.etymology: From Greek sauros (lizard), ornithos (bird), and lestes (thief); meaning "lizard-bird thief".
Saurornitholestes.description: Saurornitholestes is a genus of carnivorous dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur from the late Cretaceous of Canada (Alberta and Saskatchewan) and the United States (Montana, New Mexico, Alabama, and South Carolina). Two species have been named that are regarded as valid: Saurornitholestes langstoni in 1978 and Saurornitholestes sullivani in 2015. Saurornitholestes was a small, bipedal, meat-eating dinosaur, equipped with a sickle-like claw on each foot.

species.name: Saurornitholestes langstoni
species.etymology: Named for Wann Langston, Jr., a prominent Canadian paleontologist.

references.authors: SUES, HANS-DIETER
references.title: A new small theropod dinosaur from the Judith River Formation (Campanian) of Alberta Canada
references.journal: Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society

Savannasaurus.etymology: From English 'savanna', referring to the open grassland/savanna landscape of Queensland, Australia where its fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Savannasaurus.description: Savannasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation of Queensland, Australia. It contains one species, Savannasaurus elliottorum, named in 2016 by Stephen Poropat and colleagues. The holotype and only known specimen, originally nicknamed "Wade", is the most complete specimen of an Australian sauropod, and is held at the Australian Age of Dinosaurs museum. Dinosaurs known from contemporary rocks include its close relative Diamantinasaurus and the theropod Australovenator; associated teeth suggest that Australovenator may have fed on the holotype specimen.

species.name: Savannasaurus elliottorum
species.etymology: Named for the Elliott family — David Elliott (who discovered the holotype) and his family — in recognition of their contributions to Australian palaeontology, with the Latin genitive plural '-orum' suffix.

references.authors: Poropat, Stephen F.; Mannion, Philip D.; Upchurch, Paul; Hocknull, Scott A.; Kear, Benjamin P.; Kundrát, Martin; Tischler, Travis R.; Sloan, Trish; Sinapius, George H. K.; Elliott, Judy A.; Elliott, David A.
references.title: New Australian sauropods shed light on Cretaceous dinosaur palaeobiogeography

Scansoriopteryx.etymology: From Latin 'scansorius' meaning 'climbing' and Greek 'pteryx' meaning 'wing'; meaning 'climbing wing', in reference to its arboreal adaptations.
Scansoriopteryx.description: Scansoriopteryx is a genus of maniraptoran dinosaur. Described from only a single juvenile fossil specimen found in Liaoning, China, Scansoriopteryx is a sparrow-sized animal that shows adaptations in the foot indicating an arboreal (tree-dwelling) lifestyle. It possessed an unusual, elongated third finger which may have supported a membranous wing, much like the related Yi qi. The type specimen of Scansoriopteryx also contains the fossilized impression of feathers.

synonyms.name: Epidendrosaurus
synonyms.reason: Controversial synonym; both genera described from very similar juvenile specimens. Scansoriopteryx appeared in print first and is treated as senior pending ICZN ruling.

species.name: Scansoriopteryx heilmanni
species.etymology: Named in honor of Gerhard Heilmann, a pioneer of avian paleontological studies who championed the concept of birds deriving from an arboreal ancestry.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

Scelidosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'skelis'/'skelidos' (rib of beef, hind leg) + 'sauros' (lizard), intended to mean 'limb lizard'; the name references the animal's robust limbs.
Scelidosaurus.description: Scelidosaurus is a genus of herbivorous armoured ornithischian dinosaur from the Jurassic of England.

species.name: Scelidosaurus harrisonii
species.etymology: Named for James Harrison, the quarry owner of Charmouth, Dorset, who discovered and collected the first specimens and donated them to Professor Richard Owen.

Schleitheimia.etymology: Named after Schleitheim, the Swiss locality (in the canton of Schaffhausen) where the type material was found, with the Latinised suffix '-ia'.
Schleitheimia.description: Schleitheimia is an extinct genus of sauropodiform sauropodomorph dinosaur, from the Gruhalde Member of Klettgau Formation of Switzerland. The type species, Schleitheimia schutzi was formally described in 2020.

species.name: Schleitheimia schutzi
species.etymology: Named for Emil Schutz, who collected the type material between 1952 and 1954 and later donated it to the University of Zürich.

references.title: A derived sauropodiform dinosaur and other sauropodomorph material from the Late Triassic of Canton Schaffhausen, Switzerland

Scipionyx.etymology: From the Roman name Scipio (after the Roman general Scipio Africanus, as the fossil was found in Italy) + Greek 'onyx' (claw), meaning 'Scipio's claw'.
Scipionyx.description: Scipionyx was a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Pietraroja Formation of Italy, around 113 million years ago.

species.name: Scipionyx samniticus
species.etymology: From Latin 'samniticus' meaning 'of the Samnites' or 'Samnian', referring to Samnium, the ancient region of south-central Italy where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Soprintendenza per i Beni Archeologici di Salerno, Avellino, Benevento e Caserta

references.authors: Dal Sasso, C.; Signore, M.
references.title: Exceptional soft-tissue preservation in a theropod dinosaur from Italy

Sciurumimus.etymology: Named for its squirrel-like tail; from Latin Sciurus (the tree squirrel genus) and Greek mimos, meaning "mimic" — the name means "squirrel mimic"
Sciurumimus.description: Sciurumimus is an extinct genus of tetanuran theropod from the Late Jurassic Torleite Formation of Germany. It is known from a single juvenile specimen representing the type species, Sciurumimus albersdoerferi, which was found in a limestone quarry close to Painten in Lower Bavaria. The specimen was preserved with traces of feather-like filaments.

species.name: Sciurumimus albersdoerferi
species.etymology: Named in honor of Raimund Albersdörfer, who made the specimen available for study.

references.authors: Rauhut, Oliver W. M.; Foth, Christian; Tischlinger, Helmut; Norell, Mark A.

Scolosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'skolos' (stake, thorn, prickle) + 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'thorn lizard' or 'spiked lizard', referring to the spiky armour projections.
Scolosaurus.description: Scolosaurus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaurs within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae. It is known from the lower levels of the Dinosaur Park Formation and upper levels of the Oldman Formation in the Late Cretaceous (latest middle Campanian stage, about 76.5 Ma ago) of Alberta, Canada. The genus contains two species, S. cutleri and S. thronus. The type species, S. cutleri, measured up to 5.6 metres (18 ft) in length and 2.2 metric tons (2.4 short tons) in body mass.

species.name: Scolosaurus cutleri
species.etymology: Named for William Edmund Cutler, the independent fossil collector who discovered the holotype in 1914 and was seriously injured when the specimen fell on him during excavation.

references.authors: Nopcsa, B. F.
references.title: Palaeontological notes on reptiles. VI. Scolosaurus cutleri, a new dinosaur

Scutellosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'scutellum' (diminutive of 'scutum', shield; small shield) + Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'little shield lizard', referring to the small scutes covering its body.
Scutellosaurus.description: Scutellosaurus is a genus of basal thyreophoran dinosaur that lived approximately 196 million years ago during the early part of the Jurassic Period in what is now Arizona, USA. It is classified in Thyreophora, the armoured dinosaurs; its closest relatives may have been Emausaurus and Scelidosaurus, another armored dinosaur which was mainly a quadrupedal dinosaur, unlike bipedal Scutellosaurus. It is one of the earliest representatives of the armored dinosaurs and the basalmost form discovered to date. Scutellosaurus was a small, lightly-built, ground-dwelling herbivore, that could grow up to an estimated 1.3 metres (4.3 ft) long.

species.name: Scutellosaurus lawleri
species.etymology: Named for David Lawler, who discovered and collected the holotype fossil in Coconino County, Arizona.

references.authors: Colbert, E. H.
references.title: A primitive ornithischian dinosaur from the Kayenta Formation of Arizona

Secernosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'secerno' meaning 'to separate' or 'sever' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'severed lizard', referring to its geographic separation from other hadrosaurs in South America.
Secernosaurus.description: Secernosaurus is a genus of herbivorous hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous of what is now Argentina. This genus and its close relatives lived in South America, unlike most hadrosaurids, which lived in the Laurasian continents of Eurasia and North America. It has been suggested that the ancestors of Secernosaurus crossed into South America when a land bridge temporarily formed between North and South America during the Late Cretaceous and allowed biotic interchange between the two continents.

species.name: Secernosaurus koerneri
species.etymology: Named for Harold E. Koerner.

references.authors: BRETT-SURMAN, M. K.
references.title: Phylogeny and palaeobiogeography of hadrosaurian dinosaurs
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Sefapanosaurus.etymology: From Sesotho 'sefapano' (cross) + Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'cross lizard', referring to the distinctive cross-shaped astragalus (ankle bone).
Sefapanosaurus.description: Sefapanosaurus was an early, herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur occurring in the southern regions of Gondwana some 200 million years ago in the Late Triassic or Early Jurassic. The sauropodomorphs were the dominant terrestrial herbivores throughout much of the Mesozoic Era, from their origins in the mid-Triassic (approximately 230 Ma) until their decline and fall at the end of the Cretaceous (approximately 66 Ma). A distinctive feature of this dinosaur is the cross-shaped astragalus or talus bone in its ankle. The generic name is derived from the Sesotho word sefapano, meaning ‘cross’ and the Greek word saurus, meaning 'lizard'. The specific name refers to Zastron, the type locality, where the specimen was discovered.

species.name: Sefapanosaurus zastronensis
species.etymology: Named for Zastron, the type locality in South Africa where the specimen was discovered.

holotype.institution: Evolutionary Studies Institute (formerly Bernard Price Institute for Palaeontological Research), University of the Witwatersrand

Segisaurus.etymology: Named after Tsegi Canyon, Arizona, where the only known specimen was discovered, combined with Greek sauros, "lizard" — means "Tsegi Canyon lizard"
Segisaurus.description: Segisaurus is a genus of small coelophysid theropod dinosaur, that measured approximately 1 metre (3.3 feet) in length. The only known specimen was discovered in early Jurassic strata in Tsegi Canyon, Arizona, for which it was named. Segisaurus is the only dinosaur to have ever been excavated from the area.

species.name: Segisaurus halli
species.etymology: Named in honor of Ansel Hall, a colleague of the describer Charles Camp.

holotype.institution: University of California Museum of Paleontology

references.authors: Camp, C. L.
references.title: A new type of bipedal dinosaur from the Navajo Sandstone of Arizona
references.journal: University of California Publications in Geological Sciences

Segnosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'segnis' meaning 'slow' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'slow lizard.' The specific name galbinensis refers to the Galbin region of the Gobi Desert.
Segnosaurus.description: Segnosaurus is a genus of therizinosaurid dinosaur that lived in what is now southeastern Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous, about 102–86 million years ago. Multiple incomplete but well-preserved specimens were discovered in the Gobi Desert in the 1970s, and in 1979 the genus and species Segnosaurus galbinensis were named. The generic name Segnosaurus means "slow lizard" and the specific name galbinensis refers to the Galbin region. The known material of this dinosaur includes the lower jaw, neck and tail vertebrae, the pelvis, shoulder girdle, and limb bones. Parts of the specimens have gone missing or become damaged since they were collected. Remains from Japan originally assigned to Allosaurus were reassigned to Segnosaurus sp. (of unspecified species) in 2025.

species.name: Segnosaurus galbinensis
species.etymology: Named for the Galbin region of Mongolia, the area where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.title: Segnosauridae - novoe semeistvo teropod is posdnego mela Mongolii [Segnosauridae - a new family of theropods from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia]

Seitaad.etymology: From Navajo 'seit'aad', a sand-swallowing monster from Navajo mythology, referring to the specimen being preserved entombed in the Navajo Sandstone.
Seitaad.description: Seitaad is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur which lived during the Early Jurassic period in what is now southern Utah, United States.

species.name: Seitaad ruessi
species.etymology: Named for Everett Ruess, a young artist, poet, and naturalist who mysteriously disappeared in 1934 while exploring southern Utah near where the holotype was found.

references.authors: Sertich, Joseph J. W.; Loewen, Mark A.
references.title: A New Basal Sauropodomorph Dinosaur from the Lower Jurassic Navajo Sandstone of Southern Utah

Sektensaurus.etymology: From Tehuelche sekten, meaning "island", combined with Greek sauros, "lizard" — means "island lizard"
Sektensaurus.description: Sektensaurus is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur, possibly an elasmarian, from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of Patagonia, Argentina. Its remains were uncovered in the fluvial tuffs of the Lago Colhué Huapí Formation in the Golfo San Jorge Basin. The type and only species is S. sanjuanboscoi. Sektensaurus is the first non-hadrosauroid ornithopod of central Patagonia. The discovery of the genus increases the anatomical knowledge of ornithopods and adds new data on the compositions of dinosaur faunas that lived in Patagonia close to Antarctica at the end of the Cretaceous.

species.name: Sektensaurus sanjuanboscoi
species.etymology: Named for the Universidad Nacional de la Patagonia San Juan Bosco, where most of the paleontologists involved either studied or worked as researchers.

holotype.institution: Universidad Nacional de la Patagonia San Juan Bosco

references.authors: Ibiricu, Lucio M.; Casal, Gabriel A.; Martínez, Rubén D.; Luna, Marcelo; Canale, Juan I.; Álvarez, Bruno N.; González Riga, Bernardo
references.title: A new ornithopod dinosaur (Dinosauria: Ornithischia) from the Late Cretaceous of central Patagonia

Serendipaceratops.etymology: From 'serendipitous', referencing the unexpected nature of the find (a ceratopsian found in Australia), and Greek 'keras' meaning 'horn' and 'ops' meaning 'face'; meaning 'serendipitous horned face.'
Serendipaceratops.description: Serendipaceratops is a genus of herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur, possibly an ankylosaur, from the early Cretaceous Period of Australia. The type species, S. arthurcclarkei, was named in 2003.

species.name: Serendipaceratops arthurcclarkei
species.etymology: Named for science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke, a personal friend of the describing authors and someone who first became interested in science as a child through a fascination with dinosaurs.

Serikornis.etymology: From Greek 'serikos' (silken, of silk) + 'ornis' (bird), meaning 'silk bird', likely referring to the soft, silky appearance of the preserved feathers.
Serikornis.description: Serikornis is a genus of small, feathered anchiornithid dinosaur from the Upper Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China. It is represented by the type species Serikornis sungei. Some researchers believe it is a junior synonym of Anchiornis.

species.name: Serikornis sungei
species.etymology: Named for Ge Sun, in reference to whom the genus name translates as 'Ge Sun's silk bird'.

Shamosaurus.etymology: From Mandarin Chinese 'sha mo' (sand desert, the Chinese name for the Gobi Desert) + Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'Gobi desert lizard'.
Shamosaurus.description: Shamosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous basal ankylosaurid ankylosaur from Early Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian stage) deposits of Höövör, Mongolia.

species.name: Shamosaurus scutatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'scutatus' meaning 'protected by a shield', a reference to the extensive body armour of the animal.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

Shanag.etymology: Named after the 'shanag', the black-hatted dancers who perform in the Buddhist Cham ceremonial dance, referring to the locality in Mongolia where it was found.
Shanag.description: Shanag is a genus of paravian theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Period of Mongolia. It may be a dromaeosaurid, but some researchers are skeptical of this classification. The type species is S. ashile.

species.etymology: Named for the Ashile Formation, the former name for the geological layers in which the holotype was found, as used by Henry Fairfield Osborn.

Shantungosaurus.etymology: Named after Shandong (historically romanised as Shantung) Province in China, where fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'Shandong lizard'.
Shantungosaurus.description: Shantungosaurus is an extinct genus of very large herbivorous saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Wangshi Group of the Shandong Peninsula in China, containing a single species, Shantungosaurus giganteus. The stratigraphic interval of Shantungosaurus ranges from the top of the Xingezhuang Formation to the middle of the Hongtuya Formation, middle to late Campanian in age. Shantungosaurus is so far the largest hadrosauroid taxon in the world, with size estimates around 15–17 metres (49–56 ft) in length and 13–16 metric tons (14–18 short tons) in body mass.

synonyms.name: Huaxiaosaurus

species.name: Shantungosaurus giganteus
species.etymology: From Latin 'giganteus' meaning 'gigantic', a reference to this dinosaur being one of the largest known hadrosauroids.

synonyms.name: Zhuchengosaurus
synonyms.reason: Z. maximus is interpreted as an earlier growth stage of Shantungosaurus giganteus.
