references.title: Uberabatitan ribeiroi, a new titanosaur from the Marília Formation (Bauru Group, Upper Cretaceous), Minas Gerais, Brazil

Udanoceratops.etymology: Named for the Udan-Sayr locality in Mongolia where the holotype was found, combined with Greek 'keras' meaning 'horn' and 'ops' meaning 'face'.
Udanoceratops.description: Udanoceratops is a genus of large leptoceratopsid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of Mongolia. The holotype specimen, the partial skeleton of an adult with its bones encapsulated in calcium carbonate, was discovered in the 1980s as part of the Joint Soviet-Mongolian Paleontological Expedition, and was subsequently transported to the Paleontological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences. In 1992, it was described by palaeontologist Sergei Kurzanov. The sole species of Udanoceratops, also the type species, is Udanoceratops tschizhovi, named after a colleague of Kurzanov, D. O. Tschizhov. Additional remains have been assigned to Udanoceratops, though these may be misattributions.

species.name: Udanoceratops tschizhovi
species.etymology: Named for D. O. Tschizhov of the Paleontological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences, who was credited with the discovery of the specimen.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences
holotype.material: Collected in the 1980s

references.authors: Kurzanov, S. M.
references.title: A gigantic protoceratopsid from the Upper Cretaceous of Mongolia

Udelartitan.etymology: Combines 'UdelaR', an acronym for the Universidad de la República of Uruguay, with 'titan', a common suffix for large sauropod names referencing the pre-Olympian Titans of Greek mythology
Udelartitan.description: Udelartitan is an extinct genus of saltasauroid titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Guichón Formation of Uruguay. The genus contains a single species, U. celeste, known from fragmentary remains of at least two individuals.

species.name: Udelartitan celeste
species.etymology: From the Spanish word 'celeste' meaning 'sky blue', referencing the nickname given to some Uruguayan athletic teams.

holotype.institution: Colección de Vertebrados Fósiles, Departamento de Paleontología, Facultad de Ciencias, Universidad de la República

references.authors: Soto, Matías; Carballido, José L.; Langer, Max C.; Silva Junior, Julian C.G.; Montenegro, Felipe; Perea, Daniel
references.title: Phylogenetic relationships of a new titanosaur (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the Upper Cretaceous of Uruguay

Ultrasaurus.description: Ultrasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur discovered by Haang Mook Kim in South Korea. However, the name was first used unofficially (as a nomen nudum) in 1979 by Jim Jensen to describe a set of giant dinosaur bones he discovered in the United States. Because Kim published the name for his specimen before Jensen could do so officially, George Olshevsky renamed the specimen as Ultrasauros. Jensen's giant sauropod was later found to be a chimera, and the type remains are now assigned to Supersaurus.

holotype.institution: Department of Geology, Busan National University

references.authors: Jensen, J. A.
references.title: Three new sauropod dinosaurs from the Upper Jurassic of Colorado

Ulughbegsaurus.etymology: Named after Ulugh Beg (the 15th-century Timurid sultan and astronomer), combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Ulugh Beg's lizard'
Ulughbegsaurus.description: Ulughbegsaurus is an extinct genus of carcharodontosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Bissekty Formation (Turonian age) and Khodzhakul Formation (Cenomanian age) of Uzbekistan. The genus contains a single species, Ulughbegsaurus uzbekistanensis, known from multiple maxilla fragments.

species.name: Ulughbegsaurus uzbekistanensis
species.etymology: Named for Uzbekistan, the country where the fossils were discovered.

holotype.material: Partial maxilla with teeth

references.authors: Tanaka, Kohei; Anvarov, Otabek Ulugbek Ogli; Zelenitsky, Darla K.; Ahmedshaev, Akhmadjon Shayakubovich; Kobayashi, Yoshitsugu
references.title: A new carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaur occupies apex predator niche in the early Late Cretaceous of Uzbekistan

Unaysaurus.etymology: From 'unay', a word meaning 'black water' in the Tupi language indigenous to Brazil, referring to the black-water stream near the discovery site, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Unaysaurus.description: Unaysaurus is a genus of herbivorous unaysaurid sauropodomorph dinosaur. Discovered in southern Brazil, in the geopark of Paleorrota, in 1998, and announced in a press conference on Thursday, December 3, 2004, it is one of the oldest dinosaurs known. It is closely related to plateosaurid dinosaurs found in Germany, which indicates that it was relatively easy for species to spread across the giant landmass of the time, the supercontinent of Pangaea. The fossils of Unaysaurus are well-preserved. They consist of an almost complete skull, including a lower jaw, and partial skeleton with many of the bones still connected to each other in their natural positions. It is one of the most complete dinosaur skeletons (including complete skull) ever recovered in Brazil.

species.name: Unaysaurus tolentinoi
species.etymology: Named for Tolentino Marafiga, who discovered the fossils by the side of a road in 1998.

holotype.institution: Laboratório de Estratigrafia e Paleobiologia, Universidade Federal de Santa Maria

references.authors: LEAL, LUCIANO A.; AZEVEDO, SERGIO A.K.; KELLNER, ALEXANDER W.A.; DA ROSA, ÁTILA A.S.
references.title: A new early dinosaur (Sauropodomorpha) from the Caturrita Formation (Late Triassic), Paran Basin, Brazil

Unenlagia.etymology: From Mapuche 'unum' meaning 'bird' and 'llag' meaning 'half', meaning 'half-bird', reflecting its interpreted transitional position between birds and basal theropods.
Unenlagia.description: Unenlagia is a genus of unenlagiine theropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous period. The genus Unenlagia has been assigned two species: U. comahuensis, the type species described by Novas and Puerta in 1997, and U. paynemili, described by Calvo et al. in 2004.

species.name: Unenlagia comahuensis
species.etymology: Named for the Comahue region of Argentina, where the holotype was found.

references.authors: Novas, Fernando E.; Puertat, Pablo F.
references.title: New evidence concerning avian origins from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Unescoceratops.etymology: Named for UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization), in reference to the fossil being found in Dinosaur Provincial Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, combined with Greek 'keras' meaning 'horn' and 'ops' meaning 'face'
Unescoceratops.description: Unescoceratops is a genus of leptoceratopsid ceratopsian dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, southern Canada. It contains a single species, Unescoceratops koppelhusae.

species.name: Unescoceratops koppelhusae
species.etymology: Named for Eva Koppelhus, palynologist and wife of Philip Currie, one of the authors who described the genus.

holotype.material: Partial left dentary

references.authors: Ryan, Michael J.; Evans, David C.; Currie, Philip J.; Brown, Caleb M.; Brinkman, Don
references.title: New leptoceratopsids from the Upper Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada

Unquillosaurus.etymology: Named for the Unquillo River of Salta Province, Argentina, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Unquillosaurus.description: Unquillosaurus is a genus of large theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Los Blanquitos Formation of Salta Province, Argentina. Its precise classification is uncertain, but most researchers consider it as a maniraptoran. The genus contains a single species, U. ceibalii, known only from a single fossilized pubis (a pelvic bone).

species.name: Unquillosaurus ceibalii
species.etymology: Named for the town El Ceibal, near the site where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Colección de Paleontologia de Vertebrados de la Fundación Instituto Miguel Lillo

references.authors: Powell, J. E.
references.title: Sobre una asociacion de Dinosaurios y otras evidencias de vertebrados del Crétacico Superior de la region de La Candelaria, Prov. de Salta, Argentina

Urbacodon.etymology: Named after URBAC (an acronym honoring Uzbek, Russian, British, American, and Canadian scientists who collaborated on Central Asian paleontological expeditions), combined with Greek odon meaning 'tooth'
Urbacodon.description: Urbacodon is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur. Two species have been described, both of which are known from a partial dentary: U. itemirensis from the Dzharakuduk Formation (Cenomanian) of Uzbekistan and U. norelli from the Iren Dabasu Formation of China. Possible remains are also known from the Bissekty Formation (Turonian) of Uzbekistan.

species.name: Urbacodon itemirensis
species.etymology: Named for Itemir, the locality in Uzbekistan where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Zoological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences

references.authors: Averianov, Alexander O.; Sues, Hans-Dieter
references.title: A new troodontid (Dinosauria: Theropoda) from the Cenomanian of Uzbekistan, with a review of troodontid records from the territories of the former Soviet Union

Uriash.etymology: From Romanian 'uriaș' meaning 'giant', referencing the giant figure in Romanian folklore, reflecting the animal's notably large size compared to other local sauropod remains
Uriash.description: Uriash is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of Romania. The holotype of this genus was originally referred to Magyarosaurus hungaricus, which is now classified in a separate genus, Petrustitan.

species.name: Uriash kadici
species.etymology: Named for Hungarian geologist Ottokár Kadić (1876–1957), who discovered the fossil material in 1914.

holotype.material: Four posterior-distal caudal vertebrae (Ob.3090B, D, G, H), incomplete right humerus (Ob.3104), incomplete right and left femur (Ob.3103), left metatarsal I (Ob.3095)

references.authors: Díaz, Verónica Díez; Mannion, Philip D.; Csiki-Sava, Zoltán; Upchurch, Paul
references.title: Revision of Romanian sauropod dinosaurs reveals high titanosaur diversity and body-size disparity on the latest Cretaceous Haţeg Island, with implications for titanosaurian biogeography

Utahceratops.etymology: From 'Utah', the U.S. state where the fossil was found, and Greek 'keras' (stem 'cerat') meaning 'horn' and 'ops' meaning 'face', hence 'Utah horned face'.
Utahceratops.description: Utahceratops is an extinct genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived approximately 76.4~75.5 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Utah. Utahceratops was a large-sized, robustly-built, ground-dwelling, quadrupedal herbivore, that could grow up to an estimated 4.5–5 m (15–16 ft) long.

species.name: Utahceratops gettyi
species.etymology: Named for Mike Getty, who discovered the holotype and played a pivotal role in the recovery of fossils from the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument.

references.authors: Sampson, Scott D.; Loewen, Mark A.; Farke, Andrew A.; Roberts, Eric M.; Forster, Catherine A.; Smith, Joshua A.; Titus, Alan L.
references.title: New Horned Dinosaurs from Utah Provide Evidence for Intracontinental Dinosaur Endemism

Utahraptor.etymology: Named for the state of Utah, USA, where the fossils were found, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'robber' or 'plunderer'.
Utahraptor.description: Utahraptor is a genus of large dromaeosaurid (a group of feathered carnivorous theropods) dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period from around 139 to 135 million years ago in what is now the United States. The genus was described in 1993 by American paleontologist James Kirkland and colleagues with the type species Utahraptor ostrommaysi, based on fossils that had been unearthed earlier from the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah. Later, many additional specimens were described including those from the skull and postcranium in addition to those of younger individuals.

species.name: Utahraptor ostrommaysi
species.etymology: Named for paleontologist John Ostrom, for his investigations on Deinonychus and its relationship to birds, and for Chris Mays, who helped fund research on Utahraptor through Dinamation.

holotype.institution: College of Eastern Utah Prehistoric Museum

references.authors: Kirkland, J. I.; Burge, D.; R. Gaston
references.title: A large dromaeosaur (Theropoda) from the Lower Cretaceous of eastern Utah

Vagaceratops.etymology: From Latin vagus ('wandering') and Greek keratops ('horned face'), meaning 'wandering horned face', in reference to its close relationship with Kosmoceratops from Utah
Vagaceratops.description: Vagaceratops is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur which lived during the Late Cretaceous period (late Campanian) in what is now Alberta. Its fossils have been recovered from the Upper Dinosaur Park Formation. It is sometimes included in the genus Chasmosaurus as Chasmosaurus irvinensis instead of being recognized as its own genus.

species.name: Vagaceratops irvinensis
species.etymology: Named for the Irvine locality in Alberta, Canada, where the fossils were recovered.

references.authors: Farke, Andrew A.; Ryan, Michael J.; Barrett, Paul M.; Tanke, Darren H.; Braman, Dennis R.; Loewen, Mark A.; Graham, Mark R.
references.title: A New Centrosaurine from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada, and the Evolution of Parietal Ornamentation in Horned Dinosaurs
references.publisher: Polska Akademia Nauk Instytut Paleobiologii (Institute of Paleobiology, Polish Academy of Sciences)

Vahiny.description: Vahiny is an extinct genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of the Maevarano Formation, northwestern Madagascar. It contains a single species, Vahiny depereti.

species.name: Vahiny depereti
species.etymology: Named in honor of Charles Depéret, who described the original dinosaur material from Madagascar and presciently recognized the sauropod nature of the Malagasy osteoderms.

references.authors: Curry Rogers, K.; Wilson, J. A.
references.title: Vahiny depereti, gen. et sp. nov., a new titanosaur (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the Upper Cretaceous Maevarano Formation, Madagascar

Valdosaurus.etymology: From 'valdo', a modification of Old English 'weald' meaning 'a wood' (referring to the Weald region of England), combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Valdosaurus.description: Valdosaurus is a genus of bipedal herbivorous dryosaurid dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous of the Isle of Wight and elsewhere in England. Originally its remains were believed to belong to Hypsilophodon. In 1889, Richard Lydekker assigned them to Camptosaurus, alongside a partial lower jaw, and applied the name Camptosaurus valdensis. In the 1970s, Peter Galton reassigned these remains to a new species of Dryosaurus, then to an entirely new genus and species, that being Valdosaurus proper. The type and only species of Valdosaurus, named by Galton, is V. canaliculatus.

species.name: Valdosaurus canaliculatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'canaliculatus' meaning 'with a small channel', referring to a distinct groove between the condyles of the lower femora.

references.authors: Galton, P. M.
references.title: The Upper Jurassic dinosaur Dryosaurus and a Laurasia-Gondwana connection in the Upper Jurassic

Vallibonavenatrix.etymology: Named after Vallibona, the town in Castellón, Spain near where its remains were found, combined with Latin venatrix meaning 'huntress'; translates as 'Vallibona huntress'
Vallibonavenatrix.description: Vallibonavenatrix is a genus of spinosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Arcillas de Morella Formation of Castellón, Spain. The type and only species is Vallibonavenatrix cani, known from a partial skeleton.

species.name: Vallibonavenatrix cani
species.etymology: Named for Juan Cano Forner, the amateur fossil collector who discovered and excavated the specimen.

holotype.institution: Coleccions de la Conselleria de Cultura de Morella

references.authors: Malafaia, Elisabete; Gasulla, José Miguel; Escaso, Fernando; Narváez, Iván; Sanz, José Luis; Ortega, Francisco
references.title: A new spinosaurid theropod (Dinosauria: Megalosauroidea) from the upper Barremian of Vallibona, Spain: Implications for spinosaurid diversity in the Early Cretaceous of the Iberian Peninsula

Variraptor.etymology: From Latin Varus (referring to the Var River in the Alpes-Maritimes of southern France where it was found) and Latin raptor ('thief' or 'plunderer'), meaning 'Var thief'
Variraptor.description: Variraptor is a possibly dubious and potentially chimaeric genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of France.

species.name: Variraptor mechinorum
species.etymology: Named for Patrick Méchain and Annie Méchain-Salessy, the couple who discovered and recovered the fossil remains.

holotype.institution: Le Musée des Dinosaures Espéraza-Aude (Dinosaur Museum Espéraza), Espéraza, Department  Aude, Region  Languedoc-Roussillon-Midi-Pyrénées
holotype.material: Three type specimens from possibly different individuals; taxon considered chimaeric by some researchers

references.authors: Le Loeuff, J.; Buffetaut, E.
references.title: A new dromaeosaurid theropod from the Upper Cretaceous of southern France

Vayuraptor.etymology: Named for Vayu, the Hindu god of wind, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief', chosen to reflect the animal's inferred speed and agility.
Vayuraptor.description: Vayuraptor is a genus of basal coelurosaurian (possibly megaraptoran) theropod dinosaur that lived in the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Sao Khua Formation of Thailand. The genus contains a single species, V. nongbualamphuensis, known from a partial skeleton.

species.name: Vayuraptor nongbualamphuensis
species.etymology: Named for Nong Bua Lamphu Province, Thailand, where the fossils were discovered, with the suffix '-ensis' meaning 'from'.

holotype.material: Left tibia

references.authors: Samathi, Adun; Chanthasit, Phornphen; Sander, Paul
references.title: Two new basal coelurosaurian theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous Sao Khua Formation of Thailand
references.publisher: Polska Akademia Nauk Instytut Paleobiologii (Institute of Paleobiology, Polish Academy of Sciences)

Vectaerovenator.etymology: Named after Vectis (the Latin name for the Isle of Wight), combined with Latin aero meaning 'air' (referring to the pneumaticity of the vertebrae) and venator meaning 'hunter'; translates as 'Isle of Wight air-filled hunter'
Vectaerovenator.description: Vectaerovenator is a genus of tetanuran theropod from the Early Cretaceous period of what is now England (Lower Greensand Group; Ferruginous Sands). It contains one species, Vectaerovenator inopinatus; its holotype, consisting of the specimens IWCMS 2020.400, 2020.407, and 2019.84, comprises two anterior dorsal vertebrae, a cervical vertebra and a mid‐caudal vertebra from the late Aptian Ferruginous Sands of the Isle of Wight in southern England, discovered in 2019. Comparative anatomical analysis shows that this taxon shares homoplastic features with megalosauroids, carcharodontosaurs, and some coelurosaurs, and cannot be reliably placed beyond Tetanurae incertae sedis, but has enough autapomorphies that it can be considered a valid genus.

species.name: Vectaerovenator inopinatus
species.etymology: From Latin 'inopinatus' meaning 'unexpected', referring to its surprise discovery in the notably dinosaur-poor Lower Greensand strata of the Isle of Wight.

holotype.institution: Isle of Wight County Museum Service at Dinosaur Isle

references.authors: Barker, Chris T.; Naish, Darren; Clarkin, Claire E.; Farrell, Paul; Hullmann, Gabriel; Lockyer, James; Schneider, Philipp; Ward, Robin K. C.; Gostling, Neil J.
references.title: A highly pneumatic middle Cretaceous theropod from the British Lower Greensand

Vectidromeus.etymology: Combines 'Vectis', the Roman name for the Isle of Wight, England, with Greek 'dromeus' meaning 'runner'.
Vectidromeus.description: Vectidromeus is an extinct genus of hypsilophodontid ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation of England. The genus contains a single species, V. insularis, known from a partial skeleton belonging to a juvenile individual.

species.name: Vectidromeus insularis
species.etymology: From Latin 'insularis' meaning 'insular' or 'of an island', referring to the Isle of Wight where the holotype was found.

holotype.institution: Isle of Wight County Museum Service at Dinosaur Isle

references.authors: Longrich, Nicholas R.; Martill, David M.; Munt, Martin; Green, Mick; Penn, Mark; Smith, Shaun
references.title: Vectidromeus insularis, a new hypsilophodontid dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, England

Vectipelta.etymology: Named after Vectis (the Latin name for the Isle of Wight), combined with Latin pelta meaning 'shield'; translates as 'Isle of Wight shield'
Vectipelta.description: Vectipelta is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur recovered from the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation of England. The genus contains a single species, V. barretti, known from a partial skeleton including several osteoderms. It was historically known as the "Spearpoint ankylosaur" prior to its description.

species.name: Vectipelta barretti
species.etymology: Named for palaeontologist Paul Barrett of the Natural History Museum.

holotype.institution: Isle of Wight County Museum Service at Dinosaur Isle
holotype.material: Partial skeleton cataloged as IWCMS 1996.153, with additional referred material under IWCMS 2021.75

references.authors: Pond, Stuart; Strachan, Sarah-Jane; Raven, Thomas J.; Simpson, Martin I.; Morgan, Kirsty; Maidment, Susannah C. R.
references.title: Vectipelta barretti , a new ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, UK

Vectiraptor.etymology: Combines Latin 'Vectis' meaning 'Isle of Wight' and Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief'; the species name honors discoverer Mick Green.
Vectiraptor.description: Vectiraptor is a genus of dromaeosaurid dinosaur from the Barremian aged Wessex Formation of the United Kingdom. The type and only species is Vectiraptor greeni, known from associated dorsal vertebrae and a partial sacrum.

species.name: Vectiraptor greeni
species.etymology: Named for Mick Green, who initially discovered and prepared the type material.

holotype.institution: Isle of Wight County Museum Service at Dinosaur Isle
holotype.material: Two dorsal vertebrae

references.authors: Longrich, Nicholas R.; Martill, David M.; Jacobs, Megan L.
references.title: A new dromaeosaurid dinosaur from the Wessex Formation (Lower Cretaceous, Barremian) of the Isle of Wight, and implications for European palaeobiogeography

Velafrons.etymology: From Latin vela meaning 'sail' and frons meaning 'forehead' or 'brow'; translates as 'sailed forehead,' referring to its bony crest
Velafrons.description: Velafrons is a genus of lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mexico. It is known from a mostly complete skull and partial skeleton of a juvenile individual, with a bony crest on the forehead. Its fossils were found in the late Campanian-aged Cerro del Pueblo Formation (about 73.5 million years ago), near Rincon Colorado, Coahuila. The type specimen is CPC-59, and the type species is V. coahuilensis.

species.name: Velafrons coahuilensis
species.etymology: Named for Coahuila, the Mexican state where the fossils were found, with the suffix '-ensis' meaning 'from'.

holotype.institution: Colección Paleontológica de Coahuila, Museo del Desierto (MUDE)

references.authors: Gates, Terry A.; Sampson, Scott D.; De Jesús, Carlos R. Delgado; Zanno, Lindsay E.; Eberth, David; Hernandez-Rivera, René; Martínez, Martha C. Aguillón; Kirkland, James I.
references.title: Velafrons coahuilensis, a new lambeosaurine hadrosaurid (Dinosauria: Ornithopoda) from the late Campanian Cerro del Pueblo Formation, Coahuila, Mexico

Velocipes.etymology: From Latin 'velox' meaning 'swift' and 'pes' meaning 'foot', translating as 'quick foot'.
Velocipes.description: Velocipes is a genus of saurischian dinosaur from the Late Triassic that may have been a theropod. Its fossils were found in the Norian-aged Lissauer Breccia of southern Poland. Upon discovery, Velocipes was thought to have been a coelurosaur, but more recent studies have shown that Velocipes was probably a basal theropod or dinosauriform.

species.name: Velocipes guerichi
species.etymology: Named for Georg Gürich, who discovered the fossil material in the Lissauer Breccia of southern Poland around 1884.

holotype.material: Tibia fragment

references.authors: Huene, F. v.
references.title: Die fossile Reptil-Ordnung Saurischia, ihre Entwicklung und Geschichte [The fossil reptile order Saurischia, their development and history]
references.journal: Monographien zur Geologie und Palaeontologie, serie 1

Velociraptor.etymology: From Latin velox meaning 'swift' and raptor meaning 'thief' or 'plunderer'; translates as 'swift thief'
Velociraptor.description: A genus of small dromaeosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia. Despite its popular depiction as a large predator, Velociraptor was roughly the size of a turkey, about 2 metres long and 15 kilograms. It possessed a large, sickle-shaped claw on the second toe of each foot, characteristic of dromaeosaurids.

features: Large, sickle-shaped retractable claw on second toe
Long, stiffened tail for balance
Elongated snout with serrated teeth

Enlarged sickle claw on pedal digit II
Long, low skull with over 26 teeth in each maxilla

species.etymology: Named for Mongolia, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.material: crushed skull and sickle claw

species.description: The type species of Velociraptor. Known from numerous specimens discovered in the Gobi Desert, including the famous "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen locked in combat with a Protoceratops.

Velocisaurus.etymology: From Latin velox meaning 'swift' and Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'swift lizard'
Velocisaurus.description: Velocisaurus is a genus of noasaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of Argentina.

species.name: Velocisaurus unicus
species.etymology: From Latin 'unicus' meaning 'unique', referring to the exceptional build of the foot.

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.
references.title: Los vertebrados fósiles de la Formación Rio Colorado, de la Ciudad de Neuquén y Cercanías, Cretácico Superior, Argentina [The vertebrate fossils of the Rio Colorado Formation, from the city of Neuquén and surrounding areas, Upper Cretaceous, Argentina]
references.journal: Revista del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales "Bernardino Rivadavia" e Instituto Nacional de Investigación de las Ciencias Naturales: Paleontología

Venenosaurus.etymology: From the Poison Strip Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation (Latin venenum, 'poison') where the fossils were found, plus Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'poison lizard'
Venenosaurus.description: Venenosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Utah during the Early Cretaceous. Its type and only species is Venenosaurus dicrocei. Fossils of Venenosaurus were first discovered in 1998, by Denver Museum of Natural History volunteer Anthony DiCroce, and described as a new genus and species in 2001 by Virginia Tidwell and colleagues, who named the species for DiCroce. Venenosaurus was a relatively small sauropod, and was similar to Cedarosaurus, another sauropod from the Early Cretaceous of Utah.

species.name: Venenosaurus dicrocei
species.etymology: Named for Anthony DiCroce, the Denver Museum of Natural History volunteer who discovered the fossil site.

holotype.institution: Denver Museum of Nature and Science

Vespersaurus.etymology: From Latin 'vesper' meaning 'evening' or 'west', referencing the town Cruzeiro do Oeste ('Western Cross') near the discovery site, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Vespersaurus.description: Vespersaurus is a genus of noasaurid theropod dinosaur from the Cretaceous Rio Paraná Formation in the Paraná Basin, Brazil. The type and only species is V. paranaensis, which would have lived in the giant prehistoric Botucatu Desert.

species.name: Vespersaurus paranaensis
species.etymology: Named for Paraná state, Brazil, where the fossils were found, with the suffix '-ensis' meaning 'from'.

holotype.institution: Museu Paleontológico de Cruzeiro do Oeste

Veterupristisaurus.etymology: From Latin 'veter' meaning 'old' or 'ancient' and Latin 'pristis' meaning 'shark', combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'old shark lizard', referring to Veterupristisaurus being the oldest known representative of the carcharodontosaurids
Veterupristisaurus.description: Veterupristisaurus is an extinct genus of carcharodontosaurid theropod dinosaur known from the Jurassic of Tendaguru, Lindi Region of southeastern Tanzania.

species.name: Veterupristisaurus milneri
species.etymology: Named for palaeontologist Angela C. Milner.

Viavenator.etymology: From Latin via meaning 'road' and venator meaning 'hunter'; translates as 'road hunter'
Viavenator.description: Viavenator is a genus of carnivorous abelisaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in the Santonian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina. Only a single species is known, V. exxoni, formally described in 2016 by Filippi and colleagues.

species.name: Viavenator exxoni
species.etymology: Named in recognition of ExxonMobil's commitment to the preservation of paleontological heritage in the La Invernada area, Rincón de los Sauces, Neuquén, Patagonia, Argentina.

holotype.material: Partially associated skeleton

Vitosaura.etymology: Named in honour of Victoria 'Doña Vito' Romero, a 19th-century soldier born in the Los Llanos region near the type locality, combined with 'saura', feminine of Ancient Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Vitosaura.description: Vitosaura is an extinct genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous Los Llanos Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Vitosaura colozacani, known from a partial skeleton. Alongside Guemesia and the noasaurid Noasaurus, Vitosaura is one of the only Argentinian ceratosaurians found outside of Patagonia.

species.name: Vitosaura colozacani
species.etymology: Named for the Colozacán Valley in La Rioja Province, Argentina, where the specimen was discovered.

holotype.institution: Centro Regional de Investigaciones Científicas y Transferencia Tecnológica de La Rioja

references.authors: Velandia, Harold Jiménez; Ezcurra, Martín D.; Hechenleitner, E. Martín; Basilici, Giorgio; Martinelli, Agustín G.; Fiorelli, Lucas E.
references.title: A New Late Cretaceous Abelisaurid Species from La Rioja Province, Northwestern Argentina

Volgatitan.etymology: Named for the Volga River region of Russia (Ulyanovsk Oblast) where the fossils were found, combined with 'titan' meaning 'giant'.
Volgatitan.description: Volgatitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of the Ulyanovsk Oblast, Russia. The type and only species is Volgatitan simbirskiensis, known from seven caudal vertebrae from a single individual. It is the oldest known titanosaur from the northern hemisphere, and is considered important for being related to the Lognkosauria, a group known only from South America later in the Late Cretaceous. It was first described in November 2018 by Russian palaeontologists Alexander Averianov and Vladimir Efimov. It is estimated to have weighed about 17.3 metric tons (19.1 short tons).

species.name: Volgatitan simbirskiensis
species.etymology: Named for Simbirsk, the historical name of Ulyanovsk Oblast, Russia, where the fossils were found, with the suffix '-ensis' meaning 'from'.

references.authors: Averianov, Alexander; Efimov, Vladimir
references.title: The oldest titanosaurian sauropod of the Northern Hemisphere

Volkheimeria.etymology: Named in honor of Wolfgang Volkheimer, an Argentine paleontologist and palynologist who contributed to the study of Jurassic formations in Argentina.
Volkheimeria.description: Volkheimeria is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaurs that lived in what is now Argentina during the Early Jurassic, about 179–178 million years ago. Its type and only species is Volkheimeria chubutensis.

species.name: Volkheimeria chubutensis
species.etymology: Named for Chubut Province, Argentina, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Colección de Paleontologia de Vertebrados de la Fundación Instituto Miguel Lillo

references.authors: Bonaparte, J. F.
references.title: Dinosaurs: A Jurassic Assemblage from Patagonia
references.publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

Vouivria.etymology: Named after the vouivre, a mythological serpentine or dragon-like creature from the folklore of Franche-Comté, France, where the fossil was found
Vouivria.description: Vouivria is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur, belonging to the Brachiosauridae, that lived in the area of present France during the Late Jurassic. The type and only known species is Vouivria damparisensis. It is based on a specimen once commonly referred to as the "French Bothriospondylus" in the scientific literature, as the specimen was once identified as Bothriospondylus madagascariensis, a species known from the Middle Jurassic of Madagascar.

species.name: Vouivria damparisensis
species.etymology: Named for Damparis, the locality in Franche-Comté, France, near which the holotype was found.

references.authors: Mannion, Philip D.; Allain, Ronan; Moine, Olivier
references.title: The earliest known titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur and the evolution of Brachiosauridae

Vulcanodon.etymology: Named after the volcano near which it was found in Zimbabwe, combined with Greek odon meaning 'tooth'; translates as 'volcano tooth'
Vulcanodon.description: Vulcanodon is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic uppermost Forest Sandstone of southern Africa. The only known species is V. karibaensis. Discovered in 1969 in Zimbabwe, it was regarded as the earliest known sauropod for decades, and is still one of the most primitive genera that has been discovered.

species.name: Vulcanodon karibaensis
species.etymology: Named for Lake Kariba, Zimbabwe, where the holotype was discovered on a small island.

references.authors: Raath, M. A.
references.title: Fossil vertebrate studies in Rhodesia: a new dinosaur (Reptilia: Saurischia) from near the Tria-Jurassic boundary

Wakinosaurus.etymology: Named after the Wakino Subgroup of the Kwanmon Group (a geological unit in Kyushu, Japan), combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Wakino lizard'
Wakinosaurus.description: Wakinosaurus is a genus of possible carcharodontosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian-Barremian) Sengoku Formation of Kyushu, Japan. The genus is a tooth taxon, based solely on the middle section of a single tooth.

species.name: Wakinosaurus satoi
species.etymology: Named for Masahiro Sato, the ice hockey player who discovered the holotype tooth in Fukuoka, Japan, in 1990.

holotype.institution: Kitakyushu Museum of Natural History and Human History
holotype.material: Single damaged tooth

references.authors: Okazaki, Y.
references.title: A new genus and species of carnivorous dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Kwanmon Group, northern Kyushu
references.journal: Bulletin of the Kitakyushu Museum of Natural History

Walgettosuchus.etymology: From the town of Walgett, New South Wales, plus Greek Soukhos (the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek)
Walgettosuchus.description: Walgettosuchus is a dubious or possibly invalid genus of extinct tetanuran theropod dinosaur that lived in Australia during the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian). It is known from a single caudal vertebra.

species.name: Walgettosuchus woodwardi
species.etymology: Honours British paleontologist Arthur Smith Woodward, who first reported the specimen in 1909

Wamweracaudia.etymology: Named after the Wamwera people, a tribe inhabiting the Lindi Region of Tanzania near the Tendaguru fossil site, combined with Latin 'cauda' meaning 'tail', as the holotype consists entirely of a series of tail vertebrae
Wamweracaudia.description: Wamweracaudia is a large herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (155-145 million years ago) Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania, Africa.

species.name: Wamweracaudia keranjei
species.etymology: Named for Mohammadi Keranje, the native foreman who led the team that excavated the holotype tail material at the Tendaguru site in Tanzania.

references.authors: Mannion, P. D.; Upchurch, P.; D. Schwarz, O. Wings
references.title: Taxonomic affinities of the putative titanosaurs from the Late Jurassic Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania: phylogenetic and biogeographic implications for eusauropod dinosaur evolution
references.journal: Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society

Wannanosaurus.etymology: Named for Wannan (southern Anhui), the region of China where the fossils were discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Wannanosaurus.description: Wannanosaurus is a genus of basal pachycephalosaurian dinosaur from the Maastrichtian-aged (Upper Cretaceous) Xiaoyan Formation, about 70 million years ago, in what is now Anhui, China. The type species Wannanosaurus yansiensis was described by Hou Lian-Hai in 1977.

species.name: Wannanosaurus yansiensis
species.etymology: Named for Yansi, the locality in Anhui Province, China, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: Hou, L.-H.
references.title: A new primitive Pachycephalosauria from Anhui, China

Weewarrasaurus.etymology: Named after the Wee Warra geologic locality near Lightning Ridge, New South Wales, Australia, where the fossil was found, plus Greek sauros ('lizard')
Weewarrasaurus.description: Weewarrasaurus is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of the Griman Creek Formation near Lightning Ridge, in New South Wales, Australia. The type and only species is W. pobeni, known from the holotype, an isolated dentary preserved in opal, as well as a secondary referred dentary. It is thought to have co-existed with multiple other ornithopods of different sizes and lineages.

species.name: Weewarrasaurus pobeni
species.etymology: Named for Mike Poben, the opal dealer from Adelaide who first recognized the holotype as a fossil and subsequently donated it to the Australian Opal Centre.

references.authors: Bell, Phil R.; Herne, Matthew C.; Brougham, Tom; Smith, Elizabeth T.
references.title: Ornithopod diversity in the Griman Creek Formation (Cenomanian), New South Wales, Australia

Wellnhoferia.etymology: Named after German paleontologist Peter Wellnhofer, who described the Solnhofen specimen of Archaeopteryx in 1988
Wellnhoferia.description: Wellnhoferia is a genus of early prehistoric bird-like theropod dinosaur closely related to Archaeopteryx. It is known from a single species, W. grandis, that lived in what is now Germany, during the Late Jurassic. While Wellnhoferia was similar to Archaeopteryx, it had a shorter tail and its fourth toe was shorter than that of Archaeopteryx. Andrzej Elżanowski (2001) of the Institute of Zoology of the University of Wrocław, Poland, determined the differences resulted from a "phylogenetic reduction rather than individual variation."

references.authors: Elzanowski, A.
references.title: A new genus and species for the largest specimen of Archaeopteryx

Wendiceratops.etymology: Combines Wendi (honoring Canadian fossil hunter Wendy Sloboda) with Greek ceratops ('horned face'), meaning 'Wendy's horned face'
Wendiceratops.description: Wendiceratops is a genus of herbivorous centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Canada.

species.name: Wendiceratops pinhornensis
species.etymology: Named for the Pinhorn Provincial Grazing Reserve in Alberta, Canada, where the holotype was found.

references.authors: Evans, David C.; Ryan, Michael J.

Wiehenvenator.etymology: From Wiehen (the Wiehen Hills near Minden, Germany, where the fossil was found) and Latin venator ('hunter'), meaning 'Wiehen hunter'
Wiehenvenator.description: Wiehenvenator is a genus of megalosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic (Callovian) of north western Germany. The genus contains a single species, W. albati.

species.name: Wiehenvenator albati
species.etymology: Named for Friedrich Albat, the geologist who discovered the holotype remains at the Pott quarry in the Wiehen Hills near Minden, Germany, in 1998.

references.authors: Rauhut, OW M; Hübner, T; Lanser, K
references.title: A new megalosaurid theropod dinosaur from the late Middle Jurassic (Callovian) of north-western Germany: Implications for theropod evolution and faunal turnover in the Jurassic

Willinakaqe.etymology: From Mapuche willi ('south'), iná ('mimic'), and kaqe ('duck'), meaning 'Southern duck-mimic'
Willinakaqe.description: Willinakaqe is a dubious genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur described based on fossils from the late Cretaceous (late Campanian-early Maastrichtian stage) of the Río Negro Province of southern Argentina.

species.name: Willinakaqe salitralensis
species.etymology: Named for the Salitral, the locality in Río Negro Province, Argentina, where the holotype was found.

references.authors: Juárez Valieri, R. D.; Haro, J. A.; L. E. Fiorelli, J. O. Calvo
references.title: A new hadrosauroid (Dinosauria: Ornithopoda) from the Allen Formation (Late Cretaceous) of Patagonia, Argentina

Wintonotitan.etymology: Named after Winton, Queensland, Australia (the area where it was found, associated with the Winton Formation), combined with Greek titan meaning 'giant'; translates as 'Winton titan'
Wintonotitan.description: Wintonotitan is a genus of titanosauriform dinosaur from the Cenomanian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Winton Formation of Australia. It is known from partial postcranial remains.

species.name: Wintonotitan wattsi
species.etymology: Named for Keith Watts, who first discovered the holotype fossils near Winton, Queensland, Australia, in 1974.

references.authors: Hocknull, Scott A.; White, Matt A.; Tischler, Travis R.; Cook, Alex G.; Calleja, Naomi D.; Sloan, Trish; Elliott, David A.
references.title: New Mid-Cretaceous (Latest Albian) Dinosaurs from Winton, Queensland, Australia

Wulagasaurus.etymology: Named for the Wulaga locality in Heilongjiang, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Wulagasaurus.description: Wulagasaurus is a genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Heilongjiang, China.

species.name: Wulagasaurus dongi
species.etymology: Named for Dong Zhiming, the prominent Chinese paleontologist who has described numerous dinosaur taxa.

holotype.institution: Geiseltalmuseum of Martin-Luther Universität Halle-Wittenberg, Germany, now referred to as the Geiseltalsammlung, housed as part of the Zentralmagazin Naturwissenschaftlicher Sammlungen

references.title: New Hadrosaurid Dinosaurs from the Uppermost Cretaceous of Northeastern China
references.publisher: Polska Akademia Nauk Instytut Paleobiologii (Institute of Paleobiology, Polish Academy of Sciences)

Wulatelong.etymology: From Wulate (referring to Wulatehouqi, the region of Inner Mongolia, China where it was found) and Chinese long ('dragon')
Wulatelong.description: Wulatelong is an extinct genus of basal oviraptorid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Wulansuhai Formation (Campanian stage) of Bayan Mandahu, Linhe District of Inner Mongolia, northern China. It contains a single species, Wulatelong gobiensis.

species.name: Wulatelong gobiensis
species.etymology: Named for the Gobi Desert, the region in which the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

Wulong.etymology: From Chinese 'wu' meaning 'dancing' and 'long' meaning 'dragon', in reference to the specimen's sprightly preserved pose.
Wulong.description: Wulong is a genus of microraptorine dromaeosaurid dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian) Jiufotang Formation of China. The genus includes a single species, Wulong bohaiensis. The skeletal remains, which include preserved feathers, represent a juvenile.

species.name: Wulong bohaiensis
species.etymology: Named for the Bohai Strait, near which the Dalian Natural History Museum housing the holotype is located.

references.authors: Poust, Ashley W.; Gao, Chunling; Varricchio, David J.; Wu, Jianlin; Zhang, Fengjiao
references.title: A new microraptorine theropod from the Jehol Biota and growth in early dromaeosaurids

Wyleyia.etymology: Named in honor of J. F. Wyley, who discovered the specimen in Weald Clay deposits of Henfield, Sussex, England.
Wyleyia.description: Wyleyia is an extinct genus of indeterminate maniraptoran dinosaurs containing a single species, Wyleyia valdensis, known from the early Cretaceous period of Sussex, England. The genus is known from a single specimen, a damaged right humerus. It was named to honor J. F. Wyley, who found the specimen in Weald Clay deposits of Henfield in Sussex (England). The specific name valdensis means "from the Weald".

species.name: Wyleyia valdensis
species.etymology: From Latin 'valdensis' meaning 'from the Weald', referring to the Weald Clay deposits of Sussex, England, where the holotype humerus was found.

references.authors: Harrison, C. J. O.; Walker, C. A.
references.title: Wyleyia: a new bird humerus from the Lower Cretaceous of England

Xenoceratops.etymology: From Greek 'xenos' meaning 'foreign' or 'alien' and 'ceratops' meaning 'horned face', referring to the scarcity of ceratopsian species known from the Foremost Formation.
Xenoceratops.description: Xenoceratops is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (middle Campanian stage), and is known to have lived in what is currently Alberta, Canada. The genus has one known species, Xenoceratops foremostensis, after its place of discovery, the Foremost Formation.

species.name: Xenoceratops foremostensis
species.etymology: Named for the town of Foremost, Alberta, Canada, near which the holotype skull fragments were excavated from the Foremost Formation.

location.locality: Chin Coulee Site No. 2 (Wann Langston Jr. 1958)

references.authors: Ryan, Michael J.; Evans, David C.; Shepherd, Kieran M.
references.title: A new ceratopsid from the Foremost Formation (middle Campanian) of Alberta

Xenoposeidon.etymology: From Greek xenos meaning 'strange' or 'alien' and Poseidon (the Greek god of the sea), in allusion to the sauropod genus Sauroposeidon; translates as 'strange Poseidon'
Xenoposeidon.description: Xenoposeidon is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England, living about 140 million years ago. It is known from a single partial vertebra with unusual features, unlike those of other sauropods. This bone was first discovered in the early 1890s but received little attention until it was found by University of Portsmouth student Mike Taylor, who formally described and named it in 2007 with Darren Naish.

species.name: Xenoposeidon proneneukos
species.etymology: From Ancient Greek meaning 'forward sloping', describing the distinctive anterior lean of the neural arch, the most conspicuous anatomical feature of the holotype vertebra.

references.authors: TAYLOR, MICHAEL P.; NAISH, DARREN
references.title: AN UNUSUAL NEW NEOSAUROPOD DINOSAUR FROM THE LOWER CRETACEOUS HASTINGS BEDS GROUP OF EAST SUSSEX, ENGLAND

Xenotarsosaurus.etymology: From Greek xenos ('strange'), tarsos ('tarsus' or 'ankle'), and sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'strange ankle lizard', referring to the exceptional build of the ankle
Xenotarsosaurus.description: Xenotarsosaurus is a genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous of Argentina.

species.name: Xenotarsosaurus bonapartei
species.etymology: Named for José Fernando Bonaparte, the Argentine paleontologist who recovered additional holotype material and made major contributions to the study of South American dinosaurs.

references.authors: Martínez, R. D.; Giménez, O.; J. Rodríguez, G. Bochatey
references.title: Xenotarsosaurus bonapartei nov. gen. et sp. (Carnosauria, Abelisauridae), un nuevo Theropoda de la Formacion Bajo Barreal, Chubut, Argentina [Xenotarsosaurus bonapartei nov. gen. et sp. (Carnosauria, Abelisauridae), a new Theropoda from the Bajo Barreal Formation, Chubut, Argentina]
references.journal: IV Congreso Argentino de Paleontologia y Bioestratigrafia

Xenovenator.etymology: From Greek xenos ('strange') and Latin venator ('hunter'), meaning 'strange hunter'
Xenovenator.description: Xenovenator is an extinct genus of troodontid theropod dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian age) of North America. The type species of the genus, Xenovenator espinosai, is known from fragmentary skull bones found in the Cerro del Pueblo Formation of Mexico. It is characterized by an unusually expanded and rugose skull roof, somewhat comparable to that seen in pachycephalosaurs. This may imply Xenovenator individuals engaged in combat with other members of their species, a behavior for which adaptations had not been previously observed in non-avian paravians.

Xianshanosaurus.etymology: Named after Xianshan Hill near the fossil locality in the Ruyang Basin, Henan Province, China, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Xianshanosaurus.description: Xianshanosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian) of the Ruyang Basin in Henan Province, China. Its type and only species is Xianshanosaurus shijiagouensis. It was described in 2009 by a team of paleontologists led by Lü Junchang. Xianshanosaurus may be a titanosaur, and Daxiatitan may be its closest relative, but its evolutionary relationships remain controversial.

species.name: Xianshanosaurus shijiagouensis
species.etymology: Named for Shijiagou, the locality near Xian Mountain in Henan Province, China, where the holotype was found.

references.journal: Journal of the Paleontological Society of Korea

Xiaosaurus.etymology: From Chinese 'xiao' meaning 'dawn', referring to the early geological age of the fossil, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Xiaosaurus.description: Xiaosaurus is a genus of small herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur from the middle Jurassic (approximately 170.3 to 163.5 million years ago) of what is now the Sichuan Basin of China.

species.name: Xiaosaurus dashanpensis
species.etymology: Named for Dashanpu, the village near Zigong in Sichuan, China, where the holotype was excavated.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
holotype.material: Partial skeleton

references.authors: Dong, Z.; Tang, Z.
references.title: New ornithopod genus from the Middle Jurassic of Sichuan Basin, China

Xiaotingia.etymology: Named in honor of Chinese paleontologist Zheng Xiaoting; the generic name is derived from Xiaoting, the first part of Zheng's given name
Xiaotingia.description: Xiaotingia is a genus of paravian theropod dinosaur, possibly an anchiornithid, from Middle Jurassic or early Late Jurassic deposits of western Liaoning, China. It contains a single species, Xiaotingia zhengi.

species.name: Xiaotingia zhengi
species.etymology: Named for paleontologist Zheng Xiaoting, together with the genus name forming a combined honorific for the same individual.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: Xu, Xing; You, Hailu; Du, Kai; Han, Fenglu
references.title: An Archaeopteryx-like theropod from China and the origin of Avialae
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Xingtianosaurus.etymology: Named after Xingtian, a Chinese deity who continued to fight after being decapitated, referencing the skull-less holotype specimen, plus Greek sauros ('lizard')
Xingtianosaurus.description: Xingtianosaurus is an extinct genus of oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now China during the Early Cretaceous. The type and only species, X. ganqi, was named and described in 2019. It was placed in the Caudipteridae, alongside Caudipteryx and Similicaudipteryx.

species.name: Xingtianosaurus ganqi
species.etymology: Named for the ganqi, the battle axe wielded by the Chinese deity Xingtian, referencing both the weapon and the skull-less state of the holotype specimen.

Xingxiulong.etymology: Named for the Xingxiu Bridge (Xingxiu meaning 'constellation' in Chinese) in Yunnan, China, combined with Chinese 'long' meaning 'dragon'.
Xingxiulong.description: Xingxiulong is a genus of bipedal massopodan sauropodomorph from the Early Jurassic of China. It contains two species; the type species is X. chengi, described by Wang et al. in 2017 from three specimens, two adults and an immature individual, that collectively constitute a mostly complete skeleton. Adults of this species measured 4–5 metres (13–16 ft) long and 1–1.5 metres (3.3–4.9 ft) tall. A second species, X. yueorum, was described by Chen et al. in 2025 based on a partial articulated postcranial skeleton of an adult individual larger than X. chengi.

species.etymology: Named for Professor Zheng-Wu Cheng, who made major contributions to the biostratigraphy of China, including that of the Lufeng area, and died in 2015.

Xinjiangovenator.etymology: Named after Xinjiang, the autonomous region of China where it was found, combined with Latin venator meaning 'hunter'; translates as 'Xinjiang hunter'
Xinjiangovenator.description: Xinjiangovenator is a genus of coelurosaurian dinosaurs, possibly part of the group Maniraptora, which lived in the Lianmuqin Formation of the Tugulu Group of China, dated to the Early Cretaceous period, sometime between the Valanginian and Albian stages.

species.name: Xinjiangovenator parvus
species.etymology: From Latin 'parvus' meaning 'small', reflecting the modest size of the holotype individual.

Xinjiangtitan.etymology: From Xinjiang, the autonomous region of northwestern China where it was found, and titan ('giant'), meaning 'Xinjiang titan'
Xinjiangtitan.description: Xinjiangtitan is an extinct genus of mamenchisaurid sauropod that lived during the Middle Jurassic of what is now Xinjiang, northwestern China. Its type and only species is Xinjiangtitan shanshanesis (Chinese: 鄯善新疆巨龙; pinyin: Shànshàn Xīnjiāngjùlóng), known from a single incomplete skeleton recovered from the Qiketai Formation. The holotype preserves one of the most complete vertebral columns of any sauropod found in Asia, and has the longest complete neck known for any animal.

Xiongguanlong.etymology: From Chinese 'Xiong Guan' meaning 'grand pass', referring to Jiayuguan City (historically called Xiong Guan), and Chinese 'long' meaning 'dragon'.
Xiongguanlong.description: Xiongguanlong is an extinct genus of tyrannosauroid theropod from the Early Cretaceous period of what is now China. The type and only species is X. baimoensis. The generic name comes from Jiayuguan City (formerly called "Xiong Guan" or "grand pass") and the Mandarin word "long" which means dragon. The specific epithet, "baimoensis" is a latinization of the Mandarin word for "white ghost" in reference to one of the geological features of the type locality (nicknamed the "White Ghost Castle").

species.name: Xiongguanlong baimoensis

Xixianykus.etymology: From Xixia County, Henan Province, China (where the fossil was found) and Greek onyx ('claw'), meaning 'Xixia claw'
Xixianykus.description: Xixianykus is a genus of alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur known from a slab of rock which contains a partial postcranial skeleton unearthed in the Late Cretaceous (Coniacian-Santonian) Majiacun Formation of the Xixia Basin in Henan, China.

Xixiasaurus.etymology: Named for Xixia County, Henan Province, China, where the holotype was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', translatable as 'Henan Xixia lizard'.
Xixiasaurus.description: Xixiasaurus is a genus of troodontid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period in what is now China. The only known specimen was discovered in Xixia County, Henan Province, in central China, and became the holotype of the new genus and species Xixiasaurus henanensis in 2010. The names refer to the areas of discovery, and can be translated as "Henan Xixia lizard". The specimen consists of an almost complete skull (except for the hindmost portion), part of the lower jaw, and teeth, as well as a partial right forelimb.

species.name: Xixiasaurus henanensis
species.etymology: Named for Henan Province, China, where the holotype was discovered in Xixia County.

Xixiposaurus.etymology: Named for the village of Xixipo in Lufeng County, Yunnan, China, where the holotype was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Xixiposaurus.description: Xixiposaurus is a genus of "prosauropod" dinosaur which existed in what is now Lower Lufeng Formation, China during the lower Jurassic period. It was first named by Sekiya Toru in 2010 and the type species is X. suni.

Xiyunykus.etymology: From Mandarin xiyu meaning 'west' (referring to Western China where it was found) combined with Greek onyx meaning 'claw'; translates as 'western claw'
Xiyunykus.description: Xiyunykus is a genus of alvarezsauroid theropod from the Early Cretaceous-aged Tugulu Group of what is now China. Only one species has been described, Xiyunykus pengi.

Xuanhanosaurus.etymology: Named for Xuanhan County in Sichuan, China, where the fossils were recovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Xuanhanosaurus.description: Xuanhanosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian) of the Sichuan Basin, China, around 166 million years ago. This taxon represents one of the various non-coelurosaurian tetanuran taxa found on the Middle Jurassic of the region, uncovered in the Lower Shaximiao Formation. Although it has been known for more than 40 years, this taxon has been the subject of very few studies, although most seem to agree that it is a tetanuran, possibly a basal allosauroid, highlighting the fact that it has a vestigial fourth metacarpal.

Xuanhuaceratops.description: Xuanhuaceratops is a genus of dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Period. The genus was in 2006 dated to the Tithonian, 150.8-145.5 million years ago. A member of the family Chaoyangsauridae, it was one of the earliest ceratopsians. The fossils were found in the Houcheng Formation of Hebei Province, northeastern China.

Xunmenglong.etymology: From Chinese xun ('swift'), meng ('fierce'), and long ('dragon'), meaning 'swift fierce dragon'
Xunmenglong.description: Xunmenglong is a genus of compsognathid theropod dinosaur from the Huajiying Formation of Hebei Province, China. The type and only species is Xunmenglong yinliangis. The holotype material consists of a pelvis, tail base and hindlimbs that had previously been part of a chimera containing three different animals. The animal is described as being the smallest known member of Compsognathidae, being about the size of the sub-adult Scipionyx holotype specimen, or approximately 50 centimetres (1.6 ft) in length.

Xuwulong.etymology: Named after pioneering Gansu Province geologist Wang Yue-lun, known by his courtesy name 'Xu-wu', combined with Chinese 'long' meaning 'dragon'
Xuwulong.description: Xuwulong is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of what is now Yujingzi Basin in the Jiuquan area, Gansu Province of northwestern China. It is known from the holotype, GSGM F00001, an articulated specimen including a complete cranium, almost complete axial skeleton, and complete left pelvic girdle recovered from the Xinminbao Group. Xuwulong was named by You Hailu, Li Daqing, and Liu Weichang in 2011, and the type species is Xuwulong yueluni; the binomial name as a whole refers to Professor Wang Yue-lun; "Xu-wu" is his courtesy name.

Yamaceratops.etymology: Named after Yama, a Tibetan Buddhist deity, combined with Greek 'keras' meaning 'horn' and 'ops' meaning 'face'
Yamaceratops.description: Yamaceratops is a genus of primitive ceratopsian that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia. The genus contains a single species, Y. dorngobiensis. It was a relatively small dinosaur, with an estimated length of 50 cm (1.6 ft) and weighing around 2 kg (4.4 lb).

Yamanasaurus.etymology: Named after the locality of Yamana in southern Ecuador where the fossils were found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Yamana lizard'
Yamanasaurus.description: Yamanasaurus is an extinct genus of saltasaurine titanosaurian dinosaur from the Río Playas Formation of Ecuador, which dates to the Campanian-Maastrichtian of the late Cretaceous period (approximately 75-70 million years ago). The type and only species is Yamanasaurus lojaensis, representing the first non-avian dinosaur described from Ecuador. The holotype, consisting of fragments of a humerus, ulna, tibia, two sacral vertebrae and a single caudal, was discovered in 2017.

Yamatosaurus.description: Yamatosaurus is a genus of basal hadrosaurid from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)-aged Kita-Ama Formation of Awaji Island, Japan. The genus contains a single species, Yamatosaurus izanagii.

Yanbeilong.etymology: From Chinese yanbe meaning 'north of Yanmen Pass' (a region of Shanxi Province, China) and long meaning 'dragon'; translates as 'north of Yanmen Pass dragon'
Yanbeilong.description: Yanbeilong is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Albian age) Zuoyun Formation of Shanxi, China. The genus contains a single species, Yanbeilong ultimus, known from a single partial skeleton including several vertebrae and the pelvic girdle. It is one of the youngest known stegosaurs, alongside Mongolostegus from Mongolia and unnamed stegosaurine remains from the Hekou Group of China, both of which date to the Aptian–Albian ages.

Yandusaurus.etymology: From Yandu (the ancient name for Zigong, Sichuan Province, China, meaning 'salt capital') and Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Yandu lizard'
Yandusaurus.description: Yandusaurus is a genus of basal neornithischian dinosaur from the middle Jurassic (Bathonian age, approximately 168 to 162 Ma) of eastern Asia. The type species is Y. hongheensis, described in 1979 from the Lower Shaximiao Formation of Sichuan Province, China.

Yangchuanosaurus.etymology: Named for Yongchuan (historically romanized as Yangchuan), the district in Sichuan Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Yangchuanosaurus.description: Yangchuanosaurus is an extinct genus of metriacanthosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in China from the Middle Jurassic to Late Jurassic periods (Bathonian to Tithonian stages), and was similar (although slightly larger) in size and appearance to its North American and European relative, Allosaurus. Yangchuanosaurus hails from the Upper Shaximiao Formation and was the largest predator in a landscape that included the sauropods Mamenchisaurus and Omeisaurus and the stegosaurs Chialingosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus and Chungkingosaurus. This theropod was named after the area in which was discovered, Yongchuan, in China.

Yehuecauhceratops.etymology: From Nahuatl yehuecauh meaning 'ancient' combined with Greek keras meaning 'horn' and ops meaning 'face'; translates as 'ancient horned face'
Yehuecauhceratops.description: Yehuecauhceratops is a genus of horned centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Coahuila, Mexico. It contains a single species, Y. mudei, described from two partial specimens by Rivera-Sylva et al. in 2016 and formally named by Rivera-Sylva et al. in 2017. It was a small centrosaurine with a body length of 3 metres (9.8 ft), making it smaller than Agujaceratops and Coahuilaceratops, the other two ceratopsids in its environment; the three may have been ecologically segregated. A ridge bearing a single roughened projection near the bottom of the squamosal bone, which probably supported a small horn, allows Yehuecauhceratops to be distinguished from other centrosaurines. Its affinities to nasutoceratopsin centrosaurines, such as Avaceratops and Nasutoceratops, are supported by various morphological similarities to the former.

Yeneen.etymology: Named after Yeneen, an entity in Tehuelche (Aonikenk) culture tied to cold and winter weather; references the type locality La Invernada, a Spanish word for the wintering location of cattle.
Yeneen.description: Yeneen is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian age) Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Yeneen houssayi, known from at least one partial skeleton. Its discovery highlights the diversity of titanosaurs in this formation, which also includes Bonitasaura, Inawentu, Overosaurus, Rinconsaurus, and Traukutitan.

Yimenosaurus.etymology: Named after Yimen County (also written as Yiman) in Yunnan Province, China where it was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Yiman reptile'
Yimenosaurus.description: Yimenosaurus is an extinct genus of plateosaurid sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived in China in the Early Jurassic. The genus was first named in 1990 by Ziqi Bai, Jie Yang and Guohui Wang, along with its type and only species, Yimenosaurus youngi. The species name honours renowned Chinese paleontologist Yang Zhongjian, the father of Chinese paleontology, known as C.C. Young in English. Known material includes the holotype, an almost complete skull and mandible, as well as incomplete cervical and dorsal vertebrae, a mostly complete sacrum, an ilium, ischia, partial ribs and complete femur, and a paratype, a well-preserved postcrania with a fragmentary skull. In 2010 Paul estimated its length at 9 metres (30 ft) and its weight at 2 tonnes (2.2 short tons).

Yingshanosaurus.etymology: Named after Yingshan (a locality in Sichuan Province, China), combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Yingshan lizard'
Yingshanosaurus.description: Yingshanosaurus is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaurs from the Middle Jurassic of what is now Southwestern China. It is known from a partial skeleton discovered in 1983, including back, sacrum, and tail vertebrae, forelimb and hindlimb bones, shoulder and hip bones, and several osteoderms, including plates and a shoulder spine. The genus contains a single species, Yingshanosaurus jichuanensis, named and described in 1994. For some time after its discovery and scientific description, many paleontologists were unaware of the Chinese research published on it and questioned its validity.

Yizhousaurus.etymology: Named for the Yizhou region (Chuxiong Yi Autonomous Region) of Yunnan, China, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Yizhousaurus.description: Yizhousaurus is a genus of basal sauropodiform dinosaurs which existed in what is now Lufeng Formation, Yunnan Province of southern China during the lower Jurassic period. Although its name was revealed in a 2010 Geological Society of America abstract by Sankar Chatterjee, T. Wang, S.G. Pan, Z. Dong, X.C. Wu, and Paul Upchurch, it wasn't validly named and described until 2018. The type species is Yizhousaurus sunae.
