Yongjinglong.description: Yongjinglong is an extinct genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous of Lanzhou-Minhe Basin of Gansu Province, China. It contains a single species, Yongjinglong datangi.

species.name: Yongjinglong datangi
species.etymology: Named both for the Tang dynasty of China and for Zhi-Lu Tang of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP), in recognition of his contributions to the study of dinosaurs.

references.authors: Li, Li-Guo; Li, Da-Qing; You, Hai-Lu; Dodson, Peter
references.title: A New Titanosaurian Sauropod from the Hekou Group (Lower Cretaceous) of the Lanzhou-Minhe Basin, Gansu Province, China

Ypupiara.etymology: From Tupi (indigenous Brazilian language) meaning 'the one who lives in the water,' derived from a figure in Tupi mythology
Ypupiara.description: Ypupiara is an extinct genus of unenlagiine theropod from the Late Cretaceous Serra da Galga Formation of Brazil. It was the first member of the Dromaeosauridae to be discovered in South America and the first member of the Unenlagiinae to be discovered, but not the first to be identified as such. The type and only species, Y. lopai, is known solely from a specimen that was destroyed in a fire in 2018.

species.name: Ypupiara lopai
species.etymology: Named for Alberto Lopa, the discoverer of the holotype specimen in the 1950s.

holotype.institution: Museu da Divisão de Geologia e Mineralogia

references.authors: Brum, Arthur S.; Pêgas, Rodrigo V.; Bandeira, Kamila L. N.; Souza, Lucy G.; Campos, Diogenes A.; Kellner, Alexander W. A.
references.title: A new unenlagiine (Theropoda, Dromaeosauridae) from the Upper Cretaceous of Brazil

Yuanmousaurus.etymology: Named for Yuanmou County in Yunnan, China, where the fossils were recovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Yuanmousaurus.description: Yuanmousaurus was a sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic period of China. It is known from incomplete remains, recovered in 2000 from the Zhanghe Formation in Yuanmou County in Yunnan Province. Yuanmousaurus was a relatively large sauropod and may have reached about 17 meters (56 ft) in length. It was a basal member of the Sauropoda, but its exact systematic position is unclear. A recent study placed Yuanmousaurus within the family Mamenchisauridae. It may be a dubious genus. The only and type species was Yuanmousaurus jiangyiensis.

species.name: Yuanmousaurus jiangyiensis
species.etymology: Named for the village of Jiangyi in Yuanmou County, Yunnan Province, China, where the only known specimen was collected.

references.authors: Lü, J.; Li, S.; G. Wang, J. Zhang, Z. Dong
references.title: New eusauropod dinosaur from Yuanmou of Yunnan province, China

Yuanyanglong.etymology: From Chinese yuanyang meaning 'mandarin duck' (or 'lovebird') and long meaning 'dragon'; translates as 'lovebird dragon,' likely referring to the two individuals found together
Yuanyanglong.description: Yuanyanglong is an extinct genus of oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous Miaogou Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, Yuanyanglong bainian, known from two partial skeletons.

species.name: Yuanyanglong bainian
species.etymology: From the Chinese 'bainian' (百年) meaning 'a hundred years', commemorating the centenary of the first named oviraptorosaur taxa, Chirostenotes and Oviraptor, described in 1924.

holotype.material: Partial skeleton

references.authors: Hao, Mingze; Li, Zhiyu; Wang, Zhili; Wang, Shuqiong; Ma, Feimin; Qinggele; Logan King, J.; Pei, Rui; Zhao, Qi; Xu, Xing
references.title: A new oviraptorosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Miaogou Formation of western Inner Mongolia, China

Yueosaurus.etymology: Named for 'Yue', the ancient name for Zhejiang Province, China, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Yueosaurus.description: Yueosaurus is an extinct genus of basal neornithischian dinosaur known from Zhejiang Province, China.

species.name: Yueosaurus tiantaiensis
species.etymology: Named for the Tiantai locality in Zhejiang Province, China, where the holotype was collected.

references.authors: Zheng, Wenjie; Jin, Xingsheng; Shibata, Masateru; Azuma, Yoichi; Yu, Fangming
references.title: A new ornithischian dinosaur from the Cretaceous Liangtoutang Formation of Tiantai, Zhejiang Province, China

Yulong.etymology: From Chinese 豫 (yù), the one-character abbreviation of Henan Province (referencing the genus's occurrence there), and 龙 (lóng) meaning 'dragon', a common suffix for Chinese dinosaur names.
Yulong.description: Yulong is an extinct genus of derived oviraptorid theropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Qiupa Formation of Henan Province, central China. It contains a single species, Yulong mini. It is known from many juvenile specimens that represent some of the smallest known oviraptorids and also a single subadult specimen.

species.name: Yulong mini
species.etymology: From Latin 'mini', meaning 'small' or 'miniature', in reference to the diminutive size of the specimens, which represent juvenile individuals.

holotype.material: Five specimens including partial skeletons and skull material; syntype series

references.authors: Lü, Junchang; Currie, Philip J.; Xu, Li; Zhang, Xingliao; Pu, Hanyong; Jia, Songhai
references.title: Chicken-sized oviraptorid dinosaurs from central China and their ontogenetic implications
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Yunganglong.etymology: Honoring the Yungang Grottoes (a UNESCO World Heritage site in Shanxi Province, China near the fossil locality) and Chinese long ('dragon'), meaning 'Yungang dragon'
Yunganglong.description: Yunganglong is an extinct genus of basal hadrosauroid dinosaur known from the early Late Cretaceous lower Zhumapu Formation of Zuoyun County, Shanxi Province of northeastern China. It contains a single species, Yunganglong datongensis.

species.name: Yunganglong datongensis
species.etymology: Named for the city of Datong in northern Shanxi Province, China, the region where the holotype was found.

references.authors: Wang, Run-Fu; You, Hai-Lu; Xu, Shi-Chao; Wang, Suo-Zhu; Yi, Jian; Xie, Li-Juan; Jia, Lei; Li, Ya-Xian
references.title: A New Hadrosauroid Dinosaur from the Early Late Cretaceous of Shanxi Province, China

Yunmenglong.etymology: Named after the Yunmengshan area of Henan Province, China where it was found, combined with Chinese long meaning 'dragon'; translates as 'Yunmeng dragon'
Yunmenglong.description: Yunmenglong is an extinct genus of somphospondylan sauropod known from the late Early Cretaceous of Henan Province, central China. Its remains were discovered in the Haoling Formation of the Ruyang Basin. The type species is Yunmenglong ruyangensis, described in 2013 by Junchang Lü et al. on the basis of an incomplete postcranial skeleton. Yunmenglong shares some characters with Euhelopus, Qiaowanlong, and Erketu; a phylogenetic analysis places it as a sister taxon of Qiaowanlong, both grouped with Erketu in a position more derived than Euhelopus but basal to Titanosauria.

species.name: Yunmenglong ruyangensis
species.etymology: Named for the Ruyang Basin in Henan Province, China, where the fossil remains were discovered in the Haoling Formation.

references.authors: Lü, Junchang; Xu, Li; Pu, Hanyong; Zhang, Xingliao; Zhang, Yiyang; Jia, Songhai; Chang, Huali; Zhang, Jiming; Wei, Xuefang
references.title: A new sauropod dinosaur (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the late Early Cretaceous of the Ruyang Basin (central China)

Yunnanosaurus.etymology: Named for Yunnan Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Yunnanosaurus.description: Yunnanosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived approximately 199 to 183 million years ago in what is now the Yunnan Province, in China, for which it was named. Yunnanosaurus was a large sized, moderately-built, ground-dwelling, quadrupedal herbivore, that could also walk bipedally, and ranged in size from 7 meters (23 feet) long and 2 m (6.5 ft) high to 4 m (13 ft) high in the largest species.

species.name: Yunnanosaurus huangi
species.etymology: Named for Huang Chiching (T.K. Huang), the director of the National Geological Survey of China at the time the species was described.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.authors: Young, C.-C.
references.title: Preliminary notes on the Lufeng vertebrate fossils
references.journal: Bulletin of the Geological Society of China

Yunyangosaurus.etymology: Named for Yunyang County in Chongqing, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Yunyangosaurus.description: Yunyangosaurus is a genus of possible megalosauroid dinosaur from the Xintiangou Formation in Chongqing, China. The type and only species is Yunyangosaurus puanensis. The name was first published in the 2019 SVP abstract book by Dai (2019) before it was formally described by Dai et al. (2020).

species.name: Yunyangosaurus puanensis
species.etymology: Named for Pu'an town in Yunyang County, Chongqing, China, the locality where the holotype specimen was found.

holotype.institution: Chongqing Laboratory of Geoheritage Protection and Research
holotype.material: Partial skeleton comprising 11 presacral vertebrae, cervical and dorsal ribs, and chevrons

references.authors: Dai, Hui; Benson, Roger; Hu, Xufeng; Ma, Qingyu; Tan, Chao; Li, Ning; Xiao, Ming; Hu, Haiqian; Zhou, Yuxuan; Wei, Zhaoying; Zhang, Feng; Jiang, Shan; Li, Deliang; Peng, Guangzhao; Yu, Yilun; Xu, Xing
references.title: A new possible megalosauroid theropod from the Middle Jurassic Xintiangou Formation of Chongqing, People’s Republic of China and its implication for early tetanuran evolution
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Yurgovuchia.etymology: From the Ute language meaning 'coyote,' referencing the indigenous peoples of Utah where it was found
Yurgovuchia.description: Yurgovuchia is a genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaurs that lived in North America during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now the Cedar Mountain Formation. It contains a single species, Yurgovuchia doellingi. The remains were discovered in Utah, United States.

species.name: Yurgovuchia doellingi
species.etymology: Named for Helmut Doelling, a geologist who conducted over 50 years of geological research and mapping of Utah for the Utah Geological Survey, whose work led to the discovery of the Doelling's Bowl dinosaur sites.

references.authors: Senter, Phil; Kirkland, James I.; DeBlieux, Donald D.; Madsen, Scott; Toth, Natalie
references.title: New Dromaeosaurids (Dinosauria: Theropoda) from the Lower Cretaceous of Utah, and the Evolution of the Dromaeosaurid Tail

Yutyrannus.etymology: From Mandarin Chinese 'yu' meaning 'feather' and Latinized Greek 'tyrannos' meaning 'tyrant', translating as 'feathered tyrant'.
Yutyrannus.description: Yutyrannus is a genus of proceratosaurid tyrannosauroid dinosaur which contains a single known species, Yutyrannus huali. This species lived during the early Cretaceous period in what is now northeastern China. Three fossils of Yutyrannus huali — all found in the rock beds of Liaoning Province — are the largest-known dinosaur specimens that preserve direct evidence of feathers.

species.name: Yutyrannus huali
species.etymology: From Mandarin Chinese 'huali' (华丽/華麗) meaning 'beautiful', in reference to the perceived beauty of the animal's plumage.

references.authors: Xu, Xing; Wang, Kebai; Zhang, Ke; Ma, Qingyu; Xing, Lida; Sullivan, Corwin; Hu, Dongyu; Cheng, Shuqing; Wang, Shuo
references.title: A gigantic feathered dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of China
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Yuxisaurus.etymology: Named after Yuxi, a city in Yunnan Province, China (the type locality), combined with Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Yuxi lizard'
Yuxisaurus.description: Yuxisaurus is an extinct genus of early thyreophoran dinosaur from the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian-Toarcian) Fengjiahe Formation of southwestern China. The genus contains a single species, Yuxisaurus kopchicki, known from a partial skeleton and many osteoderms.

species.name: Yuxisaurus kopchicki
species.etymology: Named for John J. Kopchick, a biologist honored by the describers of the genus.

location.locality: Jiaojiadian area B, near Zhanmatian village

references.authors: Yao, X.; Barrett, P. M.; L. Yang, X. Xu, S. D. Bi
references.title: A new early branching armored dinosaur from the Lower Jurassic of southwestern China

Yuzhoulong.etymology: Named after Yuzhou, the ancient name for Chongqing, China, combined with Chinese long meaning 'dragon'; translates as 'Chongqing dragon'
Yuzhoulong.description: Yuzhoulong is a genus of macronarian sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Shaximiao Formation of Chongqing, China. The type and only species is Yuzhoulong qurenensis.

species.name: Yuzhoulong qurenensis
species.etymology: Named for Quren, the ancient name of Yunyang County in Chongqing, China, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Chongqing Laboratory of Geoheritage Protection and Research

references.authors: Dai, Hui; Tan, Chao; Xiong, Can; Ma, Qingyu; Li, Ning; Yu, Haidong; Wei, Zhaoying; Wang, Ping; Yi, Jian; Wei, Guangbiao; You, Hailu; Ren, Xinxin
references.title: New macronarian from the Middle Jurassic of Chongqing, China: phylogenetic and biogeographic implications for neosauropod dinosaur evolution

Zalmoxes.etymology: Named after Zalmoxis (also spelled Zamolxis), a deity or legendary king worshipped by the Getae people of ancient Thrace and Dacia (modern Romania), where the fossil was found.
Zalmoxes.description: Zalmoxes is a genus of probable rhabdodontid ornithopod dinosaur from the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Romania. The genus is known from specimens first named as the species Mochlodon robustum in 1899 by Franz Nopcsa before being reclassified as Rhabdodon robustum by him in 1915. In 1990, this name was corrected to Rhabdodon robustus by George Olshevsky and, in 2003, the species was once more reclassified as the type species Zalmoxes robustus. Zalmoxes represents one of the most common vertebrates of Transylvania during the latest Cretaceous period. The generic name refers to the Dacian deity Zalmoxis and the specific name robustus refers to the robustness of the remains. Another species, Zalmoxes shqiperorum, was named in 2003, but this species has since been reassigned to a separate genus of ceratopsian, Ferenceratops.

synonyms.name: Onychosaurus
synonyms.reason: An obscure historical name; the material is now generally treated as referable to Zalmoxes.

species.name: Zalmoxes robustus
species.etymology: From Latin 'robustus' meaning 'robust' or 'strong', referring to the robust build of the skeletal remains.

references.authors: Weishampel, David B.; Jianu, Coralia‐Maria; Csiki, Zoltan; Norman, David B.
references.title: Osteology and phylogeny of Zalmoxes (n. g.), an unusual Euornithopod dinosaur from the latest Cretaceous of Romania

Zanabazar.etymology: Named after Öndör Gegeen Zanabazar, the first Jebtsundamba Khutuktu and supreme spiritual leader of Mongolian Buddhism in the 17th century, honoring the Mongolian heritage of the fossil's origin.
Zanabazar.description: Zanabazar is an extinct genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Maastrichtian Nemegt Formation of Mongolia. The type species is Zanabazar junior, known from a single skull.

species.name: Zanabazar junior
species.etymology: Originally named Saurornithoides junior by Rinchen Barsbold in 1974, as it was considered a distinct, generally smaller, and often assumed 'younger' or less robust form compared to Saurornithoides mongoliensis.

holotype.institution: Geological Institute, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.title: A Review of the Mongolian Cretaceous Dinosaur Saurornithoides (Troodontidae: Theropoda)
references.publisher: American Museum of Natural History (BioOne sponsored)

Zapalasaurus.etymology: Named for Zapala, a city in Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina, near where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Zapalasaurus.description: Zapalasaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous-aged La Amarga Formation of what is today Patagonia. The type and only species is Z. bonapartei.

species.name: Zapalasaurus bonapartei
species.etymology: Named for José F. Bonaparte, the prominent Argentine paleontologist who led the excavation team that recovered the holotype specimen.

holotype.institution: Museo Provincial de Ciencias Naturales "Dr, Prof. Juan A. Olsacher"

Zapsalis.etymology: From Greek za meaning 'thorough' (an intensifying prefix) and psalis meaning 'pair of scissors'; translates as 'thorough scissors,' referring to the cutting teeth
Zapsalis.description: Zapsalis is a genus of dromaeosaurine theropod dinosaurs. It is a tooth taxon, often considered dubious because of the fragmentary nature of the fossils, which include teeth but no other remains.

species.name: Zapsalis abradens
species.etymology: From Latin 'abradens' meaning 'abrading' or 'scraping', likely in reference to the teeth's cutting or scraping function.

holotype.material: Single theropod tooth (type of a monotypic genus, "Genotype" in pre-ICZN terminology)

references.title: Notice of new dinosaurian reptiles from the Jurassic formation

Zaraapelta.etymology: From Mongolian 'zaraa' meaning 'hedgehog', in reference to the prickly appearance of ankylosaurs, combined with Greek 'pelte' meaning 'small shield', a common component of ankylosaurian names referring to their body armour
Zaraapelta.description: Zaraapelta is an extinct genus of herbivorous ankylosaurid thyreophoran dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia. The type species is Zaraapelta nomadis, named and described by Arbour et al in 2014. Zaraapelta is known from a single skull from the Barun Goyot Formation. It was found to be closest to Tarchia in the phylogenetic analysis within its description.

species.name: Zaraapelta nomadis
species.etymology: From the Latin genitive of 'nomas' meaning 'nomad', honoring the Nomadic Expeditions travel agency that organized many palaeontological expeditions to Mongolia.

location.locality: Khermin Tsav I, Lower White Beds

holotype.institution: Paleontological Center, Mongolian Academy of Sciences

references.title: The ankylosaurid dinosaurs of the Upper Cretaceous Baruungoyot and Nemegt formations of Mongolia

Zavacephale.etymology: From Greek zava meaning 'origin' or 'beginning' and kephale meaning 'head'; translates as 'origin head,' referring to its status as the oldest known pachycephalosaur
Zavacephale.description: Zavacephale is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurian dinosaurs known from the Early Cretaceous Khuren Dukh Formation of Mongolia. The genus contains a single species, Zavacephale rinpoche, known from a partial articulated skeleton including a nearly complete skull. It is both the oldest definitive pachycephalosaur known, as well as the most complete. Its skull bears a well-developed dome structure, as seen in most members of the clade.

species.name: Zavacephale rinpoche
species.etymology: From the Tibetan 'rinpoche' meaning 'precious one', alluding to the domed skull found exposed in the rock outcrop, reminiscent of a cabochon gemstone.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Center, Mongolian Academy of Sciences
holotype.material: Partial skull roof

references.title: A domed pachycephalosaur from the early Cretaceous of Mongolia

Zby.etymology: Named after Georges Zbyszewski, the geologist and paleontologist who studied the geology and paleontology of Portugal, where the fossil was found.
Zby.description: Zby is an extinct genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur known from the Late Jurassic, particularly late Kimmeridgian stage of the Lourinhã Formation, in central west Portugal. It contains a single species, Zby atlanticus. It is named after Georges Zbyszewski, who studied the geology and paleontology of Portugal.

species.name: Zby atlanticus
species.etymology: Named for the Atlantic Ocean, near whose Portuguese coast the fossil was discovered, with the Latin suffix '-icus' meaning 'of' or 'pertaining to'.

references.title: Zby atlanticus, a new turiasaurian sauropod (Dinosauria, Eusauropoda) from the Late Jurassic of Portugal

Zephyrosaurus.etymology: Named after Zephyros (the Greek god of the west wind), combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'westward wind lizard,' referencing its discovery in western North America
Zephyrosaurus.description: Zephyrosaurus is a genus of orodromine ornithischian dinosaur based on a partial skull and postcranial fragments discovered in the Early Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian) Cloverly Formation of Carbon County, Montana, USA. New remains are under description, and tracks from Maryland and Virginia, also in the US, have been attributed to animals similar to Zephyrosaurus.

species.name: Zephyrosaurus schaffi
species.etymology: Named for Charles R. Schaff, who discovered the type specimen in the Cloverly Formation of Montana.

holotype.institution: Museum of Comparative Zoology, Harvard University
holotype.material: Jaw fragments, braincase and associated bones, partial vertebrae, and rib fragments

Zhanghenglong.etymology: Named after Zhang Heng, the first-century Chinese scientist, combined with Mandarin long (龙), meaning 'dragon'; thus 'Zhang Heng's dragon'
Zhanghenglong.description: Zhanghenglong is an extinct genus of herbivorous hadrosauroid iguanodont dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (middle Santonian stage) Majiacun Formation in Xixia County of Henan Province, China. It contains a single species, Zhanghenglong yangchengensis, represented by a disarticulated and partial cranium and postcranial skeleton.

species.name: Zhanghenglong yangchengensis
species.etymology: Named for Yangcheng, an administrative unit during the Eastern Zhou dynasty that partially coincides with present-day Henan Province, China, where the fossil was found.

holotype.institution: Xixia Museum of Dinosaur Fossil Eggs of China

Zhejiangosaurus.etymology: Named after Zhejiang Province, eastern China where it was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Zhejiang lizard'
Zhejiangosaurus.description: Zhejiangosaurus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (Cenomanian stage) of Zhejiang, eastern China. It was first named by a group of Chinese authors Lü Junchang, Jin Xingsheng, Sheng Yiming and Li Yihong in 2007 and the type species is Zhejiangosaurus lishuiensis ("from Lishui", where the fossil was found). It has no diagnostic features, and thus is a nomen dubium.

species.name: Zhejiangosaurus lishuiensis
species.etymology: Named for Lishui, the Chinese administrative unit in Zhejiang Province where the fossil remains were collected.

references.authors: Lü, J.; Jin, X.; Y. Sheng, Y. Li, G. Wang, Y. Azuma
references.title: New nodosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Lishui, Zhejiang Province, China

Zhenyuanlong.etymology: Named after Sun Zhenyuan, who discovered the specimen, combined with Chinese Pinyin lóng (龙/龍) meaning 'dragon'; thus 'Zhenyuan's dragon'
Zhenyuanlong.description: Zhenyuanlong is a genus of dromaeosaurid dinosaur from the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China. It lived during the Aptian age of the early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 million years ago. It is known from a single specimen belonging to the species Zhenyuanlong suni (Chinese: 孫氏振元龍). This type specimen preserved a nearly complete skeleton that contains traces of feathers, including long tail feathers and large wings. In addition to further complicating diversity of Liaoning dromaeosaurids, this specimen provides the first direct evidence of well-developed pennaceous feathers in a large, non-flying dromaeosaur, raising the question of what function such wings would serve.

species.name: Zhenyuanlong suni
species.etymology: Named for Zhenyuan Sun, a representative of the Jinzhou Paleontological Museum who secured the specimen for study, with 'suni' being the Latin genitive of his family name.

references.authors: Lü, Junchang; Brusatte, Stephen L.
references.title: A large, short-armed, winged dromaeosaurid (Dinosauria: Theropoda) from the Early Cretaceous of China and its implications for feather evolution

Zhongjianosaurus.etymology: Named for Zhongjian Young (Yang Zhongjian), the father of Chinese vertebrate paleontology, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Zhongjianosaurus.description: Zhongjianosaurus is a genus of dromaeosaurid belonging to the Microraptoria. Believed to hail from the Yixian Formation, specifically the middle of the Jehol Biota, it is the smallest known microraptorine thus far discovered and one of the smallest non-avian theropod dinosaurs.

species.name: Zhongjianosaurus yangi
species.etymology: Named for Yang Zhongjian (C.C. Young), the founder of vertebrate paleontology in China, with 'yangi' being the Latin genitive of his family name.

holotype.material: Partial postcranial articulated skeleton

Zhongornis.etymology: From Chinese zhong meaning 'intermediate' or 'middle' and Greek ornis meaning 'bird'; translates as 'intermediate bird,' referring to its transitional morphology
Zhongornis.description: Zhongornis is a genus of primitive maniraptoran dinosaurs that lived during the Early Cretaceous. It was found in rocks of the Yixian Formation in Lingyuan City (China), and described by Gao et al. in 2008.

species.name: Zhongornis haoae
species.etymology: Named in honour of Ms. Hao, who donated the specimen to the Dalian Natural History Museum.

Zhongyuansaurus.description: Zhongyuansaurus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaurs known from the Early Cretaceous Haoling Formation of what is now Henan Province, China. The genus contains two species, Z. luoyangensis, named in 2007, and Z. junchangi, named in 2025, both known from a single partial skeleton. Zhongyuansaurus is similar to Gobisaurus, prompting some researchers to regard the genera as synonymous.

references.authors: Xu, L.; Lü, J.; X. Zhang, S. Jia, W. Hu, J. Zhang, Y. Wu, Q. Ji
references.title: [A new nodosaurid ankylosaur from the Cretaceous of Ruyang, Henan Province]

Zhuchengceratops.etymology: Named for Zhucheng, the city in Shandong Province, China where the fossil was found, combined with Latinized Greek 'ceratops' meaning 'horned face'.
Zhuchengceratops.description: Zhuchengceratops is a genus of extinct leptoceratopsid ceratopsian that lived during the Upper Cretaceous of modern-day China. It was first described in 2010, by Xu et al., who created the binomial Zhuchengceratops inexpectus. The name is derived from the location of Zhucheng, the Latinized-Greek ceratops, or "horned face", and the unexpected articulated nature of the holotype. The skeleton was found in the Wangshi Group, which is of Late Cretaceous age, and most fossils are only disarticulated bones of Shantungosaurus.

species.name: Zhuchengceratops inexpectus
species.etymology: From Latin 'inexpectus' meaning 'unexpected', referring to the surprising discovery of the articulated skeleton amid the otherwise largely disarticulated Zhucheng dinosaur assemblage.

references.authors: Xu, Xing; Wang, Kebai; Zhao, Xijin; Sullivan, Corwin; Chen, Shuqing
references.title: A New Leptoceratopsid (Ornithischia: Ceratopsia) from the Upper Cretaceous of Shandong, China and Its Implications for Neoceratopsian Evolution

Zhuchengtitan.etymology: Named after Zhucheng, Shandong Province, China where it was found, combined with Greek titan meaning 'giant'; translates as 'Zhucheng titan'
Zhuchengtitan.description: Zhuchengtitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Shandong, China. It contains a single species, Z. zangjiazhuangensis, named by Mo Jinyou and colleagues in 2017 from a single humerus. Zhuchengtitan can be identified by the extreme width of the top end of its humerus, as well as the expansion of the deltopectoral crest on its humerus; both of these characteristics indicate that it was likely closely related to Opisthocoelicaudia. However, it differs from the latter by the flatter bottom articulating surface of its humerus. Zhuchengtitan lived in a floodplain environment alongside Shantungosaurus, Zhuchengtyrannus, and Sinoceratops.

species.name: Zhuchengtitan zangjiazhuangensis
species.etymology: Named for the Zangjiazhuang Quarry in Zhucheng, Shandong, China, where the holotype humerus was recovered.

references.authors: Mo, J.; Wang, K.; S. Chen, P. Wang, X. Xu
references.title: A new titanosaurian sauropod from the Late Cretaceous strata of Shandong Province

Zhuchengtyrannus.etymology: Named after Zhucheng, Shandong Province, China (the type locality), combined with Latin tyrannus meaning 'tyrant'; translates as 'Zhucheng tyrant'
Zhuchengtyrannus.description: Zhuchengtyrannus is a genus of tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaur from Asia, known from the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous of Shandong Province, China. It belongs to the subfamily Tyrannosaurinae, and contains a single species, Zhuchengtyrannus magnus.

species.name: Zhuchengtyrannus magnus
species.etymology: From Latin 'magnus' meaning 'great', referring to the relatively large size of Zhuchengtyrannus among tyrannosaurids.

references.authors: Hone, David W.E.; Wang, Kebai; Sullivan, Corwin; Zhao, Xijin; Chen, Shuqing; Li, Dunjin; Ji, Shuan; Ji, Qiang; Xu, Xing
references.title: A new, large tyrannosaurine theropod from the Upper Cretaceous of China

Ziapelta.etymology: Named after the Zia sun symbol, the stylized sun emblem of the Zia Pueblo people of New Mexico, where the fossil was found, combined with Greek 'pelta' meaning 'small shield', referring to its ankylosaur armor.
Ziapelta.description: Ziapelta is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid. Its fossils have been found in the Hunter Wash and De-na-zin members of the Kirtland Formation of Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) New Mexico. It was named in 2014, in a research paper led by ankylosaur researcher Victoria Arbour. There is a single species in the genus, Ziapelta sanjuanensis. The genus is named after the Zia sun symbol, a stylized sun with four groups of rays, having religious significance to the Zia people of New Mexico, and the iconic symbol on the state flag of New Mexico, and pelta (Latin), a small shield, in reference to the osteoderms found on all ankylosaurids. The specific name is in reference to San Juan County and the San Juan basin, where the fossils were found. Multiple specimens have been described to date, though the fossils are mostly from the front part of the animal. Its closest relative appears to be either Scolosaurus or Nodocephalosaurus, depending on what cladistic model is used.

species.name: Ziapelta sanjuanensis
species.etymology: Named for San Juan County and the San Juan Basin in New Mexico, USA, where the fossils were discovered.

holotype.institution: New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science

references.authors: Arbour, Victoria M.; Burns, Michael E.; Sullivan, Robert M.; Lucas, Spencer G.; Cantrell, Amanda K.; Fry, Joshua; Suazo, Thomas L.
references.title: A New Ankylosaurid Dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (Kirtlandian) of New Mexico with Implications for Ankylosaurid Diversity in the Upper Cretaceous of Western North America

Zigongosaurus.etymology: Named for Zigong City in Sichuan, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Zigongosaurus.description: Zigongosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Middle-Late Jurassic-aged Shaximiao Formation of Zigong, Sichuan, China. Because of incomplete knowledge of Jurassic Chinese sauropods, it has been hard to interpret, with some sources assigning it to Omeisaurus, some to Mamenchisaurus, and some to its own genus.

species.name: Zigongosaurus fuxiensis
species.etymology: Named for Fuxi, a locality in Sichuan Province, China, near the fossil site.

references.authors: Hou, L.-h.; Zhou, S.-w.; S.-c. Chao
references.title: [New discovery of sauropod dinosaurs from Sichuan]

Zizhongosaurus.etymology: Named after Zizhong County in Sichuan Province, China where it was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Zizhong lizard'
Zizhongosaurus.description: Zizhongosaurus is a genus of basal herbivorous sauropod dinosaur which lived in the Early Jurassic (Toarcian) Period of China. It was a large-bodied herbivore characterized by a long neck.

species.name: Zizhongosaurus chuanchengensis
species.etymology: Named for the town of Chuancheng in Sichuan Province, China.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
holotype.material: Three syntypes: partial dorsal vertebra, humerus, and pubis

Zuniceratops.etymology: From Zuni, referring to the Zuni people of New Mexico near where the specimen was found, and Greek keratops meaning 'horned face'; thus 'Zuni horned face'
Zuniceratops.description: Zuniceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaurs that lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now New Mexico, United States. Only a single species is known, Zuniceratops christopheri.

species.name: Zuniceratops christopheri
species.etymology: Named for Christopher James Wolfe, the eight-year-old who discovered the first specimens in 1996.

references.authors: Wolfe, D. G.; Kirkland, J. I.

Zuolong.etymology: Named in honor of General Zuo Zongtang (also known as General Tso), a 19th-century Chinese military leader, combined with Chinese 'long' meaning 'dragon'.
Zuolong.description: Zuolong is an extinct genus of tetanuran theropod from the Late Jurassic period of China. The type and only species is Z. salleei. The generic name of Zuolong is in honor of General Zuo Zōngtáng (also known as "General Tso") with the Chinese word "long" which means dragon. The specific epithet "salleei" is in honor of Hilmar Sallee, who funded the expedition which led to the specimen's discovery.

species.name: Zuolong salleei
species.etymology: Named for Hilmar Sallee, who funded the expedition that led to the discovery of the holotype specimen.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology

references.title: A basal coelurosaur (Dinosauria: Theropoda) from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) of the Shishugou Formation in Wucaiwan, People's Republic of China

Zuoyunlong.etymology: Named for Zuoyun County in Shanxi, China, where the fossils were discovered, combined with Chinese 'long' meaning 'dragon'.
Zuoyunlong.description: Zuoyunlong is an extinct genus of herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur belonging to the Hadrosauroidea that lived during the Late Cretaceous in the area of present China.

species.name: Zuoyunlong huangi
species.etymology: Named for Chinese paleontologist Huang Weilong.

Zupaysaurus.etymology: From Quechua supay meaning 'devil' and Greek sauros (σαυρος) meaning 'lizard'; thus 'devil lizard'
Zupaysaurus.description: Zupaysaurus is an extinct genus of early theropod dinosaur living during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic in what is now Argentina. Fossils of the dinosaur were found in the Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina. Although a full skeleton has not yet been discovered, Zupaysaurus can be considered a bipedal predator, up to 4 metres (13 ft) long. It may have had two parallel crests running the length of its snout.

species.name: Zupaysaurus rougieri
species.etymology: Named for Guillermo Rougier, the scientist who led the expedition that discovered and collected the holotype.

holotype.institution: Museo de Ciencias Naturales, Universidad Nacional de La Rioja (UNLaR)

references.authors: Arcucci, A. B.; Coria, R. A.
references.title: A new Triassic carnivorous dinosaur from Argentina

Zuul.etymology: Named after Zuul, the fictional monster from the 1984 film Ghostbusters, due to the resemblance of its skull to the creature's face
Zuul.description: Zuul is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurine dinosaur from the Campanian Judith River Formation of Montana. The type species is Zuul crurivastator. It is known from a complete skull and tail, which represents the first ankylosaurin known from a complete skull and tail club, as well as the most complete ankylosaurid specimen thus far recovered from North America. The specimen also preserved in situ osteoderms, keratin, and skin remains.

species.name: Zuul crurivastator
species.etymology: From Latin 'crus' meaning 'shank' and 'vastator' meaning 'destroyer', reading as 'Destroyer of Shins' in reference to the presumed defensive tactic of smashing the lower legs of predatory theropods with its tail club.

holotype.material: Near-complete skeleton

references.authors: Arbour, V.M.; Evans, D.C.
references.title: A new ankylosaurine dinosaur from the Judith River Formation of Montana, USA, based on an exceptional skeleton with soft tissue preservation
